Input buffering and slower movement are done (branch `feel/buffer-speed`; protocol 33, after `feel/melee-lock`'s 32; a replayed melee press picks and keeps its lock like a fresh one (`InputBuffer.Replayed` in `GameClient`); the owner's requests
of 2026-10-29, deliberate changes, rules and values ours): **input buffering** (`SmSim.InputBuffer`, wired in `Combat.StepPlayer`): a press of Jump, melee, heavy melee, Grenade,
Switch / slot key or Reload that a running action or recovery blocks (`InputBuffer.Locked`) is kept and replayed as a fresh press until its action starts, for 0.3 s
(`SimConfig.InputBufferWindow`, `GameplayTuning.OwnerInputBuffer`; 9 ticks) and beyond that while its button stays held (letting go after the window cancels it); one at a
time, a newer press replaces it; the hold rule only for Jump and melee, never in a hit reaction or for Jump in the air without a pack (review); Fire never; Jump in a jump-pack take-off or ascent is the hold, never buffered; death clears it. Space held through the air slash's landing
starts the take-off on the recovery's first free tick (0 ticks; lift-off 6 ticks later; before: none while held), measured on the install and with live headless bots
(`--slash-test --slash-jump`, Assault and Raptor). Own record: the thrown-equipment flag byte's bits 3..7 and the raise byte's bits 6..7 (raise ticks now at most 63);
worst case still 1200. **Slower movement** × 0.9 (`SmContent.MovementScale`, `SimConfig.MoveSpeedScale` in the hash): ground speeds and the acceleration cap (run 5.85, sprint 9;
same 6 ticks to full speed), bodies, the jump pack's forward speed 14.4 and air control 7.2 m/s / 13.5 m/s², the dash's and the heavy hop's travel; not the charge, dash attack,
slash, pound dive, melee lunges or the Tactical roll; the charge's sprint gate follows (6.6375 m/s). `GameplayTuning.Load(ownerFeel: false)`: the data's speeds, no buffer.
Spec "Input buffering and slower movement"; `InputBufferTests`, `MovementScaleTests`.

Shorter locks and the sprint stop are done (branch `feel/locks-sprint-stop`; protocol 36, other open branches have 34 and 35: the integrator renumbers; the owner's requests
of 2026-10-29, deliberate changes): **lock scale × 0.7** (`SimConfig.ActionLockScale`, `LockTime`, `GameplayTuning.OwnerLockScale`; an **estimate (owner's request)** to review,
in the hash) on every move / jump / evade gate of an action: melee `MoveAt` (`Combat.MoveAtOf`; the client's leg hand-over follows), the roll's and hop's stick and next-evade
branches, the dash landing's, the evade spacing 0.8 → 0.56 s, the reactions' stick and Jump branches where the data has them before the clip's end (stun and stagger lengths stay the data's; never before the knockback ends; `Reaction.EscapeAt`), the bull rush's and
its collision stop's, a throw's evade gate (`Combat.ThrowHolds`, never before the release); not hit or damage times, lengths, combo / fire / switch / melee branches, the dash
attack, the brace, nor (on that branch) the jump pack's landing locks (feel/jump-pack-2 scales those and the dash attack's exits too). **Jump out of a melee attack**: each attack's `BRANCH_Evade`
(`MeleeStep.EvadeAt`, read by `MeleeTuning`; knife light 0.48 / 0.47 / 0.60 s) lets a Jump press end it and roll, hop or take off (before: not until the attack's end), scaled
but not before the hit when the data opens it after the hit (`Combat.MeleeEvadeOpen`, `MeleeGateAt`). **Sprint stop** (`SmSim.SprintStop`, `PlayerState.SprintStop`): every movement
key let go above the sprint gate (6.64 m/s) slows the body along its velocity (from at most sprint speed) with v² falling at a constant rate over `SimConfig.SprintStopTime` = the stop clip's
`BRANCH_Sprint_Finished` 0.833 s (`SprintStopTuning`; `SM_NAV_Bullrush2Idle_F_01`, 5.79 m root motion): 5.0 m from 9 m/s (before: 0.16 to 0.25 s); a movement key, Jump,
Fire or Aim cancels it into the normal movement; every record's melee byte carries it (64 with step 0, time 0); `SprintStop.ClipTime(speed)` for the client's pose (not posed yet).
Snapshots unchanged (1200). `smtool graph-dump --root-motion [clip..]`. Spec "Action lock scale and the sprint stop"; `LockScaleSprintStopTests` (prints the install's before / after table).

Melee lock is done (branch `feel/melee-lock`; protocol 32, another branch has 31: the integrator renumbers; the owner's knowledge of SM1, 2026-10-29: melee, the
stun strike and the charge "stick" to an enemy and "line up"; every swing steps forward). `SmSim/MeleeLock.cs`: the client picks a lock (global
`directional_targeting_ext`: 45° cone along the stick or view, apex 1 m back, 7 m, 1.5 m high, 1 m distance / 6° angle bands; line of sight; enemies only) from
its view at the input's view tick (`GameClient.ViewAt`) and sends it in the input (u16; 38 bytes an input); the server keeps it while it holds in the rewound
world (`World.SeenBy`) and in that tick's cone (`MeleeLock.Phase`: start along the stick or view, under way along the heading or stick; not through
the other side's spawn blocker), a combo keeps it (1 m leash, ours); lock ticks view the snapshot the client holds nearest their view tick, so the prediction
is exact (tests on flat ground, in a room with a crate, the steered charge). Each attack's `MeleeStep.Reach` (`SmContent.MeleeMotion`, `smtool graph-dump --melee`): its
`AttackAlignment` window (the heading turns to the target, at most 1080°/s, then holds), its distance clips (blend weights 1 / 3.5 / 7 on `FLT_MeleeTargetDistance`)
with their extracted root motion: the body follows it on the ground until `MoveAt` (after it while the stick is idle); without a target the graph's start blend
(the 1 m clip; raised where it backs off), with one the blend at the target's start distance (re-solved each tick), never nearer than 1 m; the bull rush steers to its
lock (180°/s within 45°). Client (`NetworkView.MeleeLock.cs`, rules in `SmNet.MeleePresentation`): distance clips blended at the target's start distance,
root-driven legs (no hand-over), camera assist toward the lock; the hit-stop 0.07 s and hit shakes are OFF by default since 2026-10-29 (owner; opt-in `--hit-stop`); `--no-melee-lock`, `--no-melee-assist`,
`--no-melee-variants`; `--anim-probe` reports the melee clips' foot slide. Snapshots unchanged (1200); install config `1290249E470ACC44` (after the merge with main ce23c26). Spec "Melee target lock,
alignment and lunge"; `MeleeLockTests`, `MeleePresentationTests`, `MeleeLockInstallTests`.

Jump pack paint is done (branch fix/jump-pack-paint, the owner's request 2026-10-29; client and content only, no protocol change): the worn jump pack (Assault, Raptor)
takes the **chest (torso) paint of the look** (`SmContent/Customization/WornPackPaint.cs`, owner's decision; the data's own slot would be the hidden `backpack` entry, which
both default schemes give the same colours as the torso, so the default look is unchanged): `AppearanceAssets.Build` records it in `MarineAssets.PackPaint`,
`WeaponRig.SetPackPaint` puts per-look surface overrides on the pack's meshes (the baked mesh keeps the side's default; materials shared in `WeaponAssets.PackMaterial`),
called every frame by the match (`SyncWeapons`: own look, others' from their codes, `CloneTo` for corpses) and the customizer's preview. Test: `PackPaintTests` (the rule),
`--ui-selftest` (the preview's pack material colour follows the chest swatch), bot log "jump pack is drawn in ...". Backpack weapons are unchanged. Spec "Worn jump pack paint".

Animation pass 3 is done (branch `anim/p3-transitions`; client only, no protocol change; the owner's playtest of 2026-10-29): transitions and connecting clips. Cross-fades start from a
moving copy of the shown pose (dead blending) on a smooth curve with the graphs' blends where read (charge 0.267 s, out of the sprint 0.333 / 0.1 s, out of evades 0.333 s); the sprint graphs'
stop and start clips (`SmContent.SprintTransitions`, `smtool graph-dump --sprint-edges`; `NetworkView.SprintEdges.cs`), posed by the body's speed / distance; the heavy classes sprint on their
weapon's clips (TB / LC) and the cannons hop on the LC set; the pistol's relaxed idle `SM_NAV_IdleL_CS_01` (data; pose-identical to the old idle for the MP weapons' props, so the Assault / Raptor hold the owner flagged is still open: whether the chainsword is drawn at rest); a charge off a ledge falls at once; foot pins let go softly. Probe
`--transition-probe` (jerk per switch), bot `--transition-sweep`, `--ledge-charge`; `--no-p3` for before / after. Integration point for the simulation's sprint stop: `NetworkView.SimSprintStopping`.
Spec "Transitions, connecting clips, the heavy sprint and the pistol idle (animation pass 3)".

The camera hide and the melee hit presentation are done (branch `feel/camera-hitstop`; client only, no protocol change; the owner's requests of 2026-10-29): the whole own character
(model, weapons, worn packs, the jump pack's thrust / idle / dash effects via `FxEffect.Hidden`, the eye glow) is hidden while the follow camera is within 1.4 m of the head and
shown again at 1.61 m (`SmNet.CameraHideRules`, `NetworkView.CameraHide.cs`; ours: before, 1.0 m hid the model only and left the pack effects; a wall holding the camera 1.29 m out showed
the pauldron in the lens; the camera is not shifted: the rig data has no collision offset); the melee hit-stop and the hit shakes (the attacker's 0.5 degrees and the victim's reaction
shake) are off by default, opt-in `--hit-stop` (`--no-hit-stop` is gone); the camera assist toward the lock stays. Test aids: `--bot-backup [--bot-backup-yaw d]` (with `--aim-test`),
`--camera-hide-log`, `--camera-hide-distance`, `--old-camera-hide`. Spec "The own character hides when the camera is close", `docs/changes-from-original.md`.

Charge directions are done (branch `feel/charge-directions`; protocol 39; the owner's playtest of 2026-10-29, user's knowledge and decision): the bull rush starts on F
with **W held**, no sprint and no speed (`Rush.CanStart`, `Rush.WHeld`; supersedes M31's sprint gate, `Rush.SprintThreshold` and `RushSpec.SprintMargin` are gone; aim mode and the
held trigger no longer make it the stun strike; without W, F is the stun strike; the jump-pack classes still charge from the ground only); A or D held with W turns the charge
**25 degrees** to that side (`RushSpec.SideSteer` in the config hash, `Rush.StartYaw`; a stick in between in proportion to its angle beyond the dead zone; ours, an estimate to review; W + F inside the 1 s spacing, or a mashed F replayed when a charge ends, is the stun strike), except that a
charge locking onto a target starts along the view and steers to it as before (`Combat.StepPlayerCore`); the Assault / Raptor dash attack lunges the stick's way of eight around
the view at the melee press (`Rush.DashYaw`; no stick: the view), the body turned to it playing the data's only clip `SM_JMP_DashAtk_F` (ours). Client: the body takes the
simulation's heading at once through every charge phase (`BodyYawFor` snaps instead of the 720 degree a second follow); the camera stays on the view. Snapshots unchanged (1200).
Tests `ChargeDirectionsTests` (W / W + A / W + D charges and eight dash attacks under 150 ms RTT and 5% loss: 0 mismatches); test aids `--bot-charge-dirs`, `--bot-dash-dirs`
(with `--bot-dash-attack`). Spec "Charge directions", `docs/changes-from-original.md`.

Owner's playtest fixes of 2026-10-29 (branch `fix/hitboxes-grenades-bots`; protocol 37): **jump hitboxes**: a jump-pack player is hit with the ragdoll's volumes carried
by their bones into the clip the client draws (take-off clip to 1/3 s after the press, then 27 flight clips x 9 fractions; `SimConfig.FlightHitVolumes`, `SmContent.PosedHitVolumes`);
one engine-free rule for client and server (`SmSim.FlightPoseRules`: damped fraction, low/high hysteresis, clip keys, take-off window), the server keeping each player's view per tick
(`World.FlightViewOf`); the config hash covers the clip names and counts, not the posed floats (Linux server); the client's crosshair, tracer and pierce picture test the same sets.
**View fraction**: inputs carry how far past their view tick the client drew the others (1/256, 39-byte inputs); shots and cones rewind between two ticks (`World.SeenAt`); melee,
the lock and the charge round to the nearest tick (a lock tick snaps to a held snapshot and sends 0). Shots at the drawn body (`FlyingHitboxProbe`, 80 ms): 68.4 % before, 97.5 % now.
**Grenades** (owner's change; the data's reading is right): a ground bounce first loses speed to the blueprint's Havok restitution 0.65 and friction 2 (`RigidSpec.GroundMaterial`):
frag 4.6-12.3 m after landing -> 0-1.1 m, the fuse unchanged. **Test aid**: `smserver --bot-damage-scale f` (0..1; bots mark themselves with the Hello's flags byte, 177 bytes).
`SimConfig.Hash` is cached per instance. Spec "Flying hitboxes, the view fraction, the grenade bounce and the bots' damage scale", `docs/changes-from-original.md`.
The three jumps, the dash attack's walls and the air slash's swing are done (branch `feel/jump-pack-2`; protocol 38, 37 is fix/hitboxes-grenades-bots'; the owner's
requests of 2026-10-29): **jump by the hold** (`JumpPackSpec.HoldTiers`, `JumpPackTuning.ThreeJumps`; owner's decision, "revert to the old jump behavior"): Space let go by
tick 5 after the press (the dash's 0.167 s decision) = the dash; down on tick 5 and let go by tick 12 = the **small jump**, one apex for every medium hold (7.70 m: the hold at
the decision tick; a release while rising decelerates the rise to it, `JumpPack.TierCutGravity`; costs 35); down on tick 12 (the height map's 0.4 s) = the **full jump**
(17.54 m, M14 tick for tick; 55). M45's release cut is off (`ReleaseStopsRise` false; the rule stays as an option). **Dash attack walls**: the lunge meets walls from its first
tick and within 60 degrees of head-on (`JumpPackAttackTuning.DashWallsFromStart`, `DashWallHitAngle`; was from 0.3 s and 25 degrees) into the data's wall state
(`SM_NAV_Bullrush2Idle_F_Collision_01`, the bull rush's connect clip); own camera knock; `--dash-wall-test`. **Air slash**: the graph plays its clip cropped (read now from
the clip generators: `BehaviorSequencer.Crops`, `SlashSpec.FlightClipEnd` / `ImpactClipStart` 0.4667 s): the dive plays the wind-up fitted to the dive, the landing the
overhead strike (`SmNet.SlashPose`; the client had held frame 0 and restarted at 0, showing the wind-up as a backwards swing); `--slash-trace`. **Locks**: the jump-pack
landings' move / jump locks (`JumpPack.MoveLock` / `JumpLock`) and the dash attack's hit, wall stop and run-out exits (`Rush.Begin`) × `SimConfig.LockTime` (0.7, an estimate).
Review fixes: a buffered Jump held past the decision becomes `BufferedAction.JumpLong` (own record value 7) and takes off committed to the small jump (`JumpPack.LongJump`); a charge whose move ends in its wall stop still tests that tick's contacts and the hit wins (`Rush.WallStoppedFrom`, `World.StopRushes`). `NavJumpFlight.SimulationVersion` 8. Spec "The three jumps, the dash attack's walls and the air slash's swing"; `JumpTierTests`, `DashAttackWallTests`, `SlashPoseTests`.

Loyalist barks are done (added content; branch `extras/loyalist-barks`; no protocol bump, `ContentExtras.WireVersion` 2; the owner's request of 2026-10-29): flag
`ContentExtras.LoyalistBarks` (4, `--content loyalist-barks`, in `extended`). Loyalist Space Marines only bark the owner's own ElevenLabs voice pack (32 OGG takes, 8 phrases;
`client/Extras/LoyalistBarks/assets/`, `.gdignore`d, embedded in the client only with added content; provenance in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) at the charge, kills, melee starts,
bolt-fire starts and the own player's first damage after a quiet spell (chances, 8 s per speaker, 20 s per phrase, no take twice in a row, SM1 speech first; all ours), and **T**
shouts FOR THE EMPEROR at any time (2 s cooldown, input bit 13 held 4 ticks and never read by the simulation; relayed in E3's extras envelope, now on this branch: message kind 16,
section tag 2 with the player's shout sequence, so every client hears the same take). A server without the flag drops bit 13; the bit alone is not play for the idle kick.
Code: `SmContent/Extras/LoyalistBarks`, `SmNet/Extras/LoyalistBarks`, `SmServer/Extras/LoyalistBarks`, `client/Extras/LoyalistBarks`; hooks `GameServer.ExtrasSend`,
`NetworkView.ExtrasInput` / `ExtrasFrame` / `ExtrasKill`. Aids `--no-loyalist-barks`, `--log-sound loyalist`, `--loyalist-gain`, `--bot-shout <s>`. Needs the owner's ear (level,
-2 dB on the sound bus). docs/added-content.md section 7; spec "Added content: loyalist barks". Owner's decision (2026-10-29): the automatic barks are off by default (`--loyalist-auto-barks` turns them on); the release plays only the T key's FOR THE EMPEROR.

Combat stims are done (branch `perks/inert-2`; protocol 40: scoreboard rows end with each player's equipment item; the config hash changes; install, extended: `97325DE6449F96B2`): `sm_mp_eq_stimpack` is the classes' third
equipment choice. `SmContent.StimTuning` reads the count by upgrade, `min_time_between_activations` (6 s, as the cooldown), `actn_stims_activated`'s modifiers and
`mp_reaction_immunity` by upgrade and the player graph's stim sequencer (effect at 0.3 s, free at 0.9 s) into a `ThrownSpec` with a `StimSpec` (`ThrownSpec.NoProjectile`);
the use runs as a throw that launches nothing and sets `PlayerState.StimLeft` (5 s; Master-Crafted 7 s): health-only damage taken ranged x0.75 / melee x0.5 / explosive x0.75
(0.6 / 0.35 / 0.6), melee dealt x1.35 (x2), no hit reactions (`SmSim/Stims.cs`). Not on the wire: the client derives it from the record's item cooldown, past it an agreeing prediction (`Stims.Carry`); others' uses are told from throws by the scoreboard's equipment byte (`GameClient.EquipmentOf`). Client: the stim clip over the
upper body, the action's sound and effects, HUD "STIM n.n" (`client/NetworkView.Stims.cs`); test aid `--perks a,b`. Perks: 43 active, 0 partial, 5 inert (Rapid Deployment, Tactical
Readout, Weapon Versatility, Teleport Homer, Signum Link: no value or consumer in the data). Spec "Combat stims"; `StimTests`, `StimTuningTests`.

No smoke is done (branch `fx/no-smoke`; client only, no protocol change; the owner's request of 2026-10-29, a deliberate change): smoke, dust, mist and haze sprites are not drawn in any
effect (impacts keep flash, sparks, debris and decal; explosions their fireball and flash; god rays, lights, blood, tracer streaks, shells and the physics chunks stay). The rule is engine-free and
data-driven (`SmContent.SmokeRules`: blend, texture and element names, the puff shape; `SmokeRulesTests`), applied at compile time (`CNode.Smoke` / `SmokeOnly`, skipped in `FxPlayer.DrawNode`);
`--smoke on` restores the data's look; `smtool fx-smoke auto` lists the 149 of 228 MP effects touched. The "lines on the floor through smoke" were no draw-order fault: a camera-facing card is a plane
through its centre, so the floor in front of it drew over it; alpha-blended camera billboards are now depth-tested at a plane pulled toward the camera (half the half size, at most 1 m; additive ones not;
the near fade keeps the card's own depth; `FxBatch.Pull*`, `--no-fx-pull`). `SmokeInstallPinTests` pins the fight cues' kept sprites. Same 8-player demo: effects phase 3.04 → 1.95 ms a frame, sprites 1158 → 608 (alpha 673 → 151). `--frame-stats` now prints the renderer's mean GPU time. Spec "No smoke" rows.

Performance pass 1 is done (branch `perf/pass-1`; build, client and release launcher; no protocol change; the owner's report "the performance in this build is abysmal"):
the exported game had compiled SmSim, SmNet, SmContent and SmFormats **without JIT optimisation** (Godot's `ExportRelease` configuration is not one Microsoft.NET.Sdk
optimises; `Directory.Build.props` now optimises every project of an export; collision rays 6 to 8.6x faster, the follow camera 1.8 → 0.2 ms a frame; client.cmd still builds
Debug); lean bots (merged with perf/lean-bots on integrate/2026-10-29: one mode, no flag: every headless `--bot` without `--bot-full-load` or a presentation aid, so the menu's
hosted bots, `bots.cmd` and `Launcher.ps1 -StartBots` bots; `SmNet.LeanBot`, `client/BotLean.cs`) skip every presentation-only load and also run at most 30 frames a second
(`--bot-fps n`), 30 physics steps and no effects: 3 hosted bots on 127.0.0.1 measured 254 to 278 MB working set and 0.03 to 0.06 of a core each (the same bot uncapped 0.14); `HitVolumes.Bounds` no longer recomputes a hull's margin per corner (20 to 45 ms crosshair frames while jump-pack players flew); the drops' models load
during the map load (a 100 ms frame at the first drop); human clients use the GC's SustainedLowLatency mode (`--gc-default` off). Replay of an 8-player demo with 7 bots on
the same PC: mean 12.0 → 6.4 ms, frames over 33 ms 24 → 1. Test aid `--perf-probe` (renderer CPU/GPU, draw calls, memory, GC per 5 s). Report and recommendations
(server-side bots, draw calls, allocations, vsync): spec "Performance pass 1".

Playtester launcher is done (branch `launcher/updater`; tools and release only): `src/SmLauncher.Core` (logic, tested) and `src/SmLauncher` (WinForms, `SM Reimpl Launcher.exe`, self-contained single file), shipped in every playtest zip as `0 - SM Reimpl Launcher.exe`. It installs and updates the newest published build of Yeezima/sm-reimpl-releases into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\SM Reimpl` (`versions\<tag>\`, `current.json`, the last two kept for rollback): HTTPS to GitHub hosts only, Range-resumed downloads with retries, SHA-256 against the API digest and the description hash before anything is unpacked, zip-slip-safe staging checked against `notes\CONTENTS-SHA256.txt`, atomic switch, recovery of every interrupted phase (`update.json`), disk-space checks, adopt of an unpacked folder, Check files, Roll back, Clear caches (data root `cache` only), and a self-update through a verified helper that puts the old launcher back on any failure. Player data in `%APPDATA%\sm-reimpl` is never touched. Headless aids: `--selftest`, `--status`, `--check`, `--install-latest`, `--verify`, `--rollback`, `--adopt`; the release smoke runs `--selftest` and the window off-screen. `docs/releasing.md` "The launcher".

Customizer pose and the Ork in the menus is done (branch `ui/customizer-ork`; client and profile only, no protocol change; the owner's requests of 2026-10-29, Ork O9): every marine and Chaos class in the class creator, the appearance editor and the in-match picker stands in the bolt pistol's relaxed idle (`RigClipTable.PistolRelaxedIdle` = `SM_NAV_IdleL_CS_01`, the clip `SM_Pistol_NAV` "Idle Relaxed" binds; `PreviewPoseInstallPinTests`) with the pistol in the hand and the primary stowed (`PreviewStage.HoldsPistol`; the jump-pack classes keep the melee weapon in hand), turned back 35 degrees for the front-quarter view (ours); the turntable is gone (only drag, Left / Right and the right stick turn the figure). In Extended the Ork Boy is in the menus: the creator's faction row adds Orks and a fourth class tab "Ork Boy" (`client/Customizer/Model/OrkLoadout.cs`: fixed shoota, slugga, choppa, stikkbombs and the Tactical's perks), the Join screen an Ork DEFAULTS chip, custom Ork loadouts (role `ork`, kept by `ProfileStore` in every profile), a fifth step LOOK (automatic or one of five boy models, `orkLook` in `customization.json`) instead of the armour and colour editors, the preview on his own rig in his own idle (`PreviewAssets.TryBuildOrk` / `OrkWeapons`), and a Join, Deploy or close of the in-match picker sends his class and look (`JoinPlan.OrkLook`, `LoadoutKey.OrkLook`). Faithful offers none of it: a saved Ork loadout stays, shows "unavailable here", never opens in the editor and joins as the side's default class. The customizer reads the Ork's class data too (63 to 194 ms more on a warm run, on its worker). Checks: `--ui-selftest` (pose, held pistol, no spin, drag, the Ork in Extended and none in Faithful, fit at 7 sizes with the Ork's LOOK step), `CustomizerModelTests` Ork rows. Spec "The customizer's preview pose and the Ork Boy in the menus".

The impact pass is done (branch `fx/impact-pass`; client and content only, no simulation or protocol change; the owner's requests of 2026-10-29): **stomps and slams** (every melee step with a blast, `MeleeStep.Stomp`) play the wargear's `displace_*` effect (`SmContent.MeleeEffects`, entry matched by radius and damage) on the ground under its marker plus ours sized to the blast radius (`client/StompFx.cs`: a ground shockwave of the data's `rings_outer` sprite and a flash light, the crack decal at 0.85 of the diameter, the pound's thin ring, 2 to 3 chunks per metre; no dust, smoke or shake), once per attack keyed on its start tick (`client/ImpactRules`, `MeleeHitGate`: a reconcile rewind never fires twice, a player first seen mid-attack never fires); the **power sword** (both races) plays the data's `powersword_idle` while in hand, a blue blade glow (`client/PowerBlade.cs`, an additive overlay on the blade band measured on the model) and on a hit `powersword_dmg` plus our flare and light at the contact point (`NetworkView.MeleeFx.cs`); **jump-pack thrust**: trails along the last third of their length in metres of the nozzle's path, the `rocket` flame a third as long, every thrust at the nozzle exit (`SmContent.NozzleExit`: Chaos 0.28 m out of its inside-centre markers); **lighting**: the `remaster` look is the default (`--look current` = the old default), its SSR only at medium and high (never low or off), Manufactorum's god rays removed (`--god-rays`). Test aids `--no-stomp-fx`, `--no-sword-fx`, `--old-pack-trail`, `--stomp-test`; tools `smtool fx-dump`, `weapon-parts --profile/--exhaust`. Spec "Stomp impacts, the power sword and the jump-pack thrust (fx/impact-pass)"; `docs/changes-from-original.md` rows.

`smtool gfx-dump` prints and renders the movies. Spec "HUD from the movies (ui/hud-fidelity)"; docs/discovery.md "HUD movies read in full".

Melee flow is done (branch `anim/melee-flow`; client only, no protocol change; the owner's requests of 2026-10-29): **the hammer in both hands** (a thunder hammer / daemon maul marine whose pistol is not up runs on
`SM_TH_NAV` and sprints on `SM_TH_NuSprint` through the gait blend space, `LocomotionAnimations.Hammer`, `SprintFamily.Hammer`; pistol holstered at the draw clip's swap point, `WeaponRig.StowPistol`; the graph's
`SM_1HR_NAV_Pistol2TH` over the upper body when the pistol comes down; its charge shows `SM_TH_BUL_Hit_M_*`); **the strikes' blends from their graphs** (`SmContent.MeleeFlowBlends`, `smtool graph-dump --melee-flow`: entry,
chain and exit per strike; the hand-over's upper body leaves over the move-on exit); **the clip foot lock** (`CharacterViewer.ClipFootLock.cs`, `SmNet.ClipFootLockRules`: a strike's or charge's planted foot that stands
still in the authored world is held by leg IK; melee demo planted-foot speed median 1.81 → 0.00 m/s, frames above 0.5 m/s 74 → 22 %); the melee variant layer fades in with the strike's entry; **stun-strike shake**
(0.35° heavy strike, 0.6° stomp / slam, 0.5° when a charge or dash attack hits a player; ours, `--no-stun-shake`); the charge's body turn over 0.03 s; **ledge charge**: no second bash after landing, the fall's legs ramp from
their first frame; the air slash's early-landing catch-up eased over 0.1 s. Probes on three demos (`--transition-probe-clips`, bot aid `--bot-turn-rate`): all switches median 17.5 → 16.9, p99 200 → 181, max 315 → 210 cm/f².
`--no-melee-flow` for before / after. Spec "Melee flow, the hammer in both hands and the transitions pass (anim/melee-flow)".

The primary is stowed round the right side (branch `fix/stow-right`; client only, no protocol change; owner's knowledge 2026-10-29: "should stow it to the right around their back not the left. currently
the gun floats through the air"): the pistol switch's clip carries the primary's chest prop round the left side onto `MKR_Stow_Bolter` with no hand on it (79 cm from the nearer hand). Now a switch is
`SmContent.SwitchPlan`: the old weapon's own draw played backwards to its attach tag (the primary in the right hand round the right side, released onto the back marker; the pistol back to its thigh),
then the new weapon's draw, the new one taken at its tag (`WeaponRig.Update(.., release, take)`, both stowed between; `PoseSlots.SwitchNext` cross-fades the joint). Every primary of both races (all on
the chest prop and the bolter marker). Test aids: `--switch-test` (standalone, `--switch-shots n`, `--switch-probe`, `--switch-clips`), `--old-stow`, bots `--bot-switch-every s` with
`--wait-switch-window a,b`. Spec "The primary is stowed round the right side"; `SwitchPlanTests`. Rebased onto main after anim/melee-flow: the hammer stance's pistol holster (`StowPistol`) applies on top of the switch's empty-hands interval.

Bot names are done (branch `names/bot-lore`; protocol 41; the owner's request of 2026-10-29: "give the bots lore accurate names instead of the current P1, P2, etc."): the server names each test bot (Hello flag) from its race's pool when it joins (`SmNet.PlayerNames`: 34 loyalist "Brother"/"Sergeant" names, 32 Chaos names with some epithets, 32 Ork names; ours, none a canon character or one letter from one, pinned by `PlayerNameTests`), unique among connected players, seeded (`--name-seed`, else random and printed) by the race's join order; a race change renames at the next scoreboard. Humans keep "P<id>" (no name source yet; `GameServer.SetDisplayName` is the hook). Each scoreboard row ends with the name (u8 length 0..24 + Latin-1, sanitised both ways; snapshots unchanged). Shown in the kill feed, reward line, aimed name, decorators, nameplates, Tab scoreboard (wider), count-up and NEMESIS (wider panels), bot and server logs (`GameServer.Describe`). Spec "Display names: the bots' names".

Melee and charge, second pass is done (branch `feel/melee-charge-2`; protocol 42; the owner's requests of 2026-10-29): a bull rush held in the air ends on a landing after a real fall (at least a 0.5 m free fall's speed, ours; `Rush.EndsOnLanding` / `Landed`; the speed kept up to sprint speed, the landing tick's contact still counts via `Rush.LandedFrom`), and the dash attack held at its end ends on any landing (no run-out); the knife's and chainsword's backhand, kick and shoulder chain to the stomp on a second F in their `BRANCH_Melee_Y_Combo` window (`YNext`, from the graphs; knife stomp from 0.90 s); melee forward root motion × 1.3 (`SimConfig.MeleeLungeScale`, estimate) and the weapon switch 0.6 → 0.48 s (estimate, to measure against the original); the melee lock's alignment eases (smoothstep, windows at least 0.2 s; knife turn-rate jerk 864 → 206 °/s at worst), held locks keep 15° of hysteresis, the client remembers its lock 1 s, the camera assist is gentler; an own melee hit plays the weapon's hit container sound (the power sword's `play_sm_power_sword_hit`; its swings already played `play_sm_powersword_swing`; the hum event is in no bank). Test aids `--bot-heavy-chain`, `--log-sound tag`. Spec "Melee and charge, second pass"; `MeleeCharge2Tests`.

Player collision is done (branch `sim/player-collision`, on `feel/melee-charge-2`; protocol 43; the owner's request of 2026-10-29: "the models shouldn't get stuck inside each other";
before it players had no collision with each other in the simulation): living players' capsules (0.45 m, 1.9 m) block each other in every way of moving, allies and enemies (`SmSim.PlayerCollision`,
hooked in `Movement.Step` / `Glide` / `Fly` inside a `PlayerCollision.Use` scope set by `World.Step` and by the client's prediction and replays). Prediction-exact: each input names the newest snapshot
its client held (`PlayerInput.BodyTick`, a lag byte: inputs 40 bytes), the server keeps every tick's end state (`World.RecordBodies`) and both collide with that snapshot's players carried on by their
velocity (10 ticks, 3 m, never through the stepper); the world never uses a picture older than 24 ticks and the server raises a missing one to that (`World.BoundBodies`: a client cannot shed the bodies).
A move into a body slides along it (a charge or lunge stops at contact; a body is not a wall for the charge's collision stop: `Rush.Move`, nor is the push for the evade's wall test); overlaps in the
snapshot are pushed apart half each at up to 3 m/s; a body coming down on a head is held and slides off at 6 m/s (a pound's dive lands on the head at once); a spawn with every spot taken takes the least
crowded one. Client: remote players are drawn apart (`DrawnBodies`, visual only, at most 0.45 m; `--no-body-separation`). Measured with 8 melee bots on Manufactorum: server ticks with an overlap over
20 cm 22 % -> 2 %, drawn 22-28 % -> 0-0.5 %, prediction corrections unchanged (4 to 13 per bot above 1 mm: deaths and unpredicted hits). Aids: server and client `--no-player-collision` (config hash),
server `--log-overlaps`. Spec "Player collision (sim/player-collision)"; `PlayerCollisionTests`.

**fx/melee-presentation (2026-10-30; client presentation only, no simulation, wire or config-hash change).** Other players' melee hits (and hits on you) now post the attacker weapon's hit sound, inferred from the snapshots: the attacker's step passes its hit time through the same once-per-attack gate the stomp and sword effects use, with an enemy in reach, and the victim must react (health plus shield falls or it dies) within a short window (`MeleeHitConfirm`, tested); charge and dash-attack hits (own from the hit report while a charge is or was just shown, others from the phase change into the collision state) play the data's `body_smash` impact `play_sm_bull_rush_smash` instead of the weapon's hit sound (`play_sm_sk01_bodyslam`, the wargear's other command, is in no bank). Melee weapons hum while in hand with the wargear's own idle events (hammer, maul, axe; the Space Marine sword with the axe's hum from its own on_deploy, the Chaos sword with it as a substitute, both 6 dB quieter; `play_sm_power_sword_idle` is in no bank and the chain axe has no other hum: not reproducible). The hammer's and the axe's deployed effects now play at their markers like the sword's. Aids: `--no-melee-sounds`, `--no-melee-idle-fx`, `--log-sound melee`. Spec "Melee weapon hum", "Others' melee hit sound", "Charge hit sound"; `MeleeSoundsTests`, `MeleeHitConfirmTests`.
HUD second pass is done (branch `ui/hud-2`; client, readers and tests only, no protocol change; the owner's open list of the HUD fidelity pass): the armour and health bar is drawn from the movie's `unifiedhealth_mc`
(`Hud.Vitals.cs`: the dark band, the cyan armour bar `ironhalo_mc` by the armour, the red health bar `healthbar_mc` by the health with a measured red tint, at the movie's own place which matches the footage within
2 stage px; the gold `lightdamagebar_mc` is not drawn), with the movie's starburst flash and the low-health flash clips from the own player's damage (`VitalsRules`, `HudMovieArt` groups that free old frames). The
HUD movie reader draws **morph shapes** (`GfxMorph`, DefineMorphShape and DefineMorphShape2, a placement's ratio), which the stalker scope's reticle needs: its `crosshair` clip (a ring growing with the scatter) is
rendered by itself at the frame of the scatter with the hip reticles' fraction rule (`ScopeArt.RenderCrosshair`, `ScopeView`); the lascannon's scope has none. The grenade launcher's eighteen round slots follow the
rounds left (`WeaponBoxRules.LauncherRoundLoaded`). The reward lines now carry the data's rewards the client can know (`RewardTable`, `RewardTracker`, `Hud.Rewards.cs`: headshot, double to mega kill, killstreaks,
revenge, avenger, grudge, victory in death; names from the locale); the rest of the table (assists, captures, savior, variety, long shot ...) is recorded as not reproducible. The creator's card grows with its text,
shrinks it and scrolls the longest (`CreatorView.FitCard`); `--ui-selftest` checks every perk card of every class at every fit size (`UiSelfTest.PerkCards.cs`). Aids: `--hud-rewards-demo`,
`--hud-launcher-demo`, `--scope-spread-demo`, `--perk-card-shot`. Spec "HUD from the movies (ui/hud-fidelity)" (new rows); `HudRewardTests`, `GfxTests` (morphs).

### hotfix/old-gpu: Old GPU / safe mode (2026-10-30)
A tester's GTX 960M laptop could not run the client (Godot has no DirectX 9; the default driver on Windows is Vulkan). `client/project.godot` now lists the
fallbacks explicitly (Vulkan/D3D12 to the Compatibility renderer, then ANGLE and OpenGL ES; Forward+ stays the default). New `client/SafeMode.cs`: safe mode is on
when the Compatibility renderer is in use or with `--safe-mode`; it logs one line `renderer: <method> (<driver>); ...`, makes lighting low (an explicit `--lighting`
wins, but Compatibility never goes above low), anti-aliasing off (`--aa` wins; SMAA/TAA become MSAA/off on Compatibility) and skips SSAO quality, SSIL, SSR, SDFGI and volumetric fog
(`MapLightingView`, `RenderQuality`). Launcher: "Old GPU / safe mode" checkbox (`LauncherSettings.SafeMode`, `SafeModePolicy` with tests): Godot options
`--rendering-method gl_compatibility --rendering-driver opengl3` plus `--safe-mode`; a game that fails within 8 s turns it on and is started once more. Protocol
unchanged (43). Not verified on real old hardware.

## Five perks (perks/five, protocol 44)

From the owner's recollection of 2026-10-30 (spec "Perks without data"): **Rapid Deployment** respawns in 3 s (base 5 s); **Weapon Versatility** (Tactical only) adds a third
weapon slot on key 3 with a second primary picked in the class creator, validated by the server (`Loadouts.SecondIndex`; `WeaponSlot.Second`, `PlayerState.Second` and the `Third*`
store; the Switch toggle and the wheel cycle the three; three switch cards in the HUD); **Teleport Homer** puts a respawning ally on a free spot next to the living carrier
(`World.TryHomerSpawn`; several carriers: the nearest to the death, an estimate); **Tactical Readout** and **Signum Link** (the same for now) show the enemy under the crosshair a
health and armour bar and no name, and without either perk nothing shows over an enemy (the name is gone). The bars travel in a new message `EnemyBars` (18) only to players
with the perks. Wire: the SlotSecond button, one choice byte, 14 own-record bytes, 15 projectile records at most (worst case still 1200). The five perks are no longer "NOT ACTIVE YET"
(`Perks.ServerRulePerks`). Tests: `FivePerksTests`. A 60 s headless run (server on 127.0.0.1:27163, two bots, one per side) played without a fault or exception. Not verified: the feel of any of it against the original; the HUD cards and the creator rows were not looked at in a window.
Jump pack paint follows the backpack (branch fix/br04-jumppack-paint, bug BR-04; the owner's decision of 2026-10-30, replacing the chest rule of 2026-10-29; client and content only, no protocol change, paint already travels in the appearance code): `WornPackPaint.Slot` is `backpack`, so the worn jump pack (Assault, Raptor) takes the Backpack slot's colours in the customizer preview, after save and reopen, and in the match (own view, others, corpses); the chest colour no longer paints it. Normal backpacks are unchanged. `PackPaintTests` and the `--ui-selftest` pack checks now use the backpack slot. Spec "Worn jump pack paint".
BR-02, no fire in a Tactical's charge (branch `fix/br02-no-fire-charging`; no wire change, protocol unchanged): the owner found the melta firing during the charge animation. The Tactical classes (SM and CSM, role `tactical`; `Rush.NoFire`) now fire nothing from the charge's start to its end: Fire is no longer one of the inputs that end the charge, a held charge or delayed charged shot under way at the start is cancelled, and the weapon waits like in a melee attack (`Combat.StepPlayerCore`). Other classes keep ending their charge on Fire. Tests `NoFireInChargeTests` (melta, rifle, plasma gun, lascannon, pistol; fire before, at the start, during; control: Assault unchanged). Spec "The charge" row "No fire in a Tactical's charge". Not checked against the original beyond the owner's recollection.
BR-03 (fix/br03-capture-hum): the Seize Ground hum after a capture. Cause (headless run, `--bot --log-sound match`, new `MATCH VOICES` line every 5 s): `Play_MP_Points_Total` and `play_mp_point_being_captured` are endless trigger-rate (mode 5) continuous containers that only a stop event ends (`audio-event` now prints "continuous (loop endless, transition mode 5)"); the client posted the score tick once a second without ever posting `Stop_MP_Points_Total`, so each post added another endless chain (continuations 6,900 in 90 s, 38,000 by 160 s, the 16 two-D voices stolen constantly), and capture ticks stacked chains until the stop. Fix: `SoundSystem.Post(once: true)` drops the container's continuation; `SeizeSounds.SingleShot` marks every Seize post (tested). No protocol change.
fx/character-visuals (the owner's playtest notes of 2026-10-30, items 2, 13, 16, 17; client and content only, **no protocol change**, protocol stays at the main branch's): (2) the power sword's glow is the blade overlay alone (`powersword_idle`'s edge sprites and light reached out of the blade and are not played; `--sword-idle-fx` restores them) and flares while an attack is shown (`ImpactRules.SwordSwing`; `--no-sword-swing`). (13) Armour flashes on every model (`ArmourFlashTracker`, `CharacterViewer.Flash.cs`: a rim-weighted additive overlay and a back-face outline pass, one material pair per character): the own model exact from the predicted shield, the others derived from the hits seen (the shot record's armour bit) and the class's regeneration delay, because slim snapshot records carry no shield and the 1200-byte budget is full (a wire bit would have cost 16 bytes and two projectile records); `--no-armour-flash`, `--armour-flash-demo [hit|break|glow]`. Instance shader parameters were tried first and came out wrong (the first one read as zero), so the materials are per character. (16) The melta as a **primary** was drawn all along (dark texture); the invisible gun was Weapon Versatility's **second primary**: `WeaponRig` knew only primary and pistol. It now carries `HandRole.Second`, and `BackWeapon.Owner` hangs only the primary swapped out last on the back; test aid `--second <primary>` (with `--perks secondary_weapon`). (17) `LensGlow`: two additive sprites per eye in the lens colour on every Marine and Chaos character, in the match and the customizer previews, placed by mapping each lens rectangle through the helmet mesh's UVs (the meshes store V below 0; the shader wraps them), the rig's eye markers for helmets without rectangles; `--no-lens-glow`. Tests: `CharacterVisualsTests`. Screenshots in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\screens\visuals\`. Not verified: the sword swing flare and the hit-derived flashes on other players in a real fight; the feel against the original; the colours and sizes are estimates in the refine register.

Weapon effects pass (branch fx/weapon-fx; client only, no protocol change; owner's playtest items 22, 23, 25, 26, 27 of 2026-10-30): the lascannon beam is one straight line, muzzle to end, both points taken when the shot is seen (the earlier muzzle-join-end bend read as a V when the shooter moved); the bullet muzzle leg lingers 0.12 s so tracers start at the barrel (hit origin unchanged); the melta blast is a drawn cone (`NetworkView.WeaponFx.cs`) in place of the data's `meltagun_cylinder_blast`; plasma shots draw a near-opaque roiling ball shader with the data's trail around it; the jump pack thrust fades in 0.08 s at the peak and the looping fall effect is dropped; `CharacterViewer.SetBackpackHidden` hides the armour backpack in `_bp`-named sets too (suspected cause of the Devastator pack flicker, not reproduced in a still frame). Test aids `--shot-test` (fires the weapon in hand like `--laser-test`), `--old-muzzle-leg`, `--old-melta-fx`, `--old-plasma-ball`, `--old-pack-fall`. Checked by eye: the melta cone and a bolter tracer from the muzzle; not checked by eye: the lascannon after moving, the plasma ball close up, the jump pack at the peak, the backpack flicker.
fix/camera-zoom-misc (2026-10-30, owner playtest notes 1, 11, 18, 20; client and content reader only, protocol unchanged at 44): (1) the camera lag is gone completely (`NetworkView.CameraLag.cs`, `SmNet.CameraLag`, its tests, the `--camera-lag` flag, the crosshair offset and the aim-ray and latency-probe hooks): the rig follows the view again exactly as before ui/hud-fidelity. (18) The stalker bolter and the lascannon zoomed only to the aim set's 15 degrees; their wargear carries `zoom_levels` (`aim_use_zoom_levels` true in their sets): stalker 10, lascannon 5.75 for level 1 (spec "Zoom levels of the scoped weapons"); `CameraTuning` reads them (`WeaponCamera.ZoomFovs`), the rig blends to level 1. The level cycle (`zoom_cycle`; lascannon level 2 is 2 degrees) is not implemented. (20) The C key (change loadout) is removed; Esc opens the loadout creator alive or dead as before, and the death screen now says "[ESC] CHANGE LOADOUT". (11) The stalker's reload sound: the data holds one binding per reload tag (`ACTN_SND_SP_Clip_Remove` 0, `Clip_Load` 0.214, `Pull_Bolt` 0.543, `Bolt_Release` 0.614 of the clip) and the client schedules each once; no second post path was found by reading the code, but `play_stalker_load_clip` and `play_stalker_bolt_release` resolve to the same sample (wem 123666085) 0.4 of the reload apart, which sounds like a repeat. New test aid `--log-sound reload` prints every reload-tag post with the event and the voices it resolved to, to count the posts of one reload.
Reload sounds, one sample once (fix/camera-zoom-misc, owner decision 2026-10-30): differently named reload tags whose events resolve to the same sample play it once, at the later tag (`SoundTriggers.OncePerSample`, tested). On the install only the stalker bolter changes (load clip dropped, bolt release kept); `--reload-sounds-all` restores the old posts.

Observer / spectator (feat/spectator, protocol 46, owner's request 2026-10-30; ours: a tool for promotional footage, not an original feature): `client.cmd --connect h:p --observe` (or the Join screen's SPECTATE button, not remembered) joins as a spectator. The Hello's flags byte gets a spectator bit (2); `GameServer.JoinSpectator` gives the client an id and a session but no world player, so it never spawns, has no team, score or hit shape (nothing can target or collide with it), counts toward neither `MaxPlayers` nor the balance, and is not idle-kicked; its input batches only keep it alive (the server ignores any inputs in them). It receives every snapshot (everyone, slim records: the full map, no team visibility; worst case still 1200 bytes) and the Scoreboard lists it in a new trailing spectator list (flag 8, at most `Protocol.MaxSpectators` = 4, which `--max-spectators` caps). The client has a separate frame path (`NetworkView.Observer.cs`, `ObserverFrame`) beside the player's: remote players, projectiles, effects, sound and the match UI as before, without prediction, an own model or the player's HUD; a free-fly camera (WASD along the view, Space/E and Ctrl/Q up and down, Shift fast, Alt slow, wheel speed, [ ] field of view, G smoothing, `--observe-pose`) and an over-the-shoulder follow camera (F cycles living players, mouse turns the view around the player; the sphere-cast pull-in of the other cameras keeps it out of walls), H hides the whole HUD (own overlay and kill feed, scoreboard, name tags and rings: `NoMarkers` follows it). Design notes: the flag is `--observe` (not `--spectate`, which already names the screenshot aids of a playing client); a spectator's batches carry its camera as their one input (MoveX, MoveY, Yaw = x, y, z in game metres; no size change) and the server, clamping it to the map's bounds plus 30 m (a non-number reads as the middle), picks the projectiles and shots of its snapshots by distance from that camera; H also hides the objective and zone markers. Tests: `SpectatorTests` (never spawns, not targetable, not in teams or scores, a full set of snapshots, limits, wire and the Scoreboard's size); headless run with four bots and a windowed capture (`screens\spectator\free-fly.png`, `follow.png`).
HUD pass 3 (branch `ui/hud-3`; client, one reader hook and tests, no protocol change; the owner's playtest of 2026-10-30): (3) the own damage no longer flashes the bar; `Hud.DrawDamageVignette` flashes the screen's edges in the armour bar's cyan or the health bar's colour; (4) the armour bar's starburst medallion (`c540` of `ironhalo_mc`, hidden through `GfxRaster.Hidden`) belongs to the Iron Halo perk (`Frame.IronHalo`); everyone else gets the gold `lightdamagebar_mc` frame under the cyan lines and the movie's orange health, as the owner's reference frame; (5) `PoundMarker`: four yellow double chevrons sliding inward replace the data's land-reticule effect (`--pound-marker-demo`); (6) the reward lines are 0.82 times as large; (7) the score band was 55 px too long and the weapon box 10 units too low against the owner's frame (measured side by side; the rest matched); (9) the melta's weapon-box bar is the progress to its next shot (`Frame.WeaponBarFull`); (14) names only over the aimed player, red for a foe, gold for a friend (`FillDecorators(f, me, centre.Hit)`; `DecoratorRules.PlayerVisible` and its test changed). Screens under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\screens\hud3`. Not checked: the melta bar in play, the real aimed-name path against a live target (demo frames only), a pound marker from a real jump.

Combat pass (branch `sim/combat-pass`; protocol 45; the owner's playtest notes of 2026-10-30, items 8, 10, 12, 19, 21): **8** W + F is purely the charge: a heavy press with W held that cannot charge (the 1 s spacing not over, or in the air) is lost, never a stun strike (`Combat.StepPlayerCore`; F without W is the stun strike as before; the two old tests that expected the strike now expect nothing). **10** reloads continue while the weapon is holstered: `PlayerState.OtherReloadLeft` / `ThirdReloadLeft` (own record, 8 bytes; the snapshot's projectile records 15 to 14, worst case 1200 to 1194 bytes), switching moves the reload with its weapon, a holstered weapon's reload finishes on its own timer (owner's recollection). **12** headshot bonus damage was already implemented from the data (`WeaponSpec.HeadMultiplier`, `ShieldHeadMultiplier`; bolt pistol 2.5, bolters 2.55, sniper 2, lascannon 2.25): the bolt pistol's 40 x 2.5 = 100 kills a full marine with depleted armour in one headshot; recorded in the spec with source, a test added, no code change. **19** directional melee: the stick's way of eight at the attack's start sets the facing relative to the view (`PlayerState.MeleeDirection`, 3 bits in the own record's slot byte; `Rush.DashOffset`), the hit cone follows. **21** the ledge charge's fall pose now starts once the charge has run 1 s (ground and air together; `FallRules.ChargeShowsFall`), before that the frozen charge clip stays (client only; estimate, "about 1 s" is ambiguous). Tests: `CombatPassTests`; older snapshot-size tests updated to 1194. Follow-up (review and owner, same day): a W + F press that cannot charge yet (spacing, air, mid-combo) is buffered for 0.3 s (`InputBuffer.Locked`) and never queues or strikes a stun strike; the melee direction holds through a hit that comes after the move-on time; the ledge charge's fall pose starts 0.3 s after leaving the ground (estimate). No wire change. Not verified: the feel of any of it in a window; the fall pose's look after the delay.

The feel pass is done (branch `anim/feel-pass`; client only, no protocol change; the owner's item 15 of 2026-10-30: "the tactical roll is PERFECT ... make the rest blend and transition
that well"). The roll's pattern (one whole-body clip at the simulation's clock, in from a moving copy of the pose, out at its own branch over the base graph's 10-frame 'Standard Blend',
the camera eased, nothing cut short) is written down in `client/NetworkView.Feel.cs` and applied: every whole-body action (reactions, the knife, jump-pack landings, impacts and get-ups,
the toss) leaves through the navigation conduit's 0.333 s (`SM_Base_MP` `TO Ranged Nav`; was 0.2 s ours or the stance's 0.15 s); the air slash keeps its follow-through on the upper body
when the marine moves on, and its wind-up runs on a smooth time curve (`SlashPose.SmoothDiveTime`); a remote pound no longer flicks back to its dive (a 1.5 m hand pop); a restarted clip
fades in; stance cross-fades fold layers by slerp (one arc per bone); the heavy bolter stays in its ready posture (no relaxed state in the data). Measured on a recorded session with
`--transition-probe` / `--anim-probe` (`--no-feel` for the before): flight to slash jerk median 107 to 82, p90 227 to 125 cm/f2; worst switch 227 to 198; the Devastator's lowerings 7 to 3;
bone turns above 45 degrees a frame 240 to 205. The run's bob is the data's (15 cm in the run, the clip 18; nothing added). Probe additions: bob lines, aim / ready labels; a replay waits
10 minutes for its Welcome. Spec "The feel pass: the roll's blending for every action"; `SlashPoseTests`.

fx/visuals-2 (the owner's round 2 notes of 2026-10-30, items 34, 35, 38, 40, 45, 46, 48; client only, **no protocol change**): (34) the armour recharge glow and the break flash are no longer drawn on the model (the shell outline is gone): one soft camera-facing halo card per character, turning about the vertical only (a card turning with the camera tilted into the floor), centred on the lower spine bone (the viewer's origin is not where the body is; the first try drew it a metre to the side), faded toward the feet; the subtle yellow hit flash is unchanged (it is a rim overlay, not an outline); `--old-flash-outline`. (35) The slash landing adds a cone shell: the simulation's melee test is a true cone (60 degrees of the heading, 4 m), so the shell is that cone, apex at the feet; ground wedge, dust and chunks stay; test aid `--slash-cone-demo`; `--no-slash-cone`. (38) The pistol's tracer is held until the posture blend has run and starts at the raised muzzle (the shot itself keeps its server time); `--old-pistol-tracer`. (40, 46) The melta cone stood up whatever the aim: `Basis.Scaled` scales the world axes; the columns are scaled now; colours back to the data's purple-blue. (45) Bolt tracers thinner and shorter through `FxEffect.TracerWidthScale` / `TracerTrailScale`; `--old-bolt-tracer`. (48) `CharacterViewer.Stim.cs`: the stim aura and a procedural red cross for the data's stim lifetime, for others too (the release seen starts the clock); `--no-stim-glow`, `--stim-glow-demo`. Screenshots in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\screens\fx2\`. ### feat/gamepad: controller support (2026-10-30; client only, protocol unchanged at 46)
The owner's request: the original's controller bindings, autodetected, with the keyboard and mouse back when it leaves. The install holds the original's control-screen labels (locale 110651-110693), the stick
tuning (`camera_input_tuning`: speeds, `input_mapping`, `request_damping`, now read into `InputTuning`) and the option names (gamepad on/off, button and stick layouts, vibration, targeting assistance), but not which button
does what (the `ControlMap` movie's labels are filled by native code); the owner's screenshot of the Xbox 360 screen gives that. New `client/Gamepad/GamepadRules.cs` (binding table with a source per row, stick curves,
trigger hysteresis, D-pad slots, radial selection, `SchemeTracker`: last device used wins), `PadHost` (device node: state from the events, cursor hidden in menus while the pad is in use, first-control focus on a pad press;
Godot's `ui_*` actions then drive the menus: D-pad / left stick move, A accepts, B back), `NetworkView.Gamepad.cs` (move with analog magnitude, look at the data's rates, buttons through the tap latch, D-pad swaps, sprint hold, R3 zoom cycle,
R3 = scope zoom cycle, Start = Esc menu, Back = scoreboard, hints "[START]", "[B]"). The server and the sim are untouched: it is the same `PlayerInput`. Aid: `--pad-test` (synthetic joypad events; `PADTEST` lines), `--log-input`. Verified headless
with synthetic events only (no physical controller): scheme switch both ways, look, move (full and 0.6 stick: 4.97 and 1.84 m in 1 s), aim, fire (clip drops), melee, the charge (stick forward + Y) and no charge without it,
