### sim/combat-2: the owner's playtest round 2, combat items (protocol 47, 2026-10-30)
Items 28, 31, 32, 36, 37, 39, 42, 43 and 50 of `playtest-notes-2026-10-30.md`, round 2 (rules and values: spec "Combat 2"). The jump pack's air control doubled (16 m/s, 30 m/s²);
W no longer ends the bull rush (`stickEnds` in `Combat.StepPlayerCore`); the melee lock's camera assist is gone (client); the light-attack interrupt is a reaction that any
input ends (`Reaction.Holds`: everything else holds; the review first made the stagger light too, the owner took it back); a pistol-slot trigger press ends a swing at once; the melee root motion runs a tick ahead of the clock, so the press tick steps; the
countdown drops the stick and every button; a roll keeps its horizontal travel off a ledge (protocol 30's stop removed); the switch buffer needed no change beyond the light reactions
(a reload never blocks a switch). Tests that pinned the old timings were updated (melee lock windows one tick earlier, the rush ended by D instead of W, the stun used where a
hold was meant). Protocol 47 (no layout change, snapshot worst case 1194). `NavJumps.SimulationVersion` 9.

Map silence and pickup collision (branch fix/map-silence-pickups; owner decisions 56 and 57 of 2026-10-30; no protocol change, stays 47): the map-silence switch already existed since M38 (`--map-sounds`); a headless `--bot --log-sound post` run (new kind in `SoundSystem.Post`) on `mp_tdm_09` showed no map emitter, gate hum (`play_weirdboy_shield_loop_mp`) or bed posting by default and 0 voices after the spawn; with `--map-sounds` the six gate hums and 39 other emitters post. Dropped boxes: the simulation never tests players against pickups and `PickupView` has no physics body, so no code change was needed; a sim test now pins no block, no support and pickup by overlap. Spec "Owner decision 56" and "Dropped boxes have no collision"; `docs/changes-from-original.md`.
Reaction blend (branch `anim/reaction-blend`; client only, no protocol change; the owner's item 49 of 2026-10-30: the getting-shot animation ends too snappily). Cause: a ranged hit is the additive 0.2 s `SM_REC_Flinch_*` layer (not a whole-body reaction), laid at weight 1 and cleared the frame its clip ended, so it never went through the feel pass's exit blend; the melee reactions' 0.2 s exit already blends. Now the flinch weight rises over 0.05 s and, after the clip, its last pose is held while the weight fades over the conduit's 0.333 s (`NetworkView.UpperBody.cs` `FlinchWeight`; `--no-feel` restores the cut). The transition probe labels the flinch layer (`+flinch`): flinch to ready jerk 27.4 to 3.8 cm/f2, turn 15.8 to 8.4 deg/f on one recorded duel. Spec "Getting shot: the flinch blends in and out". Evidence under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\screens
eaction` (a before / after strip of crops; subtle at that size, the probe numbers are the measure).

Map silence, part 2 (same branch; owner's details of 2026-10-30): the held power weapons' idle hums (fx/melee-presentation) are off unless `--weapon-hums`; the on-hit sounds already played once per landed hit for own and others' hits (`--log-sound melee` prints the MELEE TABLE: thunder hammer and daemon maul `play_sm_thunder_hammer_hit`, power axe `play_sm_power_axe_hit`, power sword `play_sm_power_sword_hit`). Glow untouched; the spawn barrier effect has no sound. Corpse ragdolls cannot hit dropped boxes (layers: the map trimesh and their own only). Spec "Owner decision 56b".

Regen sound loop (fix/regen-sound-loop; owner 2026-10-30: a continuous hum in matches, thought to be the shield regeneration). The armour regeneration path was already right (sound/shield-regen: `play_armor_restore` is a one-shot, the warning loop ends at a regeneration, death and spawn; a 5-minute Seize Ground run with 2 sound clients showed the warning's continuations flat after each death). The endless sound found: a tag binding's stop event was never posted; the chainsword swing (`play_sm_chainsword_swing_x1`, stop `stop_sm_chainsword_swing`; Chaos `play_ch_chainsword_swing_x4`) has an endless continuous motor layer, so each swing left a chain running until the player died (774 continuations by 80 s, the 64-voice cap reached). New `TagStopTracker` (content) and `NetworkView.EndTagSounds`: the stop is posted when the swing clip ends, restarts or changes (3 s at most). After: 6 swing continuations in 60 s, `playing` falls back to single digits when the fighting stops. `--log-sound tag` now prints the stop and `TAG STOP` lines. Spec "Tag-started sounds end with their action".

Hit sound by armour (same branch; owner's item 59): a bullet that strikes a player now plays the data's armour case (the hard `ceramite_armour` clangs, armour impact state) while the victim's armour is up and the flesh case once it is down, for every weapon, for the shooter's and for other players' shots (the victim's view). The bit is `ShotView.Armoured` / the own shield / the last hit report; unknown still plays both. The data has no separate armour-crack event (`play_iron_halo` is in no bank). `--log-sound impact` prints `body hit (armour|flesh|both)`; a 90 s headless run: 347 armour, 87 flesh, 119 unknown. `--combined-hit-sounds` restores the old sound. Spec "Hit sound by the victim's armour".

Launcher dark mode (owner's request 2026-10-31): the SM Reimpl Launcher now has a dark look matching the owner's reference colour (#302D2C). The reference image itself is one flat colour with no pattern, so the background is that colour plus a very faint diagonal weave (+-3 per channel) drawn procedurally as an 8x8 GDI+ tile (`SmLauncher/Theme.cs`; nothing from the reference is embedded). Panels, labels, links (amber), flat buttons with hover and focus outline, the text boxes, the Old GPU / safe mode check box (owner-drawn), the progress bar (owner-drawn, continuous and marquee) and every message box (`DarkBox`, a themed replacement with the same arguments) follow it; the title bar goes dark on Windows 10/11 through DwmSetWindowAttribute. No behaviour, layout or logic changed. Screenshots are in the local screens folder (`launcher-dark-*.png`).

Devastator / Havoc hop in eight directions (branch `sim/hop-directions`; owner's report 2026-10-31: "devastator hop goes straight forward still even if im pressed W+D or W+S"; protocol unchanged at 47). Cause: `EvadeTuning` set `EvadeSpec.Diagonals = false` for the `heavy_evade` set (M22 gave diagonals to the roll only), so `Evade.DirectionOf` took the nearest of four axes and an exact W+D went forward; W+S held together cancel to no stick, which is forward, exactly as for the roll. Now `Diagonals = !sideOnly`: the hop uses the roll's rule (8 sectors of 45 degrees, dead zone forward, a diagonal plays the forward or back hop clip turned 45 degrees by `Evade.YawOffset`, same distance, height and branch times; ours). Server, prediction and client animation share the path, so nothing else changed. Other evades: the Assault / Raptor dash already has 8 directions; the Ork's dodge hop is side-only by design (Ork O4). Tests: `EvadeDiagonalTests` (hop in 8 directions and no stick). Spec "Diagonal rolls (M22)".

Sticky launcher grenades (branch `sim/sticky-launcher`; owner's request 2026-10-31: "vengeance launcher grenades should not bounce. they should instantly stick to whatever they strike. they can also stick to players"; protocol 48, shared with the other branches of the release). The data already says `sticky` for `grenade_launcher_grenade_multiplayer` (and attachment to players was in since protocol 7), but also `max_bounce_count` 1, which made `World.Fly` reflect the grenade once off the level before it stuck. A sticky non-rigid projectile now sticks at its first contact with world geometry (floor, wall, ceiling) and the bounce is skipped; rigid thrown grenades are untouched. A grenade attached to a player that dies or leaves now drops (`World.Dropped`: at rest, then full gravity, never striking that host again) instead of hanging in the air. Detonation rules, wire layout (worst case 1194 bytes) and splash on the host are unchanged. Tests: `ProjectileTests` (no bounce, floor and ceiling, follow, drop on death, boomerang rewritten with a non-sticky shot).


### ui/fov-slider: a field-of-view option (2026-10-31; client only, protocol unchanged)
Owner: "add an fov slider to the game. 120 being the maximum, the default the minimum." A slider (`UiKit.FovRow`) in the Join screen and in the customizer, which is also the in-match Esc menu. It shows HORIZONTAL degrees at the window's aspect (tooltip says so), from the data's look (exploration sets' `field_of_view` 40, read as vertical: 65.5 horizontal at 16:9) to 120, and is saved as `fovDegrees` in `frontend.json` (0 = the data's look). `NetworkView.RigCamera` multiplies tan(fov / 2) of the exploration, aim and evade sets by `FovMath.Scale`; scope `zoom_levels` stay as the data says; mouse sensitivity unchanged. The slider takes focus, so a controller's left / right moves it. Ours (an added option), spec row "Field-of-view option", changes-from-original. Tests: `FovMathTests`.
Switch cancel (branch `sim/switch-cancel`; protocol 48, a rule change with no wire change; the owner's request of 2026-10-31): a weapon switch request (keys 1/2/3, cycle, wheel, D-pad) during a switch under way now cancels it and starts the requested weapon's switch (`Combat.StepPlayerCore` no longer waits for `switchLeft`; `InputBuffer.Locked` no longer holds a Switch press for a switch, so it acts at once instead of being buffered). The switch time restarts in full each time, so fire and reload still wait for the last switch (no instant fire through a cancel loop); ammunition, heat and a reload in progress follow their weapon through the three stores, holstered reloads keep running. Client: the same simulation predicts it; a restarted switch clip fades in from the weight the cancelled one had reached (`NetworkView.UpperBody.SwitchWeight`) instead of from zero. Three old tests that expected a press during a switch to be lost now expect the cancel. Spec "Switch cancel". Tests: `CombatPassTests`, `FivePerksTests`.

Melee interaction pass (branch `anim/melee-interaction`; protocol 48, no wire change, snapshots unchanged; the owner's request of 2026-10-31: the charge connect "very floaty and disconnected", "charges don't consistently lock the target and charge deliverer together", weightier impact, more interaction between melee participants). **Cause of the inconsistent connect** (measured in `ChargeLockTests` with the lock off): the contact tested only the charger's rewound picture of the others while its move was blocked by the newer body picture (sim/player-collision), so a player running at the charger was pressed against and never met; a met victim stood 1.1 to 1.2 m away at up to 49 degrees off the charger's heading; and the own client never predicted the contact (0 of 20 contact ticks), so the own charger ran on in the rush clip for a round trip and jumped into the collision stop part-way. **Simulation** (`SmSim.ChargeLock`, hooked in `World.ResolveRush` / `StopRushes`): the contact counts the blocking body too; the charger stops in the data's collision stop (`SM_NAV_Bullrush2Idle_F_Collision_01`, the wall-hit recoil: the graph's `Knocked Back` state) facing the point met; a stunned victim is moved to 0.9 m in front along that line (swept, at most 2.5 m). **Prediction** (`GameClient.ChargeLock.cs`): the own contact, stop and turn on the contact tick with the server's view and bodies (20 of 20 under 150 ms RTT). **Client** (`NetworkView.MeleeInteraction.cs`, rules `SmNet.MeleeInteraction`): the own charge's victim drawn at the lock spot until its reaction arrives; a 0.1 s hit-stop on both clips; camera kicks (charger 2.2, victim 3.5 degrees) with shakes, a faint shake for observers (replaces the 0.5 degree charge shake); the bull rush's `body_smash` container effects and `body_smash_directional` at the contact; the body smash sound layered with the weapon's hit sound; reacting bodies turned so their clip's side faces the attacker; the own predicted melee hit starts the victim's flinch on the hit frame. Bot runs on flat ground: every own and observed connect 0.90 m apart, 0.0 degrees off (before: 1.1 to 2.8 m). Aids: `--no-charge-lock` (server and clients, config hash), `--no-charge-impact`, `--no-reaction-facing`, `--no-hit-flinch`, `--no-lock-draw`, `--log-charge-impact`, `--charge-shots <dir>`. Strips under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\screens\melee\`. Spec "Melee interaction pass"; `ChargeLockTests`, `MeleeInteractionTests`. Not changed: the stun's knockback (none in the data; its clips' 2 m of extracted motion is still not applied), strikes' hit-stop (owner's 2026-10-29 removal).
Melee lunge is done (branch `sim/melee-lunge`; the owner, 2026-10-31: a longer step forward for all melee, longer the further a locked target is; no protocol bump, 48 is the shared unreleased version). `SimConfig.MeleeLungeScale` 1.3 to 1.625 (`GameplayTuning.OwnerLungeScale`, +25%, an estimate); `MeleeLock.LungeStep` closes a locked target's gap with a front-loaded burst (`MeleeLockSpec.BurstSpeed` 28 m/s, `BurstFraction` 0.6, ours; the lock range is the data's `max_melee_target_distance` 7 m), always through `Movement.Glide` (walls, ledges) and never nearer than the 1 m separation. The distance clips already lengthen the step with the target's distance. Spec "Melee lunge scale". Tests: `MeleeLockTests`.
fx/melta-fuzzy (the owner's note of 2026-10-31: "melta gun cone needs to be blurred and stretched out a lot more ... no hard outlines ... fuzzy"; client only, **no protocol change**): the melta's drawn blast cone keeps its form (from the barrel along the shot) and its purple-blue, but is the data's full 20 m long whatever the aim point (the depth test hides what lies behind a wall) and soft everywhere: `BuildMeltaMesh` makes nine nested open cone shells, the shader fades each by the wall's facing against the view (normalised by the view's angle to the axis, so a silhouette never shows as a line), weights the inner shells brighter (soft radial falloff, head-on too), fades in at the muzzle and out at the tip, breaks the edges up with two octaves of scrolling 3D noise in metres, fades within 0.9 m of geometry through the depth texture (no intersection line with walls or floor) and within 5 m of the camera (a cone passing the camera does not veil the screen). Values are ours (spec "Melta blast cone", refine register). `--old-melta-fx` restores the data's blast; new test aid `--shot-test-turn <degrees>` turns a `--shot-test` shot about the vertical (90 sideways, 160 toward the camera). Screenshots, before and after, in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\screens\melta\`. Not verified: the look in a live fight against moving targets, on the Compatibility renderer (old GPUs), the depth fade over Godot's other renderers.
Armour regeneration sound level (branch `fix/regen-sound-range`; owner 2026-10-31: "the armor regen sound should falloff past a certain distance. call it 20 feet roughly. also make it about 50% of the current volume"): a headless `--log-sound armour,post` run with six bots posts armour sounds for the local player only (`SoundOwnShield`; the data's `apply_only_if_on_player`), none for other players, so the regen the owner hears is their own (`play_armor_restore`, one voice; `set_state_impact_armor` for the restored case has no voice). The regen start and restored posts now carry -6 dB (`RegenSoundLevel`); the same function holds the smooth 20 ft (6.096 m) falloff for another player's regen, should one ever be posted. `--regen-sound-old` restores the old level. No protocol change. Spec "Shield sounds".

No guns, no aim in any charge (branch `sim/no-fire-charging-all`; owner's report 2026-10-31: "spamming zoom while charging ... stutters the camera hard and allows you to shoot mid charge sideways the storm bolter and bolter. ensure no guns can be shot while a charge animation is playing, ever"; protocol 48, also claimed by `sim/switch-cancel` for the same release). Causes: `Combat` passed Fire (all but Tacticals, BR-02) and Aim to `Rush.Begin` as "other input", which ends the charge from its `MoveAt`; so an Aim press cut the charge short and the tick then acted normally (aim state on, so the aim camera blended in; the next press, off again), and a Fire press ended it and fired the same tick (or an A / D press did, with a gun). Now the charge is ended only by the stick (not W), a Grenade press, Jump, melee or its clip's end; Fire and Aim are ignored for every class (`Rush.NoFire` removed; `noFire` is every charge tick, plus the tick an input ends a charge before its clip's end, `fireDropped`), a fire press is never buffered (the held flag follows the real button), and no aim state changes so the camera is not touched. No wire change (worst case 1194). Tests: `NoFireInChargeTests` (every weapon, both roles, aim spam, an early stick end with Fire). Spec "No fire, no aim in anyone's charge".

Sound hunt (branch `fix/sound-hunt`; owner 2026-10-31: "an annoying sound heard over and over"; client only, protocol unchanged at 48): the new `--log-sound census` (every 30 s, per event: posts, voices, 2D, looping voices, mean dB, continuations) over headless Annihilation and Seize Ground runs found no ambient source in a match (no map emitter, bed, music, weather, announcer loop or HUD tick) and one defect: `play_mp_countdown` is an endless container that was never stopped after the countdown, so a 2D swell replayed every ~10 s all match, and each round added a chain (62 continuations in 630 s Annihilation, 185 in 1200 s Seize). Now posted once. Seize Ground's capture click (25 a minute) and score tick (21 a minute) are off behind `--sound-seize-ticks` (owner's call). Spec "Sound hunt"; `docs/changes-from-original.md`.

fx/barrel-origin (the owner's note of 2026-10-31: "for all guns the projectiles and weapon effects need to emit from the barrel of the weapon"; client only, **no protocol change**; the server's shot origin, rays and projectile paths unchanged): audit of every gun (bolter, bolt pistol, stalker, storm bolter, heavy bolter, plasma gun, plasma pistol, plasma cannon, melta, lascannon, Vengeance launcher, the Chaos versions, the Ork shoota and slugga): all 25 ranged weapon models in the install carry a muzzle locator; the flash, smoke, shells, bullet tracers (M25, PR #25 muzzle leg, #30 pistol raise), the lascannon beam and the melta cone (#38) already started at it, own and others', in hip fire, aim, scope and braced (`FxPlace`, `MuzzleWorld`). What did not: the visible body of a projectile (the plasma ball, the plasma cannon's, the Vengeance grenades, the charged plasma pistol shot) was drawn from the server's launch point (the camera ray's nearest point to the eye, 1.06 m from the muzzle) and first shown 3 to 9 m out; now `NetworkView.Barrel.cs` notes each shot's origin and muzzle, draws a matched projectile displaced by origin-to-muzzle (own: the sent input's origin; others': rebuilt from the shooter's camera), fading the displacement over 3 m, with a tinted pooled streak from the muzzle to where it first shows. Found on the way and fixed: other players' projectile shots (plasma cannon, launcher, charged plasma) had no muzzle flash at all (the server sends shot records for rays only; they now play when the projectile first shows next to the shooter, the attribution reach 8 to 12 m); an own charged shot released from the pending state changes no clip, heat or cooldown that frame and drew no effects (now the prediction's fired event draws them), and a charged shot costing 15 rounds drew three flashes and impacts (now one). Aids `--spectate barrel`, `--barrel-test`, `--barrel-probe`, `--old-barrel` (spec "Weapon effects start at the barrel"). Screenshots, own and remote, in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\screens\muzzle\`. The Ork shoota and slugga have no effect data in the catalogue (no flash, tracer or smoke is drawn for them at all; nothing to move to the barrel; a stand-in set would be a new feature: owner's call). Not verified: the look against moving shooters at a distance, the Compatibility renderer, braced heavy weapons by eye, the Chaos launcher and plasma cannon remote by eye.
Air slash landing (branch `fx/air-slash-landing`; owner 2026-10-31: the power sword's and chainsword's air slash landing "should appear and feel exactly like" reference r5; client only, protocol 48 unchanged): the reference shows a huge blue-white burst at the landing (white peak, then the marine washed cyan, gone by 0.65 s). The data binds no effect to the MP slash; the matching one is the jump pack's perk landing `jumppack_land_extreme_mp` (`add_point_cool` flash bloom, streaks, spikes, light), which now plays at the data's 1.4 on the slash landing, tinted blue-white and without decals, with a blue-white light and an own-view screen flash (ours); the same for every melee weapon (the slash is the jump pack's). The dust cone of #30 is off by default (`--slash-cone` restores it); `--no-slash-flash` restores the earlier look; capture aid `--slash-shots <dir>`. Frames beside the reference under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\screens\slashfx`. Spec "Air slash landing".
Launcher layout pass (branch `ui/launcher-layout`; owner 2026-10-31: "launcher UI is overwritten and garbled"; launcher only, protocol unchanged): causes found were transparent labels, links, check boxes and panels over the tiled background (a changed status line or a shrinking AutoSize label left old glyphs, nested transparency repainted unreliably), sizes in pixels with no DPI scaling (`AutoScaleMode.Font` without reference dimensions scaled nothing, so fonts grew and boxes did not at 125 to 200 %), fixed wrap widths (560, 700, 680 px) and a fixed-height header with absolute label positions, the safe-mode box sharing the button row, a 600 px client height too short for the set-up screen, the update line drawn in the button's dark amber, and the install-folder line growing past the window. Now every control paints an opaque backdrop (`DarkLabel`, `TilePanel`/`TileTable`/`TileFlow`, tile or the header's solid colour) and invalidates on text and bounds changes, the form scales per monitor (Dpi mode at 96), labels wrap to their cell, the header is a table, the install-folder line ellipsizes, the window is 780 x 680. New `--layout-check <folder>` (and `--ui-state`, `--ui-scale`, `--ui-check`) draws six states at four scales and checks overlaps and containment (24 states pass). See docs/releasing.md "Layout".

Stomp in place (branch `sim/stomp-in-place`; owner 2026-10-31; protocol 49 shared with the charge rule): the Devastator's and the Havoc's stomp keeps the body exactly in place (`MeleeStep.InPlace`, no reach data, position and velocity held until its run branch; the chaining tick carries no motion of the kick). The F + click slide was the kick's lunge chaining into a second lunge from the stomp. The hit time was checked against the clip: tag 0.767 s (tick 23), measured foot contact 0.735 s (the same tick), so unchanged. `StompInPlaceTests`.
Score box centred (branch `ui/score-box-center`; client only, no protocol change; owner's screenshot of 2026-10-31: the timer and the limit hugged the box's right edge and the scores its left): `Hud/Hud.ScoreBox.cs` measures the block (the scores right-aligned in their fields, the two bars' drawn part read from their pictures' alpha at full fill, and the right column where the timer sits over the limit, both centred on one line) and sizes the opaque box for it with even padding (20 x 10 movie pixels, ours; the left edge keeps its 12 px slant), then moves the block so it is centred in the box (the layout is kept while the scores, limit, clock and viewport height stay the same; in Seize Ground the points' markers are lifted 19 movie pixels, ours, so they stand above the box's top edge instead of crossing it). The box is sized for two-digit scores, a timer like 8:16 and a two-digit limit; longer strings are centred just the same and use up some padding. The armour bar (Iron Halo or plain) is a different panel and is untouched. Aids: `--hud-score-demo own,enemy,limit,clock[,file.png]` (shows those values, logs `score box gaps:`, saves the picture and quits) and `--old-score-box` (before). `--ui-selftest` now also checks six cases (to 250/249 of 999 at 59:59): every gap at least 4 movie pixels and the block centred within 1 px (`UiSelfTest.ScoreBox.cs`). Screens: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\screens\scorebox\`.
Charge needs the sprint (branch `sim/charge-needs-sprint`; owner 2026-10-31: "adjust the latest change to charging with W+F. you also need to be holding shift ... if you are holding W, A, S, D, or a combination of them, then press f, you should do a stun strike in that direction"; protocol 49, no wire change, not in the config hash): the charge request is now `Rush.ChargeHeld` = Sprint held AND W held at the F press (`Rush.CanStart`, the heavy-press fall-through in `Combat.StepPlayerCore`, the melee lock's phase); any other F press is the stun strike in the held keys' direction (the directional melee rule already latched the direction at each attack's start: W or none forward, A, D, S, the diagonals), so W + F without Shift is a forward stun strike, and a heavy press in the charge's spacing strikes at once. The 0.3 s input buffer records "Shift and W held" in `BufferedCharge` at the press; a charge request replays as the charge while W is still held (the replay supplies Sprint) and is dropped if W was let go. Controller: Y with the sprint (L3 hold) and the stick forward charges (`GamepadRules.ChargeRequest`); Y otherwise strikes in the stick's direction. The bots' charge inputs already held Sprint. Text updated: the in-game help line, the tester README, the release notes, `CONTROLS.md`, `WHAT-TO-TEST.md`, `release/NEXT.md`. Tests: `ChargeNeedsSprintTests` (new), `RushTests`, `OwnerRulesTests`, `HipFireTests`, `CombatPassTests`, `ChargeDirectionsTests`, `GamepadTests`; existing charge tests now hold Shift. Spec "The charge needs the sprint"; `docs/changes-from-original.md`.

Instant fire (branch `sim/instant-fire`; owner 2026-10-31: "slight delay after letting go of left mouse button ... shoot immediately after releasing ... the same is true for lascannon ... fire the instant the left mouse button is pressed"; protocol 49 kept, no wire change, not in the config hash): delays found: (1) the charged shots' `fire_sim` `delayed_action` 0.1 s (plasma gun, plasma pistol, plasma cannon; `ChargeShot.FireDelay` -> `PendingShot`, 3 ticks after the release), now not applied (the shot leaves on the release tick; the data stays read); (2) the lascannon's tap-versus-hold: its basic shot left on the release, its charged 200 ray after a 1.5 s hold: `ChargeSpec.FiresOnPress` (a `max_charge_time` above 0, the lascannon only) now makes the press fire the basic shot at once and drops its hold-charge. No tap window, input buffer, tick alignment or client animation wait was found: the client plays the shot from the server's `ShotEvent`/own prediction in the tick it is simulated (the raise rule is unchanged). Tests: `OwnerRulesTests` (lascannon press tick, plasma release tick with a data delay), `ChargeTests`.
Stomp effects on the drawn foot (same branch; client only): the stomp's rings, cracks, light, camera shake and the inferred hit sound fire when the time of the clip actually drawn (own: `OwnClipClock`, others: `ClipClock`) reaches the foot's landing (measured 0.735 s of the clip, `FootContactFraction`; the sim hit stays at the data tag 0.767 s), not when the state's attack time does. In the own view the old gate already met the drawn landing (the drawn pose trails the prediction by a tick, the tag trails the landing by a tick): windowed bot run, 7 of 7 stomps with effects on the frame of the drawn contact, before and after. The other players' views (the clip clock runs ahead of the snapshot value) were not measured. Aids: `--stomp-sim-gate` (old gate), `--log-melee-fx` prints the frames. Logs: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\screens\stomp\`.
Key and controller rebinding (branch `ui/keybinds`; owner 2026-10-31: "add an interface in the menu for players to customize their keybinds. allow them to do it for controller as well."; client only, protocol unchanged at 48): a CONTROLS screen (`client/Controls/ControlsView.cs`) from the Join screen's footer (next to the FOV slider) and from the customizer / Esc menu's header, with a Keyboard and Mouse tab (primary and secondary per action) and a Controller tab (one). Every gameplay action is listed: the four move actions, sprint, evade / jump pack, fire, aim, melee, stun strike, grenade, reload / vent, use / pick up, weapons 1 to 3, next weapon, the scope zoom level (controller), the scoreboard and the extended content's shout (only in a build with it). Click an entry (A on the pad), press the new key, mouse button, wheel notch or pad button or trigger; Esc cancels (Start on the controller tab); Delete or a right click (X on the pad) clears; an input another action holds asks Swap, Replace or Cancel; RESET TO DEFAULTS per tab asks first; LB / RB switch tabs and the menu focus drives everything. Not rebindable (shown as fixed): the look, the move stick, Esc / Start, F1, the arrow-key turn. The store is pure (`client/Controls/ControlBindings.cs`: defaults = today's bindings, conflicts, JSON in `controls.json` beside `frontend.json`, a set equal to the defaults leaves no file; `ControlBindingsTests`), `ControlsInput` registers the keyboard and mouse table as `sm_*` actions in Godot's InputMap (applied live, also in a running match) and indexes the controller table for `PadHost`'s events. `NetworkView.cs` samples through `BindingSet.Sample` and the tap latch (`NetworkView.Controls.cs`), the pickup key, the scoreboard (both sites), the loyalist shout and the pad layer (`NetworkView.Gamepad.cs`) read the bound actions instead of fixed keys; the simulation was not touched: the charge (sprint + forward + stun strike) and the directional strikes read the same input bits, so they follow the bound actions. The pickup prompt shows the bound input. Not verified: a real controller by hand, trigger capture on hardware. `--ui-selftest` now drives the screen with synthetic key, mouse and pad events (rebind, conflicts, reset, tabs, back, the in-match overlay, layout at every window size). Spec: none (no gameplay parameter); changes-from-original row "Key and controller rebinding".
Small jump hang (branch `sim/jump-hang`; owner 2026-10-31: "you drop out of the air too fast once you hit the peak height ... hold vertical height for a bit longer before you start to drop"; protocol 49 kept, no new wire field): the data has one hang for every jump (`jump_hang_gravity` 12 m/s², `jump_hang_time` 0.5 s) and no separate hover, so the medium-hold (small) jump now hangs `SmallHangTime` 0.35 s longer (ours) with its hang gravity easing from 5 % of 12 up to 12 along a smoothstep (`JumpPack.HangGravityAt`): the same apex, about 0.25 m of drop in the first third of a second instead of 0.7 m, no snap. The jump is flagged at the apex (`PlayerState.JumpSmall`: a cut in the ascent or a hold let go below the full one's), carried by the jump byte's bit 6 in the hang (the validity check now allows it there), predicted by the client with the same code, covered by the config hash. The tap (dash) and the full jump are tick-for-tick unchanged; air control, ground pound and the air slash work in the hang. Client: the flight pose follows the vertical speed (level at the hover), the thrust still fades at the peak (#25); no clip or FX change. Tests: `JumpHangTests`. Tune: `JumpPackTuning.SmallJumpHangTime` / `SmallJumpHangFloor`.
Air slash character animation (branch `anim/air-slash-character`; client only, protocol 49, no wire change; owner 2026-10-31: "focus on the character in the reference video and the way the animation plays and looks"). The original footage (`r5-air-slash-frames-30fps`) read frame by frame: the dive hunched over the target with the blade low and the jets firing, the landing flash (not imitated), the blade sweeping up from low to overhead after the landing at about the clip's own rate, upright with the arms out, then walking on with the blade low. The data plays `SM_MEL_CS_XATK_Hv1_LS_2_7m` at speed 1 in both sequencers (wind-up 0 to 0.4667 s in the flight, the strike from 0.4667 s on the landing, entered from the jump over 'Fast Blend' 0.167 s, flight to impact 'Blend Slo-mo' 0.033 s); our 40 m/s dive (0.13 to 0.3 s, ours) is shorter than the wind-up, and the feel pass fitted the whole wind-up into it (middle rate up to about 3 to 4: the raise a flick, the sword overhead before touching down). Now one curve runs the clip from the dive's start to the strike's sync point (clip 0.6 s, the hand halfway down) at the simulation's unchanged hit (`SlashPose.StrikeDiveTime` / `StrikeImpactTime`; ours): the wind-up spreads over the dive and the first 0.133 s of the landing (rate about 1.4 to 2.3), the sword still rising as he lands, the chop on the hit; a long enough dive plays the data's way. `--old-slash-windup` restores the feel pass's curve. Capture aids for `--slash-test`: `--slash-view-pitch <rad>` (the human follow camera, this pitch after the press) and `--slash-move-on <s>` (strafes from that long after the landing). Not changed: the clip and its crops, the entry and landing blends, the hit and recovery times, the jets, the effects (fx/air-slash-landing owns the landing flash and burst). No cyan wash on the character itself is visible in the reference (the cyan is the full-screen flash's tint), so none was added. Sheet (original | before | after, frame-matched from the landing): `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\screens\slashanim\air-slash-side-by-side.jpg`. Spec "Air slash: the strike curve"; `SlashPoseTests`.
Air slash move-on and the dome (same branch; lead's review of the first sheet): the data has no separate slash landing or finisher clip (the slash states play only `SM_MEL_CS_XATK_Hv1_LS_2_7m`; the rising blade in the reference is that clip's wind-up), so the clip is unchanged; moving on after the landing now fades the strike off the upper body over the jump-pack graph's pound impact-to-run blend, 'Fast Blend BranchIn' 0.167 s (was the 0.333 s conduit; interpretation), so the marine is upright in the run about 0.17 s after the simulation frees him. `--slash-move-on` now aims beside the target and walks forward (it had strafed into the target and stood). The beige dome over the landing in the first sheet was fx/visuals-2's cone shell (`NetworkView.SlashCone.cs`, dust colours), which fx/air-slash-landing already turned off by default on main (`--slash-cone` restores it); after the merge of main the landing shows only the small blue-white burst (`jumppack_land_extreme_mp` at 0.6), no dome. Sheet: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\screens\slashanim\air-slash-side-by-side-2.jpg`.

Launcher hand-over (branch `fix/launcher-handoff`; owner 2026-10-31: "the launcher isn't properly updating itself"; launcher only, no protocol change): an old launcher copy outside the install folder (an unpacked zip's `0 - SM Reimpl Launcher.exe`) installed a newer build and replaced the install folder's launcher, but kept running itself, because only the launcher whose path equals the install folder's launcher went through the restart helper. Now `LauncherHandoff` makes any outside copy start the newer installed (or verified bundled) launcher with the same arguments plus `--handed-off` and exit, at start and right after an update; test and helper runs (`--selftest` and the rest) never hand over. Tests in `LauncherHandoffTests`. Details: docs/releasing.md.
Bolt tracer and armour-hit pass (branch `fx/bolt-tracer-impact`; owner 2026-10-31: tracers "still wrong ... less blocky", look at the armour-hit effect; client only, protocol 49 unchanged): the blockiness was the pooled streaks (muzzle leg, fallback bullet), flat hard-edged ribbons; they are now a soft glow ribbon with a thin hot core (`SoftStreak`). The data's textured tracer beam was already soft and keeps the #30 sizes. A hit on raised armour already played the weapon's data effect (`bolter_dmg_armor_heavy` and kin) and the victim's armour-hit glows (#30 halo, unchanged); it showed short orange dots where the reference shows long thin streaks, so the data's `hit_ranged_armour_generic` (metal spark fan, flash, light) is played on top, twice (its fan is a flat card). `--old-bolt-fx` restores both; aid `--bolt-fx-demo [wargear] [--bolt-fx-armour 0]` (observer: a synthetic shot at the first living player). Sheet `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\screens\boltfx\sheet-armour-hit.jpg`. Not verified: the tracer in flight (too brief for the captures), flesh-hit look, the Compatibility renderer.
