## Musou: Ork crowds at the spawn points (2026-11-01; branch `musou/ork-crowds`)

Owner's item 32 and his answers. The three positions of the battle (Manufactorum's A, B and C, the places whose full capture already stops a point's spawning) are the three spawn points; the HQ source holds a fourth crowd from the commander's coming and in the final assault. Pools replace the tide: a held point adds one leashed Ork to its crowd every second (`CrowdFillSeconds`), at 50 (`CrowdSize`) `TfwBattle.Swarm` frees the whole group (`MusouSim.ReleaseGroup`) and the point starts again from none; each point swarms on its own, no stagger. The alive cap is the owner's 150 for the crowds and the swarms (80 more a further human); the garrisons stand beside it. Each position keeps a garrison of 12 leashed Orks from the landing that never respawns (the rebuilding is gone). A target within 12 m of a crowd, or a hurt Ork, wakes the whole crowd as a swarm of what it has; the garrison wakes at 30 m as before. A crowd waits at its size while the cap is full of free Orks and is never let go below 50 for the cap's sake (a first version had a valve that swarmed the largest early after 10 s; it let crowds of 16 to 47 go in a live run, so it was taken out). Left as they were because they are scripted: the Waaagh!s' Boyz, the commander and his escorts, the Warboss, and the stranded-Ork failsafe. Capture rules unchanged: an Imperial on a point pauses its filling, a full capture stops it. The capture bug: a point is taken with no live Ork inside its volume (the map's 13.5 to 15 m radius and 10 m up and down); on main the tide kept sending Orks (about one a second from each point still held, 3 a second at the start, and a garrison rebuilt every 4 s) to the player standing on the point, so a player who kills slowly never saw it empty; shown on a real server with the new scripted capture player (`--tfw-test-capture`, `--tfw-capture-weak` for a poor aimer) on main and on this branch. Positions now have names on the HUD (A, B DEPOT, C, the next one marked) and in the world (a letter and state over each ring). `TfwRules.Version` 17. Review fix: the stranded failsafe is off with a human on the point, so an Ork stuck in the volume (a ledge it cannot leave, a shooter dithering at the ring's edge) could block a capture for good; while a point reads Clearing an Ork in its volume that stays within 2.5 m of one spot seeking for 6 s is now removed (`TfwBattle.RemoveStuck`, ours, in the spec). `CrowdAggro` 12 to 30 m (the ring plus the disc). New test aids: `TFWSWARM`, `TFWARRIVE`, `TFWQUIET`, `TFWPOINT` lines and the Orks on each point under `SM_TFW_FIGHT_LOG`, `--tfw-fight-hold`, `--tfw-test-capture`. Tests `TfwOrkTests`, `TfwHudTests`.
**Spawn-room light flicker (2026-11-01; branch `fix/spawn-room-light`; client only, protocol unchanged).** The owner's report: the light flickers madly in Manufactorum's spawn room in Musou Mode (stills: dark room, single frames of white or red in the doorway, cream-yellow washes with dark streaks that decay in 0.3 s). Measured with `godot.cmd --windowed` bots in Musou Mode, a fixed `--spectate cam:` view and the mean brightness of a frame every 0.1 s: the environment, sun (energy 2.15), sky, fog, glow, camera and ambient never change in a fight (logged per frame; forcing each of them off left the bumps), no light of the install reaches more than a few metres in a classic bot match, and hiding only the damage-flash canvas layer removed every bump (flat 83 to 86 against bumps from 82 to 113). The flash is `DamageFlash` (M38): every damage tick restarted its envelope at the peak, so a crowd of Orks hitting every few ticks strobed the near-whole screen between 1.0 and 0.45. Now a hit while a flash runs lifts it back only to the plateau (`FlashRestartAge`; a fresh hit still peaks; `--old-damage-flash` restores the old rule). Second, separate cause found in the logs: the Musou vista's far explosions (`oob_explosions_artillery_less` at scale 2.2 and the flak) played their data lights scaled to a range of 268 to 297 m at energy about 15.5 and colour (1, 0.89, 0.64), a cream wash over the whole arena (10 of 32 logged strong lights); `FxEffect.NoLights` switches those lights off (they are scenery). Not proved: that the doorway's single white frames come from either cause; not reproduced in the real spawn room with a human player. Tfw hub: the logged `aboard` flips were steady (no per-frame flip of the hub's sky or the sun).

**Musou hotfix: boss, trickle, cards (2026-11-01; branch `hotfix/boss-trickle`; `TfwRules.Version` 20).** The owner: the final boss in the courtyard just outside his room and always a large Ork; the trickling Orks back for about twice the Orks on the map; the reward cards off for now. The Warboss is placed by `TfwSites.Courtyard` (the nearest open ground on foot outside the HQ, a walk check from the HQ), his body is `MusouRules.BossScale` 1.6 and the client never draws the Boy in his place while the Nob look builds (`MusouLooks.For`), with a big Boy as the last fallback. `TfwBattle.StepTrickle` lets each sending source (Held, not being captured, not secured) send one unleashed Ork every 1.5 s up to the crowds' cap again, 470 in all. `TfwRewardRules.Enabled = false` (instance switch `TfwRewards.Offering`) stops the offers; the code and the score panel stay. Tests: TfwOrkTests (trickle, courtyard, switches); the existing crowd tests turn the trickle off per battle.

**Right shoulder, FOV shift (2026-11-02; branch `camera/right-shoulder-fov`; client only, protocol unchanged).** The owner: remove the left-shoulder fallback entirely, and at higher FOV shift the camera right by a modest amount with the aim adjusted to match, because the character covers the point of aim. `CameraSide` and its use in `RigCamera` are gone; a blocked right side only pulls the camera in, as the other legs do. `FovMath.CameraShift` moves the camera and pivot right by 0.2 m x (FOV scale - 1), 0.34 m at 120 degrees at 16:9, at most 0.35 m and nothing at the default (an estimate, refine register). The review's check of the real rig found the ray could pass the server's 1.5 m shot origin limit in a near-square window (1.65 m at 120), so `FovMath.LimitShift` cuts the shift there. The view stays parallel, so the crosshair's ray moves with the camera and the converged shot follows it with no new aim code; `FovMathTests` pins the offset per step and guards the limit and the wire: the server fires a ray built this way unchanged at every step. Scoped zoom fades the shift out with the aim blend.

## A dead player's melee direction cost every snapshot (fix/dead-melee-direction, 2026-11-02)
Playtest report: "Disconnected (no snapshot from the server)" on a local server. Logs: frames normal, players dropped one at a time, the client gave up 5 s before the server's "timed out" (so inputs kept
arriving), and 10 of 10 dropped bots had just died. Cause: `Combat.Killed` zeroed `MeleeStep` but kept `MeleeDirection` (protocol 45), and `Protocol.ReadSnapshot` refuses an own record with a direction and no
attack, so a player killed in a directional attack silently refused every snapshot through the respawn timer. A reaction or a charge (they take the melee byte) showed the same record. Fixed in the state (`Killed`,
`Respawned`, `Reaction` start clear it) and on the wire (`Protocol.WireMeleeDirection`: a direction only with an attack; no format change, the fix is on the server's side, so a server needs the new build). Diagnostic: `GameClient.RefusedSnapshots` /
`RefusedSinceSnapshot` count snapshots that arrived and were refused, and `ConnectionLost` names them first instead of "the server or the network went silent". `DeadSnapshotTests`. Live: 12 headless bots, 7 min, 190 kills, no drop
(before: 7 of 15 bots gone in 6 min).

**Musou HUD panels on the M map (ui/musou-hud-to-map, 2026-11-02).** The owner: "move the information panels in the top left of the screen to the musou battle map interface". `TfwHud` keeps only the middle prompts. The first panel's fronts, HQ, reserves and clock were already `WarMapPanel`'s rows, so that panel went without a copy; the map shows the front of this battle in gold. The second panel is the new `TfwBattlePanel`, a child of the M overlay in the DEPLOY column, fed from `TfwHud.Frame` while M is held. `--tfw-test` holds M in a battle (steps "M in a battle ..."; PNG `war-map-battle`). Client only; classic PvP untouched. M is held, not toggled, and has no controller binding, so a pad player cannot see these figures yet. In the same change (the owner, 2026-11-02): the world markers are only the small A, B and C (`TfwMarkers`: the state text under the letter and the COMMANDER or WARBOSS label went, the commander's ring stays; the boss bar's name at the top is not a marker and stays), and the bars over the elites are no longer drawn (`TfwBarsView` removed; tag 13 and `TfwBars` stay on the wire, `_tfwState.Bars` is what `--tfw-test-class` still reads). Classic PvP's Tactical Readout bar is untouched.

**Musou enemy sounds (sound/musou-ork-sounds, 2026-11-02).** The owner: "currently orks make no noise in musou mode. add their sound effects for guns, melee attacks, footsteps, shouts and grunts and other sounds from the original game." Client only, no protocol change, original events through `SoundSystem`, no gain. `MusouSoundSet` (`SmContent/Extras/Musou/MusouEnemySounds.cs`) reads each type's cues from its blueprint and wargear, keeping what the banks hold and listing the rest; `NetworkView.MusouSounds.cs` binds 16 emitters to the nearest enemies and posts from their state changes, the ground they cover and the crowd's events, through `MusouSoundBudget` (range, rate, a soft 14 voices and 6 lines). The old six-emitter `MusouVoice` is gone. `SoundEmitter.Group` keeps a crowd voice from stealing a player's. `smtool musou-sounds`, `--log-sound musou`, `--no-musou-ork-sounds`, `--musou-ork-gain`. Proven on a real server with logs: every group posts with 300 enemies, and a whole run with the scripted player passes. Not seen live: the Warboss's slam, charge hit and death, the celebration. **Nobody has listened to it**: the owner judges it in a playtest. Findings in docs/discovery.md, "Musou enemy sounds".
**Melee reliability, the sooner step, smaller clouds, the stalker crater (feel/melee-reliability, 2026-11-02).** Four owner items. The step: `MeleeLock.MotionTime` plays a swing's root motion 1.5 times faster up to the hit and stretches the rest (`MeleeLockSpec.StepEarly`, set from the install; the spec's default 1 keeps older tests on the clip's timing). The hammer and maul: `MeleeStep.TrackToHit` carries the alignment to the hit and lets `ResolveMelee` strike the lock 1.5 m farther and within 90 degrees, as primary target; the cause was that the data's window closes 0.1 to 0.2 s before a hit at 0.43 to 0.7 s, so a moving target left the cone. In Musou Mode the lock does not exist (`others` holds players only): the cleave gets 1 m more, a real enemy lock is a larger piece of work. The clouds: `CloudBoost` halved. The stalker: its container has no effect on stone, so a world hit plays the bolter's crater at 1.6 (`StalkerCrater`). No wire change, so protocol 52 stays; the config hash separates old and new builds.

**The commander's status text (2026-11-02).** The owner: "make this text much smaller and only allow it to appear when aiming close to it". `TfwMarkers` shows COMMANDER and the state at font size 14 (the letters 40), within 6 degrees of the crosshair (ours); the other positions keep their letters alone.

**No Gretchin, no lights through walls (fix/orks-and-spawn-lights, 2026-11-02; `TfwRules.Version` 21).** The owner: shots passed through the tiny Orks' upper bodies, remove them and keep the head count; and the spawn area's light flashing. The Gretchin's collision height is 1.2 m while it is drawn as a Boy at 0.7, about 1.5 m, which is the likely reason. Their shares went to the Boyz (war 0.70 / 0.30; the waves likewise), the totals unchanged; the type stays in the code. The flashing: the effect lights cast no shadows, so blasts outside reached through the walls; `MusouLightSeen` drops a flash the camera has no clear line to (Musou Mode only, `FxPlayer.LightFilter`, `TfwBlastCloud.LightSeen`). A reading of the code, not proved in the spawn room: to check in a playtest.

**Orks' hit shapes (2026-11-02).** The owner: almost all Orks have broken hitboxes; shots pass through the upper body. Three causes in `MusouSim.Raycast`: the shape used the walking height (Boy 1.9 m drawn 2.15 m, Nob 2.3 m drawn 3.0 m); the body was tested only where a ray entered its side, so a shot from above through the top missed; and shots met the enemy where it is now, not where the shooter saw it, about 0.1 s and more behind, at over 5 m/s against a 0.4 m radius. Now `ShotBody` is the drawn height at 1.5 times the radius, the body is a closed cylinder, and each shot is also tried on the last 0.2 s of the enemy's path. Melee and blasts are unchanged.

**Pad strike, menu select and ADS sensitivity (2026-11-02).** Musou Mode: left on the D-pad calls the orbital strike (the keyboard B); the scope zoom stays on the right stick. The HUD line reads R3 on the pad. Menus: the standard buttons already pressed on A (Godot's accept action); what failed was a menu opened with no focus (the first press only found a control), so `PadHost.AutoFocus` now focuses the first control of the top layer as soon as the pad is the scheme and nothing has focus. Options: "Gamepad aim sensitivity" (`padAimSensitivity`, default 1.00x) scales the right stick while aiming. Not tried on a real pad.

**One flash, no flame (fx/jump-flash-no-trail, 2026-11-02).** The owner: the jump pack's flash also on a charge started mid hop, the flash at the start only, the red flame trail removed, classic PvP and Musou Mode. The thrust effects no longer loop: `PackFlash` plays only the data's `quick flash` of `jumppack_thrust` (`FxEffect.FlashOnly`) for 0.35 s at a jump, hop, dive, dash or air charge. The ground bursts stay. Not looked at in a running game.

**Debris look (2026-11-02).** The owner: the ground chunks should have the look of Manufactorum's floor (reference screenshot). `GroundShards` uses one generated texture, fractal noise through a colour ramp (ours, no original bytes), triplanar, on every surface. Not looked at in a running game.
**Zoom in flight (2026-11-02).** The owner: zoom while flying as an Assault Marine or Raptor as on the ground. `Combat` no longer drops aim mode in the jump pack's phases; the ground pound still does.
**Melee cooldown, Musou melee spam, charges ignore the stick, designator beam (feel/melee-cooldown-charge, 2026-11-02; protocol 53).** The owner's four items. (1) Classic PvP: firing ended an attack from `RangedAt` and a press then started step 1 at once, so melee, hit, shoot, melee chained attacks; now `PlayerState.MeleeLock` (seconds, set to the started step's `ComboOpen`, counted down every tick, kept through any cancel) blocks a new attack, and a normal combo is unchanged. It is on the wire (a float in the own record after the flinch byte: record 171 bytes, worst snapshot 1199 of 1200), so the protocol is 53. (2) Musou Mode: a light press once the swing's hit has landed restarts the swing at once (the client poses from the state's step and time, and its clip clocks restart when the time goes back); before the hit it queues. (3) All modes: no stick direction ends the bull rush any more (`stickEnds` is false in the rush phase; the recoil, the dash attack's hit and run-out keep their stick branches). (4) Musou: B draws a thin short red beam from the muzzle to the aimed point with the lascannon beam's drawing. The classic replay goldens moved (the lock and the charge). Not tested in play: the beam's look and the feel of the lock.
## Musou: flung corpses (2026-11-02)

Owner's words: Ork corpses ragdolling from the artillery strike, the frag grenade and plasma cannon explosions. Found: such deaths (kinds Blast and Barrage) either gibbed with no corpse (gore on) or played their death clip in place. Now `NetworkView.Musou.cs` asks `MusouCrowd.CanFling`: within 40 m of the camera and under a cap of 16 flung bodies, the body is thrown along the death's push and falls (`CrowdView.StepFlung`: ballistic arc, one bounce, slide, then the usual sink), gibbed or not; beyond that or over the cap nothing changes. Real bone ragdolls (`Ragdoll`, the players') need a `MarineAssets` rig and joint bodies per corpse and were not tried on the crowd's skinned and vertex-animated rigs: this is a flung arc and fall, said plainly. Shot and melee deaths are unchanged. The 10 s log line gains the flung count. Spec "Flung corpses". Not played by a human; frame cost not measured with a real crowd (the per-body step is a few float operations, 16 bodies at most).

## Musou: the Firing Range (2026-11-02)

Owner's item: the first blank map concept, 100 m x 100 m, reached by a button on the Thunderhawk's wall, 200 Orks spawned continuously, a test ground for the artillery strike. `TfwRange` (in `TfwMap.cs`) is a flat walled square generated in the same world, east of the level's extent (`TfwMap.WithHub` adds its solids; `TfwMap.Version` 6; its centre seeds the enemies' graph, which now has a second, separate part that `TfwSites` ignores because it takes the largest part only). The hub gains a button (`TfwHub.RangeStation`, a lit plate on the left tech panel); E at its pad opens a confirm (`TfwRangeConfirm`), TELEPORT sends the new commands `RangeGo` and `RangeBack` (12, 13). `TfwRun.Range.cs` moves the player, `World.TfwRangeTopUp` keeps 200 enemies alive with the war's own spawn mix, a fallen player stands up after 3 s, the last to leave (or a Deploy, or a disconnect) clears the field; a war in the hub phase is otherwise untouched, so a second player in the Stormbird is not disturbed and a Deploy still takes everyone. The fire support follows a token instead of a battle (`TfwFire.Follow(object)`), `TfwOrbital` accepts a player at the range, and its shells are kept on the range's floor (the first run showed them clamped to Manufactorum's edge). Test aid `--tfw-test-range [dir]` (docs/commands.md) on a real local server: 9 of 9 passed (prompt, confirm, teleport, 200 Orks alive, they close from 27 m to 1.3 m, an orbital strike killed 121 in 14 s, the pad brings the player back, the field is empty once the last player has left); server tick mean about 1.4 ms with 200 Orks, 10 to 37 KB/s to the client. Not played by a human; the button is a placeholder plate, the range a grey checker; no dedicated map, so a second player at the range gets the same field.

**fx/hit-sound-bass-timing (2026-11-02):** owner's words: the power weapons' hit sounds were "too scratchy/fuzzy", late and a little loud. `MeleeHitSynth` is now a falling sine, a low rumble and a short low-passed click, peak at once. `OwnStrikeHitSound` plays the own swing's sound at the strike (hit time passed, enemy in reach) and the server's report then stays silent for 0.6 s. Also: A was never bound to `ui_accept` (Godot 4's built-in holds only keys), so `PadHost` adds it. Stalker checked against `wargear.oppc` at the owner's request: 50 damage, head x2, body x1, shield head x2.5, shield body x0.8, all applied, nothing changed.

**Charge reaction and Musou shout (2026-11-02):** a charge connect no longer holds the victim's reaction clip (`ReactionHold`; it held it up to about 0.1 s). `ContentExtras.ActionKeyUsers` gains Musou, so T shouts there; the automatic barks stay off in Musou.

**Armour break ring (2026-11-02):** the first break flash is red in the recharge glow's ring (`BreakRing`, `SetArmourFlash(ring:)`); later hits on bare armour keep the engulfing glow. An own hit report with the victim's shield at 0 flashes it at once (`ArmourFlashTracker.Broke`); a third party's view still waits for the next hit that shows the armour down, because no other player's shield is on the wire.

**Stalker armour headshot (2026-11-02):** owner's choice after seeing the numbers: armour head x10 (`OwnerBalance.WithStalkerHeadshot`), so a headshot leaves 50 health through Impenetrable and 20 without.

**Musou weapon drops off (2026-11-02):** owner: temporary. `MusouDropRules.WeaponDrops` = false stops KO drops and the map's crates; the core's boxes stay (`TfwDropBox`). All code kept; tests turn it on with `World.MusouWeaponDrops`.

**Melee cancels (feel/melee-cancels, protocol 54, 2026-11-02):** owner's request. A melee press now ends the Assault / Raptor hop (the jump-pack dash) at any moment and the bull rush of the Assault, Raptor and both Tactical classes (rush phase, on the ground or held in the air), and the swing starts in that tick; no animation-cancel timing. The next swing cannot start before the cancelled clip's end (`MeleeCancel`; the lock rides on `PlayerState.MeleeLock`, now kept in Musou Mode as well), so hop and charge cancelling cannot be spammed. Kept: the Tactical roll, the Devastator / Havoc hop and charge, the Ork Boy, the charge's collision stop and the dash attack. Assault / Raptor: Space ends their own bull rush at once, and Space held while falling (the long press) lifts the pack in the air, with the pack's fuel and the dash's spacing as before (`JumpPack.Begin`: `airLong`). Four older tests changed for the superseded rules (early melee in a hop, the hold that waited for the landing). Not played with a human yet; the swing from the air shows through the client's existing attack branch.
**Stim and knife visuals (2026-11-02):** `fix/stim-knife-visuals`, client only. Stim: the "Equip - StimPack" upper-body clip leaves the hands away from the weapon mounts, so the gun floated; `WeaponRig.StimStowed` puts every weapon on its stow marker (or hides it) while a stim is used. Knife: a swing handed over to the legs fades its upper-body weight to 0 over the graph exit while the simulation step goes on, so the knife stayed in a rifle-posed hand; the melee weapon now shows only while that weight is above 0.25 (`LocoTrack.MeleeWeight`, `MeleeVisibleWeight`, ours). Not seen in the engine.
**App icon (feat/app-icon, 2026-11-02):** owner's request: the owner's helmet image is the icon of the game exe and the launcher from this build on. `client/icon.ico` (256 to 16 px, area outside the ring transparent) and `client/icon.png` (512 px) are made from it. The Godot export writes it into `sm-reimpl.exe` (`application/modify_resources`, Godot's own PE editing, no rcedit); `config/windows_native_icon` sets the window and taskbar icon at runtime (the `*.ico` include filter puts the file in the pack); `SmLauncher.csproj` takes the same file as `ApplicationIcon`, and the launcher's window and shortcuts follow from its exe.

**Musou swings, thrown bodies, thinner clouds (musou/melee-ragdoll-clouds, 2026-11-02; Musou Mode only, no protocol change, `TfwRules.Version` 23):** the owner's three changes. **Swings:** the melee-spam restart replayed swing 1 for ever; every light attack in Musou now draws from the weapon's light chain (`MeleeChain.MusouSwing`: never the same twice running, never an in-place stomp, from tick and player so prediction and server agree); a bot's spam on a real server ran 2, 1, 3, 1, 3 with the knife. **Thrown bodies:** a blast or artillery death was gibbed and thrown only within 40 m under a cap of 16 that also counted bodies lying, so most of a big blast's dead vanished. Now every such death leaves a body: `MusouRagdolls`, a pool of 20 real ragdolls of the boy rig (made one a frame, woken and thrown, parts colliding with the map only), and past the pool or beyond 45 m the crowd's tumbling body (`CrowdView.StepFlung`, now stopping at walls and sinking only after it rests; Warboss and Chaos Marine always tumble); `MusouGoreRules.BlastThrow` picks up, sideways or both. The gore's burst is untouched. A round that bursts on an Ork now kills as a blast; a lascannon shot still leaves no corpse. `--no-musou-ragdolls`; the 10 s log gains the ragdoll counts and the highest rise. **Clouds:** 0.72 to 0.58 at their thickest in Musou only (`GoreView.CloudAlpha`); classic PvP's Extended gore is unchanged. Seen: `--musou-gore-demo` captures in Manufactorum (Orks limp in the air up to 10.6 m, burst intact); 20 busy ragdolls 53 against 54 fps, p99 33 against 32 ms. Spec "Musou Mode: random swings, thrown bodies, thinner clouds". Not done: real ragdolls for the Warboss and Chaos Marine; no human has played it; the cloud change and the swings' on-screen clips were not compared side by side.

**Repaint check flake (fix/repaint-check-flake, 2026-11-02):** `RowCheck` failed in the full `dotnet test` run on a busy PC, in different places each run, which blocked a ship. A frame that differs from the full repaint now gets up to 5 more looks, 200 ms apart, with no invalidation: a region nothing invalidates stays different and still fails. A stale region that a later timer repaints within about 1 s now passes.

**Musou batch and the hammer's pound (musou/batch-2026-11-02, 2026-11-02; protocol 55, no wire change; `TfwRules.Version` 24, `TfwMap.Version` 7):** the owner's ten changes. **Heal:** a melee attack that strikes anybody gives 5 % of the health back (`World.MusouMeleeHeal`). **Twice the Orks:** garrisons 24, crowds 100 at 2 a second, cap 300 (the pool's 512 slots hold the map to about 470). **Every crowd swarms:** the cap counts swarms still fighting, so a far crowd stalled under its size for good; now it goes after 60 s with what it has (`TfwSwarmWhy.Waited`), which supersedes the rule of 2026-11-01 that took the earlier valve out, at the owner's word. **Elites:** in squads of 20 (`TfwBattle.NextType`). **Boss:** `BossScale` 3, read as 3 x the model, not 3 x the old 1.6. **Bass:** `MeleeHitSynth.CutBass`, Musou only; classic keeps it, asked of the owner. **Firing Range:** the "cylinders" and "ramp" are Manufactorum's backdrop (`factory_tanks_lodh`, `factory_geo_lodh`) standing in the range, which is placed from the level's collision and they have none; `TfwRange.Collision` adds two tanks and three slopes measured from the render meshes, invisible over the level's own drawing. No Ork damage there (`World.MusouHit`). **Flinch:** `MusouCrowd.Flinch`, drawn only. **Shouts:** `MusouSoundRules` about twice to three times as often. **Hammer:** nothing in a jump pack's rules looks at the weapon, so the one delay found is the 2 s of Air-Cooled Thrusters; a hammer or maul now ignores it (`Loadouts.WieldsHammer`), both classic and Musou, hence protocol 55: if the owner's delay had another cause this does not cure it. Live: `--tfw-test-range` 9 of 9, health 100 with Orks at 1.5 m; a held fight on a real server reached 451 Orks with every crowd swarming at about 55 fps, frame p99 30 ms. Spec "Musou Mode batch of 2026-11-02 and the hammer's pound". Not seen: the 3x boss, the flinch and the walls by eye; no human has heard the bass-less sounds or played any of it.

**War ambience removed (2026-11-02; branch `musou/remove-war-ambience`; client only, no protocol change).** The owner asked for the decorative effects round the Musou map to go (they made the world look like a larger war but showed bright flash bursts with no cause). That was `TfwVistaFrame`: once per run, 7 places 240 m round the points, the install effects `oob_explosions_artillery_less` (x2.2) and `amb_anti_aircraft_fire_valkyries` (x1.5) on repeat. Deleted with its constants and fields, and the two effects (plus the unused `oob_explosions_artillery`) left the view's effect list. Kept: real barrages (`TfwBlastCloud`, `artillery_explosion`, `oob_explosion_huge` on every third shell), the muffled far war as sound only (`TfwWarSoundFrame`, not visual), the map data's own ambient effects (shared with Annihilation, unchanged) and the paused Thunderhawk code. Spec row "Far fires" removed. Built and tested; not seen in a running game.

**Ground lines over clouds (fix/ground-lines-over-smoke, 2026-11-02):** owner's report: Manufactorum's floor strips stayed sharp on top of artillery, grenade and blood clouds. They are a flat alpha-to-coverage overlay (`r300_tarmac_white`, with the ground planes' cut-out surfaces). Probed on the real map: those surfaces draw among the transparent effects with no fixed order. Every alpha-to-coverage cut-out now has `RenderQuality.CutOutPriority` (-100, first in that pass) and writes depth, so all effects draw after them and stay hidden behind fences. Before and after renders of real blast clouds on that floor confirm it. Ours; no change with MSAA off, where cut-outs stay in the opaque pass.

**Ground blood under clouds (fix/gore-under-smoke, 2026-11-03):** owner: blood splatters on the ground drew on top of the artillery's smoke and explosions in the air. The ground gore layers had priorities 1 to 3 against the clouds' 0; they are now -10 to -8, before every effect and after the map's cut-outs (-100). Airborne ink and mist stay at 0. Ours.

Ground pound, armour first (branch `sim/pound-armour-first`; tests and docs only, no protocol change, stays 49; the owner's report of 2026-10-31: a ground pound lowered the victim's health and left the armour alone). Read the install's `actn_gp_hit` again: no ignore-shield flag (`armourshield_breaker` False, `damage_armourshield` 50, shield multipliers 1; the Death From Above entry 75 + 50), so the data does not bypass armour. The simulation (`World.ApplyHit`) takes the armour part first, then the rest through the shield, then health; a probe on the real data (assault and raptor against both tactical classes, 0.5 to 6.5 m) lowered the armour every time (100 armour at 2 m: 25 left, health untouched). The report could not be reproduced, so no rule was changed; new tests `GroundPoundDataTests` pin full armour first (also ten ticks after, with the stun) and no armour taking all as health. If it still shows in a playtest, note the distance, the victim's armour before the pound and whether the pound or the air slash hit. Spec "Ground pound damage check (M37)".

Follow-up (2026-10-31): the owner saw it as the victim, on their own HUD (armour bar unmoved, health bar down). Traced the own display end to end: the snapshot's own record (Health, Shield as f32) becomes `GameClient.Predicted` (the server state plus a replay of unacknowledged inputs; only the spread bloom and stims are carried from the prediction), `NetworkView.UpdateHud` reads `Predicted.Shield` / `Health`, and the HUD bars are plain functions of them (`VitalsRules`); no smoothing, no hold, no other message. New test `GroundPoundDataTests.The_pounded_clients_own_state_shows_the_armour_drop_and_not_a_health_drop` (GameServer, two GameClients, a stun on the pound): server and the victim's predicted state both go 100/100 to 25/100 within a tick of the snapshot. No divergence found, so nothing changed; the Godot render of the bars was not checked.
**tools/ship-linux-server (2026-11-02):** `ship.cmd` builds the linux-x64 server and attaches it to every release, guarded and hash-checked like the playtest zip, so the Vultr VM downloads it from GitHub instead of an upload from the owner's PC (docs/releasing.md).  
Bots on the Linux demo server (branch `tools/linux-bots`; owner 2026-10-31: "a script to push to the vultr server that will enable me to via ssh add bots"; tooling only, protocol 49 unchanged): the Godot preset "Linux/X11" (`client/export_presets.cfg`), `release.cmd -LinuxBots` (builds the private `sm-reimpl-bots-linux-x64-<ver>.tar.gz` = the headless client export plus the `smbots` script; an older commit gets the preset added to its clean copy; the Linux export templates are fetched with the others) and the guard learned the `.x86_64` client (embedded pack verified like `sm-reimpl.exe`; test `TheLinuxBotExportIsCheckedLikeTheWindowsClient`). `smbots add|list|remove|stop|status` (bash, `tools/release/package/smbots`): bots as transient systemd units run as `smserver`, niced, memory-capped, with a free-memory guard; the owner's private `setup-smserver.sh` gained `--honor-side-requests` on the service and `--bots <pkg>`. Details and the VM test result: docs/dedicated-server.md "Bots on a Linux server".
**Twice the Orks again (musou/double-orks, 2026-11-03; no protocol change, `MusouSim.Version` 7):** the owner: "double the amount of orks on the map in the musou node battle maps on manufactorum". The 512-slot pool held the battle at about 470 with the bosses' reserve, so the pool is now 1024 (`MusouSim.Capacity`; the wire's id check reads it, hence the version) and every count of the battle doubles: garrisons 48, crowds 200 at one every 8 ticks, cap 600 (840 at most), trickle 800. The client draws the nearest 900, 500 of a look by vertex animation, since the old 200 left about 410 of 896 undrawn in the first run. Measured on a real local server with a held player: 896 alive, server tick p99 3.5 ms (max 6) of 33, 63 KB/s, client 108 to 121 fps with 859 drawn, frame p99 11 to 14 ms; on this PC only, one client. Classic PvP is untouched (Musou files only). Spec "Musou Mode: twice the Orks again".

**Reloads keep going (sim/reload-keeps, 2026-11-03; protocol 56, no wire change):** the owner: "reloads should not be cancelled by anything other than switching weapons". A melee attack, a throw, a ground pound's dive, a hit reaction, the bull rush and the dash attack no longer zero the in-hand `ReloadLeft`; it runs down through them (`Combat.StepPlayerCore`'s busy branch now calls `ProgressReload`, as the evade already did) and loads its rounds when done; nothing new starts while they last. A switch still stores the reload with its weapon (combat-pass item 10), death clears it. Other players' inferred reloads follow the same rule (`ReloadInference`: only a switch or death cancels); the own reload clip is hidden under the action clips and shows again at its point. The Musou isolation replay is unchanged (its script never reloads into an action). Spec "Reloads continue while the weapon is not equipped"; changes-from-original row "Only a weapon switch takes a reload out of hand".

**Manufactorum wall stations removed (fix/manufactorum-fluorescent, 2026-11-04; client drawing only, no protocol or config-hash change):** the owner asked for the flat olive boards with salmon glowing shapes on the classic PvP Manufactorum to go. In-engine captures traced them: the boards are `backpanel_a/b/c` (the `backPanel` material, emissive map tinted olive), the shapes are the `tech_stations` surfaces of `tech_panel_*`, `tech_panel_pipe_a/b/c`, `handle_bar_a`, `tech_panel_pipe_g` and `tech_panel_tank_a` (emissive tinted salmon), the tall keypads are `accessories_doorbutton`, and the cabinets (`tech_interface_b`) carry two more olive plates. Six wall stations at the two bases and the cabinets beside them, 146 placements in all. `MapDecor` lists them by definition and material name (the shared pipe, dome, seal and scroll definitions only within 6 m of a board or cabinet, so the monitor consoles keep their cabling) and `MapView` skips them; Musou Mode draws the same map and gets the same result. `--old-armoury-racks` restores the old drawing. Spec "Manufactorum wall stations not drawn"; changes-from-original row "Manufactorum's wall stations".

**Original hit sounds (sound/original-hits, 2026-11-04; client presentation only, no protocol or config-hash change):** the owner: every weapon on-hit sound is the original's, chosen as the original chooses and at its timing; our extra layers go; Musou Mode too. `SoundTriggers.MeleeAbilityContainers` / `MeleeHitEvents(wargear, ability, secondary)` read, per wargear and ability, the default `trigger_material_effect` container events and `post_sound_event` commands under `primary_target_actions` (first target) and `secondary_target_actions` (further targets), `hit_fx` and `hit_sim`, every ability (the combat knife's `ability_melee_ck*`, which the old light-only `ability_melee_x*` filter missed), skipping the Orks' same-named container files (`play_or_*`); `MeleeTuning.WeaponMap.AbilityOf(heavy, step)` maps the sim's strike to its ability. Client: the own strike posts at its hit time for every weapon (the report of the same victim stays silent, a further victim sounds as secondary), the others' inferred hits post the ability recorded when the gate passed, a charge plays the body smash only, the hammer and maul post no displace blast, Musou's cleave uses the same events (first hit primary, the rest secondary). The shooter's hit confirm defaults to `--hit-confirm data`. Switches: `--generated-melee-hit-sound` (the synth, Musou no-bass), `--charge-hit-layer`, `--hammer-displace-layer`, `--old-melee-hit-sound` (the last two), `--hit-confirm soft`. Finding in the data: the combat knife's light strikes carry a `hit_sim` body smash (`play_sm_bull_rush_smash`) next to the `hit_audio` `play_sm_fist_hit`; played as the data says, to confirm by ear. Tests: `OriginalMeleeHitSoundsTests`.

Review fixes for sound/original-hits (2026-11-04): the Ork Boy's choppa (no combo map in `MpClasses`) maps through `MeleeTuning.OrkChoppa` (`SoundTriggers.MeleeHitAbility`; data: `ability_melee_light` `play_or_choppa_hit`, `ability_melee_heavy` `play_ork_huge_mace_hit`); the own reports are matched to their swing by `OwnSwingLedger` (no wall-time windows); the knife's Y4 takes `ability_melee_y4`; names compare without case; `--hit-confirm` reads through `ImpactSounds.ModeFromArgs`. A Musou swing produces no hit report (its hit event has shooter 0 and `CountHits` skips it), so no double play, and the core no longer names Musou. Owner addition: in Musou Mode a hit on an unarmoured Ork (Boy, Shoota Boy, Gretchin; `MusouFleshRule`) always sounds as the flesh case, melee (own strike through the `ExtrasMeleeTarget` hook, cleave events) and the own hit-scan hits, killing blow included. Follow-up (sound/musou-armoured-both, owner "Armour and flesh"): armoured Orks ('Ard Boy, Nob, Warboss) and the Chaos Marine play armour and flesh together in every view; `MusouFleshRule.Material` decides all views, and the new client hook `ExtrasShotMaterial` (in `SoundShot`) lets observers' sounds for other players' ranged hits follow it (the server's shot record stays unarmoured for every Musou enemy; no server, wire or sim change).


### fix/aerial-tackle-pad: the aerial tackle on Y (2026-11-06; client only, protocol unchanged)
Owner playtest: on the gamepad the Assault and Raptor aerial tackle (the dash attack) was on X; it belongs on Y, the sprint charge button. The simulation starts the dash attack on a melee press in the dash window (`Rush.CanDashAttack`), and the pad sends Strike (X) as Melee. `GamepadRules.AerialTackleOnY` (called from `SamplePad`) now turns the pad's Y (stun / charge, `MeleeHeavy`) into that melee press while the window is open and drops X's melee press in it; outside the window X and Y act as before. Keyboard and mouse, the binding table, the simulation and the protocol are unchanged. Test: `GamepadTests`. Owner to check in a playtest.
**Plasma vent while aiming and sprinting (fix/plasma-vent-ads, 2026-11-06; simulation rule, no protocol change; config hash unchanged):** the owner: the plasma gun could not vent while aiming down sights, and holding R while sprinting and aiming should work. Cause: `Combat.StepPlayer` counted aim mode as busy and `Vent.Free` refused a forward sprint, so neither started a vent, and an overheated gun that aimed or sprinted waited for the passive cooling. Both gates are gone (`Vent.Free(busy)`); Fire, evade, melee, throw, switch, jump-pack and reactions still stop a vent, and the rate (45 heat/s on top of the cooling) is unchanged. Client prediction and the gamepad (RB is the same Reload bit) share the simulation. Spec "Brace and vent" rows updated (owner recollection, medium); `BraceVentTests.Venting_works_while_aiming_while_sprinting_and_both_at_the_vent_rate`.
**Melta recharge and the original melta blast (fix/melta-cooldown-vfx, 2026-11-06; client only, no protocol change).** The owner's playtest: the melta's recharge "gets reset back to 0%" by starting a charge, throwing a grenade, a Devastator kick, a Tactical charge or stomp and grenade damage. Cause: up to protocol 55 (every tester build before 4125973f) `Rush.Begin`, `Reaction.Start`, a throw's start, a melee attack from rest and a ground pound zeroed `ReloadLeft`, and the melta's recharge is a reload of one round; sim/reload-keeps (protocol 56, first shipped in 4125973f) already removed all of them. Checked on the install's data (sim, and server plus predicting client through the test harness): through the charge, a throw, light and heavy melee, a roll, a sprint, staggers and stuns the round arrives on the same tick as with no interruption. `MeltaRechargeKeepsTests` pins it for every interruption (charge, throw, light and heavy melee, roll, sprint, interrupt, stun and stagger reactions, damage, the ground pound, a switch with the melta holstered; death clears it). Every other weapon's reload shares that path; heat and the plasma charge are separate (a charge is still cancelled by design). Visuals (the owner: "change the visual effects of the melta shots to match the original game"): the data's `meltagun_cylinder_blast_*` plays again by default, once at the muzzle aimed at the end point (never split at the join point); fx/melta-fuzzy's drawn cone only with `--melta-cone`. Original asset loaded; our effect player still draws no distortion sprites (the blast's heat bubble and haze), no soft-particle fade and no beam noise (spec "Melta blast: the data's again").
**Solid bodies (fix/charge-player-collision, 2026-11-06; protocol 57, no wire change):** the owner's playtest: "Sometimes you can charge through an enemy instead of impacting on them ... ensure that players never pass directly through other players ... Ensure the charge clash and stun and recoil animations play more reliably." Cause (`SolidBodiesTests`): every move collided only with the others as its own client last saw them (sim/player-collision), so a target that stepped into the line within a round trip was run through (24 of 48 step-in runs; an eight-player crowd at 150 ms reached -0.88 m, axes all but together); the charge's 45 degree cone was measured from wherever the tick's move began, so a body 0.85 to 1.2 m off the line was met or missed by the tick's phase (20 of 189 standing-target runs at 35 m/s passed it); a charger that met a body kept its whole tick's move (up to 1.14 m past the point met). Now (`SmSim.SolidBodies`): the charge is met at the first touch of its swept reach anywhere in front, and the charger stops at that point of its move (both predicted exactly: the exact-prediction tests pass with the guard off); the server sweeps each pair of opponents' real moves after every player moved and cuts any that would bring the axes within 0.45 m (0.75 m with a charger), and a charge also meets the bodies as they really moved (not predicted: a client whose picture was wrong is corrected; in an eight-player scrum at 150 ms about 5 % of ticks, p99 3.5 to 8.9 cm). Allies keep protocol 56's rules (Musou Mode's co-op unchanged). Every connect ends its tick with the charger in the collision stop and the victim stunned, and the charger's own client, the victim's and each one's view of the other showed both for every connect at 150 ms with 5 % loss (17 of 17). Switches: `--old-body-contact` (server and clients, config hash), `ServerOptions.BodyGuard` (tests). Spec "Solid bodies"; `SolidBodiesTests`; the crowd, charge-lock, dash-attack wall and isolation tests updated (the replay golden moved with the charges; the wall's same-tick precedence is pinned with the old contact); the exact-prediction harness tests (charge, melee lock, melee 2, weapons C, evades, spawn blockers) run with `BodyGuard = false` so they keep measuring what a client predicts. Not played by a human; the Musou-side and Ashfall code untouched.
**Classic PvP: Deploy, respawn choice, heavy bolter count (fix/pvp-deploy-spawn-hb, protocol 58, 2026-11-06; the branch took 57, which fix/charge-player-collision also took; the combined playtest integration made it 58).** The owner's three classic PvP fixes (Annihilation and Seize Ground; Musou Mode unchanged, `World.ClassicPvp` = a team match without `ContentExtras.Musou`). (1) DEPLOY in the in-match customizer, pressed while alive, now sends the Setup with a DEPLOY flag (protocol 58: one flags byte at the Setup's end); the server queues `World.RequestDeploy`, the next tick kills the player (a suicide: a death, a kill-feed line with no killer, the other side's Annihilation point as for any death; no Final Vengeance blast, no drop) with no respawn delay, and the tick after it the player respawns in its spawn room with the new loadout. SET ACTIVE, closing the menu, a dead player's DEPLOY and Musou Mode keep the old rule. (2) Allies spawned on top of each other because the protocol 44 Teleport Homer spawn was automatic and the Tactical classes carry the perk by default. In classic PvP a death respawn now goes where the player chose (`src/SmSim/SpawnChoice.cs`): the spawn room (default), a control point its side holds (Seize Ground; a free spot on the point, facing the map's middle) or a living ally carrying Teleport Homer (Teleport Homer's ring spot); the choice is checked again at the respawn (point lost, carrier dead, perkless, enemy or itself: the spawn room). The automatic carrier spawn is Musou Mode's only. Every chosen spot is clear of living players by two capsule radii plus 0.1 m, and the spawn room, when no spot is 2 m clear, now takes the first spot that clear before the least crowded one. Wire: a new client message `SpawnRequest` (19) and a flags byte per scoreboard row (bit 0: alive Teleport Homer carrier; fullest scoreboard 1161 bytes). The death screen shows "SPAWN AT: ..." under the loadout hint; Next weapon (X, the wheel) or the D-pad cycles the choices (`client/NetworkView.SpawnChoice.cs`, `SmNet.SpawnChoiceRules`), resent twice a second while dead. (3) The heavy bolter was never infinite in the simulation (the install's 400 rounds, no reserve: 400 shots in about 140 s of held fire, then nothing; install pin) but the HUD's weapon box showed the movie's endless sign and no count; it now shows the rounds left in the bolter's count field (`WeaponBoxRules`). Ammo boxes refill up to 400 (unchanged). Spec "Classic PvP: Deploy, respawn choice, heavy bolter count"; tests `PvpDeploySpawnTests` (deploy in the world and over the wire, refusals, no drop, the room by default, chosen carrier, dead / perkless / enemy carrier, held and unheld points, crowded rooms, Musou's automatic rule kept, the wire, the client rules, 400 shots synthetic and on the install, the pickup cap, the HUD rule); `FivePerksTests` Homer test now sets the choice. Not verified: the death-screen line and keys in a window, a human's deploy on a live server.
Plasma visuals pass (branch `fix/plasma-visuals`, 2026-11-06; client and readers only, no simulation, wire or protocol change; the owner's request: the plasma gun's, cannon's and pistol's crosshair heat tracker, crosshair, weapon box and shot effects as in the original). **Crosshair**: besides the family's reticle (unchanged: `plasmaidle_mc` / `plasmapistol_mc` / `plasma_cannon_mc` with the charge rotation) the HUD now draws the reticle container's two plasma gauges from `Hud.gfx` (`SmContent.PlasmaGaugeRules`, `client/Hud/Hud.Plasma.cs`): the heat arc `heat_mc` under the reticle (label `normal`, the cannon's larger `plasmacannon`; `meter_mc`'s 60 frames by the heat, its `vent_txt` on the last; `overheat_mc`'s `danger` flash looped at 30 fps while overheated) and the charge arc over it (`PlasmaCharge_mc`, the cannon's `PlasmaCannonCharge_mc`, by the charge toward the last firing stage: `Hud.Frame.ChargeToFull`). **Weapon box**: unchanged (already the movie's `ammo_plasmagun_mc` / `ammo_plasmapistol_mc` heat bar and count, checked in the screenshots). **Effects** (`client/NetworkView.PlasmaFx.cs`): the shots already played the data's muzzle, tracer, charged trail and impacts; now the wargear's other bindings play too, attached at their markers: each charge state's `charging_action` (the gun's `plasma_charging_medium`, the pistol's `plasma_charging`, the ready glows and arcs), the fire-mode chamber glows (`plasma_gun_innate`, `plasma_cannon_innate`; primary in hand, secondary while charging: interpretation), and for the own player `common_data/heat`'s `high_heat` (yellow LED, chamber glow), `overheat` (red LED, the overheat blast at `fx_clip`, cool-down glow) and `overheat_complete` (green LED); the placeholder charge sphere is not shown for weapons with charge effects. Test aids `--hud-plasma-demo <prefix>` (six HUD states saved as PNGs, then quits), `--old-plasma-gauges`, `--no-plasma-fx`, `--log-plasma-fx`. Tests: `PlasmaGaugeRulesTests` (rules and an install pin). Not seen by eye: the charged-state effects of a held charge (the bots release on reaching the stage), the Chaos versions, the gauges against the original (no footage compared); `docs/changes-from-original.md` row "Plasma gauges and state effects".
**Lighting presets and the focus glow (ui/lighting-presets-focus-glow, 2026-11-06; client only and cosmetic, no protocol or config-hash change).** The owner asked for ten lighting presets in OPTIONS, GRAPHICS (names his, looks ours) and a soft white glow on whatever A or a left click would activate. Presets: `LightingPresets` (engine-free, in the customizer model: `LightingPresetChoice`, the labels and one `LightingGrade` each) and `LightingGradeView`, called by `NetworkView` every frame after the region blender on the environment the camera draws with (the map's, or the Musou hub's own sky) and the sun. Each touched value keeps its base (what the lighting code last wrote; a value that no longer holds what the view wrote is someone else's new base, so the blender's writes are graded and nothing compounds); Faithful Remaster writes every base back and stops touching anything, so a player who never picks a preset sees today's look bit for bit. Grades scale exposure, adjustment contrast / saturation / brightness, sun energy and colour, ambient energy, depth and volumetric fog density and tint, bloom and SSAO intensity; nothing is switched on that the renderer or the `--lighting` level does not already run, so it works on the Compatibility renderer (no SSAO or volumetric fog there: those factors do nothing). Saved as `lightingPreset` in `frontend.json` (`GameOptions.Lighting`), live from the main menu and the Esc menu; test aid `--lighting-preset <1-10|name>`. Glow: `FocusGlow`, one canvas layer (110, under the brightness pass) on the root, made by the menu pages, `OptionsHost` and the match's UI hookup: an additive white nine-patch halo over the focused enabled button or slider, sized to a row's words (with a choice row's value) when the row is much wider, 0.08 s fade-in (none with Reduce motion); a mouse move onto such a control gives it the focus (not while typing in a field, not with the mouse captured), so there is one highlight. Screenshot aids `--glow-focus <ROW>` / `--glow-hover <ROW>` [`--glow-at s`]. Checks: `LightingPresetsTests`, `--ui-selftest` (`UiSelfTest.PresetsGlow.cs`: the row, its order and default, saving, the grade applied once and given back exactly, the glow on focus, pad moves and the mouse). Captures in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\cache\previews\presets-glow\`. Not verified: the looks on the Compatibility renderer by eye, a real controller and mouse by hand, every Musou panel by eye.
**Swing step, the lock-on's lunge and the air jump by mode (sim/swing-step, sim/lock-reach, sim/air-jumps; protocol 59, 2026-11-06, no wire change).** The owner's five changes of 2026-11-06. Swings: a new per-weapon `MeleeTuning.WeaponMap.SwingStepFactor`, multiplied into each light strike's `MeleeStep.LungeFactor` with the hammer's older `LightLungeFactor`: every melee weapon map (knife, chainsword and gold, power sword, power / chain axe, both Ork choppa sets) 1.5 (`OwnerSwingStep`), the thunder hammer / daemon maul map 0.7 (`OwnerHammerSwingStep`, so 0.82 × 0.7 = 0.574 of the lunge scale; the maul shares the hammer's map, our assumption), the heavy classes' kick (`Displace`, a core ability) 1; heavy strikes untouched (a "swing" read as a light strike). Lock-on: `MeleeLockSpec.LungeReach` (0.7 from `GameplayTuning.OwnerLockLungeReach` under owner-feel; 1 in synthetic configs) caps a locked attack's forward motion in `MeleeLock.LungeStep` to that share of the gap to the separation, along the burst's own quadratic profile up to 0.6 of the hit time, nothing after; stateless (the gap the attack began with is solved from the gap now each tick), so prediction needs no new state. On the install (`smtool melee-steps`): a locked lunge at 4 m is 2.1 m (was 3.0), at 7 m 3.8 to 4.2 m (was 6.0); free chainsword swings 5.4 / 3.9 / 5.2 / 3.7 m (were 3.6 / 2.6 / 3.5 / 2.5), hammer 5.6 / 5.4 / 4.2 m (were 8.1 / 7.7 / 6.0). Air jumps: `SimConfig.JumpPackAirJumps` (an `ExtrasAirJumps` hook; only the Musou flag sets it, in `Extras/SimConfig.Extras.cs`) gates feel/melee-cancels' air start (`JumpPack.Begin` `airLong`): in Classic PvP (faithful and extended) an Assault / Raptor in the air only hops (the air dash, Space tap + stick), Musou Mode keeps the full jump in the air. Test aid `SM_OLD_SWING_STEP=1`. Tests: `SwingStepLockReachTests`, `MeleeCancelTests` (three tests turned to the Classic rule, shared helpers), `Extras/Musou/MusouAirJumpTests`. Not verified by a human: the feel of the new distances, and whether far locks now stop short of a hit too often.
**Musou: the melee heal per enemy (2026-11-06, Musou Mode only; `MusouSim.Version` 8, no protocol change).** The owner: "in musou mode the heal effect should heal for every enemy you hit, not just one time for each landed melee swing." `World.MusouMeleeHeal(attacker, enemy)` now gives 5 % of the whole health for each enemy struck by the cleave (`ResolveMelee`'s Musou hook) or the stomp (`MusouBlast`), each enemy once a tick (an enemy in both a step's stomp and its cleave heals once), still capped at full health. Tests: `MusouCombatTests` (three Orks heal 3 x 5 %, the cap, stomp plus cleave). Classic PvP has no melee heal and is untouched.

Plasma blast fix (branch `claude/plasma-blast-original-a36d21`, 2026-11-06; client and readers only, no simulation, wire or protocol change; the owner, playtest of bea9546d: "plasma explosion currently looks like this. i want you to make it look exactly like the original game", his screenshot a huge translucent blue dome). **Cause**: the dome was the placeholder blast sphere (`NetworkView.AddBlast`, the 15 m splash of the charged plasma cannon), drawn because `FxDetonation` found no original effect: the charged cannon's projectiles (`plasma_cannon_secondary_mp`, `plasma_cannon_chaos_secondary_mp`) list `hit_from_player_highlight` under `detonate_action/commands/area_of_effect/hit_actions` (run once per entity the blast reaches) before their own `plasma_cannon_charged_mp`, `ProjectileEffects.DetonationMaterial` took the first, and that container has nothing for default, stone or metal (only dirt and energy shields). **Fix**: `FxBinding.OnAreaTarget`; `DetonationMaterial` skips per-victim bindings, so the charged cannon plays its container's `plasma_gun_mp_overcharged_dmg` (Chaos `csm_plasma_gun_mp_overcharged_dmg`; scale 1.5 on world surfaces, the data's). Lookup shared by client and tests: `EffectCatalogue.ProjectileFor`, `DetonationPlays`. Unchanged (already original): the cannon's basic shot (`plasma_cannon_mp`: `plasma_gun_charged_dmg` / `csm_plasma_gun_charged_dmg`), the gun's and pistol's charged shots (`plasma_gun_secondary_mp`: `plasma_gun_mp_charged_dmg`), the gun's and pistol's hit-scan basic shots (their impact containers; no detonation, no sphere). The original effects are sprites, decals and a light; none holds a sphere mesh. Melta bomb (not offered): its per-victim `plasma_gun_mp` container is no longer played at the blast point (its own `emp_grenade` plays). Before aid `--old-plasma-blast`. Checks: `PlasmaBlastTests` (synthetic rule; with the install: all six plasma wargear files, every shot stage, every MP map surface resolve to effects in master_fx; the old rule left the charged cannon empty on stone and metal). Captures (bot match on Manufactorum, `godot.cmd --windowed`) in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\cache\previews\plasma-blast\`: `before_cannon_charged_dome*.png`, `after_cannon_charged*.png`, `after_gun_charged.png`. Not done: the per-victim `hit_from_player_highlight` is not played on the players a blast reaches (as before); the krak grenade's per-victim screen effects still play at the blast point (unchanged).

Melta effects hard attached (same branch, 2026-11-06; client only; the owner: "when firing melta this small red glow and blue gas venting to the sides should stick to the player's melta gun exactly. hard attached to it. only the weapon shot effect that extends out from the barrel to the target should be indepedent of the weapon position"). The melta's fire effects are the data's `attached` ones, `light_led_red_1` at `fx_light_red` and `melta_gun_venting` (1.2 s) at `fx_l_muzzle_vent` / `fx_r_muzzle_vent`; since feel/scope-lascannon (owner's change of 2026-10-29) every shot's attached effect followed its marker for 0.08 s and then stayed in the world. Now the melta's follow for their whole life (`NetworkView.ShotFollowSeconds`; an effect's particles are laid out from its origin every frame, so all of it moves with the gun), for the own player and remote ones (same `FxShot` path, `FxPlace(shooter, marker)`); the beam `meltagun_cylinder_blast_4` (a target effect) is placed in the world at the shot as before. Plasma left on the 2026-10-29 rule (its muzzle effects are named in that change); a decision for the owner. Aids `--old-melta-follow`, `--log-melta-follow`. Check (windowed bot match, effect origin vs marker 0.5 s after each shot, measured after the effect update): before 1.3-18 m away (released), after 33 of 33 at 0.000 m (attached). Captures: `before_melta_vent_left_behind.png`, `after_melta_vent_on_gun.png` in the plasma-blast previews folder.

**Quick throw, quickdraw switch, grenade models and the Musou strike cooldown (2026-11-06; branch `claude/grenades-quickdraw-1412b6`; config hash, no protocol change; Musou `TfwRules.Version` 25).** The owner's three requests of 2026-11-06 (verbatim in spec "Quick throw and quickdraw switch"). **A (all modes):** the grenade leaves the hand 0.1 s after the press (was the toss graph's 0.2 s; `GameplayTuning.OwnerThrowReleaseScale` 0.5) and the throw ends at the release (`ThrowDuration` = `ThrowRelease`, was 0.667 s), so fire, aim, switch, melee, evade and jump start on the next tick; the client fits the toss clip's wind-up to the release (`ActionHandoff.TossClipTime`) and blends the arm out with the next pose. Thrown grenades are drawn with their blueprints' models from the install (`renderable_ext`: frag `frag_grenade/geo_frag_grenade`, blind `grenade_guardsman/pp_grenade_lodh`; `NetworkView.Grenades.cs`, read in the background and built at the map load; they roll with their travel; `--placeholder-grenades` = the old spheres). The detonations already played the original `frag_grenade_explosion` / `krak_grenade_explosion` (M25b); unchanged, listed for the owner because his sentence about the explosion's effect was cut off. **B (all modes):** switch press to the new weapon's first shot 0.1 s (`OwnerQuickdrawTime`; was 0.48 s + the raise, 0.65 to 0.68 s) with `SimConfig.QuickdrawSwitch`: the weapon comes up during the switch (ready ticks held), so no raise after it; anything else that lowers it still does; the client enters the ready posture over 0.06 s after a switch (`NetworkView.Quickdraw.cs`). **C (Musou only):** the orbital strike has a 60 s cooldown per player in a battle (`TfwFireRules.OrbitalCooldownSeconds`, `TfwFire.OrbitalTicksLeft`), refused by the server and not sent by the client while it runs; the battle panel reads "B ORBITAL STRIKE IN n S" in grey (own block byte 14 carries it again); at the Firing Range none (every press a strike, no cooldown started). Classic PvP has no strike. Tests: `GrenadesQuickdrawTests` (release ticks 6 → 3, every action on the tick after the release, the cooldown of the item, switch to shot 21-22 → 3-4 ticks with presses every other tick, the hash, the install's values), `TfwFireTests` (the cooldown, the range, Classic). The client test aid `TFWTEST orbital` now expects the cooldown and a refused second call. Previews in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\cache\previews\grenades\`.

**Shot looks on players (pvp-hit-fx, 2026-11-06; client and SmContent only, no protocol or config-hash change).** The owner gave three reference images of the original and a short clip: a subtle yellow glow brightest where the bullet hit (armour left), a larger soft red glow when the armour breaks, and a red-orange fiery burst with dark smoke for further hits with no armour, randomized. Found in the data: the player blueprint's `armourshield_broken` plays `sm_armor_break_shoulders` on `rig_spined` (red centre glow, white flash, red shoulder light, sparks), which we never played; `CharacterSurface.ArmourBroken` reads it and the client plays it on another player's body at the break (*original asset loaded*; `ArmourFlashTracker.TryTakeBreak` hands each break out once). The armour-hit effects (`sm_armor_dmg`, shoulder and body glows) and the weapons' `broken_ceramite` effects (`bolter_dmg_body_tough_mp` and others) were already the data's and still play. Ours: the yellow hit flash is a faint rim plus a soft spot round the shot's hit point (`CharacterViewer.FlashCode`, the point kept in the model's frame); the break shows the engulfing red glow (deep red, one soft falloff, weaker white-pink armour flash) instead of the 2026-11-02 ring; a hit with no armour shows one of 8 seeded bursts (`HealthHitBurst`: core bloom, fire lobes, dark smoke puffs from the install's own sprites, turned and sized at random) instead of the body re-flash and red streaks. Musou Mode's gore is untouched. Switches: `--old-hit-glow`, `--old-break-ring`, `--old-health-hit`; aids `--log-hit-fx`, `--pvp-hit-fx-demo armour|break|health|cycle`. Side-by-side captures with the references in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\cache\previews\pvp-hit-fx\` (`1_armour_hit_vs_ref.png`, `2_armour_break_vs_ref.png`, `3_health_hit_vs_ref.png`; a bot match on 127.0.0.1 with the demo). Tests: `CharacterVisualsTests`, `ArmourBreakRingTests`, `EffectCatalogueTests`. Not verified: real shots in a live fight (the demo drives the real impact path, not the network), the own model's spot (it has no hit point: centred on the chest), every variant by eye.

**Jump pack flash, ready jets and air-strike legs (claude/jumppack-visuals-air-melee, 2026-11-06; client only, no simulation, wire or protocol change).** The owner, for the Assault Marine and Raptor: the white-blue launch flash at every jump start, the ready jets of his reference image 4 only while a jump can start (cutting out smoothly after a jump), and the legs that "warp and jumble" in mid-air melee. Reference: his recording of the original at 11:13 (the 11:09 one named in the brief is a plasma clip): the flash is a white-blue bloom lighting the marine's back for about 0.2 s. **Flash**: the data's `quick flash` of `jumppack_thrust` (fx/jump-flash) now also at a charge started on the ground. **Jets**: the data's full-power idle effect (`jumppack_innate_full_power_combo`, Chaos `chaos_jumppack_center_full_power`) loops on the pack and its opacity (new `FxEffect.Opacity`) follows `SmNet.JetReadiness`: the simulation's own start rules read, not changed (ground: no phase or the landing's lock run and power for the jump; air: the hop's spacing in no phase, the hang or the fall; others timed from their landing and dash as seen), fading out in 0.2 s and back in 0.25 s (ours); the no-power entry stays under it on the ground. `JetReadinessTests` checks the rule against the simulation's own take-off on every tick of a jump (it found the lock's off-by-one tick). **Legs**: the clip foot lock (anim/melee-flow) held each foot a strike's clip put down at a world point, so in the air the leg IK stretched the legs back toward it as the body flew on; a strike more than 0.1 s in the air no longer locks (`SmNet.AirLegRules`). Aids `--old-pack-idle`, `--old-air-legs`, `--log-air-legs`, `--jump-test-air-melee`, `--feel-shots-on jump|jets-off|jets-on|air-melee`. Frames under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\cache\previews\jumppack\` (`ref2` the original's, `ours`). Seen: the flash and the jets cut out and back. Not seen: the warping itself (the scripted strike from the capture's high camera shows no clear difference before and after); the ready jets' flames look shorter and fainter than in reference image 4 (the data's beams at its length; not changed). Spec "Jump pack: the launch flash, the ready jets and the legs in an air strike".

**Musou: packs, twice the Orks again, no melee wedges (musou/ork-swarm-2x, 2026-11-06; `TfwRules.Version` 25, `MusouSim.Version` 8, no protocol change; Musou Mode only).** The owner: "make the orks stop running in straight lines in musou mode. they should pool up at their spawn point before fanning out, swarming their target in a rough blobby formation. double the amount of orks on the map again. also remove the small red attack incoming indicators that appear under them when they are melee attacking." Cause of the lines: each Ork followed the flow field from its own walking-graph cell to the next cell's centre, so the cells' shortest ways merged into files, worst round corners. Now a leash group let go together (a crowd, a garrison, a new muster of the trickle) is a pack (`MusouSim.Pack.cs`): its centre each tick, a lead point down the field from it, and each member heads for its own spot in a disc (2 m² an Ork) round that lead point with a slow wander; near the target each takes its own place up to 160 degrees round from the side it came from, walking round to it. The trickle no longer walks off one by one: it musters leashed at its source until 10 have gathered (or 10 s). Counts doubled again: pool 2048, garrison 96, crowd 400 (one every 4 ticks), cap 1200/640/1680, trickle every 0.75 s and 1600 in all, 1800 drawn (1000 VAT a look). The melee wind-up wedges are off in a war (`MusouTelegraphs.Wedges`); the 5-wave run keeps them and its steering (`MusouSkirmishPinTests`). Tests: `TfwPackTests` (one pack per release, the muster, a blob of 120 through a wall gap: ratio under 1.6 in the open and at least 2 m across round the corner where the old way made a file 0.7 m wide, the surround from several sides, determinism, the counts). Test aid `--tfw-swarm-shots`. Perf (measured under 100 % foreign CPU load, spec "Musou Mode: packs and twice the Orks again"): server tick p50 about 5 ms with about 1790 Orks; windowed client 105 to 121 fps away from the swarm and 41 to 48 fps inside it with 1700 drawn (52 to 59 with 900 drawn); to re-measure on a quiet PC before shipping.

**Musou Ork guns (musou/ork-weapon-fx, 2026-11-06; client only, Musou only, no protocol or config-hash change).** The owner: "the ranged attack orks don't have weapon models in their hand, and their shots are invisible. no muzzle flash, no occasional tracer, nothing. flesh that out. musou mode only." The Shoota Boy now holds the playable Ork's shoota (`ork_coop_boy_2hand_shoota_rapid`, model `shoota`, wield mount `RIG_Prop_M_Chest`): `MusouGunModels` reads the wargear and model on a worker and joins it to the look as one more rigid piece (a new `MarineAssets`, so the Ork class's shared `boy_ranged` look is untouched), so the skinned tier and the vertex-animation bake both carry it. Each round the simulation already reported (`MusouEventKind.Tracer`: shooter, end point, hit or miss) now plays the wargear's own effects, read from the install by `MusouOrkGunEffects` (a small `EffectCatalogue` of the Musou guns): `shoota_muzzle` at the muzzle (the skinned skeleton's prop bone, else the place and facing with the muzzle measured in the aiming stance), `shoota_tracer` on every 3rd round of each Ork (ours: "occasional"; the data draws it on every round), and the `shoota_coop` impact by surface: the player's on a hit, on a miss the first wall or floor within 30 m past the simulation's end, none in the open. `MusouGunFxPlanner` (engine-free, tested) bounds the cost: flashes within 45 m, tracers 70 m, impacts 35 m, and crowd-wide token buckets (flashes 40/s burst 8, tracers 16/s burst 4, impacts 14/s burst 4), nearest rounds first; the cadence counts every round, drawn or not. A firing Shoota Boy, whose simulated state stays "seek" while he stands through a burst, plays his two-handed aiming idle for 0.6 s after a round instead of running on the spot (`MusouCrowd.Guns.cs`, one hook in `MusouCrowd.Frame`). The fire sound (`play_or_shoota_fire`) was already posted by the crowd's sounds under their Gun budget; unchanged. Switch: `--no-musou-guns` (as before); capture aid `--musou-gun-cam` with `--spectate shot`; a `musou guns:` log line every 10 s. Measured (windowed, 5-wave run on Manufactorum, wave 1, 80 Orks, 4 runs of 75 s): mean 135 fps with the guns against 137 without, frame p50 in the 40-skinned state 10.2 against 9.0 ms, inside the run-to-run noise; the guns' own code 0.002 to 0.009 ms a frame; in one 100 s run 496 rounds gave 441 flashes, 158 tracers, 302 impacts, 194 effects held by the caps. Not measured: a crowd of hundreds of Shoota Boyz firing (a stress run on the war map gave no Ork shots at the bot). Checks: `MusouOrkGunTests` (11: the gun table, the tracer cadence, the culls, the caps and refill, nearest first, the wargear's muzzle, tracer and impact container, the compiled names). Captures in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\cache\previews\musou-ork-guns\` (`ork-shoota-in-hand.png`, `ork-guns-firing-flash-tracer.png`, `ork-guns-firing-2.png`, `ork-shoota-closeup-impact.png`). Spec "Added content: Musou Ork guns"; changes-from-original row in the Musou table.

**Musou Boss Orks and the Warboss model (musou/boss-orks, 2026-11-06; `MusouSim.Version` 8, `TfwRules.Version` 25, no protocol or wire format change; Musou Mode only).** The owner: "randomly spawning boss orks (they spawn with an elite retinue of elite ork enemies). the bosses have massively incresased hp, damage, and are scaled up 3x from their usual size" and "the final boss should use a warboss model"; designed with him in the session's chat (docs/musou-boss-orks-design.md, his answers there). Four new enemy kinds (`BossBoy`, `BossShootaBoy`, `BossArdBoy`, `BossNob`, wire types 7 to 10) made from their base by `MusouBossOrks.From`: 3x the body, 10x the health but at least 3000, 2x the damage, 1.5x the reach (ours), the 'Ard Boyz' pace at most (ours), stagger-immune and only scratched by shells; 1000 points and a sure box. `TfwBattle.BossOrks.cs` brings them in a battle only, while someone is in the field: the first 1 to 2 min after the landing, then 1.5 to 3 min after the last came, at most 2 alive, at a sending spawn point 40 m clear of every player, each with 20 free 'Ard Boyz and Nobs that fight on after it dies; the rolls come from the battle's places, so the same battle brings the same bosses. The Warboss: 15000 health (was 4000), swing 60, slam 60, charge 75 (1.5x), and at the owner's word the battle's commander is now the Warboss (leashed at the HQ with his old escort; the bar and the HQ label say WARBOSS). The client draws him with the campaign's `warboss_regular` and head on his own rig (`WarbossLooks`, docs/discovery.md "Warboss model"; a singleplayer dependency), as tall as the old 3x Nob body, the Nob body as the fallback; Boss Orks are their base's look at 3x. HUD: BOSS ORK INCOMING and BOSS ORK SLAIN, an orange bar each under the boss bar (their bars are pinned in tag 13, and they are leaders in the entity feed so every client knows them), a line on the M panel. Tests `TfwBossOrkTests`; `MusouBossTests` follow the new damage and health. Not done at the owner's word: no headless run and no screenshots ("i'll playtest all changes for this session manually"); nobody has seen the Warboss model drawn, so whether his mesh binds and his picked clips look right is unverified; the retinue walks with its boss but has no leash to it. Review fixes: the stuck-Ork rule of a position being cleared never removes a Boss Ork (as the stranded failsafe only moves it); the HUD reads a bar's kind from the client's live tracks, so a reused id never calls out a false boss; the Boss Ork looks are built before the Warboss model, so none waits on its read; `TfwBattleTests`' commander test now expects the Warboss.

**Musou Mode co-op for up to 4 players (branch `claude/coop-4p-host-3d260e`, 2026-11-06; server, front end, release files; no protocol or wire change, protocol stays 58).** The owner: "add support for 4 players to host on a locally hosted server that works the same way as the locally hosted server of classic pvp mode. this change is for musou mode 4 player co op." Most of the team was already in the run since TF4 (one side, a Deploy takes everyone, the fallen wait while another fights, the Ork cap grows per human, per-human scores, drops and cards, four Stormbird spawns); what blocked other players: the front end hosted Musou for this PC only, and the server had no cap of its own. **Server:** a Musou match admits at most 4 players (`TfwCoop.MaxHumans`, `GameServer.PlayerCap` through the new hook `ExtrasPlayerCap`; the fifth is refused "server is full (this match takes 4 players)"; every other profile keeps 16; the start prints `musou: co-op, at most 4 players`). **Co-op rules (ours):** a human who joins during a battle is flown in at the landing zone with its retainer on the next tick (`TfwRun.JoinLate`; before, it waited in the Stormbird with no say), and only a death itself cancels a pickup (before, a teammate already down cancelled every pickup each tick, so the living could never call one). With 4 humans the 8 AI-Marine ids leave room for 2 lords on a final assault (unchanged contract; spec row, confidence low). **Front end:** MUSOU MODE on the main menu opens a page like PLAYER VERSUS PLAYER's: PLAY ON THIS PC (the one-press start of 2026-11-01, 127.0.0.1 only), HOST LOCAL LOBBY (the Host panel on the Musou profile with its reach row free: THIS PC ONLY or LAN / INTERNET; HOST MUSOU), JOIN LOCAL LOBBY (an address, joined with `--content musou`); STOP MUSOU SERVER stays under MUSOU MODE. `--menu-screen musou|musouhost` opens them; the UI self-test walks the page. **Release:** "6 - Host Musou Mode on this PC.cmd" and "7 - Host Musou Mode for friends (LAN).cmd" (templates `HostMusou*.cmd`; `Host.cmd` with `SM_HOST_MUSOU=1` runs `--content musou` and no `--map`), the READ ME and the release notes say how to host and join. **Test aid:** `--bot` on a Musou Mode server is a co-op bot (`NetworkView.TfwCoopBot.cs`: deploys after `--coop-deploy-after` s, fights the nearest Ork, COOPBOT lines; straight walk, `--coop-nav` for the graph). Tests: `TfwCoopTests` (cap, 4-human landing, late join, pickup, fallen wait), `TfwRunTests` and `TfwHudTests` updated for the late join. Live runs on 127.0.0.1 (a hosted Musou server `--bind 127.0.0.1 --content musou`, 3 headless co-op bots, a 4th joining mid-battle; logs in the private tmp-build folder `coop-run4`): the three landed together by the landing zone each with a retainer, the server logged the 4th's late landing ("a human joined the battle under way and landed at the landing zone; in the field: P1, P2, P4"), the bots fired (44 to 1356 shots each) and the battle counted 156 Orks killed; no exception on the server or any client. Every client ended in one long stall (26 to 60 s, main thread busy in the network and prediction step, then a time-out) on a PC at 100% CPU from other sessions' test runs, also with one human left alone and in runs where no bot had fired: the client's tick loop catches up without a cap after slow frames (`GameClient.Update`; core netcode, not changed here; a follow-up). A windowed screenshot from a placed camera (`--spectate cam:`) shows another player in the Stormbird's bay (private cache, `previews/musou-coop/stormbird-two-players-bay.png`).
