### Musou: Ashfall draft 8 roadways (2026-11-06; branch `musou/ashfall-roadways`)
The owner: "no 3d objects should be placed in roadways." Generation rule: no placed item's collision box within 0.5 m of a roadway (the avenues and the perimeter road along the road tiles' lines, and the level's Road parts; bridges may span a road with 2.5 m of headroom), resolved at placement in `AshfallDraft8.cs` before the overlap rule (move across the road up to 14 m, shrink, the next model, else left out; never into a stronghold leg's band; the overlap rule never moves an item back onto a road); `AshfallRoadway`. Without the rule 187 items stood in the roads, now 0: 91 moved or shrunk, 50 left out (covers, rubble, the west monument and the east arch). Level version 13, `DressVersion` 11, hash `0xB2335BB6CF43E872`. Aids: `RebuildWithoutRoadwayRule()`, `smtool ashfall-plan --no-roadway-rule`, gallery `--ashfall-no-roadway-rule`. docs/musou-ashfall-graybox.md "Draft 8 roadways".

**The charge clash (feel/charge-clash, protocol 59, 2026-11-06; no wire change).** The owner, with a recording of the original: "the player should never, ever phase through another player model. both models 'clash' ... sticking together like a lock on." The recording (frames 163 to 199 at 30 fps): the rush homes onto the target, meets it at 6.07 s shoulder to chest, the two travel together about 0.18 s, then the charger recoils while the stunned victim stays about a metre in front. The data says the same: the collision stop `SM_NAV_Bullrush2Idle_F_Collision_01` shoves 1.83 m forward in 0.2 s, then 1.11 m back. Cause of the phasing: that shove collided with the victim's body as the charger's client last saw it, and after the stop the server's walker guard allowed 0.45 m of overlap (150 of 150 lagged control runs overlapped). Now (`SmSim.ChargeClash`): a rush whose victim reacts opens a clash; through the shove's 6 ticks the charger's step ignores the victim's body (predicted exactly by its own client: `GameClient.ClashBodies`) and the world carries the victim by the charger's move through the level (`World.CarryClashes`; a victim the level stops holds the charger back, `HoldClashes` after the guard); the guard with any charger or charge stop is 0.85 m (the touch less a 5 cm slack the shared collision never reaches, was 0.75 m); the own client predicts the clash from its view of the victim (`ChargeClash.Predicts`: an opponent that can react); remotes are drawn up to 0.9 m apart (`DrawnBodies.MaxShift`, was 0.45 m); the own charge's victim is drawn carried with the own body until the snapshots catch up (`NetworkView.LockDrawn`). `ChargeClashTests`: 900 charges (20 to 45 m/s, 0 to 300 ms, plus or minus 40 degrees, offsets to 0.9 m, standing, strafing and oncoming targets), closest 0.850 m (an oncoming sprinter pressing into the recoil, at the slack; 0.900 m without an oncoming target); the lock 0.900 m on every shove tick, shove 1.83 m, 2.0 m apart after the recoil; at 150 ms with 5 % loss the shove predicted exactly on 120 of 120 ticks and no view drew the two closer than 0.900 m. Headless bot run on 127.0.0.1 (3 v 3, Tactical, Assault, Raptor, Chaos Tactical; 4 min, `--log-overlaps`): 15 clashes, the clash pairs exactly touching on all 105 samples, opponents with a charger never more than the 5 cm slack inside each other; every own charge impact drawn 0.90 m apart (17 of 17); in the bots' views no drawn bodies more than 7 cm inside each other (8 of about 137,000 samples above 5 cm). The run found the own charge's victim, held at the lock spot after the own stop, drawn up to 0.36 m inside the own body: the lock draw now runs before the drawn bodies' separation. New diagnostics: `--log-overlaps` also prints the charge pairs and the clash pairs; a bot prints a DRAWNOVERLAP line for a drawn overlap over 5 cm. Frames of our charge beside the recording's under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\cache\previews\charge-clash\` (`comparison.jpg`; our strips are the bot's wider camera). Test aid `--no-charge-clash` (server and clients, config hash). Spec "The charge clash". Not played by a human.

The owner's concept art (storm clouds, a warm break behind the keep, grey haze, rough grey stone, fires, ash and debris at several depths) and his notes, plus his shadow report. Air: ash and flakes doubled, far debris chunks and dust banks, every layer invisible near the camera (1.2 to 22 m by size). Markers (`TfwMarkers`, rules in `SmNet` `TfwMarkerRules`): black ground-ring decals 0.22 m wide (a flat band on Compatibility), letters 24 m up shown within 25 degrees of the view's heading and hidden on or near the point; the graybox's coloured discs and letters no longer drawn over the kit look. Test aids `--ashfall-concept off`, `--ashfall-grime off`, `--tfw-old-markers`, `--ashfall-old-markers`, `--tfw-no-capture-hud`. Tests `TfwMarkerRulesTests`. **Musou far Orks move smoothly (musou/far-ork-smooth, 2026-11-06; server send order and client drawing, Musou only, no protocol, wire or config-hash change).** The owner: "figure out why the orks movement at distance looks so choppy." Root cause: with about 1800 Orks the crowd fills the 55 KB/s budget, and `MusouInterest` ordered the due Orks by priority alone, which under load keeps the 1 : 0.5 : 0.2 band ratio of their waits, so an Ork beyond 40 m waited about 38 ticks between records (up to 46; a real local run, `SM_TFW_STRESS=1800,0`). The client then held him still: it carried a runner on past his newest record for at most 6 ticks and only after a step of at most 6, and a gap over 30 ticks even restarted his track (3,000 to 3,800 restarts in 10 s). Fix: (1) the server sends any known enemy unsent for 15 ticks (`MusouSendRules.MaxWaitTicks`) before the other due ones but the leaders, the longest unsent first; (2) the client carries a runner on for his last step plus 3 ticks (6 to 30) and draws him from his last drawn place moved on at the sampled speed, pulled onto the sampled place with a 0.2 s time constant (snapped beyond 4 m or a 2-tick sample gap), so a correcting record is a glide (`MusouClientState.Smooth`). Real run (headless, 60 fps cap, a busy shared PC, 30 to 48 fps achieved), share of a running Ork's frames without motion, old / new: about 10 m 70 to 78 % / 3 to 4 %, 30 m 85 to 89 % / 9 to 13 %, 60 m 95 to 97 % / 0 to 0.2 %, 100 m 98 to 100 % / 0 to 1.2 % (t 30 to 50 s); records at 60 and 100 m every 31 to 38 ticks / every 15; bytes received 50 KB/s / 48 to 55 KB/s (the budget is unchanged). Engine-free measure (`MusouFarMotionTests`, the real interest and budget, 60 fps): at 1800 Orks clustered as the stress ring, stalls at 30, 60 and 100 m 84 to 94 % / 0 %, the largest frame step 44 times a frame's run / 1.0; at 300 Orks nothing changes (no budget pressure). `MusouClientState.Sample` costs about the same (0.4 to 1.9 ms a frame for 1800 in the test either way, noisy: other agents' tests ran at once). Test aids: client `--musou-old-far-motion` and server `SM_MUSOU_OLD_FAR_SEND=1` restore the old behaviour; client `--musou-motion-log` prints `MUSOUMOTION` lines. Not verified: a windowed look by eye, the residual 9 to 13 % at 30 m (likely Orks pressed still in the crowd, not checked), whether near Orks' wind-up records come late under the full budget now that overdue far ones go first.
**Musou: Guardsmen as defenders, the capture under fire, the Boss Ork cleave (musou/guard-formations, 2026-11-06; `TfwRules.Version` 28, no protocol or wire change; Musou Mode only).** The owner: "re add the imperial guardsmen infantry formations to the game. they move and act on their own to defend existing points. only allied space marine lords and players and retainers go capture new territory"; "the boss orks should be able to cleave guardsmen the way that players cleave orks"; "players should be able to make progress capturing a point even if orks are still defending it. only stop capturing if no player remains on the point." `TfwBattleRules.GuardsmenEnabled` is true again (`SM_TFW_GUARDSMEN=1` is now redundant). `TfwBattle.StepPosition`: only a capturer (a living human or AI Marine: lords and retainers) adds progress, always at the full rate (the half rate is gone), Orks on the point or not: Clearing now means capturers with Orks on the point, Securing capturers alone, and both grow the progress; with no capturer the point is Held and decays 2 % a second as before; a secured point is kept by any Imperial, Guardsmen included, and falls with Orks alone on it. The HUD says "CLEARING n%". `TfwBattle.StepSquads`: the squads never go for a point not secured; with none secured they hold the landing zone, otherwise they are shared over the secured points by the Orks within 40 m of each (`LandingGoal`, `SquadPost`; numbers ours, spec "Guardsmen as defenders"). `GuardSim.Cleave` and `World.TfwGuardCleave`: a Boss Ork's melee blow on a squad strikes up to 20 men of any squad in its front half within its reach, by the players' cleave rules; survivors fall (2 m, 10 % die). Measured on a real server (loopback, headless client, other agents' work on the same CPU): 60 Guardsmen cost 0.16 to 0.21 ms a tick; the whole tick ran p50 3.5 to 6.5 ms, p99 87 to 195 ms with 1200 to 1640 Orks, the spikes as with no Guardsman fighting (not separated from the shared load). With `SM_TFW_WIN_TEST=6` and `--tfw-test-win` the walker secured A with Orks on it; the squads walked from the landing zone to A, fired 1485 shots (887 hits) and all 70 men (7 squads) were lost in about 60 s against about 1600 Orks; A fell and was retaken, so a point can still fall (balance unchecked by a human: the men may be too weak against the doubled hordes). That run's 4 crate checks failed (crates not listed for the client), not traced to this change. Tests `TfwGuardFormationTests`; `TfwBattleTests`, `TfwOrkTests`, `AllyNavTests`, `TfwBossOrkTests`, `TfwHudTests` follow the new rules. Not verified: no Boss Ork met a squad in a real run (the cleave is unit-tested only), no client was measured windowed with the Guardsmen (a headless client measures no frame rate), not played by a human.
## Musou: the Ashfall window pass (2026-11-06; branch `musou/ashfall-windows`)
Owner: "send a collison box adjustment pass that ensures i can shoot through all the windows in the structures on the map." `smtool ashfall-kit-collision` now finds every through-opening of each kit model on the gate's 144-cell grid (a framed free run along raw X or Z that passes out of the wall on both sides: windows, arches, doorways; blind niches excluded), clears the fit's cells in them before merging and forbids merges over them, and the collision quality gate fails a used model with an opening less than 90 % clear. 130 openings in 26 models, all open (68 before). The kit's ramp wedges became movement only (they filled arches under stair flights). Level version 13, hash `0x2D90FDEF0587A5AA`. `AshfallWindowTests`: 622 shots through placed windows pass, 622 into the walls beside them stop. Open: slab-merged rubble, cover and collapsed-wall pieces keep their gaps filled (`AshfallDraft5.Coarse`). Docs: musou-ashfall-graybox.md "Window pass"; spec "Ashfall window pass (kit collision)". Not played by a human.
**Strafe and run direction blend (branch `anim/strafe-blend`, 2026-11-06; client only, no protocol change).** The owner: "when changing strafe or run direction there are many times an animation snaps to another instantly". Measured first: new direction events in `--transition-probe` (an event per heading change of the drawn ground velocity, worst bone jerk around it; `--transition-probe-directions` prints each) and a bot script `--direction-sweep` (with `--bot --bot-gait`: run and walk reversals, 90 / 45 degree changes, diagonals, sprint into and out of a strafe or backpedal, the same in aim mode and the ready run), two recorded demos (tactical, Chaos tactical, assault, Havoc, Ork Boy) replayed at 60 fps. Cause: a reversal takes the damped velocity through zero, where its heading turns 180 degrees between two frames, so the blend space's weights flipped to the opposite clips in one frame (relaxed run reversal jerk median 115 to 225 cm/f^2, max 238; ready run 42 to 47). Fix: the direction x band weights and the idle share follow a 0.05 s critically damped spring (`SmContent.GaitWeightSmoother`, `NetworkView.GaitPlace`; the aim pitch stays immediate, the movement is not delayed): relaxed reversals 5 to 6 median (Ork 6.3), ready 10 to 15, steady run p99 36 to 58 -> 7 to 13. Unchanged and not snaps by the measure: aim-walk direction changes (sector cross-fades, 13 to 16, at the aim walk's own steady p99), the sprint. Left: the stop foot pins engage during a reversal (ready reversal turn 14 vs 9 deg/f without them), the sprint loop's seam (35 to 48 cm/f^2 on the fingers and toe when the sprint clip wraps, also before). Test aid `--old-gait-snap`. Spec "Weight smoothing (anim/strafe-blend)"; tests `GaitWeightSmootherTests`. Not seen by a human.
**Musou: patrols, hunter columns and no Ork stuns (musou/ork-patrols-nostun, 2026-11-06; `TfwRules.Version` 28, no protocol, wire or `MusouSim.Version` change; Musou Mode only).** The owner asked for large Ork formations all round the map, 20 times the Orks, and patrols that walk set routes and hunt the players wherever they are; the same day he cancelled the 20x (counts exactly as before, no impostor crowds) and asked: "remove all stun effects by orks in musou mode. they should never impede player movement or action". **Columns** (`TfwBattle.Patrols.cs`, `MusouSim.Patrol.cs`): each battle sends 4 route patrols and 2 hunter columns of 40 fodder Orks, 4 abreast, out of the crowds' existing cap (a column forms only when the cap and the pool have room), so the map holds no more Orks. A route patrol walks a loop of the battle's places on the walking graph at 2.6 m/s (A* off the tick from the start, taken 3 s after it; a way back with no drop reused reversed); a hunter's head walks down the shared flow field to the nearest target at 3.4 m/s with its ranks on its trail. Each Ork's leashed home moves with its place and it walks after it (the home's velocity plus a pull, `MusouSim.MoveHome`), a target within 25 m of its place wakes the whole column as one pack, the head waits while the middle Ork is 4 m behind, an Ork 20 m behind is let go alone, and a woken or wiped column forms again 30 s later at its source while that source sends. **No Ork stuns** (`TfwCombatRules.EnemiesImpede`, false): no enemy attack puts a player in a reaction in a war (the Nob's, every Boss Ork's and the Warboss's staggering swings, his slam's stagger and his charge's 3 m knockback); the damage stays; no other Ork effect held a player (none grabs, roots, slows or blocks the body); the players' own barrage keeps its stagger; the 5-wave test aid keeps the old staggers (its pin unchanged). The boss strike path is one `World.MusouBossHit`; test aids `World.MusouLandAttack`, `MusouLandBossStrike`, server `SM_TFW_NO_PATROLS=1`, TFWFIGHT lines name the columns. Tests: `TfwPatrolTests` (formation in ranks, routes round a wall, the march, waking as one pack and re-forming, a hunter finding a far player round a wall, the cap, determinism, the moving home, the real map with a position still secured), `TfwNoStunTests` (every kind's melee and ranged hit, the slam and the charge: damage dealt, no reaction, the player moves and fires the next tick; the old rule still staggers; the barrage keeps its stagger; a classic PvP world has no Musou path); the crowd-counting tests run with `Patrols = false`. Perf (shared, loaded PC; spec "Musou Mode: patrols, hunters and no Ork stuns"): server tick p50 3.7 to 6.2 ms with columns against 4.8 to 5.6 ms without, Musou step 2.6 to 4.5 against 2.6 to 4.1 ms, at the same Ork counts. Not done: no human playtest, no screenshots (headless runs only), client fps not measured (no client change, the same Orks drawn).
**Musou Ork voices, no shot flinch, no spread (musou/ork-voices, 2026-11-06; Musou Mode only).** The owner: Orks "need to scream, yell, and taunt often", constant grunting near, "muffled, similar to weapons fire" far; remove the shot Orks' "turn around 180" hit reaction; "in musou mode only completely remove bullet spread". **Voices:** why they were quiet: the Ork voices' own distance curve falls to -49 dB at 20 m, and the crowd budget let 0.8 barks a second through. Each slot now has a voice emitter (`MusouSoundSlot.Mouth`) whose positioned voices take the bolter's distance curves (`SoundEmitter.AttenuationOverride`, `SoundSystem.AttenuationOf`, `MusouSoundRules.VoiceCurveEvent`: volume and low-pass, the multiplayer guns'); 24 slots within 45 m; grunts every 0.8 to 2 s and barks every 1.5 to 4 s per Ork, also while winding up and striking; a running bark is a taunt (celebration line) 20 % and a roar 25 % of the time; caps 23 voices (under half the pool) / 18 lines; ranges and rates in the spec. Measured on a real server under `SM_TFW_STRESS=300,0` (scripted player in the crowd, `--log-sound musou`): about 5 grunts, 2.5 barks and 0.8 taunts a second; the `musou sounds:` line now gives the nearest enemy's distance. **Flinch:** the drawn flinch of a shot Ork is off (`--musou-ork-flinch` restores it); the simulation never stopped a shot Ork. **Spread:** `SimConfig.NoBulletSpread` (hook `ExtrasNoBulletSpread`, set only by the Musou flag) zeroes the scatter, the bloom and the melee flinch scatter in `Spread.After`, `Spread.HalfWidths` and the reticle; no hash or protocol change (Musou's block covers it). Tests `MusouNoSpreadTests`. Not heard by a human: the voices' loudness and muffling. Test aid `--musou-ork-voice-curve own`.
**Instant step and 20 % longer steps (sim/instant-step, 2026-11-06; branch `melee/instant-step`).** The owner: the step forward of a swing should begin the instant the swing starts, and every melee weapon's step should be 20 % longer; responsiveness matters (Musou Mode most). Cause found with `smtool melee-steps`: the clips' free-swing root motion builds up slowly and lands mostly after the hit (chainsword strike 1: 0.15 m of 2.2 by the hit), so the first tick moved 0 m. Now `MeleeLock.Profile` (switch `MeleeLockSpec.StepFront`, `GameplayTuning.OwnerInstantStep`) re-shapes each strike's motion up to its move-on time into an ease-out of the clip's own total (first tick 0.3 to 0.5 m, total and hit time unchanged, no new recovery or lockout; the in-place stomp untouched); `MeleeTuning.OwnerStepBoost` 1.2 multiplies every light and heavy strike of the melee weapon maps. `smtool melee-steps` now prints a timeline (first tick, by the hit, half-way time, peak). The client follows the same profile (`MeleeLock.MotionAt` / `StartBlend`; `MeleePresentation.RootDriven` takes it) and the clip stride stretch (`HammerStrideScale`) now covers every weapon's strikes, light and heavy. Test aids `SM_OLD_INSTANT_STEP=1`, `SM_OLD_STEP_BOOST=1`, `--old-strike-legs`. The config hash changes (no wire change). Tests: `InstantStepTests`. Not verified by a human: the feel.

**Playtest pass of 2026-11-06 evening (branch `musou/ashfall-concept-look`, from integration f9be5527; the owner's notes of that evening).** One branch with: the Ashfall concept pass (look, grime, black rings, raised letters, capture tracker; above); far Orks moving smoothly (`musou/far-ork-smooth`); draft 8's roadway rule (`musou/ashfall-roadways`) and the window pass (`musou/ashfall-windows`) together as level `Version` 14, pinned hash `0x2BB88406D096C7EF` (each alone was version 13); the Guardsmen back as defenders, capture with Orks on the point, Boss Orks cleaving Guardsmen (`musou/guard-formations`) and the patrol and hunter columns with no Ork staggering a player (`musou/ork-patrols-nostun`) together as `TfwRules.Version` 29; the strafe and run reversals blended (`anim/strafe-blend`); and the Ork voices, no shot flinch, no Musou spread, the hammer's legs, the instant step and the longer step (`claude/competent-shaw-1fc7e5`). The owner's 20x horde was cancelled by him before any of it was built. Left open: 368 openings in rubble, cover and collapsed-wall pieces stay closed for shots (the placement merges those families into slabs, `AshfallDraft5.Coarse`); the Guardsmen may be too weak (70 men fell in about 60 s holding A in a scripted run); nothing of the pass has been played by a human.

**Night batch 2026-11-06: Musou death spike and near wind-ups (branch `night/death-spike`; Musou Mode only, client drawing and the server's send order, no protocol, wire, config-hash or rules-version change).** (1) The owner: "when a grenade explodes many orks die instantaneously ... remove the moment of extreme frame time". A new test aid measures it headless: `--musou-death-spike-test [N]` (the scripted gore feed's new `burst` case: N Orks 8 m in front of the camera die by a blast in one tick every 4 s; the crowd is drawn even headless; per frame the main thread's own CPU, via its cycle count, since the shared PC sat at 100 % load; `--musou-death-spike-ab` takes turns old/new so both meet the same load). Found: when warm, the per-death work is 1 to 2 ms for 60 deaths; the second after costs about 1.8x a quiet frame (16 against 9 ms), mostly from what then flies (20 ragdolls in the physics, 40 thrown bodies probing the walls, the gore) and the sounds' engine side; the first burst of a run was 52 to 63 ms (nodes built on first use: the dolls' meshes, crowd skeletons, the sounds' first loads). Changed: the deaths are handed out the nearest first, at most 24 a frame and 5 ragdolls, none later than 0.1 s, each drawn dying in place meanwhile under the skeleton that drew the Ork, which its body keeps (`MusouDeathRules`, `NetworkView.MusouDeathSpread.cs`, `CrowdView.KeepSkinned`); the death yells and falls go with the body; the ragdoll pool is dressed in every thrown look after load, one doll a frame (`MusouRagdolls.Prewarm`). Result: warm bursts within the noise (worst frame medians 16.5 / 15.8 ms at 60 Orks, 16.7 / 16.0 at 150), the cold one 52 to 63 / 31 to 39 ms (single samples). `--musou-old-deaths` restores the old hand-out. (2) Near wind-ups under a full budget (the open item of musou/far-ork-smooth): `MusouWindUpLatencyTests` (engine-free, the real interest, budget and event window; 1800 Orks as the stress ring, 16 near Orks winding up) found a near wind-up's record 0.81 ticks late on average, at most 2 (67 ms), and its telegraph up to 4 ticks behind a grenade's 60 deaths; at 300 Orks 0. Now an enemy within 15 m whose state changed goes right after the leaders, before the overdue far ones, and a telegraph's first copy before every other event copy: 0 ticks late in every case, far Orks still every 15 ticks (`MusouSendRules.NearChangeFirst`, `TelegraphFirst`; server `SM_MUSOU_OLD_NEAR_SEND=1`). Not verified: anything the GPU does (shader compiles on first use, the overdraw of near gore clouds, skinning the dolls) and a windowed look by eye of the staggered deaths; a real battle's load; a real server run of the wind-up latency (only the engine-free measure).

**Late batch 2026-11-06, stream D: Musou run flow (branch `claude/late-d-musou-flow-662256`, from `night/death-spike` d5839bfa; Musou Mode only; `TfwRules.Version` 31 (30 is main's), no protocol change; two new war commands on the Musou wire).** (1) Grenade mass kill: measured on the server (`TfwGrenadeBurstTests`: three big frags into 150 / 400 packed live Orks, 130 / 279 killed) the blast ticks cost 0.6 to 1.3 ms warm against 0.45 / 0.8 ms quiet, so the server is not the hitch; on the client (headless `--musou-death-spike-test 280`, 200 deaths a burst, 100 bodies) the Musou frame is about 19 ms of CPU on this loaded PC with the hand-out 2 to 4 ms, and the burst's extra cost is engine time (physics, nodes) plus a 72 ms cold first burst. One fault found and fixed: at a slow frame rate the night batch's 0.1 s deadline let a whole burst out in one or two frames; overdue deaths now come at most 48 a frame, 8 of them ragdolls (`MusouDeathRules.DuePerFrame`; `--musou-death-deadline-all` restores, `--musou-death-spike-deadline-ab` compares). Not removed: the cold first burst and the engine side; nothing the GPU does was measured. (2) Deploy after death: a fallen human presses Enter (A) to come back at its own landing place for 1 supply (`TfwCommand.Redeploy`, `TfwRun.Flow.cs`, HUD line under the prompt). (3) The host (lowest human id) has BACK TO STORMBIRD in the Esc menu during a battle (`TfwCommand.ReturnToShip`, the core's `MatchMenu.AddRow` through the new `ExtrasMatchMenu` hook): 20 s in Pickup, free, deaths do not call it off, then everyone is back in the Stormbird; a battle not won counts as left. (4) After a battle's Warboss falls, 500 Orks come from a 45 m ring round the players at every bearing, 12 a tick (`TfwBattle.Victory.cs`; none after the final assault; `TfwRun.VictoryWave` off only in tests). Tests: `TfwFlowTests` (8). Not verified: any of it in a real match by a human; the wave's look and difficulty on Ashfall; whether the 3 s extraction prompt leaves enough time to choose a deploy with no retainer up.

**Night batch 2026-11-06: Classic PvP bots and jump-pack fuel (branch `night/classic-bots-jetpack`; protocol 61).** Owner's three requests, Classic PvP only (Musou bots and Musou's pack unchanged). (1) Bot accuracy: the aim error angle is scaled by 15 m / distance (`BotAimModel.DistanceScale`) so the accuracy setting holds at every range, and the default `--bot-accuracy` is 0.97 (was 0.03); measured in bounded 3v3 runs: 32 % of shots at 0.65, 36 % at 0.93 overall (Tactical and Assault bots 46 to 54 %, heavy-weapon bots 12 to 25 %), so the owner's 49 % overall is not reached by aim alone (spec "Bot accuracy 49 %"). (2) Reaction time: a bot's first ranged shot on a new target waits 250 to 450 ms (seeded; target forgotten after 0.4 s, so one re-entering view waits again) and its first melee press or charge on an enemy in reach waits 200 to 350 ms; an enemy starting a melee attack within 4 m re-arms that wait (`BotFireDiscipline`, `BotMeleeReaction`, `NetworkView.BotMeleeReady`); off with a perfect aim and `--bot-no-discipline` (the probe flags). (3) Jump-pack fuel: Classic PvP holds the data's `power_settings/max_power` 100 again (one full jump, 10 s empty to full); Musou Mode keeps 300 (`JumpPackSpec.DataMaxPower`, `SimConfig.JumpPackOwnerCapacity`, hook `ExtrasJumpPackOwnerCapacity`). Protocol 60 to 61 because the fuel is server-authoritative; the Musou hash is unchanged (`MusouIsolationTests`). Tests: `JumpPackCapacityModeTests`, `BotMeleeReactionTests`, `BotFireDisciplineTests`, `BotAimModelTests`.
**Night batch 2026-11-06: Ork movement (night/ork-movement; no `TfwRules.Version`, `MusouSim.Version` or protocol change; Musou Mode only).** The owner: 3x Boss Orks "walk against walls looking the wrong direction while running forward". Cause: `MusouSim.Move` faced a running Ork along its desired (flow field) direction, not its moved velocity, and the walking graph's 0.4 m wall margin is a normal Ork's, so a 1.8 m Boss Nob ground along walls. A Boss Ork in Seek now turns (6 rad/s) to face its smoothed actual velocity (it keeps its facing when slower than 0.8 m/s) and leans off walls nearer than its radius minus 0.4 m along the gradient of a lazily computed distance-to-wall field on the walk graph (`MusouNav.EdgeDistance`, `EdgeGradient`). Tracing a scripted layout found the real stall: with a player straight through a wall the old code made a Boss Ork (and a plain Boy) shuffle at the wall's corner for good, because `WayIsStraight` (a length test) read straight on one node and round on the next; a Boss Ork now also checks `NavGraph.StraightWalk` and keeps to the flow 1.5 s after finding a wall in its line (arrives in 11.5 s instead of never; the crowd is untouched, the same flip still affects ordinary Orks). Patrol columns: measured stopped-for-ranks seconds per column over 180 s bounded runs (open floor with a 24 m and a 2.5 m gap, and the test arena's real graph): 0.0 to 0.5 s each, so the earlier fix already held in these layouts; the wait is now bounded anyway (2.5 s, then laggards over 9 m are let go and the head creeps at 0.6 pace). Tests `MusouBossMovementTests`, `TfwPatrolTests` (stall measurements). Unverified: the live stall was not reproduced, and nobody has watched a Boss Ork on Ashfall.
### Night batch 2026-11-06: Musou rules (Guardsmen strength, endless ammunition, grenade refill, AI Marines' damage)
**Branch `night/musou-rules` (from 5a6b76e0; `TfwRules.Version` 30, no protocol or wire change; Musou Mode only).** The owner: "scale up the guardsmen to what you believe will half the time win, half the time lose against ork counterattacks"; "ammo should be infinite in musou mode"; "grenades should refill every 30 seconds automatically"; "bots in musou mode should retain all player attributes and statistics - except make them take 90% reduced damage". `GuardHoldTrial` (tests, `GuardHoldTrialTests`): a headless deterministic trial with no player, the field's 6 squads on a secured point against one full crowd of 400 at the run's middle elite share from a seeded bearing; at the old strength (85 health, 5 a shot) the field held 0 of 20 and was gone in about 36 s having killed about 5 Orks (the scripted run's 70 men in about 60 s); x4 held 0, x4.25 7, x4.5 11, x4.75 12, x5 20, so `GuardRules.Strength` is 4.5 (382.5 health, 22.5 a shot; the 20-seed test is `[Trait("Speed", "Slow")]`, about 1.5 min; `SM_GUARD_SWEEP=4,4.5` prints a sweep). `World.TfwSupply.cs`: `TfwEndlessAmmo` keeps every living player's reserve full in every slot (humans and AI Marines; the reload, heat and vent unchanged; a brace weapon or one without a reserve gets its clip back once empty), replacing the AI Marines' own top-up; `TfwGrenadeRefill` gives one grenade every 30 s while a player is short of its item's most; `ExtrasDamageTaken` (a new hook in `DamageScale.cs`, applied at the melee, shot/blast, charge and Ork hit sites) scales every hit on an AI Marine by 0.10. `GuardSimTests` follow the new strength (TF3's box fight with Boyz scaled the same, the strike test with a Boy nobody kills). Not verified: no human has played it; the trial leaves out players, lords, retainers, Boss Orks, the trickle and reserve squads, so the real hold may differ.

**Stream A 2026-11-06 (late): jump escape, hop-cancel momentum, descent recharge (branch `claude/beautiful-edison-35f3b8`; protocol 62).** Owner's batch, the Assault Marine and Raptor. (1) Jump escape, every mode: a fresh Jump press ends any hit reaction (stun, stagger, interrupt) at any time of its clip, any melee attack (not only from `BRANCH_Evade`), a throw (before the release nothing is spent), every phase of the charge, the landing locks and the pound or slash recovery, in the press tick; the press then starts the hop or the jump by the usual rules (`JumpEscape`, `MeleeCancel.Apply`, `JumpPack.Begin` `escape`). The hop in flight keeps its data spacing. (2) A hop cancelled by melee keeps no upward speed and carries 0.4 of its horizontal speed (`MeleeCancel.HopCarry`, an estimate) under the air swing, the swing's step or lock-on lunge added (`Combat`: the air swing). (3) Fuel: the data's values were already in use in Classic PvP (max 100, costs 35 short / 55 full, recharge 10/s; a hop is free); what made the second full jump fall short was our ground-only recharge rule. Sound mix pass and reload sounds (branch `sound/mix-and-reloads`, 2026-11-06; client and content only, protocol unchanged; owner's playtest notes). Mix (all values ours, spec "Sound mix pass and reload sounds"): every gun's fire sound +4 dB; on-hit sounds (shot impacts on the level and on players, melee hits, the hit confirm) +4 dB through new `SmHit` / `SmHitLpf1..20` buses with a 250 Hz 24 dB/oct high-pass (`VoiceOffset.HighPass`); the master bus ×1.1 with a limiter at -0.3 dB (`SoundSystem.ApplyMasterVolume`, also from the Options menu); the jump pack's launch and apex voices hold 0.5 s, then fade over 0.3 s to -15 dB (`VoiceOffset.TailDb`; the launch is a 1.1 s burst plus two 1.7-2.0 s thrust layers, measured with `smtool audio-decode`). `--sound-mix-classic` restores the old mix. Reloads: the cause found by reading the code is a second post path: the reload clip laid over the upper body (M35) also fired its behaviour tags as an animation (`SoundLayerTags`) whenever the legs were in a blend, doubling the scheduled reload sounds at slightly different times, and the stop events those tag posts owed (`TagStops`) cut the playing sounds when the layer ended or its time jumped back. Reload clips now post no tag sounds (`SoundTriggers.ClipTagsPostSounds`); a reload picked up again after a prediction correction schedules only the tags still ahead (`ReloadSoundGuard.Remaining`). Tests `SoundMixPassTests` (no install). Not checked by listening: the levels, the high-pass, the tail fade and the reload fix in a live match (`--log-sound reload` counts the posts of one reload).

The owner: "you should be able to make an appearance, save it in one of 10 slots, then apply that appearance to any loadout." The appearance editor gains a first section, MY APPEARANCES:

Test aid: `--warboss-test --model weirdboy`. Tests: `MusouWeirdboyTests` (7). The owner's additions (same day): his shield's break throws every Ork within 20 m down (the fall Musou Mode's shove uses; the Warboss, Boss Orks and Weirdboyz stand), and his death is a green psychic burst (the charged plasma cannon's `plasma_gun_mp_overcharged_dmg` at scale 2, tinted green; capture `previews\weirdboy-model\burst_00*.png` from the new `--fx-tint`) that kills every Ork within 20 m but the Warboss and the Boss Orks (the owner: "Spare Boss Orks"), credited to his killer (`MusouWeirdboyTests`, 11). Review fixes: the flesh-only hit sound for him, teleports and arrivals only where players can walk to, a failsafe move mid-stun brings his shield back, a bolt hits from where it was thrown. Open: no in-game frame yet (only the stage and effect captures); a thrown-down survivor plays the fall clip, not a physics ragdoll; the shield's strength looks; the shield's 300 and every timing are estimates for a playtest; the original's AI cadence is not in the data.

**Manufactorum console posts removed (fix/pvp-manufactorum-red-lights, 2026-11-07; client drawing only, no protocol or config-hash change):** the owner sent two captures of the red-lit wall objects near both spawn areas. In-engine captures (a hide-list experiment on the same camera) traced all of them, the dot posts, the dash rows and the thin black cable lines, to one original object definition, `tech_panel_pipe_e`, the fittings of the monitor consoles (49 placements, layer `e_adm_dressing`, stacked with `monitor_a` at the two bases and at the other console groups); the 2026-11-04 pass had kept it as a console part. It is original content drawn through our emissive-map approximation, not a debug overlay. `MapDecor.Always` now lists it; the monitors, cabinets and everything else stay. Spec row "Objects not drawn on `mp_tdm_09`"; changes-from-original row "Manufactorum's console posts". No unit test: `MapDecor` reads Godot arguments and the client project cannot be referenced from a test project.
**HUD: the empty clip's last round turns off (branch `claude/fix-bolter-hud-last-round-c9cdc2`, 2026-11-07; client display only, no sim, protocol or config-hash change; Classic PvP and Musou).** The owner: on the Tactical Marine's bolter and relic bolter the weapon box's last round stayed white after it was fired. The sim was right (the clip count reaches 0 and stays 0 until a reload refills it; a reload starts only on the reload key or a trigger press at 0). The display was wrong: the clip's tick strip (`ammo_count_mc`, 100 frames, frame 0 full) masks the white ticks with a band that stops moving at frame 95 and leaves the first tick lit through frame 98, which `WeaponBoxRules.BarFrame` picked for 0 rounds (and for 1 round, correctly); only frame 99, where the mask is gone, shows every tick spent. Fix: `WeaponBoxRules.ClipEmpty` / `EmptyBarFrame` pick frame 99 for a clip of 0 on the bolter strip (bolter and relic bolter; lead review 2026-11-08 limited it there, `UsesEmptyBarFrame`, since only that strip was checked; the bolt pistol, storm bolter, lascannon and melta strips keep the old frame until checked); heat bars (plasma, heavy bolter) are not clips and are unchanged, and the Chaos side shares the same strips. New aid `client.cmd ... --hud-clip-demo <png prefix>` saves the weapon box at full, 3, 2, 1 and 0 rounds (`_0.png` .. `_4.png`). Test in `HudMovieTests`. Waits for the owner's screenshot approval.
**Plasma tracers in safe mode (fx/plasma-tracers-safe-mode, 2026-11-07; client only, no simulation, wire, protocol or config-hash change; normal mode unchanged).** The owner: in GPU safe mode (Compatibility renderer) no plasma tracer is drawn, for the gun or the pistol. Cause: not found on this machine. Forced to `--rendering-method gl_compatibility` (an RTX card on OpenGL 3.3) the plasma bolt is created and the sprite-shader effect (`FxBatch`, the one shader every effect shares) draws it, with the charged shot's blast and the overheat/muzzle effects; no shader error is logged; there is no safe-mode switch in the tracer code. What differs on an old card is only the one shared sprite shader (depth-texture reads in the soft-particle fade, `textureGrad` on an atlas) and that a 0.09 m wide, 1.8 m long bolt is a very thin quad: either could drop it there without any error on this machine, which is unproven. Fix: in the Compatibility renderer the bolt is also drawn as a pooled streak (`StreakAdd`, a plain unshaded additive mesh with vertex colours, no sprite shader, the path the bolter's muzzle leg already takes), same colour (the bolt's blue or Chaos purple), the bolt's 1.8 m tail (`PlasmaBolt.SafeTail`), a width matching the bolt's 0.09 m (`PlasmaBolt.SafeWidthScale` of the 0.16 m soft glow), the same head speed, gone as the head arrives (no lingering muzzle glow). `PlasmaBolt.UsesPooledStreak(compatibility)`; test `TracerRulesTests.BothPlasmaBoltsGetThePooledStreakInSafeModeOnlyAndItMatchesTheBoltsSize`. Captures (`--bolt-fx-demo`, forced Compatibility vs Forward+): the gun's bolt shows in both. Not verified: on the owner's old card (the cause is unproven, so it is unproven that this fixes it); the plasma pistol (same code path, no clean capture); first-person own view in safe mode; the blast and overheat FX on an old card.
**fix/melta-burn-onhit (2026-11-07, classic PvP; the owner's melta clip: the burn showed ~2 s after the kill and only as a small flame at the centre).** Cause, from the code and the data: the data's on-hit effect `meltagun_dmg_burn_limb_armor` x1.5 is one effect played at the single hit point and exists in the melta's container only for the armour-up surface, so a shot that broke the armour (a kill) played none, so the late flame in the clip is not explained by this effect's data (unconfirmed which effect it was); the effect itself has no start delay (its elements start at 0, life 2 s, `fx-dump`) and the melta's blast has no flight time (`PlayTracer` returns 0), so there was no timer, snapshot or ragdoll wait to remove. I could not reproduce the clip's 3.4 s timestamp in a controlled run (the real kill timeline needs a live melta fight): the measured values below are for the demo shot through the real `FxImpact` path. Fix (client visuals only, `NetworkView.MeltaBurn.cs`, `ImpactRules/MeltaBurnRules.cs`): every melta hit on another player plays the same original effect on 14 bones, head to feet including both arms (`rig_head` .. `rig_rfoot`, heights 0.2 to 1.9 m in the log), attached, in the hit's own frame, on armour up or broken alike; a kill hands the followers to the corpse skeleton (holding the last place between) so the burn runs its normal life; one set per victim per 0.25 s, pooled effects (priority 2), cached bone lookups; the effect player draws sprites, so safe mode (Compatibility) is unchanged. Measured with `--log-hit-fx --pvp-hit-fx-demo meltakill`: burn starts at the hit frame (HITFX line `t 0.144` against the shot at `t 0.15`, delay 0 ms), before: none on a broken-armour hit and one point on armour. Frames in the owner's chat. Aids: `--old-melta-burn` (before), `--pvp-hit-fx-demo melta|meltakill`. Tests: `MeltaBurnRulesTests` (the trigger is the hit event: weapon, body hit, victim; no death or corpse input). Musou's Orks and the Chaos melta: the Chaos twin uses the same code path (wargear name contains melta); Musou Orks have their own gore path (`NetworkView.OrkBlood.cs`) and are left as they are. Ours: the bone list, scale 1.0 and the 0.25 s gap (not in the refine register yet). Waits for the owner's screenshot approval and playtest.
**Crosshair scales with the FOV (ui/crosshair-fov-scale, branch `claude/crosshair-fov-scale-7492ac`, 2026-11-07; client only, no protocol, wire or config-hash change; waiting on the owner's screenshot approval).** Playtesters: a high FOV makes the crosshair too big; the owner: original FOV keeps the original size, scale from there. The FOV slider (`FovMath`, horizontal degrees from the data's look, about 65-66 at 16:9, to 120) widens the camera's vertical angle through `tan(v/2) x Scale`; the crosshair was one fixed size. New `ReticleFovScale` (`client/Customizer/Model`): factor `tan(reference/2) / tan(live/2)` on the camera's real vertical FOV, where the reference is the same camera state (hip/aim/evade/weapon-switch blend) at the default setting (`NetworkView.Camera.cs` tracks `fovRef` beside `fov`), so it is exactly 1 at the default and aiming down the sights alone does not resize it (live FOV chosen over the setting only; scoped zoom is unscaled, and the scope has its own overlay reticle). Applied in `Hud.DrawReticlePic` / the movie hit marker (reticle spread frames, plasma heat and charge arcs) and the old-style circle, ticks and hit marker; text, panels and cards are untouched. The spread: the movie reticle shows art frames picked by the scatter's fraction (not pixels), so it scales as a whole and keeps its frame; the old-style ticks' opening was already an angle at the live camera FOV (`NetworkView.SpreadPixels`) and is left as is. Musou shares `DrawCentre`. Tests `ReticleFovScaleTests`. Screenshots at the minimum, default and maximum FOV sent to the owner. Row in changes-from-original.
**Hammer and maul: swing anywhere in the hop, shorter F,F recovery, the steered slam (branch `claude/hammer-hop-ff-steer-aedb1b`, 2026-11-07; protocol 63 unchanged, no wire change; the config hash covers the new step fields; Classic PvP and Musou Mode).** The owner's report on the thunder hammer and the daemon maul (Assault, Raptor), with his 6.7 s recording of the original (two F,F slams at 60 fps; measured frame by frame, kept outside the repo). (1) **Hop swing**: the gate was not the hop, the landing or the buffer: from the hop's `BRANCH_Dash_Attack` (0.333 s of the 0.73 s flight) a melee press started the jump pack's dash attack (a lunge with the sword's clip) instead of the hammer's swing, and while the dash attack's 1 s spacing ran the press was lost. The hammer and the maul now cancel the hop into swing 1 at any point, flight or landing (`MeleeStep.HopSwing` on swing 1, `Rush.CanDashAttack`); the other melee weapons keep the data's dash attack (the lost press during its spacing is an open question for the owner). (2) **F,F recovery**: the slam played its whole clip (3.0 s, hit 1.1 s; the left-side slam 2.0 s) before anything could start; it now frees a new string 0.633 s after its hit (1.733 s), the light combo's own gap from X3's hit to its reset (1.333 − 0.700 s), and presses kept by the input buffer fire on that tick, so mashing swings at once (`MeleeTuning.Finisher`, `MeleeStep.StringResetAt` on heavy finishers, `Combat.StepPlayer`). The recording shows the slam's hit at about 1.1 s (matching the data) and the marine kneeling until 0.8–1.0 s after it, but no follow-up press, so the original's value is not visible. (3) **Steered slam**: before, the slam simply followed the view at once over its whole clip (its data has no alignment window), with no limit, and the own model followed the camera. Now it turns toward the view like a turret at 300 degrees a second (measured in the recording: about 100 degrees in 0.33 s and 120 in 0.43 s, by eye) inside a window that closes at the hit and opens 185 / 300 = 0.617 s before it, so it reaches the owner's 185 degrees at most; it holds its facing before and after; the lock-on's alignment does not act on it; the hit cone and its stun follow the final facing (the blast stays centred). The own model shows the simulation's heading during it (`NetworkView.Turning.cs`). No new input: the yaw of every input carries it. Test aids `SM_OLD_HOP_SWING=1`, `SM_OLD_SLAM_RECOVERY=1`, `SM_OLD_SLAM_STEER=1`; capture modes `--swing-test hopswing|slamsteer`. Tests `HammerHopSlamTests` (hop presses at 0.07, 0.33, 0.60 s and in the landing; the slam's reset at tick 52 for a light swing, a stun strike and a single buffered press, 91 before; the steer clamp at 185.0 degrees on synthetic and install data, Marine and Chaos; the hit landing only on a target the slam was steered to); `WeaponTimingStreamBTests` install check updated (the finishers now have a reset). Spec "Hammer and maul: hop swing, slam recovery and the steered slam"; changes-from-original rows. Not played by a human yet; gameplay waits for the owner's playtest.
### Classic PvP bots: centre hold, roaming, spread routes and fixed loadouts (branch `claude/pvp-bots-centre-loadouts-86df6b`, 2026-11-07; client test aid, no protocol change)

The owner asked for bots that hold defensive spots round the map centre when nobody is left outside the enemy spawn (or after a wipe), never wait outside the enemy spawn, roam until the enemy comes out and pressures the centre, take different routes and spread out (Annihilation in particular), and carry a fixed list of loadouts. `SmSim.BotMapPlan` (built per side on the thread pool after the spawn watch): a 25 m no-loiter zone round the enemy's door and start, eight centre holds 5 to 16 m out (one per sector, near cover, by team rank), up to 12 roam points (farthest-point sampling) and three spawn-exit lanes (left, middle, right); `SmSim.BotRoamer`: hold 12 to 20 s, roam a point, come back; one lane leg per life; long chases bend through a via point by rank. An enemy in the room or zone is no longer chased (the M44a door wait is now `--bot-door-wait`); a seen one is still fought; Seize Ground keeps its point logic. Loadouts: `SmSim.BotLoadouts` (the owner's 8 presets as side-free wargear stems; `smtool bot-loadouts auto`: all 16 class presets legal against the install, Raptor's thunder hammer = Daemon Maul, stims = equipment, Twin Link = Improved Twin-Link), one drawn per match at connect; chosen in the new `ClientOptions.ReviseOnMap` once the Challenge names an `mp_*` map, so Musou bots join as before; explicit loadout flags win, `--bot-preset none|a|b|c`. Aim and difficulty unchanged. Tests: `BotMapPlanTests` (13), `BotLoadoutsTests` (10). Bounded local runs (server `--bind 127.0.0.1`, Manufactorum, Annihilation, 3v3, 300 s, `bots.cmd --for`): plans built in 133 to 355 ms; each side's three bots took three different lanes; **0 ticks in the no-loiter zone** for all six bots (about 7,000 ticks each); teammates a median 58 m (Marines) and 70 m (Chaos) apart, under 5 m 2 % of the time. First run found the lane leg checked after the idle hold (bots went to the centre spot first); fixed. Correction (2026-11-08): bots did die in that run (score 19 to 19; the trace CSV writes living ticks only), but a dead bot's input skips `BotInput`, so lives were never counted and no lane leg after a respawn ran; fixed with `BotNoteDead` from the input sampling. A live wipe was not seen; the centre hold was exercised by a Marines-only run (3 bots, 150 s, no enemy alive): each ran its own lane, then held its own centre spot (8.6 to 14.6 m from the centre, three different spots) 35 to 42 % of the time, roamed a point and came back (2 to 3 cycles each), 0 ticks in the zone. Waits for the owner's playtest.

Melee push (same branch, 2026-11-08, owner: "periodically choose to close in and attempt melee combat ... a route that minimizes the enemy's ability to see the bot ... raptor and assault marines in particular try to stay low but approach the enemy with hops and dashes, then jump on them and shoot/melee"): `SmSim.BotPush` rolls every 15 to 30 s (Assault / Raptor 75 %, Tactical 35 %, heavy 15 %; Annihilation only); `SmSim.BotApproach` plans, off the frame loop, a hidden cover cell (14 to 28 m) and a hidden staging cell (4 to 11 m) the enemy's eye cannot see, scored on distance plus 3 x the seen share of each leg; `SmSim.BotHopper` gives a pushing jump-pack bot alternating forward dashes (no power) and small hops (only above the full jump's cost) every 0.9 to 1.6 s, and the jump-and-pound script jumps onto the target from 16 m instead of 30 m during a push. A pushing bot keeps closing in sight instead of strafing until 9 m, where the charge (ready at once) and melee take over; the push ends on the target's death or return to its spawn zone, the bot's death, 4 s in melee reach, or 30 s. `--bot-no-push`. Tests: `BotApproachTests` (6). Bounded local runs (3v3, 300 s, Manufactorum, Annihilation): 21 pushes in the first run (Assault 3, Raptor 4, Tactical 3 and 2, Devastator 2, Havoc 0) and 27 in the run after the death fix (Raptor 9, Assault 8; 14 of them ended with the pusher dead, 11 on the target's death or retreat, 1 timeout). The planned approaches were seen less than the straight line on every bot (mean 29 to 73 % against 32 to 100 %; the Raptor 41 % against 60 %); jump-pack pushes dashed 1 to 6 times and hopped up to 6 times and ended in 18 to 32 jumps at the target and 18 to 27 pounds per bot. The same run counted 80 lane legs after respawns (each bot's lane changing every life). No push ended as "melee done" (4 s in melee reach): each ended first on a death or the target's retreat; whether the pushes feel right is for the owner's playtest.

**Headshot medal, score and scream (branch `claude/headshot-scoreboard-loading-b4160e`, protocol 64, 2026-11-07).** The owner: "No headshot scream audio. No headshot medal onscreen after the kill ... add a +50 points to score as well as a headshot medal icon and description from the original game." Cause of the missing medal: the headshot line was the client's guess (a killing head hit in the own hit reports within 1 s of the kill, matched against the player under the crosshair), which failed whenever the crosshair had left the victim. The server now decides it: `ScoreRules.IsHeadshotKill` (the killing hit of an enemy was a weapon's shot on `HitZone.Head`; not melee, thrown items, landings, perk blasts, splash or flame cones) sets `KillEvent.Headshot`, and the kill feed carries it as cause code 6 (a weapon kill on the head; the entry stays 9 bytes, snapshots unchanged). `PlayerScore` gains headshot kills and assists (the data's `xp_settings_pvp/assists`: a hostile non-killer who dealt at least 25 % of the damage the victim took in that life); the score is `ScoreRules.Of`: 50 a kill + 50 a headshot (the data's headshot reward is 35: changes-from-original "Headshot medal, score and scream"); each scoreboard row carries headshots and assists (u8 each; fullest scoreboard 1193 bytes). Client: `Hud.AddOwnKill(victim, headshot)` from the server's flag (the crosshair guess is gone) shows the medal line: icon `mp_bonus_headshot`, name locale 105720, +100, and the description locale 105721 under it; every headshot kill in the feed plays the victim class's speech-bank `death` exertion where it fell (`NetworkView.Headshot.cs`; lines found for all six MP characters: tactical_marine, assault_marine, devastator, chaos_space_marine, chaos_havoc, chaos_raptor). Classic PvP gameplay is unchanged (no damage, timing or team score changes). Tests: `HeadshotScoreTests` (headshot and body kills, the killing hit decides, the rule's exclusions, assists and an earlier life, the wire, the fullest scoreboard), `HudRewardTests`, `TeamsTests` updated. Waits for the owner's playtest. Open: whether SM1 played the `death` exertion on every death or never in MP (the MP data binds none); assists are counted, not scored.

**Tab scoreboard in black and white (branch `claude/headshot-scoreboard-loading-b4160e`, 2026-11-07; client only).** The owner: "the scoreboard needs to look like the reference image except using only black and white colors ... the player icon is just the icon they spawned in with when they first joined the lobby ... no extra text." The text panel (`ScoreboardText`, monospace BBCode with mode, limits, class and a footer) is replaced by `ScoreboardView`, drawn on a 1920 x 1080 stage: an opaque black band with each side's big score and VS between them, one column per side (own side left) with a header row and a row per player: icon, name, KILLS, DEATHS, RATIO, ASSISTS, SCORE, PING (the install's words; protocol 64 brings assists and the score). Musou Mode gets one column with KILLS, DEATHS, SCORE (the run's points from tag 12) and PING through the new hook `ExtrasScoreboard` (`Extras/Musou/Tfw/NetworkView.TfwScoreboard.cs`). The own row has a faint white fill and a white bar. Icons: `SmContent.JoinIcons` freezes each player's shoulder decal (a custom emblem first, else the left pad's badge) the first time its look is known after it appears on a scoreboard, and forgets it when it leaves, so a returning player shows its new emblem; the picture is the pad's own texture made grey. The Chaos default scheme has no pad decal, so Chaos players show an empty frame. Verified live: `godot.cmd --windowed` against `server.cmd --bind 127.0.0.1` with 5 bots (PvP: kills, deaths, assists and scores as the server counts them) and a `--content musou` server (one column). Tests: `JoinIconsTests` (4). Waits for the owner's screenshot approval.

**Loading screen (branch `claude/headshot-scoreboard-loading-b4160e`, 2026-11-07; client only).** The owner: "add a loading screen that replaces the 'connecting to IP address' when loading into musou mode or classic pvp mode. its just straight black and says LOADING in the center." `NetworkView.Loading.cs`: a canvas layer above the HUD and the join's back hint, black with LOADING in white (Bahnschrift, the HUD's face; 40 px at 1080) from the view's start until the client is connected; any error (refusal, no answer, load error) hides it and the error shows as before. The join's "Esc: back to the menu" hint now shows only once the join failed (Esc still goes back while loading). Headless bots skip it. Screenshot aid `--loading-shot` (join an address with no server). Waits for the owner's screenshot approval.

**Classic PvP join while the own Musou server runs (branch `claude/headshot-scoreboard-loading-b4160e`, 2026-11-07; client only).** The owner: "when you try to join a classic pvp match when you still have musou mode local server running the 'enable extended mode' error message appears ... it should automatically stop the musou server and attempt a rejoin silently." Cause: while the front end's hosted Musou server runs, the session keeps the Musou profile (`FrontEndView.SyncContentLock`, `_lastContent`), so a lobby join offers the Musou config and the Classic server refuses it (`RejectReason.ConfigMismatch`). Fix: `SmNet.MusouJoinRetry.Decide` (pure) says retry only for a ConfigMismatch while this client's `HostedServer` runs Musou, the join offered Musou, the lobby's remembered profile is not Musou, no `--content musou`, the address is not the hosted server itself (loopback on its port: `IsHostedTarget`), and no retry yet. `ModelViewer.TryMusouRetry` then calls `FrontEndView.StopOwnMusouServer` (`HostedServer.Stop`: the process this client started, by its handle, never by name; the lobby's profile put back, as STOP MUSOU SERVER does), rebuilds the plan for that profile and joins the same address again under the loading screen, with no message; a failed retry shows its normal error. `NetworkView.RejectedBecause` exposes the reason. Tests: `MusouJoinRetryTests` (decision and loopback rule). Not verified live end to end (needs the front end hosting Musou and a separate Classic server); the rule and the stop path are the tested parts.
**Versatility primary and knife during melee (fix/versatility-knife-stow, 2026-11-07; client only, no protocol change).** The owner: with Weapon Versatility the primary "goes crazy in the air" in the knife stun-strike combo, should be holstered top left of the left leg pointing down during all knife and stun-strike animations, and the knife points straight up in front of the chest when a light combo ends. Causes: (1, 2) no Space Marine weapon is flagged two-handed (`RigWeaponMount.TwoHanded` is for the Ork only), so `WeaponHands.InHand` kept the selected primary in hand on `RIG_Prop_M_Chest` while the knife was out, and the strike clips drive that prop through the air; (3) the strike handed over to the legs fades its upper-body weight over the 0.333 s exit but the knife stayed drawn until the weight fell below 0.25, riding the blend to the rifle-posed arm (knife up in front of the chest). Fixes: `MeleeHolster.OnThigh` (engine-free, tested) puts the selected primary on `RIG_L_Thigh` for as long as a strike is shown (`WeaponStowSpots.ForThigh`, mode "thigh" in `WeaponRig`); the knife leaves the hand at upper weight 0.85. No change without the perk, for other classes or the lascannon. Test aids: `--viewer --weapons primary,pistol,melee,second --hand melee` shows the thigh holster; `--swing-shots` frames log a `SWINGFRAME` line with the strike step and time. Tests: `MeleeHolsterTests`. Spec "Weapon Versatility's primary on the thigh during melee". Not verified by a human; the thigh spot is fitted by eye.
Safe pushes, cover and posts (same branch, 2026-11-08, owner: "change the bot behavior so that they only approach for melee if there is safe way to do it out of sight. they should also not push when they are being actively shot at. they should prioritize taking cover when their hp gets low to regenerate, then rejoin the fight. make one boss play at the top of the side ramps, one devastator on top of the balcony next to the capture points A and C. the rest play around the center of the map and the side lanes."; test script, ours). A rolled push now waits for its approach plan and goes ahead only when the enemy sees at most 25 % of the walk to the last hidden cell (`ApproachPlan.Safe`); no push starts within 4 s of damage, and a hit ends one that has not closed in (`BotPush.UnderFireStart`/`UnderFireAbort`). At low health a bot hides from the enemies on the map (`BotRetreat`, `BotCover`: the nearest hidden cell 2-30 m away, planned off the frame loop and replanned when seen) until 90 % health and armour or 35 s (`--bot-no-retreat`). On Manufactorum each side's lowest-id Devastator/Havoc holds the 8 m balcony beside a point and its lowest-id Tactical the top of a side ramp (6 m deck), both on the side's own half (`BotPosts`, anchors read from our nav graph; `smtool bot-posts auto [--grid]`; `--bot-no-posts`); "boss" was read as "bot". Three local 3v3 Annihilation runs of 300 s: run 1 started the retreat at 40 % health and counted threats within 60 m only; 18 of 20 retreats ended in death within 1-4 s, some "in cover" from a rifle beyond 60 m, so the start went to 60 % and the threat range to 150 m (run 2: 6 of 19 recovered, run 3: 4 of 21; most deaths are Assault/Raptor in melee reach, where the bot fights instead). The run-1 ramp holder strafed and evaded off the ramp's edge (28 % of its life within 6 m of the post in run 2), so holders no longer roll or advance and step back onto the post while firing past 2.5 m; run 3: the four holders spent 56, 60, 84 and 83 % of their lives within 6 m of their posts. Pushes in run 3: 7 rolled, 3 with a safe approach (seen 18 % against 25 % straight for the Assault), 4 dropped as unsafe or without a hidden approach; 2 of the 3 safe pushes ended in melee ("melee done"), the first in any run. Tests: `BotCoverTests` (6).


**Musou expansion S2, the Bomb Squig and the Rokkit Boy (2026-11-07, branch `musou/exp-s2` from `musou/expansion` 667e3011; `MusouSim.Version` 14, `TfwRules.Version` 34, `Protocol.Version` stays 63; Musou Mode battles only).** The Bomb Squig (`MusouSim.Squig.cs`, `MusouSquigRules`): a drop director in the World (`World.TfwSquigs.cs`) lands one behind each human every 60-120 s during a battle (12-20 m, off-screen first, at most 8 alive); it falls 1.2 s (`Spawning`, drawn from 14 m with the drop pod's whistle), runs at 7.5 m/s at the nearest player, AI Marine or Guard squad, lights a 1.8 s fuse within 10 m (`WindUp`), and bursts as the original frag (200, r 10, the data's stepped fall-off) through S1's `World.MusouOrkBlast`, so it hurts Orks, elites and Guards and sets off other Squigs one a tick. Any hit sets it off at once; a running player (3.5 m/s, 1.6 m) kicks it 12 m along his run (`Knocked`), an unlit fuse set to 1.0 s; credit to the shooter, else the kicker within 10 s. The Rokkit Boy (`MusouSim.Rokkit.cs`, `MusouRokkitRules`): 6 % of a battle's crowds (`TfwBattle.CrowdKind`), holds 25-45 m, a rocket every 5 s; the rocket is the first Musou projectile with collision: 16 m/s, it bursts at the first solid (weapons mesh), Ork (the shots' bodies, not its shooter) or player chest, or after 4 s; burst r 3.5, 120, linear to 25 %, through the Ork blast. Wire: Telegraph cues 24-29 (drop, fuse, kick, Squig burst, rocket fired with its serial and aim point, rocket burst). Client (`NetworkView.MusouSquigRokkit.cs`): the original `rokkit_firing_line`, `rokkit_missile_trail`, `rokkit_dmg`, `squig_explosion` (compiled from master_fx on a worker) and the frag's own detonation effects and sounds for the Squig; `play_or_missle_launcher_fire`, `play_or_squig_vox_roar`/`_taunt`; one incoming warning (`MusouRocketWarner`: the single most threatening rocket, 1 s before its nearest pass within 5 m, never stacked) as a screen-edge arc and the whine on the rocket. Looks: the Squig on its own rig (`SquigLooks`, `squig_bomb` on `havok_squig__hkxx`), else a labelled placeholder (a Boy at x0.4); the Rokkit Boy `boy_ranged_pro` (*original asset loaded*) holding `ork_coop_boy_rokkit_launcha` (`boy_pro_rocketlauncher`): its wargear has no wield entry, so it is held by a mount of ours (owner 2026-11-08), its own `RIG_Prop_M_Chest` locator (the Shoota's very spot) on that bone, as the Shoota (`MusouOrkGunRules.OwnMounts`; seen in a windowed capture, both hands at the chest). Seen in a windowed capture: `squig_bomb` on its rig (35 bones, 10 clips), the four effects compiled. Placeholders: the fuse beep (a generated tone), the fuse glow (a light), the edge arc; the drop pod whistle as the fall and the rocket's whine. Capture aid: server env `SM_MUSOU_S2_DEMO=<s>`. Tests: `MusouExpansionS2Tests` (17). Open: every value an estimate for a playtest; the skirmish (`MusouDirector`) unchanged.

**Musou expansion S1, the foundation (2026-11-07, branch `musou/exp-s1`; `MusouSim.Version` 13, `Protocol.Version` stays 63).** The Musou entity wire record grows to 11 bytes with a full type byte (108 entities a section, was 119); five placeholder kinds (BombSquig, RokkitBoy, Stormboy, BigShootaNob, ScrapMek, types 12 to 16) are in the enum and the type table but not spawned. Target preference by kind in Tfw battles (`MusouTargetRules`: ordinary Orks favour Guards, AI Marines and objectives over players; elites and bosses favour players, then Marines; a preference other than the nearest is walked to directly within 40 m). A neutral Ork blast (`World.MusouOrkBlast`, `GuardSim.Blast`, `MusouDeathKind.OrkBlast`) with a Squig-detonation queue for S2, and the friendly-fire table. Tests: `MusouExpansionS1Tests`. **Musou expansion S5: the Librarian (branch `musou/exp-s5` on `musou/expansion`, 2026-11-07; `MusouSim.Version` 13, no protocol change; Musou Mode only).** A playable psyker class. `MusouLoadout.Prepare` appends `sm - librarian` after the other classes under Musou only (the Tactical's body, perks and melee choices, no gun, pistol or grenade, the Assault's power sword combo as his melee; the indices of the others never change and the PvP and extended config hashes are untouched, `MusouIsolationTests`). Powers (`Extras/Musou/Librarian/`): `LibrarianRules` holds every number (kind ours, owner brief), `LibrarianPsyker` runs Psychic Stress (0 to 100; lightning 5/s, Pull and Shockwave 50 each, cooling 12.5/s after 1 s, lock at 100 until 0, a melee swing -6, cooldowns 8 s and 12 s), chain lightning (30 m, 8 m jumps, 40 targets, 90 dps x0.85, a blast-type hit so a Weirdboy's shield wears), Warp Pull (cone, 25 m; ordinary to 2 m, elites 35 %, bosses immune) and Psychic Shockwave (9 m, 40 damage, ordinary Orks thrown 20 to 25 m, elites and bosses not moved). The World feeds it the sanitized input through one new core hook (`ExtrasSampled`, an empty partial outside Musou) and the Musou step; keys Fire, Grenade, Reload. Nothing is in the core `PlayerState`: stress, cooldowns, cast counts and up to 8 lightning links per Librarian travel on a new Musou Mode tag 16 (`LibrarianWire`, `GameServer.TfwLibrarian.cs`, `TfwClientState.Librarians`). Client: the links drawn with the Weirdboy's bolt trail tinted blue, the Pull and Shockwave effects, a stress bar HUD, and the force sword (`ForceBlade`: the power sword with a rainbow-iridescent glow about 3x brighter). Tests: `MusouLibrarianTests`. Psychic Ward is a future idea only. Open: the body is the Tactical's (no psyker model found, *placeholder*); the HUD layout and the effects' look are untested in a game window and need the owner's screenshot; the class has no entry in the front end's class picker yet (join with `--class librarian`); the 5-wave Musou run has the class and the powers but no tag 16 (the war's sender only); every value is an estimate for a playtest; 'cone 30 degrees' was read as the half-angle. Follow-up (owner update, same day): the lightning is now drawn procedurally by `LibrarianBolts` (jagged crossed-ribbon bolts, near-white core and `#5aa0ff` glow, re-rolled every 60 ms, a side fork, a spark on each struck chest, a hand glow, a 0.15 s fade, width falling x0.85 a link; pooled, 16 links on the wire, 4 Librarians a section); nothing is copied from the owner's third-party reference. Sounds: **placeholder hook only** (`LibrarianSfxHook`), no original sound wired. Looks: the Librarian armour pieces (`sm_armour_mp_librarian_*`) are **not** applied (the customizer's armour loading was not investigated for them); he wears the plain Tactical look.

**Musou expansion S3, Stormboy squads and the Big Shoota Nob (2026-11-07, branch `musou/exp-s3` from `musou/expansion` 667e3011; `MusouSim.Version` 14, `TfwRules.Version` 34, `Protocol.Version` stays 63).** Two new states on the wire (Airborne 13, Overheated 14; 11 and 12 left for S2/S4) and six Telegraph cues (32 to 37; 22 to 31 left for S2). Pool side (`MusouSim.Stormboy.cs`, `MusouSim.BigShoota.cs`): the Stormboy's hop (a parabola 5 m high over 1.3 s onto a graph node), orders (walk to a place, fight a target within 15 m, back to the orders past 22 m), the landing shove (Orks within 1.5 m pushed 1.2 m, no damage) and the shot-down fall and crash (`TakeCrashes`; `World.MusouStormboyCrashes` sets off the frag grenade's data blast, 200 r 10, as an Ork blast credited to the shooter, and throws down the fodder that lives); the Big Shoota Nob's posts and his own gun cycle (4 s at 12 rounds/s, 4 damage, then 3.5 s overheated). Battle side (`TfwBattle.Stormboys.cs`, `TfwBattle.BigShootas.cs`): `TfwPatrolRules.Hunters` 0, two squads of 8 from 20 s, re-formed 30 s after a wipe; orders counterattack the latest secured point, hunt (nearest by walk, ties to the least hunted) when it is retaken or half the squad is lost, back to capturing with no human alive, hold the nearest Ork point otherwise; a Big Shoota Nob and a leashed squad of 10 outside each position's ring. Tests: `MusouExpansionS3Tests` (hop and nav landing, shove without damage, crash blast, no crash on the ground, orders and switching, failed counterattack to the nearest by walk, tie and leaving player, wipe and re-form, pack and 3 s cadence, burst and overheat cycle, no Ork damage, posts, wire); the hunter test in `TfwPatrolTests` is replaced. **Musou expansion S5, second pass: the Librarian finished (on `musou/expansion`, 2026-11-08; `MusouSim.Version` 15, no protocol change; Musou Mode only).** The look: every Librarian wears his player's own Tactical look with the install's MP Librarian torso and belt, right pad and psychic-hood backpack put on by package name (`LibrarianLook`, through a new client hook `ExtrasLook` in `LookFor`; *original asset loaded*, seen in game). The class choice: PLAY AS LIBRARIAN in the Stormbird's Esc menu, the DEPLOY button's Setup and the instant class change with its smoke (offered only while the match is Playing: a pick during the countdown was dropped by the server). The gauge: in the weapon box's place and style, the stress as the heat bar (blinking while locked), PULL and WAVE cells with their cooldowns. **Musou expansion S4, the Scrap Meks and their contraptions (2026-11-08, branch `claude/elegant-torvalds-092dba` from `musou/expansion` 859eb68d; `MusouSim.Version` 18, `TfwRules.Version` 36, wire tag 17, `Protocol.Version` stays 63; Musou Mode war battles only).** All numbers in `MusouMekRules`. Pool side (`MusouSim.Mek.cs`): the Mek never attacks; a player or AI Marine within 20 m makes him run (up the flow field where it leads away, else straight away); at work he stands in the new state `Building` (11); `LaunchTurretRocket` fires S2's rocket with his id as shooter and the new turret cue. The store (`MusouMeks.cs`, owned by the battle in `TfwBattle.Meks.cs` and stepped from `World.TfwMeks.cs`, one call in `TfwStep`; no edit to `TfwBattle.cs`): five slots, each Mek at the Ork spawn spot farthest from the players, a dead one's slot refilled 300 s after his death; his hiding place on rings of 12 to 42 m (far from players, near walls, 10 m from other Meks' places), given up when a player comes within 22 m or he cannot get there; builds of 15 s, at most 3 a Mek and 1 shield generator on the map, a flight breaks a build off; his death destroys all his contraptions. The shield generator's 10 m dome stops hit-scan shots, cones and blasts from outside (`DomeEntry`, `Shielded`; one-line hooks in `MusouPlayerShots`, `MusouCone`, `MusouBlast`); the beacon queues a drop of 10 every 30 s, flies it when fewer than 40 of its Boyz live and lands it 3 s later, and its destruction cancels the drop in flight and the queue (the rule written into `docs/musou-expansion.md`); the turret fires every 4 s at the nearest target it sees within 50 m; the trap is sprung by a player, AI Marine or Guardsman within 3 m for 50 % of a player's health and armour (Guardsmen the same flat amount), Orks spared, and a trap destroyed by a player goes off as an Ork blast (r 4, 150) credited to him. Contraptions take players' shots (`TfwMekShot`), blasts, melee and Ork blasts. Client (`client/Extras/Musou/Meks/NetworkView.MusouMeks.cs`): placeholder looks (the Boy's body with a drawn wrench; contraptions from simple shapes; the trap's pulsing red light and spikes; a green dome), the install's sparks, shield pulse and break, drop-pod landing and whistle; the turret's rocket drawn from the turret through S2's `StartRocket`. Capture aid `SM_MUSOU_S4_DEMO=1` (the Meks build 24 to 32 m in front of the first human, take no damage and never run; client `--tfw-fight-meks` faces them in `--tfw-test-fight`). Tests: `MusouExpansionS4Tests` (16: the 5 cap and 300 s respawn, the flight, 3 a Mek and one shield, the 15 s build and its loss, cleanup on death, the beacon's drops, cap, queue and cancel, the turret's period and range, turret rockets hurting Orks and setting off Squigs, the trap's 50 % sparing Orks, the shot trap's blast with credit, the shot ray, the dome outside only, a war shot through and inside the dome, the wire, tag 17 through the client state, skirmish isolation). The Big Shoota Nob now holds the co-op Big Shoota Nob's own gun (`ork_coop_nob_big_shoota`, model `ugeshoota`; its wield entries name no nodes, so Musou's gun loader adds a mount, `MusouOrkGunRules.Mounts`, without touching the Ork class's table) and plays its own muzzle, tracer, impacts and fire sound, with his own blueprint's sounds. ### Musou expansion S6: the battle flow (branch `musou/exp-s6`, 2026-11-08; Musou Mode only, `MusouSim.Version` 18, `TfwRules.Version` 36, no core protocol bump)
The owner's brief of 2026-11-07, stage S6 (design in `docs/musou-expansion.md` "S6 design"). **Far layer:** `TfwArmy` formations with a shared slot layout (`TfwArmyLayout`, server and client), an aggregate part and real members; real within 90 m of any human (each co-op player; AI Marines never), aggregate past 120 m, at most 16 Orks / 1 squad promoted and 32 / 2 folded back a tick; promotions spawn in the impostor's own slot, real members fill slots from the front so a death never moves an impostor. The Ork pool is 2560, but every existing spawner keeps 2048 (`TfwBattleRules.CrowdPool`) and the armies' real Orks (at most 480) count outside the crowds' cap, so the old flow is unchanged; GuardSim has 40 squads (wire ids 448). **Clash:** `TfwClash`, Lanchester with cohesion at 2 Hz; Monte Carlo 1,000 even seeds per size: A won 517, every loser routed before being wiped out, the winner kept 47.1 % at least (mean 54.7 %, mean 83 s; scale-free, so 200/500/1,000 give the same shares). **Waves:** first after a 90-150 s lull, then every 180-300 s; 200/500/1,000-1,200 at 70/25/5 %; muster at the Ork stronghold farthest from every human, committed destination = the Imperial point farthest from every human (one of the two farthest); only its loss redirects. **Guardsmen:** 60 men every 60 s split by need; garrisons capped at 200 with the overflow moving on; lost destinations redirect. **Retreats/rallies:** Orks at ≥ 50 % with no leader within 100 m, Guardsmen past 50 % or when the point falls; a human within 15 m rallies once a minute, 30 s no-retreat, start reset. **Six Defenders** (`MarineRole.Defender`, `DefenderRules`): puppet ids 65516-65527 (the core's reserved range too), min(6, 12 − 4 − 2 x lords), autonomous posts by pressure, never capture, back 30 s after death. **Wire/client:** tag 18 (19-byte records, 2 Hz); impostors through the crowds' vertex-animation tiers (900 Orks, 400 Guardsmen), aggregate losses as bodies; `WaaaghBarkPlanner` (3 voices, 4-8 s, nearest first, no voice twice in a row) on a new 300 m Waaagh sound group. Tests `TfwClashTests`, `TfwArmyTests`, `TfwArmyClientTests`; aids `SM_TFW_ARMY_TEST=clash:<n>|rally`, `--tfw-fight-look-armies`, `SM_ARMY_PROFILE=1` (`ArmyProfileTests`). **Measured** (this PC, other sessions on the CPU; real map, one headless or windowed client, `SM_TICK_STATS=5`): 200 v 200: the whole tick mean 14-24 ms, p50 5.4-6.9 ms, p99 57-140 ms, max 155 ms, at the run's base load (850-1,200 Orks; the spikes there before the wave arrived too); 500 v 500: mean 4.3-6.2 ms, p99 6-8 ms, one max of 132 ms as the wave promoted; 1,000 v 1,000: mean 4.3-8.7 ms, p99 6-79 ms, one max of 154 ms at the promotion; the synthetic arena (`ArmyProfileTests`, Release): mean 0.2-0.7 ms, worst promotion tick 3.9 ms, never more than 13 deaths a tick (the caps spread them). Send rate 60-78 KB/s a client with 280 real Guardsmen and 1,000-1,500 Orks, over the 55 KB/s budget (not separated from the existing Musou load). **Found:** near a player the real Guardsmen (4.5 x, night batch) crush a wave of their size (200 v 200 kept all 200; 1,000 v 1,000 kept 961), while far the clash is even: the near/far balance differs (owner's call). A near army's aggregate remainder waits for promotion and does not fight (the 1,000 v 1,000 garrison kept 720 aggregate men idle beside the real fight). Captures (owner's cache, `previews/musou-s6`): a 500 v 500 clash and a rally. Implemented, not playtested.

### Musou performance pass and expansion S7 (branch `musou/perf-pass`, 2026-11-08; Musou Mode, plus a default-off FSR 2 setting; `TfwRules.Version` 38, no protocol or wire change)
The owner's performance brief of 2026-11-08 (first explosion, distant decisions, invisible rendering, FSR 2), stage S7 (profiles at 200 / 500 / 1,000, captures, Classic regression) and his answers to S6's balance questions. Report with every number: `docs/musou-perf-pass.md`. **Measuring:** `tools/musou-perf.ps1` (one 127.0.0.1 server, one windowed client, same scene each time: `SM_TFW_ARMY_TEST=clash:N` on Ashfall, or the 200-death burst), server `SM_TICK_STATS` now with `TICKSECTIONS` / `TICKBYTES` / `TICKSPIKE` (`SmSim.SimProfile`), Musou and Tfw phases in `--frame-profile`, `--perf-ab` (one change on/off every 5 s in one battle) and `--perf-ab-shots`. **Found and fixed:** a thrown body's tumble quaternion drifted off unit length and Godot's product threw out of the whole Musou frame, 421 to 767 times a run, the 1 to 2.3 s hitches of every Musou battle (`CrowdView.StepFlung`); worst frame after warm-up 1,096-2,334 ms -> 443-459 ms, p99.9 142-226 -> 20-23 ms; the burst's worst frame 1,560 -> 27 ms; the 72 ms cold first burst no longer occurs (cold 26.6 vs warm 23.5 ms). The server's 138 ms tick after each landing was the walk graph's edge distances computed lazily by the first Scrap Mek (now on a worker at load); route searches run side by side. Guardsmen looks made in the Stormbird (the landing still has one 420-460 ms client frame: it is in the HUD, stations and markers' first battle frame, `tfw: orders, stations, hud, markers`, not yet split). **Rendering:** the crowd's far tier batched per 32 m cell with boxes (500 v 500 A/B: GPU 5.24 -> 4.58 ms, primitives 45.9 -> 29.0 M); Ashfall's grime overlay measured (+0.5 ms GPU, +190 draws) and left as it is; off-screen effect culling tried, no gain, left off (`--fx-cull`). **FSR 2:** Options > Graphics > Upscaling (off by default; Native AA, Quality 0.67, Balanced 0.59, Performance 0.5), Forward+ only, FSR 2 replaces MSAA/SMAA/TAA while on, HUD native; Quality vs MSAA+SMAA: GPU -17 %, render CPU +0.17 ms. **Far layer:** its sections cost 0.00-0.01 ms a tick at every size (the tick's 4-6 ms are the Ork AI and the core step); the 72-80 KB/s per client is Musou's 58 KB/s budget plus a 13 KB/s core snapshot of 16 players (owner's call). **The owner's decisions (2026-11-08):** near matches far (army Guard squads made real at 0.135 of the field's strength: 200 v 200 near 4 of 8 held, was 8 of 8), fight off-screen (a near army's remainder clashes in the far layer), base is a target (first wave on the test arena at the base at 226 s), far and unseen deaths leave no body. Tests `NearFarBalanceTests` (gated `SM_ARMY_BALANCE=1`, base-target fact always), `TfwArmyTests` updated. Measured on a quiet PC with a Debug client; nothing played by a human.

**Follow-up the same day (the owner's answers):** the near Guard share scales with the army's size (0.135 / 0.072 / 0.087 at 200 / 500 / 1,000; trials held 4 / 5 / 4 of 8); a Musou client's core messages count inside its send budget (59-62 KB/s a client, was 72-80); Options > Graphics > Ashfall grime EXACT (default) or FAST (folded into derived kit materials: GPU 4.12 -> 3.78 ms, draw calls -26 %); the FSR tooltip names the cut-out edges' next-map update; the landing hitch is the next item (ship now, fix after).
