Armour bar fix (branch `ui/armour-bar-fix`; client only, no protocol change; owner 2026-10-31: "the new yellow armor status bar was just laid over the old one"): the old layer was the movie's gold `lightdamagebar_mc` frame, which `Hud.Vitals.cs` drew under the yellow armour bar for everyone without Iron Halo (a second, full-length gold armour bar showing beyond the cut yellow one); it is no longer drawn: one armour bar layer in every state. The blue and white bar with the star on the left is the Iron Halo perk's alone (`Frame.IronHalo`, by perk, any class that takes it); without the perk the bar is yellow in every state, and the clip's frame 99 (the starburst alone, shown at no armour or when dead) is skipped, so the star only appears with Iron Halo. The damage vignette already followed the rule (armour damage yellow unless Iron Halo). Aid `--hud-vitals-demo <png prefix>` (steps six health/armour states in a match, saves a window shot each, quits); ui-selftest `ArmourBarChecks` (`Hud.VitalsArmourLayers`: one layer for plain and Halo at full and half armour, none for plain at no armour). Crops under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\screens\armourbar\` (`bars_tactical`, `bars_assault`, `bars_devastator`, `bars_devastator_halo`: full, half, no armour, half and half). Health fill white at partial health (found in the crops, fixed): from frame 50 on the movie's `healthbar_mc` swaps its bar for an additive white flash version (`c558`) and the flash clip `health_flash_mc` (`c559`), and keeps a white end cap (`c557`); drawn still they made the fill white (magenta under the Halo's tint). `GfxRaster.Swap` (new, like `Hidden`) draws `c558` as the normal `c550` and `c559` as the diamond `c553`, and the cap is left out: the fill is red at every health level, with or without Iron Halo (the own-damage vignette replaced the movie's flash). ui-selftest checks health 100, 50 and 20 % for plain and Halo (`Hud.VitalsHealthWhiteShare`; it fails without the fix). Health crops: `health_{devastator,halo,assault,tactical}.png` (full, half, low, half with half armour, broken armour).
Launcher check-box row (branch `ui/launcher-checkbox-row`; owner 2026-10-31: "weird things are happening over and around the area where the OLD gpu checkbox is"; launcher only, protocol unchanged): reproduced on current main (not only on the old build of the owner's screenshot, whose installed launcher predated the layout pass, 7cd91e2 < 11f060a; the build tag 0aafd85 on that screenshot is the tester build, which already had the pass), with a new repaint test: the real window shown off-screen is taken through the state changes and captured with PrintWindow (what the compositor really shows), and compared with a full fresh repaint. Cause: `CheckBox`/`RadioButton` (ButtonBase) are `Opaque` controls that never get a background erase, and the owner-drawn version painted its background only from `OnPaintBackground`, which an opaque control is not asked for; so the box's row showed a black strip behind the text and kept stale pieces of the buttons above it (the LAN button's second-line text from an earlier narrower layout), at every start and after every change. Fix: `DarkGlyph.Paint` fills the whole client rectangle (the tile) first, every time; check and radio boxes also invalidate on focus, enabled, visible and bounds changes. New `--row-check <folder>` (and as part of `--layout-check`, at 100, 150 and 200 %): 22 frames (idle, checking, offered, downloading, error, set-up and back, box ticked and focused, button hover, resizes, minimise while a state changes, restore), each live frame against the fresh repaint (text box frames and the progress gradient excluded), plus the overlap check; the safe-mode row is saved cropped as `row-*.png`. Screens: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\screens\launcher-row\` (`before\`, `layout\`).
Red break glow and blood splash (branch `fx/red-glow-blood`; owner 2026-10-31 with two original screenshots of an enemy marine engulfed in a red-magenta glow the moment his armour is gone; client only, protocol 49 unchanged): the break glow replaces the subtle round-2 red halo with a strong red glow (the halo card re-profiled to a soft bloom centred on the torso, 2.1 x larger, a hot white-pink flash on the armour in the first moments, the armour's own colours still read, 0.9 s); `ArmourFlashTracker` re-flashes it for 0.2 s on each damage tick with no armour (own: health drops with the shield at nothing, `OwnShield(..., health)`; others: a seen hit on an already-broken body); `BloodSplash` (new) sprays deep red additive droplets (streaks of varied length, blobs, a mist puff, gravity) from the hit point of a hit with no armour (armour-up hits keep #57's sparks; the own-screen vignette is untouched). The data's blood effects are dark alpha-blended, so the splash is procedural; the flesh effect still plays. Estimates tagged ours in the refine register. `--old-break-glow` restores the old halo; `--bolt-fx-demo --bolt-fx-armour seq` shows break then re-flash and blood. Sheets in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\screens
edglow\`. Re-flash captured on a stationary player (`--bolt-fx-demo --bolt-fx-armour seq --time-scale 0.4` with an idle headless client). Not verified: melee hits, the own view in a live match.

**Musou MU0 (2026-10-31): the switch.** A new experimental added-content profile `--content musou` (flag 8, not in `extended`; the owner's request: a Musou-style mode toggled like Faithful and Extended that leaves every existing mode unchanged). Six new Extras hooks (step, melee, blast, match flow, join side, server created), dispatchers for the existing four, envelope tags 3–5 (`MusouWire`), the enemy pool contract (`MusouSim`), the CONTENT row's third button and a Host panel locked to this PC, Annihilation and no bots (START MUSOU). `MusouIsolationTests` pins the faithful and extended config hashes and a 900-tick replay captured before the hooks. No enemies yet: MU1 (sim and director), MU2 (network and crowd), MU3 (combat, Warboss, HUD) follow. docs/added-content.md section 8.

**Musou MU2 (2026-10-31): network and crowd.** The server sends each client the enemies by interest (near every tick, mid every 2nd, far every 5th; Warboss and Nobs first) within 55 KB/s, events (deaths, hits, strikes, tracers, telegraphs) in 3 copies at most 35 % of the budget, and the director; the client interpolates and draws the nearest 150 enemies: about 40 skinned near, the rest vertex-animation textures baked in memory at load (160–220 fps with 150 on the lead's PC). Test aid `SM_MUSOU_DUMMIES=N`. Not yet: ragdolls, a crowd for spectators, a Low setting in the menu. Reviewed twice; spec rows "Musou enemy interest" to "Musou looks".

**Musou MU1 (2026-10-31): enemies and waves.** Lightweight server enemies (Boy, Shoota Boy, 'Ard Boy, Gretchin, Nob, Chaos Marine, Warboss) follow one shared flow field to the players, take attack tokens, wind up and strike or shoot; five waves (80 to 300, at most 250 alive solo, 400 in all) with breaks that refill, a shared lives pool, the Warboss after wave 5. The owner's rules: every player starts and respawns in the Space Marine spawn room with the bolt pistol only; the Warboss starts in the Chaos spawn room. Manufactorum: 300 enemies converge with none stuck, under 2.3 ms p99 a tick (Release). A stranded-enemy failsafe keeps a wave from never ending. Open: the Chaos spawn room's blockers seal it for the enemies (the Warboss starts outside it). Spec rows "Musou enemy types" to "Musou score".

**Musou MU3a (2026-10-31): combat and the Warboss.** Players' shots, cones, projectiles, blasts and charges hit the horde (tracers end on the enemy hit, perk variants count); the Musou-only cleave hits up to 8 enemies a swing, heavy steps stagger and knock back; the Warboss slams, charges, calls three Waaagh!s and enrages, each telegraphed for the client. PvP results are unchanged (the MU0 pins). Spec rows "Musou player hits on enemies" to "Musou Warboss abilities". Next: the HUD and effects (MU3b), the Chaos room opened for enemies, the golden weapon drops.

**Musou: the Chaos spawn room opened for enemies (2026-10-31).** The Musou enemies' graph is built without the spawn-room blockers (cached apart from the bots' graphs), so the Warboss starts inside the Chaos spawn room as the owner asked and walks out (337.5 m, about 71 s on Manufactorum); enemies may also enter the Space Marine room. Spec row "Musou enemies and the spawn rooms".

**Musou MU3b (2026-10-31): HUD and effects.** The Musou HUD (wave, enemies left, lives, KOs and points, the KO chain, the break countdown, the Warboss bar, WAAAGH! and ENRAGED call-outs, the end panel), hit markers and blood on enemies, ground telegraphs for melee wind-ups and the Warboss's slam and charge, Ork voices (at most 6). Client only; headless and lean bots draw nothing; it hides itself when the feed stops. Test aid `--musou-hud-demo`. Not verified live: hit markers on real enemy hits (bots do not target Musou enemies). Spec rows "Musou HUD" to "Musou telegraphs".
**Musou weapon drops (2026-10-31).** The owner's golden drops: a Nob's KO drops one weapon per living player, rolled from that player's class (each sees only their own); E equips it with full ammo; it glows gold (the weapon's own model, a light beam, a floor glow) and lasts 60 s or until its player dies. Envelope tag 6, sent only to the drop's player. The join gap of the pistol-only start is closed. Test aid `SM_MUSOU_DROP_TEST=1`. Spec rows "Musou weapon drops" and "Musou drop look".

**Musou: Chaos Marines drop weapons too (2026-10-31).** The owner: "Make Chaos Marines drop weapons too." A Chaos Marine's KO now drops a golden weapon like a Nob's (waves 4 and 5); `MusouSim.Version` 4.

**No window, no focus for test runs (tools/no-focus-steal, 2026-10-31).** The owner: test Godot windows "appear for a moment, take focus, then disappear". Measured with the new `tools\window-watch.ps1` (EnumWindows and GetForegroundWindow every 10 ms, each window's process tree): headless starts (bots.cmd, `& _console.exe --headless`, the Host panel's ProcessStartInfo, Launcher.ps1's hidden Start-Process, release.cmd's smoke processes) showed no window and moved no focus; the culprit was every windowed test client started directly (`--position -4000,-4000 -- --test-window`): Godot clamps the position into a screen, so the window was created at the primary screen's top-left and activated (SW_SHOW + SetForegroundWindow, during setup, before any game code), and --test-window's NoFocus then hid it about 1 s later. Five such windows from other agents' runs were caught during one 4-minute watch. Fix: `godot.cmd` (`tools\godot.ps1` on `tools\quiet-launch.ps1`) is the one way tests and agents start Godot: headless by default with CREATE_NO_WINDOW for the console wrapper (its child inherits the window-less console, output into a log file), and `--windowed` on a private desktop (CreateDesktop `WinSta0\sm-reimpl-test`), where Vulkan renders and screenshots and recordings work but nothing is on the owner's screen, takes the foreground or gets his input. bots.cmd, client.cmd with `--bot` / `--test-window`, movie.cmd with `--test-window`, release.cmd's smoke tests and playtest bots (and the launcher's window test, which also took the foreground now and then) and the packaged `Launcher.ps1 -StartBots` use it or CREATE_NO_WINDOW; the Host panel already did. A client started with --test-window any other way now also moves itself off-screen (no clamp after creation) and says to use godot.cmd. The owner's "desktop 2" (a Windows virtual desktop) was not used: IVirtualDesktopManager.MoveWindowToDesktop only moves a window after it exists (the flash and the focus change happen at creation), and making a second virtual desktop needs the undocumented, build-specific internal interface and shows up in the owner's Task View.
**Scoreboard ping (protocol 50, 2026-10-31).** The owner: "add ping (ms) value in the scoreboard for each player". The server times every snapshot it sends to a peer and takes a round-trip sample when an input batch first acknowledges it (`GameServer.NoteSnapshotAck`); `RttEstimator` smooths the samples (first as it is, then 1/8 of each difference; 0..999 ms). Each scoreboard row carries it as a u16 before the name (65535 not measured; 16-byte rows, the fullest scoreboard 1145 bytes; snapshots unchanged, worst case 1194); the Tab and end-of-match scoreboard has a right-aligned PING column (green below 80 ms, yellow below 150, red from 150, a dash when not known; ours), and the panel is sized from the resolved font's measured character width (no wrap with Consolas, Cascadia Mono or Courier New; the font shrinks on narrow windows; test aid `--scoreboard-font`). Send times sit in a 64-tick ring per peer, one sample per acknowledged snapshot. The scoreboard already goes out once a second, so the ping refreshes with it. Tests `ScoreboardPingTests` (estimator, wire, size, loopback links of 0, 40 and 100 ms each way, loss and jitter, spectators). Spec rows "Scoreboard ping: measurement", "smoothing", "wire and display".

Launcher row, third pass (branch `launcher/row-fix`; owner 2026-10-31, screenshot of the a873bcc launcher: the "Old GPU" check box drawn over pieces of the version lines and a ghost "Host ..." button text; launcher only, protocol unchanged). The screenshot came from the released launcher 2026.1031.207 (a873bcc), which predates #58: reproduced exactly with that code at 100 % and 125 % in the owner's state (735 px window, a873bcc tag, a previous build, the mouse over "Host a match on this PC"); main with #58 no longer shows it, so the owner needs a release built from a newer main. Three further defects found on main and fixed: (1) the window's pixel sizes never followed the display scale (setting `AutoScaleMode` on a form whose layout was not suspended scaled it while still empty, so at 125 % and above only the fonts grew; the old `--ui-scale` simulation scaled by hand and hid it), now the form is built with its layout suspended and scaled once by Windows Forms, and the simulation goes the same way (`AutoScaleDimensions` 96 / f); `--ui-scale` is now the absolute display scale on any PC; (2) the notes box overlapped the button row in a small window at 150 % and above (the scroll heights were constants), now `KeepRowsApart` sets the scroll height from what the rows need, after each layout; (3) wrapped labels could end up 0 px tall (a maximum width set during a parent's layout), now labels and check boxes wrap natively in their table cell (`Wrap`). The check box wraps its text by its own measure (`DarkGlyph.Preferred`). `--layout-check` adds 175 %, the owner's 735 px state, the error and set-up states in the smallest window, 1366x768 at 125 % and 1920x1080 at 175 %, a text-fit check and a scale check (75 states); `--row-check` takes `--ui-width` (the owner's state). New `LauncherLayoutTests` in the Windows-only `tests/SmLauncher.UiTests` (trait `Category=Window`; SmLauncher.Tests stays plain net10.0) run both, waiting for each window to settle: each fails on the old code (the a873bcc check box paint, the unscaled sizes, the fixed scroll heights).
Follow-up (same branch, lead's review): the window tests moved to the Windows-only `tests/SmLauncher.UiTests` (SmLauncher.Tests is plain net10.0 again). They failed under load in `faithful-build.cmd` (3 of 3 runs): every failure was "did not settle within 3000 ms", never an overlap or cut text; with all test assemblies running at once a layout burst took up to 2.1 s (115 settles logged, most about 100 ms). The settle wait is now three equal passes within 10 s and names what kept changing when it times out. The check windows, `--screenshot` and the UiTests now run on the private desktop `WinSta0\sm-reimpl-test` (`PrivateDesktop`; fallback: off-screen on the current desktop): tools\window-watch.ps1 saw 0 windows and 0 foreground changes during `--layout-check`, `--screenshot` and the test runs. The window re-clamps to the work area after a DPI change or a move to another monitor.

**No firing while sprinting (protocol 51, 2026-11-01).** Branch `sim/no-fire-while-sprinting`. The owner, with a recording of a Devastator sprinting and firing the lascannon: "you should not be able to shoot while sprinting." Cause: M27's hip-fire rule let a held trigger take the Sprint bit away and fire in the same tick (`Combat.StepPlayerCore`, `shooting`), following the behaviour graphs' sprint-to-fire transitions; rifles and pistols showed their 6 / 5 tick raise first, but the always-ready weapons (lascannon, which fires on the press since sim/instant-fire, heavy bolter, plasma cannon, melta, grenade launcher) shot on the press tick at sprint speed. Now, while the sprint is applied on the ground (Sprint, stick forward; not aim mode, a jump-pack phase, an evade, a reaction, the charge, a brace or a melee lock) the trigger does nothing for every weapon (`sprintNoFire`): no shot, charge or raise; the sprint cancels a held charge, a pending charged shot, a raise and its shot and a burst's later rounds, so a release mid-sprint fires nothing; the held trigger no longer ends the sprint; `Combat.SprintApplies` (the vent's rule) drops its trigger terms. After the sprint the exit timing is unchanged (rifle 6 ticks, pistol 5, always-ready at once); a semi-automatic or charge weapon held through needs a new press, full-auto fires on (`FireHeld` stays the real button). Reload, detonation, throws and the braced heavy bolter are not blocked (ours; detonation is an owner question). The client needed no change: own muzzle FX and sounds follow the prediction's fired events and clip / cooldown / heat changes. No wire change; snapshots unchanged (worst case 1194). Tests: `NoFireWhileSprintingTests` (every weapon kind, the lascannon press, charges released mid-sprint, held auto-fire, bursts, raises, the exit timing, server and prediction agreement); `HipFireTests`, `OwnerRulesTests`, `ChargeTests` and `CombatAcceptanceTests` scripts updated. To restore M27's behaviour, revert `sprintNoFire` in `Combat.StepPlayerCore` and `SprintApplies`.

**Only the hop cancels the stomp (protocol 51, 2026-11-01).** Same branch and protocol as the sprint rule above. The owner: "make it so that devastator/havoc stomp can only be cancelled by a hop move. shooting, aim down sight, or any other action should never interrupt a stomp animation." Of the actions, only a shot (from the stomp's `RangedAt`, or the pistol's quick shot) could end it, and a melee press in a combo window could chain out of it; `Combat.StepPlayerCore` now skips both for a `MeleeStep.InPlace` step (the heavy classes' stomp); aim mode, switches, Reload / the brace, grenades, the sprint and the charge were already held off by every melee attack. The hop from the stomp's `BRANCH_Evade` still cancels it (the branch gate kept; whether the owner wants it from the start is open). Presses are left unused, so the 0.3 s input buffer may replay one after the stomp. No client change (the aim pose and camera follow the predicted `Aiming`). Evade.cs untouched. Tests: `StompUninterruptibleTests` (each action mid-stomp, the hop, normal play after; they fail with the two guards removed).
Stomp to move (branch `anim/stomp-to-move`; owner 2026-11-01: "if devastator stomps and then sprints immediately after, or walking after a stomp ... the legs are doing sprint/walking things, and the upper body/arms are still doing stomp animation"; client only, no simulation, wire or config-hash change). Cause: `NetworkView.HandoffUpperWeight` fades a strike off the upper body after the legs are handed over (M40-T4) over its graph's move-on exit, but a graph without one (`MP_SM_MEL_TB_Displace`, the heavy classes' kick and stomp; the knife's) fell back to the clip's tail: the stomp stayed whole on the upper body from the move gate (0.933 s) to 1.517 s while the legs sprinted at 9 m/s. Now such a strike leaves over the base graph's navigation conduit 'Standard Blend' 0.333 s (`NavConduitBlend`, the blend its whole-body exit already takes): under half of it 0.15 s after the hand-over, none after 0.27 s. The sim's move gate is unchanged. Devastator and Havoc checked (sprint and run); the knife and the kick take the same path (not captured); the Ork's actions have their own hand-over (unchanged). Aids: `--old-handoff-exit` (before), `--bot --stomp-move-test walk|sprint [--stomp-move-pitch rad]` (stomp, then move on at the gate, the human camera, a log line per frame with the frame number and the stomp's upper-body weight). Spec "Strike hand-over without a graph exit".

**Shell casings fall faster (2026-11-01).** The owner found spent bolt casings far too floaty: the casing mesh alone now falls with its particle's data gravity × 2.5 (`FxPlayer.CasingGravityScale`, ours); smoke and sparks of the same spray and every other effect keep the data's gravity. Casings have no floor clamp (they sink through the floor before they vanish), unchanged.

**Storm bolter ammunition (protocol 51 batch, 2026-11-01).** Branch `sim/stormbolter-ammo`, on top of `sim/no-fire-while-sprinting` (no protocol bump: the batch is unreleased). The owner: "the storm bolter for tactical is currently not using a bullet every shot - resulting in firing for twice as long on full automatic before requiring a reload." Cause: `WeaponTuning.Read` took a shot's cost from the delivery's `ammo_used` alone (1); the storm bolters (`sm_`, `csm_mp_ranged_storm_bolter`) spend a second round through their `fire_sim` (`delayed_action` 0.05 s ? `consume_ammo` 1, the second barrel, which the fire effects flash at `fx_muzzle01`). Now `WeaponTuning.ShotAmmo` / `FireSimAmmo` add every `consume_ammo` of the `fire_sim` (same ammunition only) to `WeaponSpec.AmmoPerShot`: the storm bolter spends 2 rounds a 0.1 s shot, its clip of 100 lasts 50 shots and 5 s on full auto (was 10 s), then the reload; the reserve of 500 is 250 shots. A probe of every `_mp_` wargear found no other firearm with a `fire_sim` `consume_ammo` (bolters, heavy bolter, plasma, melta, lascannon, launcher, pistols and the Chaos twins spend 1; charge stages unchanged). Ours: both rounds go at the shot (the data's 0.05 s delay is not kept; the HUD drops 2 per shot). Server and prediction share `Combat.StepPlayer` and the config (the rounds per shot are in its hash); `OwnerBalance.Measure` (`smtool weapon-dps`) counts shots per clip by the rounds per shot; the server's startup list prints "(2 rounds per shot)". Tests: `StormBolterAmmoTests` (50 shots, 5 s, reload; the bolter control; an odd clip; the hash; an install pin), `ShotAmmoTests` (the reader).
**Controller B backs out of menus (2026-11-01).** The owner: "make the b button exit the active menu that is open - on controller". Godot's `ui_cancel` already held B in most screens; the gaps were closed and the rule made explicit: `PadHost.IsBack` (Esc through `ui_cancel`, or the pad's B itself) now drives the loadout screen and the Esc menu's BACK/RESUME, the appearance editor (the armour part first, then the editor), the emblem importer, every `UiKit.Dialog` (a confirm picks its cancel button, a text prompt cancels) and the CONTROLS screen; B on the connection screen goes back to the front end like Esc, and B backs out of "Loading your loadouts..." like Esc. While a rebinding waits, B is bound on the controller tab (it asks Swap/Replace/Cancel about Use) and cancels the capture on the keyboard tab, as Esc does. In a match B stays Use, but the B that closes a menu is no Use: `NetworkView.PadMenuClosed` blocks the Use of a B pressed under a menu or in the frame the menu closed, until B is let go (the hold would otherwise send Interact the next tick). Client only; no protocol or config-hash change. Tests: `UiSelfTest.PadBack.cs` (synthetic `InputEventJoypadButton` on the screens above) and `--pad-test` (Start, B: the menu closes with no Use sample; a B tap without a menu is one Use). Spec row "Menu back" under Controller (gamepad). Not covered by a test: the armour editor's inner step back, the connection screen's B.

**No firing during the roll; no upper limit on aiming up (protocol 51, 2026-11-01).** Branch `sim/roll-fire-pitch`; rides in the unreleased protocol 51 (no wire change). (A) The owner: "you can currently shoot any gun while rolling as tactical marine. ensure you can never shoot while the roll animation is playing." Cause: the roll's `BRANCH_ToRanged` (0.667 s of the 1.167 s clip; `EvadeMove.RangedAt`) let a held trigger end the roll and fire in that tick (`Combat.StepPlayerCore` passed Fire to `Evade.Begin` as ranged input); before the branch the weapon already did nothing. Now, for the Tactical classes' roll (`Combat.IsRoll`: not the dash, no hopping move), Fire is no longer ranged input, the trigger is blocked for the whole roll (`rollNoFire`, as `sprintNoFire`: no shot, charge or raise) and in the tick the stick, Aim or a grenade cuts the roll short (`rollCut`, as the charge's `fireDropped`); a charge held into the roll is cancelled (M21); after it a full-auto trigger fires on, a semi-automatic, charge or press-fired weapon needs a new press (`FireHeld` kept real). The heavies' hop and the jump-pack dash are unchanged (hop: Fire ends it at 0.4525 s with a shot; dash: nothing in flight, Fire ends the landing part at 0.378 s). Evade.cs untouched. No client change for the FX (they follow the prediction's fired events); the hip-fire info text names the roll. (B) The owner: "all classes should be able to zoom directly upwards into the sky. there should be no upper bound to the Y axis angle they can shoot at." Clamps found: `PlayerInput.Sanitized` ±1.4 rad; the client's `MaxPitch` 1.4 (mouse, pad, bots, fresh-aim ray); the camera sets' upper limits (exploration 70°, rifle aim 85°, heavy 55°) in `RigCamera`; a projectile's `extra_aim_angle` could lift a shot past vertical. Now the simulation keeps up to π/2 (`PlayerInput.MaxPitch`; down still −1.4, `MinPitch`), the client's view goes to 89.9° (`MaxPitchUp`: Godot's look-at with world up and `FreshAim.Turn`'s yaw read-back need a horizontal part) in hip fire and aim mode alike, the camera keeps the rig's place for the sets' old limit above it (`lookupPitch`) and only turns, the lower limits are unchanged, bots aim up to 89.9°, and the projectile lift is capped at straight up. The upper-body aim poses keep their clips' range (±70°, brace ±80°); spectator cameras unchanged. Tests: `RollFirePitchTests` (every weapon kind in the roll, the charge cancel, held triggers at the roll's end, the stick and aim cut tick, the hop unchanged, the pitch's sanitize and wire, shots at 89 / 89.9 / 90° in hip fire and aim mode, prediction agreement rolling and firing at 90°); `EvadeTests` and `LockScaleSprintStopTests` updated. To restore the old behaviour: pass `fireDown` to `Evade.Begin` and drop `rollNoFire`; set `MaxPitch` back to 1.4 and `_pitchMax` to the sets' blend. Review follow-up (same branch): `FreshAim.Turn` has separate down and up limits (the fresh-aim ray: −1.4 rad down, 89.9° up); new tests for the melta's cone and a projectile with `extra_aim_angle` at 89–90°, and for the tick where the stick cuts the roll with Sprint and Fire held (nothing fires until Shift is let go). Merged with `sim/movement-fixes` (the `Evade.Begin` call keeps both the roll's ranged input and the new `world` argument).

Scope tint to the screen edges (branch `hud/scope-overlay-fill`; owner 2026-11-01: "stalker overlay doesn't reach the edge of the screen"; client and content reader only, no protocol change): on a window wider than the movie's 16:9 stage the strips beside the scope picture were a black bar at the mask's alpha, lighter than the mask's own (not black) tint, so a visibly untinted band showed at left and right (`ScopeView._Draw` side fill; `ScopeArt.Render` left that area transparent). `ScopeArt.Render` now carries the mask's edge column out to the screen's edges (so the picture is full width at the render size), and the stale-picture side bars (a window just resized) use the mask's sampled colour and alpha (`ScopePicture.EdgeR/G/B`). The lascannon scope shares the code. Checked by screenshot at 1920x1080, 1680x1050, 2000x1070, 2560x1080 and 1024x768 (`--bot --aim-test --bot-stand --primary "Stalker Bolter"`, `godot.cmd --windowed --resolution WxH`). No UI self-test check: the overlay needs the install's movie, which the self-test does not render.
Movement fixes (branch `sim/movement-fixes`; the owner's report of 2026-11-01; protocol 51, no wire change, shared with the batch's other unreleased rules). (A) The Devastator / Havoc hop flew its height curve level from the take-off height with no gravity, so off a ledge or down stairs it stayed up (a walk-off before the curve even rose again), and with W held the stick's branch ended it in mid-air, after which the walk-off rule dropped it straight with no forward speed (`Evade.Step`, `Evade.Begin`). Now over a drop (feet more than 0.05 m above the ground plus the curve) gravity pulls it down on top of the curve (`Evade.HopFall`), and input does not end a hop falling below its curve (`Evade.FallingBelowCurve`): it keeps its forward travel to the ground; up stairs, slopes and flat ground are unchanged; a clip that ends in the air falls on as a walk-off. The client shows the fall pose for a roll or hop falling off a drop after 0.3 s in the air (`EvadeFallingInAir`, the charge's delay). (B) No time delay exists: `smash_available_delay` is 0 and the press acts on its own tick; the only gate is the data's 8 m height split between the pound and the slash (`MP_SM_NAV_JP_Sim`: `FLT_Distance_Above_Ground in [8, 1000]`), the same for every melee weapon; the data gives the hammer / maul its own `Hammer Dash State` below 8 m (not simulated: the sword's slash plays). Kept as the data; whether the hammer should always pound is an owner decision. Air-Cooled Thrusters' 2 s `smash_available_delay` is a second, perk-only delay. (C) A Space tap while falling (off a ledge, at a jump's apex or in its fall) is now the dash on its release: the press waits in the input buffer, is not replayed while Space is down (`InputBuffer.AirTapPending`), and its replay after the release starts the dash (`JumpPack.Begin`'s air tap, `Evade.CanDashInAir`; `Evade.Begin` lets a dash start in the air with the stick then); a hold stays the long press (the small jump on landing). Spacing and no-cost unchanged; no per-airtime limit (none in the data: the base graph's jump-pack evade has no `BOOL_IsSupported` test). The client ends the jump's view and sound without a landing when a dash takes over in the air. (D, the lead's addition with the owner's two requests of 2026-11-01) A charge held in the air off a ledge (`Rush.Held`) now turns with A / D at up to 60 degrees per second (ours; `Rush.AirSteer` in `Rush.Begin`'s held branch), velocity and heading together at the held speed, for the Assault, Raptor, Tactical and Chaos Tactical; the heavy classes have no charge, the Ork's sprint attack is unchanged, the ground charge too. Tests `MovementFixesTests` (the steered charge's turn, speed and drift, a target reached on the bent path only, the Tactical and the Ork; hop off three ledges and down stairs losing height while going forward, up stairs and a ramp unchanged, the clip's end in the air, the pound or slash on its own tick at every point of a full jump, the air tap off a ledge, at the apex and in the fall, a hold, the spacing, prediction against the server for both); the protocol pins move to 51. Spec "Movement fixes"; docs/changes-from-original.md.
Review follow-up (same branch `sim/movement-fixes`): a fresh Space press while an earlier air tap still waits in the buffer replaces it (`InputBuffer.Begin`), so it no longer dashes on the press with Space down; a melee or heavy press refuses the dash in both of its air entries (`Evade.Begin`); a hop counts as falling below its curve only over a real drop (`Evade.FallingBelowCurve` probes the ground; `Evade.Begin` gets the level from `Combat`), so a low ceiling cannot lock its input. New tests: two taps in the spacing, the melee press with a tap, a chain of air dashes (each over 5 m lower), the low ceiling, and server-against-prediction runs for taps after a ledge walk-off and for the steered ledge charge (Assault and Tactical).

**True Grit bolter idle (2026-11-01; branch `anim/relic-bolter-idle`; client animation, plus the simulation's raise delay: config hash, no protocol or wire change).** The owner: "the relic bolter - equippable with true grit perk, has a broken idle animation. the gun and arm need to point straight down at the ground at idle ... i believe its the same idle animation as bolt pistol." Cause: the client picked a weapon's animation family by name (`HipFireAnimations.FamilyOf`: only `bolt_pistol` and `plasma_pistol` are pistols), so the pistol-slot bolters (`*_pistol_bolter`, `*_pistol_bolter_gold`) took the rifle's relaxed idle `SM_NAV_IdleL_S_01` and ready posture: the one-handed gun held forward and level, the melee hand raised to a foregrip, on every view. Their wargear files say `weapon_type = "weapon_1hand"` and `animation_set = "pistol"`, as the bolt pistol's do, so `NetworkView.AnimationFamilyOf` now gives them the pistol family (idle `SM_NAV_IdleL_CS_01`, relaxed and ready runs, raise, recoil, one-handed sprint stop, turns, the pistol tracer's raise) and the bolt pistol's reload clip and flinch set (interpretation). Aim mode was already the pistol's; the switch clips go by slot. The simulation reads the same data: `MpClasses.AnimationSetOf` reads `common_data/fire_mode_primary/entry/animation_set`, and a weapon naming "pistol" (only the bolt pistols and these bolters) takes the pistol family's raise in `MpClasses.WithRaise`: 0.167 s = 5 ticks from the press to the shot instead of the rifle's 6 (config hash, no protocol change; test `OwnerRulesTests.The_true_grit_bolter_raises_in_the_pistols_five_ticks`; the server's log now prints 5 ticks for all four). The bolt pistol and the primary bolter are untouched (names not matched). Checked on Space Marine Assault with the Relic Bolter in a spectator's view of a bot and the own view (idle, walk, aim, the raise and shot, the melee strike and its hand-over); the Chaos twin takes the same name rule. Aids: `--old-pistol-bolter-anim` (before), `--bot --carry-test [--carry-pitch rad]` (a 24 s cycle: idle, walk, aim, sprint, shot, melee, a long idle; a log line per phase with the family, idle clip and place), `--observe-orbit <deg>` (the spectator's follow camera turned round the player). Spec "True Grit bolter: animation set".

### ui/mouse-sensitivity: a mouse sensitivity slider (2026-11-01; client only, no protocol, wire or config-hash change)
Owner: "we need a mouse sensitivity slider in all game modes". `UiKit.MouseSensitivityRow` (0.10x to 3.00x, step 0.05, default 1.00x) sits beside the FOV slider in the Join screen footer and in the customizer header, which is also the in-match Esc menu, so it is reachable in Annihilation, Seize Ground and added content (Musou) alike; it applies live (`MouseSensitivity.Selected`, set by `CustomizerServices.UpdateSettings`) and is saved as `mouseSensitivity` in `frontend.json` (a missing or out-of-range value reads as 1.00). `NetworkView.MouseLook` = `MouseSensitivity.Look(_mouseScale)` replaces `_mouseScale` in the player and spectator mouse look, so hip fire, aim and scope scale alike; the gamepad look has no such setting and is untouched. Checks: `MouseSensitivityTests` (clamp, scaling, settings round trip) and the UI self-test (slider on both screens, range, live apply, persistence, number shown). The original PC game's mouse option is not confirmed here: logged in `docs/changes-from-original.md` as a client convenience.

### camera/hop-and-walls: the hop looking down and the camera at walls (2026-11-01; client plus `StaticMesh.SweepSphere`, no simulation behaviour, protocol, wire or config-hash change)
The owner's clip showed a backwards Devastator hop looking down with the character leaving the top of the screen. Cause: `RigCamera` read the evade set's curve at the view's pitch clamped to the set's 80 to 125 file degrees (the blend to that place was the only thing moving), so a view at -70 degrees kept the place of a view at -10: 3 m further back and 2.5 m lower, looking at the floor. Every evade does it (the roll, the dash); the sets' curves orbit to 0, so `CameraRig.SetPlacePitch` now keeps only the upper limit: chest off the view axis 47 -> 16 degrees, head distance steady at 3.64 m. Second pass, the walls: `CastClear` is a real swept sphere (the old ring's rays started a radius beside the cast, behind a near wall, and read 0), `SmNet.CameraBoom` adds a 0.2 s hold, a 0.15 m margin and a ramped release capped at 5 m/s to the old fast pull-in, height and side legs come before the pivot leg so a wall behind keeps the camera at the shoulder (0.93 m from the head, not 0.07 m), a blocked right side crosses the camera to the left shoulder (`SmNet.CameraSide`), and `NetworkView.CameraAim.cs` turns the camera up to 10 degrees toward the uncollided rig ray's hit, so the crosshair and the shot stay put (aim shift 0.83 -> 0 m at a wall). The own character's hide (1.4 / 1.61 m) is unchanged. Aids: `--camera-test hop|wall|corner|pillar [--camera-test-pitch r]`, `--old-camera-collision`, `--old-hop-camera`. Known limit: with both sides blocked the camera stays in the shoulder's place it can reach, and the hard cast still cuts at once. `FreshAim.TurnRigid` keeps the converged shot off a pitch clamp while the ray lies off the view. Spec "The follow camera at walls and in the hop"; `CameraBoomTests`.
### ui/menu-rebuild: the menus rebuilt to the owner's reference (2026-11-01; client only, no protocol, wire or config-hash change)
Owner: every menu in a Half-Life 2 style layout, title "SM - Reimpl". `UiKit` is now one look (DejaVu Sans Bold embedded in the client assembly, white, transparent text buttons, brightness on hover and focus, an underline on a chosen toggle); `MenuKit.cs` holds the layout measured from the reference (title capitals y 448 to 494 at x 118, rows 22.5 apart from y 551 at x 119) as fractions of the window's height, with the rows' text never under 10.5 real pixels. `FrontEndView` replaces the Join screen with pages (main, lobby, host, join local) and `OptionsView` (GRAPHICS, SOUND, CONTROLS; `GameOptions` in frontend.json, applied by `OptionsHost`, which touches only what differs from the defaults, never the window in a test run and nothing in a bot). JOIN SERVER has the fixed `JoinTargets.PublicServer`; JOIN LOCAL LOBBY is the one address field. The host page splits the bots into ADD LOYALIST BOT and ADD CHAOS BOT (`HostBots.PlanSides`). MUSOU MODE is on the main menu; the `--musou` gate is gone. The customizer keeps its dark background and lost its sliders and CONTROLS button (they are in OPTIONS). The Esc menu is `MatchMenu` over a dim: RESUME, LOADOUT (the creator), OPTIONS, LEAVE MATCH; a picker opened by itself on death still goes straight to the creator. The background image is one optional file, `client/assets/menu/background.jpg`, not committed: the owner's final image decides how it ships; without it the menus are plain dark. Music volume covers the match's countdown and result stingers, the game's only music in a match (`GameOptions.CategoryOf`). The renderer stays the launcher's choice (shown as text in GRAPHICS).
### TF0: Musou Mode's contracts (2026-11-01; branch `musou/tf0-contracts`; no protocol change, Musou's config hash only)
By the owner's decision of 2026-11-01 `--content musou` now runs the war on the generated map `tfw_war` (a stub flat slab, placeholder demonstration: no enemies yet) and there is no Skirmish/Campaign choice; the old 5-wave run stays only as a test aid, `--map mp_tdm_09`, pinned by `MusouSkirmishPinTests` (captured on main 2ed1501e before any hook). New hooks `ExtrasPlayerInput`, `ExtrasGeneratedMap`, `ExtrasCommand`, `ExtrasPlayerName`, `ExtrasLoadMap`; `NextPlayerId` skips ids held by players without a peer; message kind 17 (`ExtrasCommandMessage`, `GameClient.SendExtrasCommand`, `ContentExtras.CommandUsers`), dropped by every other profile (`ExtrasCommandIsolationTests`). `MusouSim.Version` 5, `TfwRules.Version` 1, `MusouPhase.Campaign` 6, envelope tags 7 to 10 reserved. `TfwContracts.cs`, `TfwMap.cs` (names and positions), `TfwWire.cs` and the stub partials hold the frozen contract; from here on the dispatchers and core stay untouched by TF1 to TF8. The design's assumptions, checked: the core has no respawn routine (it is inline in `World.Step`), so the war gets `World.TfwRespawnAt`; `MusouHit` looked up the player first, so a Guard attack is routed before that lookup. Faithful and extended pins unchanged.
### TF2: the war between the battles (2026-11-01; branch `musou/tf2-war`; no protocol or config-hash change: nothing calls it yet)
`WarSim` and `WarRules` (`src/SmSim/Extras/Musou/Campaign/`) are the design's section C: three fronts stepped at 1 Hz, pure and deterministic, with the phase, a battle's result and a lord's wound as inputs and `TfwWarView` as output. TF4 drives it from the run (`Enter`, `Step` once a second, `PlayerWon`, `PlayerLeft`, `WoundLord`, `FinalBonus`, `View`), and raises `TfwRules.Version` then. The design's constants met all four calibration targets, so none moved: unattended, an HQ falls at 47.2 min (first siege 33.1 min), 188.7 min in the hub (× 4.00), three wins on lane B open the final at 28.2 min before any siege, and a run takes 37.3 min with an assumed 8 min final. The shape to look at in a playtest: with a lord the Imperials start ahead (m·I 125 against 110), so every lane gains a node alone at about 9.9 min and loses it at about 28 min; a player who unlocks the final before then gets both other lanes' bonus (× 0.7225, +4 squads) without playing them. Numbers in spec "the war between the battles", tests `WarSimTests`.
### TF1: the war's map (2026-11-01; branch `musou/tf1-map`; no protocol change, map version 2)
The owner's decision: for now an empty square box the size of Manufactorum and a small Stormbird control room. `TfwMap.Solids` (arena slab and walls, the Stormbird's closed shell) replaces the stub slab, and the collision, the client's drawing (`client/Extras/Musou/Tfw/TfwMapView.cs`, placeholder demonstration) and the ragdolls' world are all made from it. The server builds the enemies' graph over the arena alone (`GameServer.BuildTfwNav`, cached as `tfw_war-musou-<key>.nav`, 229,441 nodes) and `CreateTfw` passes it to the war; `MusouSim.WidenBox` and `TfwMap.WireBox` keep the Stormbird inside the wire's box. The walls are 24 m, not the design's 12 m: its apex of 7.4 to 8.9 m was the Manufactorum spawn room's ceiling, and a full jump in the open reaches 17.54 m and clears 12 m (`TfwMapTests`). Touched outside the milestone's own files, one small edit each: `CreateTfw`, `World.StartTfw`, `MusouSim` (`WidenBox`); `TfwLoadMap` moved out of `NetworkView.Tfw.cs`. Camera in the room measured with `--camera-probe`: spec "War camera in the room". Spec "War map" and the rows after it.
### TF5: the AI Marines (2026-11-01; branch `musou/tf5-marines`; no protocol or config-hash change: no match spawns them until TF4)
`MarineBrain` (pure) and `World.TfwPuppets.cs`: server-side players without a peer, whose input is the same `PlayerInput` a client sends. `World.TfwSpawnRetainer(owner, at)` gives a player its Tactical retainer (Follow, Hold, Attack: the orders leave the command queue in `TfwPuppetsStep`, the run's other commands stay queued; only the sender's retainers obey). `World.TfwSpawnLord(lane, at)` brings a lane's lord and his retainer, autonomous, to `TfwRun.ActivePosition`. TF4 meets this on `TfwRun`: it sets `ReviveWindow` (read as `ReviveWanted(player)`), `ActivePosition`, `WarTimeScale`, `LordFallen`, and calls `TfwDismissMarines` after a battle and `TfwResetMarines` for a new run; `World.TfwRevive` keeps what the player carries, a respawn would not, and marks it armed so the pistol-only strip leaves it alone. `GameServer.NextPlayerId` skips 65520 to 65527 on every profile, so a human after 65,500 joins is never taken for a puppet (a constant, pinned to `TfwContracts`, because the core cannot name it). The Marines fight through TF3's `TfwGuardsStep`, the tick's one fight, so each shot counts once. On the install's classes each lord reached the position and helped clear six Boyz (kills 3, 3 and 4 with 3, 3 and 2 by the retainers); a loopback server ran 7 puppets for 18,000 ticks with a retainer and two others killed at 5 min. Numbers in spec "the AI Marines", tests `MarineBrainTests`.
**The weight pass (branch `feel/weight-impact`; 2026-11-01; client only, no simulation, wire or config-hash change).** The owner: "a lot of actions and animations feel very floaty. send a pass of weight/impact to pretty much all animations/actions that i haven't specifically said feel very good". Softer landings (8 to 20 m/s) show 0.3 to 0.8 of the data's crouch; a pitch-only camera impulse (`CameraImpulse`, read by `FxApplyShake` in `NetworkView.Fx.cs`, `NetworkView.Camera.cs` untouched) dips on landings, the own pound and blasts, kicks on heavy-weapon shots and on heavy footfalls; the data's recoil clips are laid at 1 to 1.5, the flinch at 1.3 (shot) and 1.6 (own melee hit), additive layers now taking weights up to 2; strikes and reactions enter with a 0.125 s fade floor. No hit-stop or melee shake: the owner removed them on 2026-10-29, so those candidates stayed out; the roll, the owner's blends and timings, the run clips and the footstep sound are untouched. Numbers in `WeightFeel` (tests `WeightFeelTests`); `--old-feel` and six part switches restore the old look; capture aid `--feel-shots`. Spec "The weight pass".
### visual/pack-halo: one pack on the heavy classes, the Devastator's Iron Halo (2026-11-01; client and content, no protocol, wire or config-hash change)
Owner: the Havoc had a loyalist backpack as well as its own, and the loyalist Devastator showed no Iron Halo. Both classes' fixed bolt pistol (`*_pistol_bolt_pistol_devastator`) has a `backpack` attachment with the loyalist `sm_lascannon_backpack_001`; `WeaponRig.Configure` drew it as a worn model over the armour's backpack slot, in the match and the preview. `WornItems.Draws` now leaves out a weapon's `backpack` attachment, so each class wears only the slot's pack; the grey box is gone from the Devastator too, which now shows its weapon's own pack (`sm_hbolter_mp_bp_001`, ...). The halo was no socket problem: only the Havoc's class override was ever drawn, the perk file's own attachment (`sm_acc_iron_halo`) was never read. `PerkInfo.Packages` and `AppearanceResolver.PerkPieces` add it as a `perk` piece unless a class override replaces it. The perk is offered only to Devastator and Havoc, so no other loyalist class can show a halo. `HeavyPackAndHaloTests`, spec "Heavy classes' back", "Perk's model on the body".
### sim/evade-cooldowns: the data's cooldown on the roll, the hop and the short hop (2026-11-01; part of protocol 51, no wire or config-hash change)
Owner: "Add the game data cooldown to tactical roll, devastator/havoc hop, assault marine/raptor short hop ... Currently they are completely spammable." The data has one value, `min_time_between_activations` 0.8 s, on all three MP evades, and the simulation read it from M21 on, but feel/locks-sprint-stop's 0.7 lock scale made it 0.56 s. `Evade.LockTicks` now takes it unscaled (24 ticks, from the start of the move: an interpretation, the graphs' `BRANCH_Evade` self-transitions need it). A press in the cooldown does nothing (`Evade.RefusesJump`): it ends no reaction or charge and starts no jump-pack take-off, so a refused tap shows nothing and, like the others, is buffered; only the buffer's 0.3 s window carries a press over (the hold rule no longer does, with nothing else under way: `InputBuffer.HoldKeeps`). A jump-pack hold in the cooldown is still a jump, taking off on tick 6 from the press. The stomp, ledge and air-dash rules are unchanged. Spec "Evade cooldowns"; `EvadeCooldownTests`. To check in a playtest: whether 0.8 s from the start feels like the original (a mashed roll now comes every 0.8 s; the spec row "What a repeat now gives").

### TF3: Guardsmen and leashed defenders (2026-11-01; branch `musou/tf3-guards`; no protocol change)
`GuardSim` runs up to 24 squads of 10 in two rows of five (straight steering, separation over a `SpatialGrid`, the graph's cells, a squad query every 10 ticks, hash-rolled shots); `World.TfwGuards` holds it and steps the fight from `TfwStep` while anyone is in the pool or the squads. Orks target a squad as a negative `MusouTarget.Id`; `MusouSim._target` is now `int` (a `ushort` clamp turned the id into 0, so a Guard target was lost every tick), events carry player 0 and `MusouEnemy.TargetPlayer` shows players only (`TargetOf` gives the stored id). A blow reaches `TfwGuardHit` through `MusouHit` and lands on the nearest man. `SpawnLeashed` / `ReleaseGroup`: defenders hold until a target is within 30 m of home, walk back when none is, and a hurt member frees the whole group. Measured: the design's 40 hit points lost the box (60 men dead by 45 s, 39 Boyz left), so the Guardsman has the install's 85: 6 squads beat 60 Boyz in 34.4 s, 20 men lost, deterministic; a guard step with 200 men costs 0.12 ms median (Release). `MusouSkirmishPinTests` unchanged. Battle wiring (spawning, orders, clearing guards between battles), wire tags 9 and 10 and the client's crowd come with TF4, TF6 and TF7a. Implemented but not played: no client shows the Guardsmen yet. Review follow-ups: a squad whose order cannot be reached stops after 1 s without getting nearer, so `Arrived` cannot stall; Guard target ids start at -2 (`GuardTargetId` = -(squad + 2)), so squad 0 is not `FlowField`'s -1 for an unreached node.
### TF7b: the war's HUD and hub (2026-11-01; branch `musou/tf7b-hud`; no protocol change, `TfwRules.Version` 4)
The war can be played from the client. In the Stormbird E opens Destination (`WarMapPanel`, menu style, keyboard, mouse and controller) and Equipment (the in-match picker on its loadout screen); M holds the map over the game; Z, X, V and P held 1 s give orders in a battle (`TfwOrders.cs`, read in `TfwFrame`, so `NetworkView.LoyalistBarks.cs` is untouched). `TfwHud` shows the fronts, HQ, reserves and scale, in a battle the objectives, Guardsmen, retainer and order, and the pickup, revive and extraction prompts; `MusouHud` drops WAVE and lives in the Campaign phase and names the commander on its boss bar; `TfwMarkers` draws rings, pillars and a beacon. TF4 and TF6 carried no guards count, retainer, pickup, revive or extraction state, so tag 7 gained a 14-byte per-client block, `TfwOwnView` (85 bytes, change-driven, countdowns in whole seconds so it stays near 1 Hz); `TfwRules.Version` 4. X and V clash with Next weapon and Melee: for a war's match those keys are taken out of the InputMap only, nothing saved, and put back when the view goes. The open map stands in `_pickerLayer`, so no core file changed. The match HUD's "RESPAWN IN" was wrong in a battle, so `hud.Data.Alive` is overridden while fallen and `TfwHud` says KILLED. TF7a's `_tfwState` is the one client state, its command pump (and `--tfw-deploy`) the one sender. Checked with `--tfw-test` (63 steps through real input events on a real server, headless and windowed, with `SM_TFW_DOWN_TEST` for the revive and the extraction) and `--bot --tfw-bot`. Not played by a human; the orders have no controller binding; a win through to the commander was not run end to end (the script leaves by pickup or extraction).

### TF6: the war on the wire (2026-11-01; branch `musou/tf6-wire`; no protocol change, `TfwRules.Version` 2)
Tags 7 to 10 and the commands of kind 17 work end to end on loopback: `TfwWire` (layouts), `TfwGuardInterest`, `TfwEventWindow` and `TfwFeed` (`TfwSend.cs`), `TfwClientState` and `TfwCommandSender` (client, engine-free), `GameServer.TfwSend.cs` and `GameServer.TfwCommands.cs`. TF4 fills `GameServer.TfwFeed` (the `WarSim`, the reserves, the objectives, `GuardSim.CopyTo`, the Guard events) and keeps a director set: tags 8 to 10 are quantised over its box, so they wait for it, and `MusouNewRound` clears it. Decision on the frozen command: the design's Hold and Attack name a place, the frozen 4 bytes have no room and the server has no camera to find the crosshair's point, so those two commands are 10 bytes (the 4, then 3 × i16 in 0.1 m) and `TfwCommandRecord` gained `Vector3 Point = default`; every other command and every existing caller is unchanged, and `TfwRules.Version` went to 2. Musou's and the war's bytes share one client budget: `MusouInterest` is left alone and spends first, the war refills from what its bucket shows was left of 58 KB/s, up to 20 KB/s. Measured with 160 dummy Orks and 120 Guardsmen all within 15 m of the player (the worst case) and 360 shots a second: 58.0 KB/s, largest message 1200 B, every man known to the client, though at about 5.7 updates a second each, since the Orks' 44 KB/s comes first; a playtest should tell whether the near men look stepped. Faithful, extended and 5-wave servers send none of it (`TfwWireTests`). The tag 8 contract has no room for the guards, retainer, pickup or revive counters the HUD needs (design section G): TF7b needs a decision on them.
### TF9: Musou Mode finished for the slice (2026-11-01; branch `musou/finish`; no protocol change, `TfwRules.Version` 5)
The owner: "From now on three-front war is called Musou Mode": every text says so now, and `Tfw` in code means it (`docs/added-content.md`). Second owner's rule: "The run should not end if you have under 2 supplies after a won battle." `TfwRun.Downed` now lets that extraction happen, takes what supplies there are and goes on; the prompt follows (`TfwHudModel.Prompt`). Nothing else ended a run in that case: the deploy asks for transport only, and with none the run waits in the hub for the HQ's next one (600 war s, 40 real minutes at the hub's 0.25) while the war can still be lost by an HQ falling. A run left short is lost by its next extraction from a battle not won. Tag 7's own flags gained bit 1, deployed: a player who joined mid-battle now sees the core's RESPAWN IN and no KILLED (`TfwHudModel.RunHoldsRespawn`).

The first battles won on a real server: `SM_TFW_WIN_TEST=45` (once a second every enemy within 45 m of a human falls, the boss too) and `--tfw-test-win` walked a run through real keys: two battles on front A, each through P1, the P2 depot, P3, the commander and the free pickup, the front moving 1 to 2 to 3, then the final assault to the Warboss's death and the win screen, 107 steps. The positions were secured by the server's own Guardsmen. Label: *implemented and run with the fighting left out*: no scripted player has beaten these enemies with its guns, and no human has played it. The Warboss has no leash and came to the player, so he fell before the player reached the HQ.

Measured on a real local server (Release, below-normal priority, 30 Hz, 1 client on loopback, new test aid `SM_TICK_STATS`; 12 logical CPUs, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER; tick = the step and everything sent with it, 10 s windows):
- Whole win run (60 windows, 10 minutes): mean 1.2 ms, worst window p99 3.2 ms, worst tick 16.1 ms, 13.6 KB/s mean, 31.4 KB/s peak (the final assault, 90 Guardsmen, 7 Marines), largest packet 998 B, 1 tick skipped. An earlier run showed stalls up to 0.67 s and 372 skipped ticks in clumps that did not follow the head count; the rerun had none, so they are put down to other work on the machine at below-normal priority, not proven.
- Load held by `SM_TFW_STRESS=180,20` (about 170 Orks, 170 to 200 Guardsmen, 3 Marines: a node battle has no more, 7 were only seen in the final, with fewer men): mean 1.85 ms, p99 2.6 to 2.9 ms, worst tick 5.3 ms, 50 to 59.5 KB/s, largest packet 1200 B, no skipped tick. That is the whole tick against the design's 2.5 ms p99 for the war's part alone (the war's part was not timed by itself), and under its 60 KB/s. The median stays about 2.1 ms from 0 enemies up to 180, against 0.08 ms in the hub: a fixed cost of a battle that was not traced.
- Client on the same load, one windowed client on the private desktop (`--frame-stats`, test window size, not a 1080p measurement): 111 to 124 fps, frame p50 6.7 ms, p99 31 ms, worst 58 ms; `GuardCrowd` 1.0 ms a frame; 40 skinned + 110 vertex-animated Orks and 20 + 100 Guardsmen drawn. TF7a saw the same p99 without a crowd. A headless client measures nothing here (capped at 6.9 ms).

Not done: a human playtest, the fights themselves on a real server, the extraction under 2 supplies on a real server (unit tests only), a second client's bytes, and a joiner's HUD on a real server (model and wire tests only). A joiner still sees the pickup prompts of the battle's own players (`TfwHudModel.Prompt` is not told it is out of the field).

### TF7a: the Guardsmen drawn (2026-11-01; branch `musou/tf7a-crowd`; no protocol change)
The real Exterminatus Guardsman (*original asset loaded*: body, head, rig, clips, lasgun, effects) now stands in the war. `GuardRig` is the rig profile and clip table; the lasgun's backwards look came from an assumed mount: the wargear names `rig_prop_m_chest` on both sides, so `GuardLasgun` reads it (and `--guard-test` does too). The look is one `MusouLooks.Look`, so `MusouCrowd`'s tiers moved into `CrowdView` and both crowds share them; `MusouVat` bakes any clip list. `GuardCrowd`: 20 skinned, the rest vertex-animated, 120 visible (60 in safe mode); near men blend the four aimed runs and the aim triple and lay the recoil over them, far men play one baked clip. Tag 10 drives recoil, `lasgun_muzzle`, `lasgun_tracer`, the light reaction and a death clip (no ragdoll yet). A real battle reaches it: with TF4 merged, `--tfw-deploy a` (test aid until TF7b) sends the Deploy, and 60 Guards of the server's run are drawn from tags 9 and 10 with no malformed section (shots and hurts seen; in 5.5 minutes no Guard died, so a death has only run on the scripted feed). `--guard-demo N` stays as the scripted load (*placeholder demonstration* of the behaviour) because a battle seldom holds 120 men. Measured on the private desktop at 1080p on an idle machine (RTX 4070 Ti SUPER): 120 Guards + 150 dummy Orks 157 to 169 fps, p50 5.5 ms, p99 22 to 26 ms; one Guard and no Orks shows the same p99 (24 to 25 ms) at p50 5.3 ms, so those spikes are not the crowd's; 80 + 60 170 fps. The tracer's pink and thin blue are the data's colour curves (docs/discovery.md "Guardsman"). Not done: the six additive flinches, the ragdoll, lasgun sound, impact effects, a spectator sees no war (the observer's frame has no extras hook).

### TF4: the battle and the run (2026-11-01; branch `musou/tf4-battle`; no protocol change, `TfwRules.Version` 3)
`TfwBattle` (the chain of positions, the leashed defenders, the arrivals, the securing, the commander, the failsafe) and `TfwRun` (transport, supplies, deploy, pickup, revive window, emergency extraction, the final assault, the end) make the war a game; `World.Tfw.cs` runs them, and `TfwStepMatch` now replaces the Musou flow. What the reading of the earlier milestones found: `MusouDirector` is built on the war's map with Stormbird markers off the graph, which is harmless (it falls back to open nodes) and it never runs, so the commander and the Warboss live in `TfwBattle`, and a `MusouBoss` with no director has its Waaagh!s' Boyz sent from the sources; `TfwBossStep` replaces `MusouBossStep`, which would count squads as dead; `TfwCreditKills` wraps `MusouCreditKills` so a Guardsman's KO reaches `orksKilled`; the stranded failsafe is `TfwBattle`'s, since no director drains it. The Campaign director starts at the first deploy, so a hub nobody left sends tag 7 alone. `GameServer.TfwFeedRun.cs` feeds TF6's `TfwFeed`; `TfwRun.Idle` is a test aid for the tests of the queue and the wire themselves. Merged with TF5: the run spawns and dismisses the AI Marines, `TfwRetainerUp` reads the roster, the fight's stand-in `TfwMarinesFight` is gone, Hold and Attack take the sender's clamped point (`Marine.AttackAt`; no point: the retainer's own place), a retainer's post is reset when it recovers, at the battle's landing zone. A real retainer revived a fallen player in `TfwRunTests`. No client has played a battle: implemented but not played. The HUD still shows WAVE 1/1 in the Campaign phase until TF7b. Spec "the battle and the run"; tests `TfwBattleTests`, `TfwRunTests`.
**Armour and health bar colours (branch `hud/bar-colours`; client and one rule, no protocol change; owner 2026-10-31, third attempt: "the health and armor status bar is still the wrong color as assault marine and tactical marine").** Cause: `Hud.Vitals.cs` drew everyone without the Iron Halo perk with the Iron Halo's cyan clip `ironhalo_mc` flat-tinted a saturated yellow (`ArmourYellow`, FDCA0D in the window) over the movie's red health (core EF1521). The owner's three reference frames of the original (an Assault Marine) show cream lines (FFF2C5, F9F5BB, FAEFB1) with a cream diamond outline over an orange-red fill (core FF491B, FA3203, F03115). The movie has exactly that bar: `lightdamagebar_mc` (lines 251, 252, 174 = FBFCAE, a plain diamond outline, cut by a mask: frame 0 whole, 1 to 98 cut, 3.62 movie px a frame), which earlier passes had read as "gold" and drawn once at full length under the yellow (the double bar of item 81). Now the plain bar is that clip at `VitalsRules.PlainArmourFrame` (nothing at no armour), one layer; the plain health fill gets `PlainHealthTint` (measured to the references: core about F02E15, edges EF720C in our shots); the armour vignette is the clip's cream. Iron Halo (by perk, Devastator or Havoc) is unchanged: cyan and white with the starburst, red health. The class never decides it: a Devastator without the perk has the plain bar. `--hud-vitals-demo` steps nine states (adds armour broken with half and low health, and 20 % armour); ui-selftest `ArmourBarChecks` also checks the colours (`Hud.VitalsArmourCyanShare`/`VitalsArmourYellowShare`: the plain bar neither cyan nor saturated yellow, the Halo's cyan). Shots (private): tactical, assault, devastator, devastator_halo, chaos_tactical, raptor, havoc_halo, nine states each, and an original-versus-ours comparison. Not checked: the original's bar at 0 armour and below 26 % armour (the data's lines turn white there), the bar's size against the reference (ours looks about 7 % smaller; that frame's scale is uncertain).

**Bar colours follow-ups (same branch, after review).** (1) The white low-armour bar (below about 26 %) was ours by accident: from frame 76 `lightdamagebar_mc` swaps its outline and lines for two 10-frame flash clips (`armorflash_mc` c530, c531: pure white at frame 0, fading to the normal colours at alpha 0.25 by frame 9), and a nested clip drew its first frame; they are now drawn at their resting frame (dim lines, `Hud.PlainArmourFrameOf`), spec row "Armour bar: the plain clip at low armour" (unverified: whether SM1 flashes once or loops is script). (2) No blank bar while the armour or health moves through frames not yet rendered: each layer keeps its last picture (same variant only) until the new one is ready, `HudMovieArt.Hold` keeps that picture from being evicted, and evicted keys are no longer rendered by the worker (the backlog of a fast sweep used to delay every later frame). (3) ui-selftest counts armour bar layers per frame over every path (Iron Halo clip, plain clip, M44 fallback: `Hud.NoteArmourDraw`) and checks at most one and never two kinds in a frame, also with the Iron Halo toggled every other frame, and that a one-frame-a-step sweep of armour and health never blanks a layer (it showed 122 blank frames before (2)).

**MUSOU MODE starts its local server (branch `fix/musou-local-server`; client and tools, no protocol change; owner 2026-11-01).** Cause of "No server was found next to the game": `client.cmd` runs Godot's editor binary, so `ServerLaunch.FindExecutable(OS.GetExecutablePath().GetBaseDir())` looked in Godot's tools folder (a released build carries `server\`); HOST LOCAL LOBBY was disabled in dev runs for the same reason. Fix: `tools/client.ps1` builds `src/SmServer` and passes `--server-exe` unless the caller gave one (a failed build only warns; the client still starts). The rules are `SmContent.MusouLocal` (pure, `MusouLocalTests`): a press with no server starts one, a press while a Musou server of this client is still starting says so and waits (the Host panel's pending join connects by itself when it listens; never a second server, never an early join), a press on a ready one joins it. STOP MUSOU SERVER is a main-menu row directly under MUSOU MODE, shown only while a Musou server started by this client runs (polled every frame, so it is right after a match, after the Host panel's STOP SERVER and when the server dies); it calls `HostPanel.StopHosted` (`HostedServer.Stop`: only the process this client started), restores the lobby's profile and says "Musou server stopped.". The release smoke test gained step 5 (`--auto-musou` against the zip's `server\`: `--content musou`, `--bind 127.0.0.1`). Test aid `--auto-musou --musou-cycle` (with `--server-exe`, `--host-port`) runs press, press while starting, press when ready and stop, and logs `musou-cycle:` lines. UI self-test: the row's visibility and the not-ready press.

## Musou pass 2, M1: battles on Manufactorum (2026-11-01)

Owner's item 4. Every battle is fought on Manufactorum read from the player's install. `tfw_war` stays one world, the level plus the generated Stormbird placed 110 m past the level's south edge from its bounds, because the server cannot change maps. The Seize Ground points A, B, C are P1, the depot and P3, run in either order by node parity; the commander stands in the Chaos start area; the landing zone and the sources are hash-seeded draws from the walking graph's open nodes (`TfwSites`). Without the map the server exits 2 with a message that names it. `TfwMap.Version` 3, `TfwRules.Version` 7, tag 8 gains each radius and the sites. Changes from the design: the spawn-room blockers go (with them Marines could not reach the commander), `GameMap.AddedContent` carries the battlefield to the server's war, `TfwHub` is computed so the client's stations and the tests follow it, and the map's effects and sounds also read through `ExtrasMapFile`. The empty arena moved to the tests as `TfwTestArena`. ## Musou pass 2, M2: allied navigation and line of sight (2026-11-01)

Guardsmen and AI Marines go round Manufactorum's walls: `AllyFlow` keeps eight flow fields over the walking graph, one per goal node, worked on one at a time at 20,000 nodes a tick. Squads bound for one point share its field. A man follows the field from his own node and waits for his squad when 3 m ahead; an AI Marine steers to the farthest node it can walk to straight, so it never cuts a corner into a wall end. A shot needs a line of sight (men and Marines alike choose an enemy they see), and a squad stops walking while an enemy is within 8 m, so a front forms. All three points are live from the landing and each squad goes for the nearest not secured; a secured point keeps a squad while two are free. A human or an AI Marine alone secures at half rate at any time, not only with every Guardsman gone. `GuardSim.PlaceForTests` is gone: the win test's squads walk. New aids: `SM_TFW_FIGHT_LOG`, `SM_TFW_KEEP_HUMAN`, `--tfw-test-fight`. `TfwRules.Version` 11 with M3. Tests `AllyNavTests` (synthetic maze).

## Musou pass 2, M3: Ork AI, swarm and tide (2026-11-01)

The causes the design listed are fixed. Melee tokens: 6 on a player, 12 on a squad, reached at the men, and an Ork without one waits at its own slot instead of orbiting. Arrivals: a tide of one Ork a second from each point. Defenders: a garrison of 12 on each point, rebuilt one per 4 s. The leash: a woken Ork never walks home. Identical paths: a bearing of its own, a slot, a spawn disc, wider spacing while far, and 30 % flanking. All of it sits behind `MusouSim.Swarm`, set only by `StartTfw`. Elites follow 0.10 + 0.50 p.

The owner changed four things during the milestone. Only a full capture stops a point; an Imperial on it pauses it, and spawning returns on the very tick a capture stops or a retake is done. Guardsmen are off behind `TfwBattleRules.GuardsmenEnabled`, so players and AI Marines capture at the full rate. The count is 200 alive, +80 a further human, capped at 460 inside the 512-slot pool. Musou must stay isolated from PvP.

Two consequences: the commander comes once each point has fallen, not when all three stand at once, because without squads to hold them a battle could hang; and the tide went to 1 s to feed the doubled count.

Measured on a real server at normal priority: 200 Orks cost a mean 1.1 to 2.2 ms a tick, p99 2.4 to 5.7 ms in steady play with lone spikes to 24 ms, no skipped ticks, and at most 55.8 KB/s, under the 58 KB/s ceiling. A landing costs 6 to 8.5 ms, the sites' raycasts 2.1 to 3.2 ms of that, so nothing was spread. A cold start takes 5.1 s on 12 cores and 71.7 s on one busy core, so Musou's start limit is 600 s with a "Preparing the battlefield" line. Ticks of up to 2.4 s showed at below-normal priority while other agents loaded the machine: the slow ticks sampled used no CPU time, and they went away at normal priority. Frame time at 200 Orks is not measured yet (M12). New aids: `SM_TFW_GUARDSMEN`, a `TFWSLOW` line. Tests `TfwOrkTests`.

Owner's items 1, 2 and 14. **Item 1.** The design left the snapshot's appearance version untraced; it is not in the snapshot: a client asks for a look only when a scoreboard row (`ScoreEntry.AppearanceVersion`, sent every second) names a version it does not know, and the server answers an `AppearanceQuery` from the peer's `AppearanceState`. A retainer has no peer, so both places read `GameServer.PeerlessLook`, which calls the new hook `ExtrasPuppetAppearance`; Musou Mode answers with the owner's version, race and published code (lords and their retainers keep the default). The smoke is tag 11 kind Smoke (three messages), drawn by `TfwSmoke`: 40 puffs, no depth test, fully opaque 0.5 s, gone at 2 s. The client takes the waiting look when the class changes (`OwnLooks.Update(false, ...)` then the next frame's alive counts as the respawn), says "You are now playing ..." and no longer says "applies when you respawn". **Item 14.** Tag 13: the 'Ard Boy, Nob and Warboss, health as a byte of their full health, ten sections a second at most, a client gets the 64 nearest of up to 120 (`TfwBars.PerClient`; at most 2.1 KB/s); `TfwBarsView` draws one MultiMesh with one small shader. `TfwRules.Version` 8, no protocol change; the hook is added to `ExtrasBoundaryTests.Hooks`. Tests `TfwClassBarsTests` (the retainer's look over the wire, the class change in the sim and over the wire with the new look and the retainer following, bars selection and cost, a swarm of 120 elites). Test aid `--tfw-test-class [dir]` (docs/commands.md): a scripted player on a real server deploys as slot 2 in the Stormbird, checks and photographs the swap, the retainer's paint and the bars. Seen: the smoke fully covers the model from the first frame (a first version with depth test left an arm showing; no depth test and 40 puffs cover it); the retainer wore the owner's paint (the resolver names `blood_raven_red` for both) but stood in deep shade in some captures, where it read black. Not done: the Deploy button still says "DEPLOY WITH SLOT n", not the owner's words "deploy as selected custom class"; a second class change needs a new Setup (the core's `SetupInterval`); the bars are depth-tested (a wall hides one) and have no distance fade. Wire notes for M8 and M9: `TfwClientState.NewFire` is emptied by `TakeNew()` in `TfwGuardsFrame` before `TfwFireFrame` runs, so a view that wants tag 11 must read the frame's sections (the smoke does) or `TakeNew` must move.
## Musou pass 2, M10: gore (2026-11-01)

Owner's items 8, 22 and 23. Client only: `client/Extras/Musou/Gore/` draws what the engine-free `MusouGoreRules` and `MusouGoreField` (`src/SmNet/Extras/Musou/Gore/`) decide, from the death and hit events that already exist (no wire, no protocol, no new hook, `TfwRules.Version` unchanged). Budgets: 12 deaths a frame, queue 96, pools of 256 gibs, 768 droplets, 64 ground pools, 192 spatter, 48 mist, 48 slashes, the design's distance bands, counts thinned while the pools fill. `--no-musou-gore`; `--musou-gore-demo [N]` is the scripted feed (36 s cycle: cleave sweep, shots, lascannon, frag, barrage, 8 s of about 30 kills a second). Hammer swings (branch `anim/hammer-swing`; the owner, 2026-11-01; no protocol change: the config hash covers the new factor, 52 stays the unreleased version): **(1) the step**: the thunder hammer's and the daemon maul's three light strikes lunge 0.82 of the lunge every melee weapon has (`MeleeStep.LungeFactor`, `MeleeTuning.HammerLightLungeFactor`; ours, an estimate of the owner's "1 to 2 meters less"): live, no target, chained 7.94 / 8.51 / 7.35 -> 6.52 / 6.96 / 6.02 m; a locked target is still closed by the hit. **(2) the legs**: measured first (new `--swing-test stand|walk`, `--log-lunge`, the `SWING` lines of `--anim-probe`, `--swing-trace`, `smtool melee-steps`): the clip foot lock held the back foot in the world while the body went 1.625 times the clip's root motion, so the leg sat at its 0.995 limit in 51 to 59 % of the strikes' foot-frames, trailed 1.24 m behind and snapped forward over up to 0.35 s at the next strike. Now the hammer's light strikes stretch the clip's stride by the body's travel (`CharacterViewer.ClipStrideScale`), a held foot out of reach is let go, a released one leaves in 0.1 s: 58 / 59 / 51 % -> 8 / 11 / 4.5 %, the pose jump at the chain 19 / 14 / 15 -> 7 / 11 / 8 cm/f^2. `--old-hammer-legs`, env `SM_OLD_HAMMER_LUNGE=1` for before / after. **(3) the air slash**: the jump-pack graph has a separate "Hammer Dash State"; the hammer and the maul now show `SM_MEL_TH_XATK_Combo3` (flight 0.4333 to 0.5333 s at 0.2, landing from 0.5667 s at 0.8; `SmNet.HammerSlashPose`) instead of the sword's clip; damage, stagger, timing and effects unchanged; jump -> slash jerk median 49.5 -> 12.5 cm/f^2. `--old-hammer-slash` = before. Spec "The hammer's swings and air slash"; tests `HammerSwingTests`. Not done: the hammer's dash attack and ground pound clips, the heavy strikes' legs.

## Musou pass 2, M8 and M9: orbital support and the far war (2026-11-01; branch `musou/p2-fire`; `TfwRules.Version` 15, no protocol change)

The owner's items 10 and 12, and his two changes the same day: artillery only on call, and the Thunderhawk runs paused. B sends the command Orbital with the crosshair's point; `World.TfwOrbital` decides (battle, in it, alive, on the battlefield, 60 s cooldown) and lays the walking barrage, first impact 1 s later; the cooldown travels in tag 7's own block (86 bytes) and shows in `TfwHud`. `TfwFire` on `TfwRun` holds the shells, `GameServer.TfwFire.cs` sends tag 11, `TfwFireView.cs` turns the records into whistles, bursts, shock and the muffled war, `TfwBlastCloud.cs` is the plume, clods, dust and fireball the install has no effect for. Fire KOs carry `MusouDeathKind.Barrage` and no player. M0's `TfwFireFrame` could never see a record, as `TakeNew` ran first; `TfwFireTake` copies them. Rerun the balance (M4): barrages are now the player's tool. Test aids in docs/commands.md. Nobody has heard any of it.

**Paused Thunderhawk runs:** `TfwFireRules.RunsEnabled` false stops every run, the aircraft's load and the campaign bank. Written and working before the pause: the schedule (at least 45 s), the path, side guns with targeting, damage and credit (`World.TfwRound`, tests through `TfwFireForTests`), tag 11's Run and Round records, the mesh and wing guns, jets, tracers, flyby, engine and hit sounds. Left: tracers were never judged in a capture, the guns are placed by eye, the aircraft flies through the drawn bridges above its 35 m, a run's rounds were few on the real map (about 20 to 50 a pass), the jets read purple, the flyby's timing was never heard. To resume: set the switch, restore F10 and the FireTest run bit in `TfwFireView.cs`.

**No orbital cooldown, no flyby in the war (`musou/no-orbital-cooldown`, 2026-11-01; `TfwRules.Version` 16, wire format unchanged):** the owner: "simply completely remove the cooldown on the artillery strike support call when pressing the B hotkey" and "remove the plane flyby sound". Every B press in a battle calls one strike, also over a barrage under way (`TfwFire`'s cooldown is gone, nothing else refused one; the client's check on the own block too, its byte stays, always 0; the key still fires on the press alone; the client's command queue and the server's 8 commands a second, shared by all orders, stay). `TfwHudModel.OrbitalText` is a constant. `play_ig_valkyrie_flyby` is out of `WarEvents`, the war's only flyby, with the code that flew its emitter across the sky. The paused run's own flyby (`FlybyEvents`) stays, played only by `TfwRunBegins`. By the owner's word no test, game or review was run: two builds only; the hand-edited tests and `--tfw-orbital-test` are unrun.

## sim/light-melee-flinch: light melee only flinches (2026-11-01; protocol 52)
The owner's rule: no light melee attack (the knife's included) staggers, stuns or interrupts; only stun strikes, charges, stomps and kicks do. `World.ResolveMelee` takes a `light` flag (the normal combo, the sword slash; not the heavy list or the heavy classes' kick, `MeleeStep.Kick`, set from `ability_displace_kick` by `MeleeTuning`) and calls `Spread.Flinch` instead of `TryReact`. The flinch is `PlayerState.FlinchTicks` (0.5 s, restarted by each hit), widening every shot's scatter by up to 6 degrees (`Spread.After`, also the crosshair); both numbers are ours (spec "Light melee flinches", refine register). It is in the own record (one byte, protocol 52, full record 167 bytes, snapshot worst case 1195), so prediction stays exact; the spread rules version is 2. Updated pins: `ReactionTests` (light hit, combo, no-HitReact window, prediction window, protocol), the `Protocol.Version` 52 and 1195-byte pins in the other SmNet tests. New: `LightMeleeFlinchTests`. Musou enemies' hits (`MusouHit`, `TfwCombatRules`) are untouched. Perks: none describes a light interrupt; the perks that change a strike's reaction (`PerkValues`) show only heavy strikes' changes, and a perk that changes a light attack's reaction kind is now moot in play (none known).

## Stall keep-alive and freeze diagnostics (fix/stall-keepalive, 2026-11-01)

A playtester on the Compatibility renderer (AMD integrated GPU) was dropped when his thunder hammer landed a hit; his log ended "the connection is gone (Disconnected)". It could not be reproduced with hammer hits, but a rendered bot on that renderer with a cold shader cache froze 13.5 s in its first draw and was dropped by the server ("timed out"): any long freeze of the main thread dropped a player from any server, because the client sent only from its frame. Fix, no protocol change and nothing needed on a deployed server of protocol 51: `GameClient` runs a background keep-alive (`GameClient.KeepAlive.cs`): after 1 s without an `Update` it re-sends the newest `InputBatch` every 0.5 s, with its inputs made neutral (so the frozen player stands still, the server skips every tick in it as already simulated, the acknowledgement is not newer, and the idle kick sees no play), up to 30 s of stall. It runs only on the real UDP transport (`IClientTransport.ThreadSafeSend`, `UdpClientTransport.Send` now locked) and ends on `Leave` or when the connection ends.
