### Musou Mode: two allied Marines (branch `hotfix/musou-allies-two`, 2026-11-08; Musou Mode only, `TfwRules.Version` 41, no protocol or wire change)
The owner, 2026-11-08: "nerf all non-player allied space marines. reduce their total count to 2, and they roam the map together attacking and defending." **Removed from battles:** the players' retainers (`TfwSpawnRetainer`, their orders `MarineOrders`/`TfwOrderMarines`, the 180 war-second recovery), the lane lords and their retainers (`TfwSpawnLord`, `LordFallen`; the war map still names and wounds a lane's lord as war data, but no lord fights) and expansion S6's six Defenders (`DefenderRules`, `TfwSpawnDefenders`, `TfwBattle.DefenderPosts`); `MarineRole` is gone. **The pair** (`AllyRules`, `MarineBrain.cs`, `World.TfwPuppets.cs`, `TfwBattle.Allies.cs`): `TfwRun.Land` lands two (`World.TfwSpawnAllies`: Tactical "Brother Varro" leads, Devastator "Brother Calix" follows) at the landing zone whatever the number of humans; a late joiner brings none. Once a second `TfwBattle.AllyGoal` picks the secured position the Orks press hardest (Orks within 40 m plus inbound Ork armies, at 8, kept at 4) to defend, else the contested position under way, else the nearest not secured, then the HQ (won: the landing zone). The leader goes there (waiting while the follower is beyond 8 m, no sprint while it lives), the follower keeps 2 to 4 m behind him; the pair never captures (`TfwBattle.SetAllies`), revives a fallen human with an open window (the window stays open while one of the two stands) and a dead one is back at the landing zone 30 s later (a lone survivor leads; one back follows). The pair wears the host's look; the own block's retainer state shows the pair (HUD "ALLIED MARINES: ..."), its order is always Follow. **Orders:** the server drops Follow, Hold and Attack; the client no longer sends them and frees Z, X and V (X next weapon and V melee work again in Musou); the battle panel's hint shows only the pickup. The puppet id range (12 ids, 65516 up) is unchanged. The 5-wave run never had AI Marines (they need a war), so nothing changes there. Tests: `TfwAllyPairTests` (two in a battle for 1 to 4 humans and with a late joiner, the leader reaches a contested position with the pair together 90 % of the time, the defend and attack choice, the 30 s respawn at the landing zone), `MarineBrainTests` rewritten for the pair (cohesion on the way to two goals, kills, revive, respawn and lead hand-over, loopback server 10 simulated minutes), the run, HUD, co-op and army tests moved to the pair. Not checked: a playtest on Ashfall (the pair's pathing on the real map and how the balance feels), the Godot `--tfw-test` scripts (updated, not run).
### Hotfix: the bolt blast nerf (branch `hotfix/bolt-blast-nerf`, 2026-11-08; Musou Mode only, `TfwRules.Version` 41, `MusouSim.Version` 20, no protocol change)
The owner: "we need to nerf explosive bolt weapons. the explosion needs to be half its current size, both the area of effect damage. make the vfx 60% smaller and remove the ragdoll effect, it simply rips enemy corpses apart as soon as the target dies or knocks them down if it deals damage to them and they don't die." The bolt blast's reach is halved, 2.5 m to 1.25 m (`TfwCombatRules.BoltBlastRadius`), with the fall-off's distances (full to 0.5 m, 30 % at 1.25 m), so the area that takes damage is a quarter of what it was; the 30 damage at the centre stays (read as "half the size of the area of effect", not half the damage). The client plays the frag detonation it reuses at 0.4 of its size (`BoltBlastFxScale`; `FxDetonation` takes a scale, 1 for everything else). `World.MusouBlast` takes `bolt` (`TfwCombatRules.BoltBlastKnocksDown`, on): a kill is the new death kind `MusouDeathKind.BoltBlast` (7), which gore bursts as an explosion (gibs, `explosive_heavy`, no corpse) but `MusouGoreRules.Thrown` leaves out, so no ragdoll or flung body; a fodder Ork hurt and alive falls where he stands (`MusouSim.KnockDown` with distance 0 and no death roll), any other enemy staggers with no knockback. Classic PvP never reaches it (the bolt blasts need `MusouSim.War`). Tests: `TfwMeleeTests` (the halved reach, an Ork at 1.6 m untouched, the kill's cause and gore, a hurt Boy knocked down and not moved, an 'Ard Boy staggered and not moved).
### Hotfix: hosted server lag (branch `hotfix/musou-server-lag`, 2026-11-08; server loop pacing and `client.cmd`'s server build, no gameplay, protocol or wire change)
The owner, with a screen recording of local Musou play: "it feels like something is killing server performance". **Recording** (6.7 s, 30 fps capture): no client freeze (never two identical captured frames in a row; 40 of 202 frames repeated singly, so the client drew about 24 to 30 frames a second at 2544 x 1432); the camera follows the Marine with small back-and-forth jumps, not a slow frame rate. At the time the owner ran the shipped tester build (Release server hosted by the client) while other sessions' builds and test sweeps held this PC at 40 to 100 % CPU. **Measured (headless `--tfw-test-fight` client on Ashfall, `SM_TICK_STATS=5`, new `TICKPACE` line: wall time between tick starts and between snapshot rounds, updates that ran more than one tick, GC collections, pause and allocation):** `Thread.Sleep(1)` on this Windows PC sleeps 15.5 ms at best (the default timer resolution: the server never raised it) and, at normal priority with the CPU busy, p90 30 ms and up to 83 to 119 ms. So the 30 Hz loop woke late: even an idle server (0.03 ms ticks) had 107 to 233 ms between tick starts and skipped ticks; with a Musou battle and one client, side by side at the same load (CPU 96 to 100 %, other sessions' sweeps), the old loop skipped 225 and 3,091 ticks, had 113 to 884 ms between tick starts and snapshot gaps over 100 ms in 53 of 63 and 73 of 73 five-second windows (the client interpolates 100 ms behind: past that the world stops, then snaps). GC is not a factor (0 collections in every window, 1 to 2 MB/s allocated, workstation concurrent GC). The S6 route searches and the perf pass's send budget showed no stall of their own. **Fix:** on Windows the loop's 1 ms pause is a high-resolution waitable timer (`CREATE_WAITABLE_TIMER_HIGH_RESOLUTION`; fallback 1 ms timer resolution) and the loop thread runs above normal priority (review 2026-11-08: only the thread, not the whole process, so a server hosted on the player's PC never takes CPU from the client's render thread; the measurements above had the whole process raised) (`src/SmServer/LoopPacing.cs`; `SM_OLD_LOOP_PACING=1` restores the old loop, a test aid); the Linux VM is unchanged. Same load, same binary, side by side: skipped ticks 0 and 0, tick starts p99 35 to 48 ms (max 79 to 89; the tick is 33.3 ms), snapshot gaps over 100 ms in 2 of 63 and 1 of 74 windows (max 113 to 137 ms), tick mean 4.0 to 11.3 ms against 14.8 to 67.6 ms (the old loop's ticks were themselves preempted). Idle server at 100 % CPU: tick starts max 34.8 ms with the fix against 107 to 233 ms. **Also:** `client.cmd` handed the front end a **Debug** server (`fix/musou-local-server`); a Debug server ran a one-player Musou battle at 13 to 88 ms a tick (skipping up to 1,687 ticks), so `client.cmd` now builds and hands over the Release server, as `server.cmd` and the tester zip do. Classic PvP: the same pacing applies to a hosted or Windows dedicated server (steadier ticks, no rule change). A third pair (90 s fight): old loop 1,900 ticks skipped of about 4,200, snapshot gaps up to 598 ms, and its scripted player never got to the fight in 8 minutes (killed); fixed loop 0 skipped, snapshot gaps max 120 ms, and the client's own prediction corrections (new `--tfw-test-fight` note) 3,105 sampled, p99 0.098 m, 181 over 5 cm, 2 over 50 cm (the landing's move among them). Not verified: the owner's own playtest; the old loop's client corrections (its run never reached the fight); the client's play code is unchanged (only the test note) and its frame rate on his PC under load was not measured.
**Release in parts (branch `tools/release-parts`; owner, 2026-11-08: "minimise the data uploaded per release"; tooling and launcher, no gameplay
change, protocol 64 unchanged).** A ship uploaded about 255 MiB (the 218 MiB playtest zip and the 37 MiB Linux server tar) over a slow line. Now
the build is also cut into nine parts (engine, dotnet, client, media, ashfall, server, launcher, source, meta; `src/SmLauncher.Core/Parts.cs`), each
a zip named by a fingerprint of its files, kept in one stable published release `parts` of the releases repository; a build's own release carries
only its manifest (`...-Windows.parts.json`, about 110 KB: every file's path, SHA-256, size and part, every part's zip hash and size). `ship.cmd`
asks `smtool release-parts plan` which parts the `parts` release lacks and uploads only those (never over an existing asset). The launcher reads
the manifest (vouched for by GitHub's digest and the description's "Download check", like the zip), downloads only the parts carrying a file the
installed builds do not have, hashes each part and every file, copies the rest from the installed build, checks the result against the build's own
file list, and falls back to the full zip when a release has one; resumable through `update.json` (source `parts`). To keep parts stable: the
Windows export no longer embeds its pack (`sm-reimpl.pck` beside the exe, under 1 MB), so the 110 MB engine is the same file every build (the guard
accepts that exe only while its `pck` section is still Godot's empty 8-byte placeholder and has no trailer, and allows `.pck` in binary packages
only as a verified Godot pack); the launcher is versioned by the last commit that changed it and its publish is reproducible (checked byte for byte).
The full zip goes up only on the bridge release (the first build with parts, while no published release has a manifest: launchers from before
this change take only a zip, so that release stays visible) or with `-FullZip`. The Linux server tar is no longer uploaded (`-Linux` still does):
the VM builds the server from the shipped commit with `tools/release/vm-build-server.sh` (docs/releasing.md, "Updating the Vultr server"). Measured
on two local builds (0fdd9371, 2586f6d2): launcher, engine, dotnet, media and ashfall zips byte-identical; a code-only release uploads meta 0.6 +
client 4.9 + server 2.0 + source 7.2 MiB + the manifest, about 15 MiB; with a launcher change about 57; worst case every part, 187 (the bridge
adds the zip once, 218). `release.cmd -Smoke` now lets the launcher part alone install the build from the parts (`--install-parts`), then runs
the usual smoke test in that folder: passed (500 files verified, server, bot, lean bot, HOST A MATCH, Musou). Tests: `PartsTests` (51: the split,
the manifest's refusals, the selection, the upload plan, installs, updates, damaged parts and installed files, the zip fallback, resume, the local
install) and the guard's new rule (`PackageScannerTests`). Not run: a real upload (`ship.cmd`); the VM script on the VM.
**Hotfix: Ashfall floor shimmer (hotfix/ashfall-floor-shimmer, 2026-11-08; client only, Musou Mode only, no protocol or hash change).** The owner: "the floor shimmers a lot in musou mode ashfall map." Measured with two new test aids: the gallery's `--ashfall-shimmer` (Ashfall's street views with the game's camera, MSAA 4x + SMAA, SSAO and SSIL; a sub-pixel turn, a slow walk or a still camera with everything animating; per-pixel temporal flicker over the floor, frames and heat maps) and `--ashfall-frames` (consecutive frames of a real match). Ruled out by measurement: z-fighting of the road and plaza slabs with the ground under them (the ground drawn 8 cm lower changed nothing), mesh LODs, unfiltered noise in the grime (band-limiting it changed nothing), shadows, SSAO/SSIL, volumetric fog, the airborne layers; with MSAA the floor's aliasing is small (2 x 2 supersampling barely lowers it). Found: with FSR 2 upscaling (the Options' new choice) the grime's overlay passes shimmered on the far floor even on a still camera, 0.58 % of floor pixels flickering against 0.08 % folded (FAST) and 0.05 % with MSAA; now the grime is folded while FSR 2 is on (0.07 %), and the Graphics option applies again when it is off. In real matches the overlay passes also lost and regained whole patches of floor and wall as the camera moved (their depth equals the surface's only up to rounding); each pass is now drawn 1e-4 of its distance nearer the camera along its own view ray (the same pixels): median flicker per burst 4.8 -> 3.1 % and 3.4 -> 1.8 % in two A/B pairs (noisy). A pull written through `POSITION` broke the FSR 2 jitter and was not kept; under FSR 2 the plain passes stay. Test aid `--ashfall-grime-pull off`. Spec "Ashfall grime under FSR 2 and its depth pull". Frames and numbers in the private shots folder `ashfall-shimmer`. Not verified: the owner's own settings (resolution, upscaling) and his playtest; the Compatibility renderer's floor (its numbers did not move).
**Fix: no description under the headshot medal in Classic PvP (fix/headshot-no-description, 2026-11-08; client only, no protocol change).** The owner: in Classic PvP, Annihilation and Seize Ground, "Kill an opponent with a headshot." must go; the "+100 Headshot" line and its icon stay. The text (the data's `display_description`, locale 105721, added with the headshot medal in e70554ea) is drawn by two paths, `Hud.DrawEvents` and the movie's `DrawMovieRewards`, both through `Hud.RewardDescription`; that now returns nothing unless the new `Hud.RewardDescriptions` is set, and `NetworkView` sets it only while `MusouActive`, so Musou Mode draws exactly what it did and Classic never does. What the code scores: a headshot kill is 100 (`KillScore` 50 + `HeadshotScore` 50), which the line shows as "+100"; the e70554ea title's "+50" is only the headshot part. Nothing in score or wire changed. Tests: `UiSelfTest.HeadshotMedal.cs` (Classic default draws none; Musou switch accepted with a locale, none again); the existing `HudRewardTests` (rules, unchanged). Screenshot (headless, `godot.cmd --windowed`, `--hud-headshot-demo`) for the owner's approval: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\cache\previews\headshot-no-description\headshot-medal-classic.png`. Not run: the full `dotnet test`; the in-game Musou HUD by eye.

Classic PvP bots: the 2026-11-08 pass (db0595d8: safe pushes only, no push under fire, cover at low health, ramp and balcony posts) now runs in Seize Ground only (owner 2026-11-08: "in annihilation classic pvp only, roll back the most recent ai changes. for seize ground keep them."). Annihilation bots behave as after the melee push (8dc42b18) and before that pass: a push goes ahead at once on its concealed approach, no retreat, no posts. A mode switch, not a deletion: `NetworkView.BotRecentAi` (`BotRecentAiRules.Applies`, test aid `--bot-recent-ai` forces it on in both) gates the retreat, the posts and the push's safe-plan and under-fire rules; the engine-free `BotPush`/`BotApproach` keep their new parameters with old-behaviour defaults. Seize Ground never pushed or held posts, so there the pass reduces to the cover rule. Tests: BotRecentAiModeTests (3) plus BotCoverTests and BotApproachTests pass; both builds 0 errors; headless `bots.cmd` 2v2 for 60 s against `--mode annihilation` and `--mode seize`: both run, no `retreat` lines in Annihilation, one in Seize. Full `dotnet test` not run (owner rule). Not verified: the owner's playtest.
**Hit decals only on the map (fix/hit-decals-map-only, 2026-11-08).** The owner: ranged hit decals should not stick to a player; they appear only when the shot misses players and strikes the map. Reverted night/weapon-fx's `StickToPlayer` (armour sparks, armour-hit glow, health burst back in world space; `--old-hit-stick` removed) and `FxImpact` now skips the weapon's hit container (decals, exit wound) for a player victim (`HitDecalRules.DrawsContainer`); the melta burn, sparks, flashes, blood and sounds stay. A Musou enemy hit (no player id) is unchanged. Test aid `--pvp-hit-fx-demo decals` (a player hit, then a map hit, alternating). Tests: `HitDecalRulesTests`. Client only, no protocol change. Not verified by a human.
**Sound louder and farther; Musou Ork voices on their own curves again (sound/louder-farther, 2026-11-08; client and tools only, no protocol or config-hash change; both modes).** The owner: all game sounds "clearly hearable and relatively much louder from much further away ... both game modes", "the game in general is too quiet. make everything much louder"; and "revert the request i made awhile ago that made ork yelling, barks, and other sounds and noises be quiet the further away you are. use the original game's exterminatus sound levels". Measured first with `smtool audio-mix` (new `--loudness` and `--speech character/type`): no bug that made us quieter than the data (bus chain the data's, no double-counted bus volume, no RTPC on these events, options at full); the data's mix is simply quiet (a remote bolter -25.5 dB at the voice at 5 m, -60.9 at 60 m). `SmContent.SoundLoudness` (ours): every voice +9 dB, every bank distance curve (dry volume, low-pass, its end, the `distance` RTPC) read at the distance / 2.5, in `SoundSystem.MixOf` and `Audible` and for the loyalist barks; `--loudness-gain`, `--loudness-range`, `--loudness-original`. Bolter at 5/15/30/60 m: -25.5/-32.0/-41.6/-60.9 dB before, -14.6/-17.2/-21.0/-28.7 after; Ork bark -32.8/-61.1/-103.6/-112.1 before, -17.2/-26.7/-43.7/-77.6 after (spec "Sound loudness: louder and farther"). Musou: the Ork voices keep their own bank curves again (`MusouSoundRules.VoicesOnWeaponCurve` false; `--musou-ork-voice-curve weapon` restores 2026-11-06); the 2026-11-06 rates, taunts, ranges and the voice emitter stay; the loudness rule applies on top, as the lead's brief asked. Tests `SoundLoudnessTests`, `MusouEnemySoundTests`. Not heard by a human; the +9 dB and x2.5 wait for the owner's playtest.

**Distance floor (sound/louder-farther, 2026-11-08, the owner's second note).** "revert the change we made previously where we said that barks and all combat sounds will get quieter the further away they are. sounds should scale down to 20% of their normal sound when turned down by distance." `SoundLoudness.FloorFraction` 0.2 (read as amplitude: -14 dB, ours; `--loudness-floor`): the dry volume curve never takes a voice more than 14 dB under its 0 m level, and positioned voices are no longer cut at their curve's end (`MaxDistanceOf`); the loyalist barks do the same in `BarkDistanceDb`. With the floor, at 0/30/60 m: bolter -13.3/-21.0/-27.3 dB, chainsword hit -14.3/-28.3/-28.3, Ork bark -17.2/-31.2/-31.2. The Musou crowd's budget ranges still choose which Orks sound. Not heard by a human.

**Melee hits x2 (sound/louder-farther, 2026-11-08, the owner: "all modes: raise melee weapon on hit sounds by 2X. give the on hit sound of melee weapons the same treatment as we did for ranged weapons - reduce the distance falloff and cap it").** `SoundLoudness.MeleeHitGainDb` +6.02 dB (`--melee-hit-gain`) on the swings' data hit events (`PostDataMeleeHit`: players and Musou enemies, own and others') and the Musou enemies' melee hits (`MusouCue`, group MeleeHit, whose crowd range is now 50 m like the guns'); these already went through `SoundSystem` and so took the range scale and floor. The generated hit sound (`--generated-melee-hit-sound`, a Godot player outside the mixer) now takes the gain, range scale and floor too (`SoundLoudness.InverseDistanceDb`). The charge's body smash is not a weapon hit and keeps the global rule only. Chainsword hit at 5/15/30/60 m: -30.3/-45.8/-69.0/-91.1 dB on main, -6.4/-16.9/-18.3/-18.3 now. Not heard by a human.
### Musou Mode: the retainers back, no Ork ammunition boxes (branch `claude/retainers-no-ammo-drops`, 2026-11-08; Musou Mode only, `TfwRules.Version` 44, no protocol or wire change)
The owner, 2026-11-08: "remove the ammo box drops from ork kills in musou mode. return the player retainer bots with orders as well." **Boxes:** `TfwDropBox` (an enemy KO's ammunition or equipment box, owner's item 3) is behind `TfwRewardRules.KillBoxes`, now false (`World.TfwKillBoxes` turns it on for the box tests); Boss Orks lose their sure box too. Not touched: a player's own death drop (the core's `StepPickups`, a separate path, still runs in Musou for humans and AI Marines), the golden weapon drops and the weapon crates, and Classic PvP. **Retainers:** restored beside the two roaming Marines of `hotfix/musou-allies-two` (a4a4b393), which stay: `MarineRole` is back as Retainer / Ally; `TfwRun.Marines` holds both and `TfwRun.Pair` the pair alone (`AllyRules.Count` counts the pair only); `World.TfwSpawnRetainer` in `TfwRun.Land` and `JoinLate`, `MarineOrders` / `TfwOrderMarines` / `TfwTakeOrders` and `TfwRun.Order` (Follow, Hold, Attack to the sender's retainer only; the pair takes none), `MarineBrain.PlanRetainer` with `RetainerSituation` (the old Plan), the 180 war-second recovery on the war clock (`TfwRun.StepRecovery`, `WarTimeScale`), the owner's revive (the window stays open while the own retainer or a Marine of the pair stands), the own block's retainer state, order and recovery, the retainer wearing its owner's look (the pair the host's). Client: Z/X/V orders, the crosshair-enemy Attack, the battle panel hint and the RETAINER HUD line are back as before a4a4b393; the revive prompt names YOUR RETAINER while it stands, else THE ALLIED MARINES. The lane lords, their retainers and the six Defenders stay gone. The orders never left the wire (commands Follow/Hold/Attack, `TfwOwnView` Retainer/Order/RecoverySeconds), so the protocol is unchanged. Tests: `TfwRetainerTests` (ported from before a4a4b393 without the lords), `TfwRewardsTests.Ork_kills_leave_no_ammunition_box_in_musou`; the pair's and co-op's tests now count the pair by `Pair` and a retainer per human.
**Revert: Musou grenades back to vanilla (musou/grenades-vanilla, 2026-11-08; Musou Mode only; `TfwRules.Version` 44, `MusouSim.Version` 22, both to be renumbered at integration; no protocol change).** Owner, verbatim: "revert the change to grenades in musou mode - make them function as they do in vanilla space marine". Reverted: (1) item 21's three-frag fan (24 degrees apart) is gone: one press, one frag (`World.TfwFrags` removed); (2) the doubled blast radius and fall-off (`TfwCombatRules.BiggerFrag`, `FragRadiusScale`, `FragsPerThrow`, `FragSpreadDegrees` removed): the data's radius, fall-off and damage; (3) the thrower is no longer spared (`IgnoreSelf` false as in Classic); (4) a human life carries the item's `SpawnCount` (Classic's count), not the full `Count`; (5) the tag 11 kind Frag and the client's two-ring effect stay in the contract but nothing sends them. The late-D "grenade mass kill" work was measurement only (no rule), so nothing more to revert there; the Stormboy crash and Squig burst already use the plain data frag. The grenade refill (`TfwGrenadeRefill`) stays, now every 15 s instead of 30 (owner, 2026-11-08: "vanilla grenades every 15s"; pinned by `TfwSupplyTests`), the only restock now that Ork ammo drops are being removed. Finding: a single frag that strikes the front of a crowd in the air (12 to 16 m ahead in the test rig) stalled against it at almost no speed and never went off (hidden before by the two side frags); `TfwGrenadeBurstTests` put the crowd 24 m ahead. Not fixed (outside the revert). Tests: `TfwMeleeTests` (one frag, data radius, thrower hurt-able, no Frag record), `TfwGrenadeBurstTests`.
**Fix: Musou corpse arcs (claude/corpse-arcs, 2026-11-08; client only, Musou Mode only, no protocol, rules or hash change).** The owner: "completely remove the corkscrewing corpses flying in the air in musou mode. corpses should never fly in a way that is not a natural looking straight line parabolic arc away from the explosion." Causes, both paths of a blast death (`MusouGoreRules.Thrown`): the near ragdolls (`MusouRagdolls.Throw`) gave each of the 15 parts its own random 1.5 m/s scatter and 8 rad/s spin, which wound the joints into a twisting corkscrew; the crowd's tumbling bodies (`MusouCrowd.AddFlung`) spun at up to 9 rad/s about a random axis integrated every frame (a helix about the chest); the throw's direction varied 35 degrees; a wall threw a body back and the floor bounced it. Now one engine-free rule (`SmNet.Extras.Musou.MusouFling`): the flat velocity never changes in the air, gravity 9.8, one tumble about the horizontal axis square to the flight (head leading away from the blast) at a quarter turn per flight time, at most 2.5 rad/s; a crowd body's turn is computed from its flight time (at most 90 degrees), not integrated; a ragdoll leaves as one rigid body (all parts the same velocity plus the tumble's turn about the chest, gravity scale 1, no linear damping, angular damping 0.5) and takes its own damping back 0.15 s after the arc's flight time, then settles as before; the throw's spread is 8 degrees (`MusouGoreRules.ThrowSpreadDegrees`); no bounce; a wall stops the flat travel. Knockdowns from charges and hammers are clip-driven (no spin): unchanged. Classic PvP's death ragdoll (`Ragdoll.cs`) untouched. Tests: `MusouFlingTests` (3: away from the blast and up, one horizontal axis square to the flight with the cap, a straight monotonic ground track and one arc), `MusouGoreTests` (spread). Preview: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\cache\previews\musou-corpse-arcs\after\` (the death-spike aid, 30 Orks, a fixed spectator camera; bursts at frames 20 to 27, 50 to 56, 80 to 86). Spec "Musou: corpse arcs".
**Musou: the Guardsmen spread out on the way and round a held point (musou/guard-spread, 2026-11-08; `TfwRules.Version` 44, `MusouSim.Version` unchanged, no protocol or wire change; Musou Mode only, the near simulated Guardsmen).** The owner: "guardsmen need to spread out much more when running to a point. after its captured they splinter and spread out around the point to defend it. on the way to the point guardsmen get stuck on corners and walk in straight lines directly next to walls. they need to spread out." Cause: every man followed the shared ally field from his own node (`FlowField.Next`), the shortest way, so a squad became one file along walls and round corner tips, and stood as one 2 x 5 block on the point. Now (`GuardRules.Spread`, false restores the old walk; all numbers ours, spec "Musou Mode: the Guardsmen spread out on the way and round a held point"): on the move a man's place is a loose two-rank order (3.5 m abreast, ranks 3 m, the second rank half a gap aside, a fixed per-man shift up to 0.75 m) round the squad's place, squads in three lanes 6 m apart, each place pulled in until it is 1 m off walls and in a straight walkable line of the squad's place (`GuardSim.FitScale`, every 6 ticks a man); the order closes over the last 6 m. The squad's way and a blocked man's way take, of the field's neighbours that get nearer, the best directness + 1.5 x wall clearance (to 2 m) (`GuardSim.WayNext`; no new field, always nearer so no loop). A man getting under 30 % of his step for 0.5 s detours 2 s by the way or sideways. `TfwBattle.Send` now passes the point's radius: on arrival a squad splits into 3 fire teams over 120 degrees round its own bearing at 0.8 of the radius, each beside cover (`GuardSim.SetPosts`, `CoverSpot`), facing out. Armies' squads (S6) walk in the open order but keep their hold blocks. Measured, the new aid `smtool musou-guard-route` (Ashfall's generated graph, six squads from the landing zone to each position, no Orks; SVG + PNG + `route-log.txt` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\cache\previews\musou-guard-spread`): man-samples beside a wall on the way 28.6 / 19.9 / 10.8 % old to 8.9 / 7.8 / 7.2 % (positions 0 / 1 / 2), mean distance to the nearest man on the way 0.66 to 0.78 m old, 1.40 to 1.56 m new (3.1 m on open ground), last man in 54 to 107 s old, 58 to 110 s new, every man on the point at the end in both. Tick time, `tools/musou-perf.ps1 -Scene clash200 -Headless` (a garrison of 200 plus the field, 260 Guardsmen, about 1600 Orks; other sessions' work on the same CPU): before whole tick mean 7.88 ms, p50 7.25, p99 median 24.0, guards section 0.36 ms mean; after 5.82 / 5.66 / 8.0 ms, guards 0.28 ms; send 60.1 and 59.7 KB/s a client; the difference is within the machine's noise, no rise. Tests `TfwGuardSpreadTests` (open order, lanes, fire teams, wall clearance round AllyNavTests' wall, a detour round a wall on the point, determinism); `GuardSimTests`, `AllyNavTests`, `TfwGuardFormationTests`, `TfwBattleTests`, `GuardHoldTrialTests`, `TfwArmyTests` and the other Musou battle classes pass. Not verified: no human has seen it; the balance (`GuardHoldTrial` spawns its squads standing, unchanged, but spread men in a real battle may fight differently); the full `dotnet test` not run.
**Musou melee feel (musou/melee-feel, 2026-11-08; Musou Mode only, `TfwRules.Version` 44 (other Musou branches bump today too: the lead renumbers at integration); no wire change).** The owner: "bring back the slashing visual effect that would appear over enemies that were hit by player melee attacks. make the effect red for chain weapons and the combat knife, blue for power weapons. add a bit of screen shake. increase the aoe cleave radius of all melee weapons". Why the slash was gone: the M10 slash (item 22) was drawn by `MusouGoreFrame` through the dark `GoreView`, and since the original Ork blood replaced the dark gore (2026-11-07) `GoreView()` is null and the frame returns before the hit events. The slash is now its own view (`MusouSlashView`, `NetworkView.MusouSlash.cs`, called from `MusouHitFx` on every marker 3 hit, whatever the gore setting): a glowing curved stroke, red for the chain weapons and the knife, blue for the power weapons (`MusouSlashRules.ColourOf`; every wargear in the data fits one of the two; a retainer's weapon is unknown, so red); the dark gore no longer draws its own slash. The own melee hit shakes the camera 0.008 rad (0.001 for each further enemy, a swing capped at 0.014; `--musou-melee-shake f`). The cleave's reach (core range + 0.5 m) is times 1.5 (`MusouCombatRules.CleaveRadiusScale`) in the war for every melee weapon, the Scrap Mek melee too; the 5-wave skirmish keeps the old reach (its replay pin). Tests: `MusouMeleeFeelTests` (reach, colour per wargear, shake cap), with `TfwMeleeTests`, `MusouGoreTests`, `MusouSkirmishPinTests` and the rest of the Tfw tests passing; the full `dotnet test` not run. Screenshots (scripted feed, `--musou-slash-weapon`): `previews/musou-melee-feel/musou-slash-red.png` and `musou-slash-blue.png`. Test aids: `--no-musou-slash`, `--musou-melee-shake f`, `--musou-slash-weapon wargear`.
**Ork facing (musou/ork-facing, 2026-11-08; `MusouSim.Version` 22, `TfwRules.Version` 44).** Owner: orks should face the player more; gunners ran away yet still shot. Cause: server-side (a gunner's facing snapped to the target on burst start and otherwise followed its walk), the wire (256 yaw steps) and the client's angle interpolation are fine. `MusouSim.Facing.cs`: `TurnTo` (limited turn), `MusouFacingRules` (fire cone 30 degrees, gunner turn 720 deg/s, engaged turn 480 deg/s, engage range 1.5x ranged range / 10 m melee; all ours, spec "Musou Mode: Orks face their target"). Behave/Big Shoota: rounds only within the cone, `_faceWant` makes a moving engaged Ork face its target. Tests: `MusouFacingTests` (facing away turns then fires within the cone for Shoota and Rokkit, backing off faces the target, a Boy closes in facing it); the skirmish replay golden recaptured. Tick: 600 Orks, 0.586 to 0.623 ms a tick (sim only, about +6 percent). Not run: the full `dotnet test`, a live server SM_TICK_STATS run, the client by eye. Other Musou branches also bump the versions; renumber at integration.

**Musou combat feel, the pilot (claude/combat-feel, 2026-11-09; client only, Musou Mode only, plus two Options rows for every mode; no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner's combat-feel brief; plan, the pilot pair (the power sword's strikes, the bolt pistol), predicted cosmetic contact and the options approved by him that day. **Measured before** (127.0.0.1, `--feel-probe`): press to predicted reaction 0.3 to 1.1 ms (every action); predicted contact to the server's hit report 181 to 209 ms, median 186 (the client 5 to 7 ticks ahead of the newest snapshot: the input lead the lead is fixing); only the own melee hit sound played at contact; the slash, flash, shake, blood, shot impact, gun hit sound and markers waited for the report; the crowd is drawn 3 ticks (~100 ms) behind the report's tick. **Changed** (`MusouContactRules`, `MusouContactLedger`, `NetworkView.MusouContact.cs`; core hooks `ExtrasOwnStrikeContact`, `ExtrasOwnShotEnd`, `ExtrasOwnShotContact`, `ExtrasShakeTotal`): the own power sword strike shows its slash (its own faster, thinner, brighter stroke), the lead flash, the capped shake and the secondary hit sounds on the Orks the client sees in the server's cleave reach and count (20 in the war, 8 in the skirmish) on the frame of the predicted hit; the own bolt pistol's shot stops at the first Ork on its ray (the server's body shape, `MusouSim.ShotBodyOf`) with its flesh impact and hit sound on the shot's frame; the server's report of that Ork within 0.6 s adds no second copy; deaths, gore and the hit and kill markers stay the server's (no kill predicted). Own gun hit sounds one a shot, 10 a second. Musou's shakes no longer stack (strongest + 25 %, cap 0.04 rad). The rank and file are drawn pushed back from blows (0.12 m shot, 0.2 m melee, 0.15 s), clip and facing kept; the old flinch (a stagger clip pushed along the Ork's own facing, the 180-degree turn of 2026-11-06) stays off. Options: Camera shake and Screen flashes (0 to 100 %, default 100 % = as before; the game has no vibration). **Measured after**: the contact feedback plays on the predicted contact's frame (0 ms after it, by construction) instead of 156 to 250 ms later; predicted contacts the server confirmed: 10 of 10, 6 of 6, 5 of 6, 11 of 12 in four runs after matching the server's cleave count (before that fix 118 of 146: the client predicted up to 24, the server strikes 20); frame times unchanged within the noise (dense run p99 22 to 32 ms both ways). Independent review fixed before commit: a report matches only a predicted contact of its own kind (melee or shot), the shielded Weirdboy is never predicted (his shield's pulse is the server's), knocked and dying Orks are not pushed. Movie Maker with the Compatibility renderer crashes Godot at the map load (that renderer's evidence is stills). Switches `--musou-old-contact`, `--no-musou-recoil`; aids `--log-musou-contact`, `--feel-probe`, `--tfw-feel-capture` (a short scripted fight for captures), `--tfw-melee-aim`, `--tfw-melee-pistol`. Tests `MusouContactTests`, `GameOptionsTests`. Captures in the owner's media folder (`<media folder>\previews\musou-combat-feel`). Not done: the other weapons (they keep the confirmed path until the owner has seen the pair), the elites' armour feedback, the sound mix by ear (all runs were silent), a human playtest.
**Musou air jumps launch aloud (sound/musou-air-jump-sound, 2026-11-08; client only, no protocol change).** The owner: "additional jumps in musou mode (assault marine, raptor) make no noise. they should make the same noise as the initial jump." Cause: the launch sound posted on the edge into a jump from no jump or pound (`Jumping(now) && !wasUp`); an air jump goes from the hang or the fall (both counted as jumping) to the take-off, so it never fired. `SmContent.JumpLaunchSoundRules.LaunchesNow` adds that transition (also the ascent when a snapshot skipped the take-off); only Musou lets a jump start there (`SimConfig.JumpPackAirJumps`), so Classic PvP is unchanged (the test checks the old rule everywhere else, the pound escape stays silent). Tests in `JumpFlightPoseTests`. Not heard by a human.

**Musou far battle and Marine barks (musou/battle-ambience, 2026-11-08; client and tools only, Musou Mode only, no protocol or hash change).** The owner: "add looping barks and voice lines for orks, bolter fire, lasgun fire, artillery, explosions. any time artillery explosion sounds play the screen shakes a tiny bit - semi often in musou mode, to make the map feel more alive"; "add random barks for space marines, the player, allied space marines, retainers in musou mode. use intense voice lines from the campaign for this purpose." `SmContent.MusouAmbienceScheduler` (five kinds, each on its own clock: Ork mobs of 2 to 4 voices, bolter and lasgun bursts, artillery heard late by distance, explosions; 35 to 140 m round the listener) played by `NetworkView.TfwBattleAmbienceFrame` in battles through the sound system (own voice group, at most 14 voices); every artillery boom, the old war bed's too, shakes the camera 0.01 rad at most every 4 s (Reduce motion: none). Marine barks: `MusouMarineBarkRules` and `MusouBarkClock`; the player as Titus, the allied pair and other players as Sidonus or Leandros; campaign lines found in the speech bank's unnamed dialogue events (`HircDialogueEvent.LeavesUnder`, `AudioCatalog.DialogueLeaves` and `PostNode`, `SoundSystem.PostLine`; new `smtool audio-speech`), every 6 to 14 s near Orks, else 20 to 40 s. Measured on a real server with a hidden windowed client in a battle: about 3.3 far sounds a second, a shake every 5.5 s, Titus barking every ~28 s while calm; ally barks not seen (the allied pair walked out of 60 m). Tests `MusouBattleSoundsTests`. Not heard by a human; which lines are "intense" is a guess (the keys are unnamed).
**Musou: at most 20 bodies thrown per grenade throw (claude/corpse-arcs, 2026-11-08; server and client; MusouSim.Version 22, so a new config hash).** The owner: "limit the number of flying orks per grenade throw to 20. the rest get knocked down or if they died explode." `World.MusouBlast` (a frag's, a launcher's or a plasma burst; not the bolt blasts, a melee stomp, artillery or Ork blasts) now orders its enemies nearest the blast first (`SortNearest`, ties by id) and gives each owner a budget of `MusouCombatRules.BlastThrownMax` = 20 thrown deaths per throw: blasts of the same owner within `BlastThrowWindowSeconds` = 0.5 s of the first share it (a throw is a fan of 3 frags). Kills past it die as `MusouDeathKind.BoltBlast` (torn apart, no corpse; already on the wire since version 21). A fodder Ork the blast leaves alive (from the stagger intensity) is knocked down (`KnockDown`, thrown back the old knockback); elites stagger as before. With the corpse arcs above this also matches the client's pool of 20 ragdolls. Test: `TfwMeleeTests.One_grenade_throw_throws_at_most_twenty_bodies_the_other_kills_are_torn_apart_and_survivors_fall` (40 Boys round a frag: 20 thrown, 20 torn apart, 3 tough Boys knocked down). Spec "Musou: corpses a throw sends flying".
**Musou Mode: plasma pierces and burns (musou/plasma-pierce-burn, 2026-11-08; Musou Mode only, `TfwRules.Version` 49, `MusouSim.Version` 24, no protocol change; the integration is at 48 and 23, the lead renumbers).** The owner: "in musou mode all plasma weapons should pierce all enemies the shot passes through + do burning lingering plasma damage over time to them." In a war, a shot or ball of any plasma weapon (`TfwCombatRules.PlasmaShot`: gun, pistol, cannon, light and charged) no longer stops at its per-weapon cap (`TfwPierceProjectile`, `TfwPierceShot`): each enemy on its path takes its direct damage once, with no 0.85 fall-off; the map still stops it and a charged ball's splash goes off where it ends. Each enemy hit burns (`World.TfwPlasma.cs`): 50 % of the hit in 6 ticks 0.5 s apart over 3 s (ours, low confidence: the owner gave no numbers), renewed to 6 ticks by a new hit and never stacked, a quarter of each tick on the Warboss and Boss Orks, quiet ticks (new `MusouSim.Damage(quiet)`, no Hit event), kills credited to the shooter. Tag 11 kind Burn (7) tells the clients; `NetworkView.TfwPlasmaBurn.cs` draws two blue-white billboard flames per burning enemy in one MultiMesh (192 quads, 70 m, placeholder look). Tests: `TfwPlasmaTests` (20: five Orks hit, the bolter's cap, the wall, a ball through five bursting on the wall, the switch off, six ticks totalling half the hit, quiet ticks, renewal, boss share, kill credit, the Burn record over the wire, which weapons, Classic PvP plasma stops on the first player). Not run: the full `dotnet test`; the client flame was built, not looked at in a playtest.
**Musou: solid big Orks and the melee lock on them (musou/boss-collision, 2026-11-08; `MusouSim.Version` 24, `TfwRules.Version` 49, no protocol or wire change; Musou Mode only).** The owner: "musou mode - boss and elite and warboss orks should have collision with the player - lock on of melee weapons should work with them as well." Before it a player passed through every Ork (they only kept a soft ring off the players themselves) and the lock (protocol 32) knew only players. Now `MusouSolids` makes the Warboss, Nobs, the four Boss Orks, the Big Shoota Nob, the Weirdboy and the Scrap Mek (not dying or vanishing) solid: the shared movement step's bodies (`PlayerCollision`) take a body of its own radius and height that never steps aside (`PlayerBody.Radius/Height/Fixed`, all 0/false for players, so Classic's math is the same; `PlayerCollision.Relate` gained a two-height form). The bodies follow protocol 43's picture: the World keeps each tick's big Orks (`World.MusouSolids.cs`, hook `ExtrasRecordBodies`/`ExtrasBodies` in `WorldBodies.cs`), quantised as the entity records carry them (`MusouSolids.Quantised`, the one quantisation `MusouWire` now uses too; the server's send hook sets `MusouSim.WireBox`); the client builds the same bodies from its crowd records at the input's body tick (`MusouClientState.SolidsAt`, `MusouSolidView`, set on `GameClient.ExtrasSolids` by the Musou view). The lock: the step's lock view (`World.LockView`, `GameClient.LockViewAt`) adds each big Ork as a living player of no side under id 60000 + its id, standing at its body's front toward the attacker less a player's radius; melee hits, charges and shots keep the players' view (`SeenBy`, `ViewAt`). Wire: nothing new (the leaders are sent first, near ones every tick). Ordinary Boys and Gretchin stay walk-through. Tests (`MusouSolidsTests`): a sprint into each big kind stops at the radii's sum on the server, Boys/Shoota Boys/Gretchin are walked through, the own prediction built from the wire's records equals the server's position bit for bit over 120 ticks of sliding round a Warboss with a Boss Nob near, the lock takes a Nob in the cone and not a Boy and a locked press starts the attack, Classic's lock view is `SeenBy` itself. Related suites (player collision, solid bodies, melee lock, charge clash and lock, isolation, Musou wire, client, send, boss, combat) 230/230. Not run: the full `dotnet test`. Note: the Weirdboy is solid but still teleports away from anyone who closes in; a bot client without the Musou view collides with the players only (the server corrects it).
**Musou: smooth crowd motion (branch `claude/crowd-smooth-456d46`, 2026-11-08; Musou Mode only; `MusouSim.Version` 22, no core protocol bump).** The owner: "musou mode - stormboyz look extremely choppy while jumping and flying ... do the same for all guardsmen, orks." Measured first with a new engine-free metric (`MusouCrowdSmoothnessTests`: probes with known true paths among 300 or 1,800 Orks and 100 or 300 Guardsmen through the real send interests, event window and client states at 60 fps; per group the frame-to-frame step change and its deviation from the true step, stalls, distance from the true place, turns per frame). Causes: a hopping Stormboy (Airborne) was never carried on or glided and was drawn on chords, so he hung in the air and jumped up to 9.6 m; the Guardsmen had no carry-on or glide and got only the 3 KB/s Musou left of the client's budget (a far man drawn still in 97 % of his moving frames); the overdue far Orks took a full budget and a Boy fighting 3 m away had a record every 6th tick; facings stepped per record. Fixes: the hop cue carries the flight's ticks (event player field; `MusouSim.Version` 22) and the client draws the pool's exact arc (`MusouClientState.ArcOf`), holding a landed Stormboy on the landing until a ground record; every Ork and Guardsman glides (place and facing, `DrawnMotion`), Guardsmen and runners starting from a stand are carried on (`CrowdMotionRules`); the server sends a near Ork at least every 2nd tick before the overdue far ones (`MusouSendRules.NearMaxWaitTicks`) and gives the Guardsmen at least 8 KB/s, charged back to Musou's next refill (`TfwSendRules.GuardFloorBytesPerSecond`, the client's total unchanged at about 58 KB/s); a skinned crowd member stays skinned 3 m past the near line (`CrowdView.SkinnedHoldMetres`). Result under a full budget, before / after: Stormboys' worst step off the true one 619 to 928 cm / 14 to 19 cm (p99), up to 9.65 m / 1.8 m off (3.7 m once, near); Guardsmen 0.2 to 0.4 cm and 6 cm at most against up to 5.45 m; near fighters 0.83 / 0.10 m. Left: a landed Stormboy stands until his next ground record (up to 15 ticks far: 8 to 14 % of his moving frames under a full budget), the far Orks lost 5 KB/s to the Guardsmen (30 m runners 0.14 to 0.19 m off). Live run (Ashfall, `SM_TFW_STORMBOY_TEST=1`): server tick and bytes unchanged within noise; a hop's frames in the owner's cache `previews/musou-crowd-smooth/stormboy-hop` (before-/after-NNN, 0.1 s apart). Test aids: client `--musou-old-crowd-motion`, server `SM_MUSOU_OLD_NEAR_RATE=1`, `SM_TFW_OLD_GUARD_SHARE=1`. Spec "Musou Mode: smooth crowd motion". Not seen by a human; the AI Marines (player snapshots) and the far armies (tag 18's own easing) unchanged.
**Fix: no flicker on Ashfall's walls and kit models (fix/ashfall-no-flicker, 2026-11-08; client only, Musou Mode only, no protocol, level or hash change).** The owner: "there is still flickering all over the map in ashfall musou mode with FSR off, and the wall objects and other instances of them around the map are flickering with all variations of FSR on", with a recording (2560 x 1440, FOV 120, grime EXACT). Its frames (extracted with the portable Blender) show whole blocks of the boundary wall switching between the plain and the darker, grittier face from frame to frame, and under FSR 2 a speckle over the same blocks. Two causes, both found by measurement: (1) the boundary's masonry shader hashed each block's variant from floor() of the interpolated face coordinate, and the faces lie on whole metres, so the hash flipped between two neighbours with every sub-pixel camera change or FSR jitter; the face is now a per-vertex rounded, flat varying. (2) The kit models' grime overlay and its multiply pass (the overlay's next pass) tied in the transparent sort, so per instance and per frame either drew first (about 12 % apart where the soot lies): whole floor slabs and wall feet switched brightness with any camera change, in about half the launches (chance decided it). Attribution within one launch: the depth pull's size (0 to 1e-2) changed nothing, the overlay without the multiply or the multiply without the overlay's colour was clean; fixed render priorities (overlay -12, multiply -11, between the cut-outs and the ground decals) cure it in 6 of 6 launches against 4 of 6 bad with the old order. Not causes: coplanar or overlapping placements (none under the switching slabs; the drawn ground 15 cm lower changed nothing), volumetric fog, light shafts, SSAO/SSIL, sun shadow, omni lights, mesh LODs. The flicker check (gallery `--ashfall-shimmer` with `--shimmer-region full`, `--shimmer-move jitter`, `--shimmer-aa off|fsr-*`, FLICKER lines; the Compatibility renderer with `--rendering-method gl_compatibility`): changed patches over the whole frame, wall view like the recording, before -> after: MSAA + SMAA 0.68 -> 0.002 %, AA off 0.63 -> 0.008 %, FSR 2 Native (all changed pixels) 1.69 -> 0.26 %, Quality 0.084 -> 0.000 %, Balanced 0.049 -> 0.000 %, Performance 0.062 -> 0.000 %, Compatibility 0.42 -> 0.021 %, a slow turn 1.2-1.5 -> 0.000 %; gate view (grime order) MSAA 2.1 -> 0.011 %, AA off 3.5 -> 0.005 %, plaza 2.4 -> 0.023 %. What remains is edge creep on silhouettes and slab joints under the jitter, the same with no grime. Spec "Ashfall boundary block variant per face" and "Ashfall grime pass order"; test aids `--ashfall-old-wall-hash`, `--ashfall-grime-order old`; tests `AshfallNoFlickerTests`. Frames, heat maps and strips in the private previews folder `ashfall-no-flicker`. Not verified: the owner's own playtest at his settings; a real match (the check uses the gallery's frozen map with the game's camera).

**Plasma light shot as a small charged shot (fix/plasma-light-tracer, 2026-11-08; client presentation only, no simulation, wire, protocol or config-hash change; all modes).** The owner: the plasma pistol has no tracers, all plasma weapons but the cannon should have a larger tracer, "model the light shot tracer after the charged shot tracer exactly, but scale it down to .75%" (read as 75 %, 0.75x). Cause of the pistol's missing tracer: its `BasicAbility` is the charge ability (`ability_ranged_primary`), whose delivery names no tracer; the real basic shot is its secondary, and the fallback of fx/tracers-impact found none to draw there (not read from the install by this session; the new path no longer needs a data tracer). Now the light shot of the plasma gun and pistol (either side) launches a ball like the charged one (`ProjectileLook` of the highest projectile stage, same material) and plays the charged projectile's trail effects (same tint), all at 0.75, from the muzzle straight to the end point at the charged speed or whatever crosses in 0.1 s (`PlasmaLightShot`, `NetworkView.PlasmaLightShot.cs`); a pistol still coming up releases it from the raised muzzle; no sprite-shader-only bolt, so the Compatibility renderer draws it the same way (ball = plain unshaded mesh; the trail is the charged shot's own effect: not verified on an old card). Tests: `PlasmaLightShotTests` (scale, which weapons, charged stage, flight cap); `TracerRulesTests` still pass. Test aids: `--old-light-bolt`; capture `--bolt-fx-charged` (with `--bolt-fx-demo`: the charged reference ball instead). Screenshots, light left and charged right, gun and pistol: `<media folder>\previews\plasma-light-tracer\forward-plus\` (`gun_light_vs_charged.png`, `pistol_light_vs_charged.png`) and, in the Compatibility renderer (SAFE MODE on, the ball and trail draw like the charged shot's; both show the same hard-edged blue slab at the trail's front, pre-existing), `...\compat\*_light_vs_charged_compat.png`. Not run: the full `dotnet test`; own first-person view; a clean first-person capture; Musou in-game.

**Plasma trail slab fix (fix/plasma-trail-slab, 2026-11-09; client only; owner: "too blocky ... smooth it out and make it a distinct thick bolt of plasma").** Cause: the charged ball's data trail (`plasma_gun_charged_trail`) holds two `Streamer` ribbons, `short trail` (beam_gradient, 2 to 4 m wide) and `blue trail` (add_trail_soft, 1 to 6 m wide), which draw as hard-edged quads: the blue slab. The gun's and pistol's ball trails (light shot and charged shot, Forward+ and Compatibility; not the plasma cannon, untouched) no longer draw those streamers (`FxEffect.SoftHead`) and instead get a smooth thick bolt behind the ball: a soft glow ribbon (1.1 m wide at the charged size, 0.75x for the light shot) round a hot core, 4 m long, the side's colour, a plain mesh (`BallBoltNote`/`DrawBallBolts`, `NetworkView.PlasmaLightShot.cs`); the ball, its light, sparks and rings are as before. Also fixed: the light ball's mesh was placed in world space under the game-space projectile root (now `ToLocal`), and a hitch frame could skip a ball (drawn at least once). Test aids: `--old-trail-slab` (the data ribbons), `--log-ball-bolt`. Captures: `<media folder>\previews\plasma-light-tracer\slab-fix4\` (light shot with the new bolt, Forward+ and Compatibility). Not run: the full `dotnet test`; the charged bolt from a real server projectile (only the demo's reference ball); a player's-view capture.

**Plasma light ball: real speed, the data's trail softened (fix/plasma-trail-slab, 2026-11-09, second pass; client only; supersedes the thick bolt above).** The owner: copy the original's projectile look and ballistics; asked which, he chose: the light shot keeps its instant hit and damage (the data's raycast), the drawn ball flies at "real speed, faster than 90 if possible, no drop", and the look is "the original data look, softened". So: the light ball flies at 2x the charged ball's 90 m/s = 180 m/s (`PlasmaLightShot.SpeedFactor`, ours), no drop, no 0.1 s cap; its impact effect waits for it (the existing travel delay). The thick bolt (`BallBoltNote`) is gone; the data's trail effects play again at 0.75 (light) or 1 (charged), their streamers softened: the ribbon head swells from a point over its first 40 % and fades in, the tail fades out over its last 40 % (colour and alpha: additive materials ignore alpha alone), so no hard-edged rectangle starts or ends it (`FxEffect.SoftHead`, `FxPlayer.DrawStreamer`; plasma gun and pistol only, not the cannon). The charged shot's ballistics are the server's, from the data (speed 90, gravity x0 to 5 s then x0.75), unchanged. Tests: `PlasmaLightShotTests` (scale, weapons, charged stage, 2x speed). Captures: `<media folder>\previews\plasma-light-tracer\soft-data2\` (charged reference, soft trail before the tail fade) and `soft-data3\` (after: the demo's slow-motion frames only caught the shot's start, not the flight). Not verified: the final softened trail in flight (head and tail ends), the pistol, the plasma cannon for the same slab, a real server charged shot, player's view, Musou, the full `dotnet test`.

**Musou audio pass (musou/audio-pass, 2026-11-09; client only, Musou Mode only; no protocol, wire, hash or Musou-rule change).** The owner's four sound items. Cause of the cut melee hits, found by reading the voice code: the pool of 48 positioned voices is full in a Musou crowd, and a new voice steals the quietest, oldest one, which releases a one-shot mid-play; the power axe and thunder hammer hit events also carry Stop actions; and the data's hits are short (0.16 to 0.7 s). Cause of the muffled barks: the data's explosions post Set/Reset volume and low-pass actions (`play_big_damage_med_explosion` carries 11) that apply to every voice, plus voice stealing and the SmSfx limiter. New: `SoundEmitter.ProtectSpeech` (the own character's lines) and `SoundEmitter.Tail` (melee hits), set only through Musou hooks (`ExtrasTrackEmitter`, `ExtrasMeleeHitEmitter`), so Classic PvP routes every voice as before; `MusouAudioRules` (gate, bolter list, numbers), `NetworkView.MusouAudio.cs` (deep fire layer, thump, first-hit smack then blast), far Ork mobs at 60 to 130 m, -8 dB, low-pass +40. Test aid `--no-musou-audio-pass`. Not heard by a human: the refine register lists every number.
 **Melee reverted (2026-11-09, owner):** the melee hit tail, protection flags, reverb buses, the power sword's +6 dB and borrowed curve are removed; every melee hit sounds as in Classic PvP. The own bark also waits 2 s after a melee attack.

**Musou: a 120 KB/s stream and the client's own volleys, part 1 (claude/musou-net-budget-7251f4, 2026-11-09; server send budget and an engine-free client planner; Musou Mode only, no protocol, wire or config-hash change).** The owner: "can we feasibly increase the network packet budget to increase the visual showcase ... a ton of tracers, lots of actions", then "option 2 plus a 120 KB/s budget ... maximize client sided rendering/drawing effects". **Measured first** (`tools/musou-perf.ps1 -Scene clash500 -Headless`, a temporary per-kind event counter, not committed): the stream was full (56-68 KB/s), but of Ork records (39-42 KB/s; about 22,000 due records a second held back at 1,371 Orks), while the events used 0.2-3.2 KB/s with no copy dropped. The tracers are limited by the simulation's shooter tokens (8 Shootas at a player, 10 at a Guard squad) and the client's caps (1 round in 3, 16 tracers/s, 70 m), not by the network. Write-up with every option: side-session notes `musou-net-budget.md`. **Budget:** Musou 110 KB/s in up to 6 messages a tick (55 in 4), the war 35 KB/s with a 15 KB/s floor in up to 3 (20 / 8 / 2), the war's share of the client's stream 104 KB/s (58), so that the whole stream runs at about 120 KB/s: measured 105-128 KB/s at 1,055 to 1,424 Orks (the core snapshot, the sections outside both budgets and the war's reading of Musou's spending put it above the sum; 120 measured 125-135, 112 measured 118-132). Due records held back fell to 0-7 a second; server tick mean 4.7-6.1 ms, no skipped ticks (as before). `SM_MUSOU_OLD_BUDGET=1` (server) restores the old budgets: a test aid, and the switch for a server whose remote players cannot take about 1 Mbit/s. **Volleys:** `MusouVolleyPlanner` (`SmContent/Extras/Musou/MusouVolley.cs`, tests `MusouVolleyTests`) gives every standing Shoota Boy and Boss Shoota Boy near the camera with a player or Guardsman 8-30 m ahead (within 50 degrees of his facing, a clear line) bursts of his own at the Shoota's rhythm, misses only, at most 48 shooters and 24 rounds a frame; an Ork firing for the server is left to it for 2 s. It costs no bytes and no server time; two clients see different volleys. Not yet: drawing them (the hook into the client's gun effects and sounds waits for big-shoota-fx's client-built rounds), the raised client caps, any human look. Pre-existing, found while updating the tests: with more than about 3 times a tick's records of Orks within 15 m, an Ork never sent can stay unsent (the near-overdue order keeps serving the known ones).

**Musou: the client's own volleys drawn, and higher gun caps, part 2 (claude/musou-net-budget-7251f4, 2026-11-09; client only, Musou Mode only, no protocol, wire or config-hash change; built on big-shoota-fx's client-built rounds, 3add8558).** `NetworkView.MusouVolleys.cs` runs `MusouVolleyPlanner` each frame after `MusouRoundsFrame` and adds its rounds to the frame's rounds (`_musouRoundsNow`), so flash, tracer, impact and fire sound follow under the guns' caps; targets are the living players and the shown Guardsmen; a line of sight is the weapons raycast; an Ork firing a server or burst-cue round is left to it for 2 s; it joins within the tracer reach of the camera (120 m). Caps raised (ours, the owner's "a ton of tracers"): Ork tracer every 2nd round (3rd), flash / tracer / impact reach 70 / 120 / 45 m (45 / 70 / 35), 120 flashes, 60 tracers, 40 impacts a second (40 / 16 / 14); the Guardsmen's shot effects 70 / 120 m and 24 a frame (45 / 90 / 12). `--no-musou-volleys` turns the volleys off. **Measured** (windowed client on the hidden desktop, Release server on 127.0.0.1, the Firing Range test aid `--tfw-test-range`, 200 Orks closing on the player; 9 of 9 PASS): from 10 to 30 s the server's burst cues gave 293 rounds and the volleys 753 (257 bursts, up to 42 shooters at once), 1,040 rounds drawn, 519 tracers; the gun effects cost 0.03-0.06 ms a frame; live effects reached the effect player's cap of 160; frames p99 19.7-23.4 ms on this loaded PC. In the clash 500 scene (the player held 35 m short) almost no gun Ork came within 120 m of the camera, so the volleys stay near the player's own fight by design. Not verified: a human's look, an old GPU, the 160-effect cap's eviction under a bigger fight.
**Musou: Ashfall draft 11, the battlefield layout (branch `claude/quizzical-lamarr-2bba9c`, 2026-11-09; Musou Mode only, map `tfw_war_field`, field version 1, level hash `0x94488BF0597BA823`; draft 10 untouched on `tfw_war`, hash `0xA47761F67B43DC1C`; no protocol or `TfwRules` change).** The owner's layout brief (docs/ashfall-layout-brief.md) as one big draft on a separate generator path (`Extras/Musou/Ashfall/Field/`), selected by the map name on server and client (`--map tfw_war_field`; `client.cmd --ashfall-layout field` when hosting) so draft 10 stays the rollback. Protected areas planned first (bases, three moved points with open zones, two assembly areas, ten 24 m army corridors), then four districts of ruin islands and clusters on flat ground; the kit pass runs every standing rule with the corridors as roadways; the stronghold, its twin towers and the compound's walls are copied from draft 10 bit for bit (re-placing them moved pieces). `AshfallBattlefield` measures any layout on its final collision; `smtool ashfall-plan --layout` draws the overlays and lists every constraint, `smtool ashfall-clash` runs the clash bench. Field: all 65 constraints pass (army routes 37.5 to 49.5 m at their narrowest, approaches A 2 / B 6 / C 5, reinforcements at most 80 s, waves at most 51 s); draft 10 fails 27 of 31 (no 20 m route anywhere). Bench at 1,000 a side: frontage 41 m at B and 38 m at A (draft 10: 18 m and 10 m), never single file (draft 10 is at A), retreat 20 to 51 s (draft 10 31 to 74 s). Formation and routing AI investigated (the anchor's single-body route and fixed width), not changed. Tests: `AshfallDraft11Tests` (14). Docs: docs/musou-ashfall-graybox.md "Draft 11 battlefield layout"; previews in `<media folder>\previews\ashfall-battlefield\`.

**Musou: Ashfall draft 12, the city layout replaces draft 10 on `tfw_war` (branch `ashfall/draft10-redo`, 2026-11-09; Musou Mode only, city version 1, level hash `0x1E3B60672DF1809B` after the stair pass; rollback `tfw_war_draft10` = draft 10 bit for bit, hash `0xA47761F67B43DC1C`; `tfw_war_field` draft 11 unchanged; no protocol or `TfwRules` change).** The owner's request ("redo the layout of the ashfall draft 10 map. no stairs inaccessible or blocked by walls or other objects. lined up buildings and walls ... roads placed properly to facilitate movement of armies") on draft 11's plan path (`AshfallCity`, `AshfallLayout.City`): draft 10's ±92 grid widened into twelve 22 m army avenues with edge avenues, a middle avenue and a north loop; A and C moved onto the north avenue, B kept at the crossing; 28 blocks of buildings in rows on one frontage line along their roads with dashed kerb walls; the fortress and the compound copied from draft 10. Stairs: the new final-collision check (`AshfallStairAccess`, walks with the game's movement) found draft 10's two-storey ruins (AC-051, a 1.1 m plinth with a 0.57 m door step) unreachable, 26 flights outside the stronghold; the city gives such flights an entry ramp from the door (else the pool's next model) and its pass enforces the check (nothing left to remove in this run). Numbers: all 66 battlefield constraints pass (draft 10: 27 of 31 fail); army routes 24.6 to 27.4 m at their narrowest (draft 10 14.5 to 19.5); approaches A/B/C 3/5/3 (0/0/0); 210 stairs, none unreachable outside the stronghold; clash bench fronts after 20 s at 1,000 a side B 35, A 37, C 39 m, never single file (draft 10: 18, 10, 9 m, single file at A and C). Open for the owner: the army layer's anchor takes one body's shortest walk, which cuts through the blocks' alleys at A and C (2.3 m); width-aware routing or closed yards would fix it. Not played in a match yet. docs/musou-ashfall-graybox.md "Draft 12 city layout".

**Musou: Ashfall kit stairs, the owner's stair pass (branch `ashfall/draft10-redo`, 2026-11-09; Musou Mode only; city `0x1E3B60672DF1809B`, field version 2 `0x42DC676411C2038C`; draft 10 untouched).** The owner: "fix the greybox collision for the rest of the 3d models that have stairs - you can't walk up all the stairs currently." On the city and the field: entry ramps onto raised floors, ramps for runs over the 0.4 m step, 45-degree ramps for flights the scale made too steep, landing slabs on broken upper floors, 1.6 m flights, rubble mounds under the stair-access rule, and the final-collision stair check enforced on both maps. **Musou: armies route on the avenues (branch `ashfall/draft10-redo`, 2026-11-09; Musou Mode only, `TfwRules.Version` 58; Classic untouched).** The owner: "Yes, route on avenues." The armies' routes are searched with `NavGraph.FindPathWide` (a node's clearance from the walls, a link's cost raised up to 21 times under a 20 m front, shortcuts only as wide as the way), so formations march the avenues; single bodies keep the shortest walk. City, the landing zone to A and C: narrowest 0.0 m before, 25.3 and 26.3 m after (12 s longer marches); clash bench at 1,000 a side: route 4.3 / 2.3 m -> 25.5 / 26.3 m at A / C, first contact 78 / 85 -> 77 / 76 s, the front the avenue's width (15 to 17 m). `smtool musou-army-routes` measures the war's own routes on all three maps; `TfwWideRouteTests`. docs/musou-ashfall-graybox.md "Army routing on the avenues".

**Musou: Ashfall kit detail inside the arena (branch `ashfall/kit-hi-res`, 2026-11-09; Musou Mode only, client and the private kit files; no protocol or rules change; Classic untouched).** The owner: "ensure all the 3d assets used in the main play map are high res". No model had been decimated. The Blender bake had halved the textures and weathered each Meshy file at its 2 m file scale, so the city's 8 to 33 times larger buildings wore building-sized smears over the source's masonry, and the expansion has no normal maps. The 29 models placed inside the arena are re-baked from the source at their arena size and 2048 px: `smtool ashfall-kit-bake-scales`; `ashfall_bake.py --scales`, which fades patterns finer than 6 texels and bakes a relief normal map where the source has none. They load at 2048 and draw finer LODs inside the arena in Forward+ (`AshfallKitDetail`; not in safe mode); models placed only outside keep the 1024 bake. City cost: Forward+ frame 2.6 to 3.9 ms -> 3.0 to 4.9 ms, peak video memory 634 -> 979 MiB; Compatibility frame time unchanged, 322 -> 519 MiB; bundled kit 80.8 -> 141.9 MiB. Collision untouched. `--ashfall-kit-detail old` draws as before; gallery `--ashfall-closeup`. docs/musou-ashfall-graybox.md "Kit detail inside the arena".

**Musou: Ashfall draft 10, lanes and stairs (branch `claude/ashfall-lanes-stairs-a2b890`, 2026-11-09; Musou Mode only, `AshfallMap.Version` 17, `DressVersion` 13, level hash `0xD20B0CBDD8445C42`, no protocol or `TfwRules` change).** The owner: "make a pass at the rendering of the ashfall map. make the lanes to each point from the stronghold, and between each point. there should be clear pathways between them all. strengthen the rule that clears space at the bottom of stairs. currently there are still stairs that cannot be walked up. fix the collision greyboxes for those." **Lanes** (`AshfallLanes`): eight paved connectors 12 m wide (the gate, the plaza's north, west and east edges, A south and east, C south and west) as Road parts, so they are drawn as road and the draft-8 roadway rule keeps every object off them (99 items moved or shrunk, 55 left out, mostly low walls); with the avenues they make nine pathways (the stronghold's courtyard and the Imperial base to A, B, C; A-B, B-C, A-C), each walked end to end both ways with the player's capsule on the whole level. **Stairs** (`AshfallDraft9.cs`, `AshfallStairs.cs`): draft 9 kept 45 and dropped 183, many visible flights (AC-051 ruin stairs 0.5-0.9 m wide, 51-54 degrees, about 70 stalling on the model's own lintels, frames and risers, AC-050 stairs on a plinth). Now narrow flights get a 1.2 m ramp, up to 55 degrees, the foot carried to the floor 1.5 m out, the model's own boxes cleared 1.5 m in front of every foot, a corridor carved through the model's own boxes where the walk stalls, kept only when its foot and landing are open and the walk up and down neither stalls nor lifts over a step in one tick with the model's other flights present, exact neighbours merged; other items keep out of a **3 m** zone at every foot (was 1.5 m), the width plus 0.5 m a side. **143 stairs** (84 carved), all walked up and down on the whole level; 36 dropped (roof steps, steps that do not rise or are 0.2-0.4 m wide, two AC-053 and some AC-044 flights with no landing in the model). Collision 221,600 triangles (budget raised 220 k -> 225 k). **Rendering** (client): a worn kerb band along both edges of every lane and the paved road (one multimesh, `--ashfall-lane-marks off`); gallery KITPERF on the kit look, render GPU ms off -> on, Forward+ (Vulkan, medium): point A 2.23 -> 2.25, overview 5.23 -> 5.20, spawn street 4.12 -> 4.09, gate street 1.81 -> 1.82, +1-3 draw calls; Compatibility (OpenGL 3): 1.07 -> 1.08, 2.33 -> 2.35, 2.19 -> 2.19, 0.83 -> 0.83 (no measurable cost; the level change itself was not measured separately). Tests `AshfallDraft10Tests`; deliberate test changes and what stays open in docs/musou-ashfall-graybox.md "Draft 10 lanes and stairs"; spec rows "Ashfall stairs (draft 10)", "Ashfall lanes (draft 10)", "Ashfall lane marks (draft 10, client)". Shots: `<media folder>\previews\ashfall-lanes-stairs\`. No independent review (owner's rule for Ashfall refinement drafts). **Same day, stair access** (owner: "don't use asset buildings that have stairs with no access point. replace them with properly scaled ones that do."): buildings whose model has a flight with no floor at an end, or one nothing leads to (a roof stair), are refused and replaced by the pool's next model with the same fit, models with walkable stairs first (AC-046, the stair tower, as a replacement-only candidate for towers): 13 replaced (8 towers, 7 of them now AC-046 stair towers), none left out; the keep stays as authored (owner); hash `0xA47761F67B43DC1C`. The owner's layout brief and his answers are in `docs/ashfall-layout-brief.md`.

**Musou: Ashfall kit detail is low in old-GPU mode (branch `ashfall/kit-hi-res`, 2026-11-10; client only).** The owner: "Use low detail ashfall textures for old gpu mode users". In safe mode (the Compatibility renderer, picked on a weak GPU or by the OPTIONS toggle, or `--safe-mode`) the arena models load at 1024 px with the plain LOD threshold, as with `--ashfall-kit-detail old`; Forward+ keeps 2048 px and the finer LODs. The rule is engine-free (`AshfallKitDetailRule`, `AshfallKitDetailRuleTests`); the client logs the detail it picked. The loader also frees each file's full-size textures after shrinking them (they had stayed in video memory). City, peak video memory: Compatibility 519 -> 173 MiB (322 before the hi-res pass), Forward+ 979 -> about 820 MiB. The gallery's `--ashfall-closeup` crashes in the Compatibility renderer, also on dd3bab58's loader; the map view works.
