**Musou: no Ork formations, 80 % of the Orks (branch `claude/musou-ork-movement-fffa33`, 2026-11-09; Musou Mode only; `TfwRules.Version` 53, to be renumbered at integration).** The owner, with a screenshot: "large rectangular formations of orks that move from their points to imperial captured points. they walk through objects, don't interact with the world or fight. completely remove those orks from musou mode ... reduce the total amount of orks on the map to 80% of current." They were expansion S6's Ork army aggregates (counted men past the 480 real cap or 330 m, drawn as up to 900 impostors in formation slots along the army's way). Now an Ork army is real Orks alone (`TfwBattle.MakeOrks`: made in its slots wherever it stands, 16 a tick, never folded back, the rest never made), the client draws no Ork impostor, the far clash and a point's count take only real Orks; the Guard armies keep theirs. Every bulk Ork count at 80 % (armies' real cap 384, waves 160/400/800, garrison 77, crowd 320 at the same 53 s fill, alive caps 960/512/1344, trickle 1280, patrols 32, retinues 16, Big Shoota squads 8, the victory wave 400). Profile (180 s, a wave of 1,000): all Orks at most 2588 to 1684, aggregates 984 to 0, tick mean 7.07 to 2.88 ms, p99 40.0 to 4.4 ms. Tests: `OrkArmyAggregateTests`; the crowd tests' counts updated. Test aids: server `SM_TFW_OLD_ORK_ARMIES=1`, client `--musou-old-ork-armies`, `OrkTotalsProfileTests`. Spec "Musou Mode: no Ork formations, 80 % of the Orks". Not seen by a human.

**Musou: gore by source, the players first (claude/musou-net-budget-7251f4, 2026-11-09; client budgets and the server's event order; Musou Mode only, no protocol, wire, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner: "i'm not consistently seeing gore effects from both ranged and melee attacks ... ensure that all player attacks in particular - then allied space marine attacks have high priority for generating gore effects during heavy fighting. or find a client side workaround." **Traced:** a hit's blood impact (`MusouHitFx`, `OrkBloodHit`) went through one bucket of 16 a second for every attacker and only within 30 m of the camera; a kill's dismemberment (`OrkBloodDeath`) through 8 kills a frame, first come; every blood effect played at priority 0 in an effect player of 160, where the Ork and Guardsmen tracers (priority 1, at the higher rates of the same day) took the room; on the server hits ranked after the crowd's tracers (the event channel itself was not full). **Fix:** `MusouGoreBudget` / `MusouGorePriority` (`SmNet/Extras/Musou/Gore`): own, ally (other humans and AI Marines), other, each with its own rate (40 / 20 / 10 a second), reach (60 / 40 / 30 m) and kills a frame (16 / 8 / 4); blood at priority 2 / 1 / 0 and the crowd's tracers at 0; the server's window ranks a human's hit, then an AI Marine's, after the strikes and before the tracers, and in each client's stream its own kills, then the other deaths, telegraphs and strikes, then its own hits (`MusouInterest.OwnFirst`). Review fixes: the predicted own pilot-gun hits use the own budget and reach too (they kept the old shared bucket), and `--musou-old-gore-budget` restores the one shared bucket exactly. A `musou gore budget:` log line by source and the effect player's drops by priority (`FxPlayer.Evicted`, `Refused`, counters only). `--musou-old-gore-budget` (client) and `SM_MUSOU_OLD_HIT_RANK=1` (server) restore. Tests `MusouGoreBudgetTests` (7). **Measured** (windowed co-op bot `--bot --bot-full-load` on a Release server on 127.0.0.1, 3 AI Marines, up to 2,200 Orks shown, 190 s, same build): own hits that drew their blood 357 of 857 (42 %; 154 refused by the shared rate, 346 beyond 30 m) before, 784 of 819 (96 %; 24 by the rate, 11 beyond 60 m) after; blood refused by a full effect player 1,361 before, 0 at the own priority after; own kills given their blood 0 refused by the cap in either run. Left as found: about a third to a half of the own kills play no dismemberment at all, by the original data's own chance for the weapon and strike (the killing hit's impact still shows); in heavy fighting the effect player is full (160) and drops the oldest own blood when nothing lower is left (130 in the run). Not verified: a human's look; the client's frame cost (not profiled in these runs).

**Musou: Guard vantage teams (musou/guard-vantage, 2026-11-09; Musou Mode only, `TfwRules.Version` 52 (the lead renumbers); no protocol, wire or `MusouSim.Version` change).** The owner: "make small squads of guardsmen position themselves up in buildings randomly at times around the map - they should only position on high ground vantage points with good lines of fire around them within 50m of a friendly captured point. if there is no friendly captured point then they still defend the stronghold/imperial base but also venture out in front of their home base to take up high ground vantage point positions around the imperial base." **Finder** (`GuardVantage.Find`, once a level and base, on a thread of its own at the battle's start; the first team waits on it, so the battle is deterministic): from the walking graph and the weapons mesh alone, no hand-placed spots, so it follows the Ashfall redesign. A node counts when it stands 3 m over the median of the lowest floors 4 to 16 m round it (so a pit's rim or a plateau's middle does not), can be walked to from the base and back (forward and reverse searches over walk and drop links: real stairs, no jump packs), has room for 3 to 6 posts on its own floor in a straight walkable line, and has 30 % of 48 lines of fire (16 directions x 10/20/30 m, eye to a ground chest, raycast on the weapons mesh) clear; one per 3 m bin (highest, then nearest a floor's edge), the best kept 8 m apart. **Teams** (`TfwBattle.Vantage.cs`, `GuardVantageRules`, `Enabled` false restores the old Guardsmen): every 20 to 45 s a team of 3 to 6 men leaves a field squad standing at its post (`GuardSim.Detach`; the squad keeps 4; armies' squads never send one) for a free spot by a score-weighted roll within 50 m of a secured point, or with none in front of the base (towards the Ork HQ) within 50 m, or 100 m on a level with nothing nearer (Ashfall now); it walks the graph's way, takes the spot's posts facing its open side (`GuardSim.OrderPosts`), fires as any squad, holds 60 to 150 s, then walks back and merges into its squad (`GuardSim.Merge`); a lost point or a base spot once a point is taken sends it to the nearest spot that counts, else back; at most 4 out, one a spot. Ashfall (the graph of 755,649 nodes): 95 vantage points, heights 3 to 5.6 m (its walkable floors stop near 6 m), 4 / 7 / 4 within 50 m of points A / B / C, none within 50 m of the base, 8 in front of it within 100 m; the finder took 3.9 s in Debug and 0.97 s in Release (747 candidates, 30,148 rays) off the tick. The aid's battle on Ashfall's graph (teams every 5 to 8 s for the picture, frozen Orks): with B secured, 4 teams sent in 150 s, all 4 holding spots 5.5 m up within 50 m of B, every man (4, 4, 5, 5) on his spot, up a building's stairs; with no point, 6 sent to buildings about 80 m in front of the base, 2 back and merged. Tick cost on the synthetic battle (68,000 nodes): 0.154 ms a tick with teams out against 0.152 ms without (noise). Aid: `smtool musou-guard-vantage [--secure k|none]` (overview and close-up PNG and a log; `<media folder>\previews\musou-guard-vantage\`). Tests `GuardVantageTests` (the finder takes a raised platform and not a pit, a closed room or an unreachable roof; teams only within 50 m of the secured point, one a spot, climbing the ramp at walking speed and all men on the spot; the base's front only, the base squads keeping 4; the far radius; a fallen point; the hold then the merge; the switch; the tick cost) and `GuardVantageAshfallTests` (Slow: counts on Ashfall). Not verified: no human has seen it; the client shows a team's men leave and come back as new ids in the same places (no pop seen yet); the balance of a point's defence with men away; the full `dotnet test`.

**Menu background: the owner's OpenArt picture (ui/menu-background, 2026-11-09; client asset only).** The owner asked for his screenshot-style picture as the main menu background, "but first ... remove the ui elements from the screenshot". The picture is AI-generated by the owner on OpenArt (owner, 2026-11-09: "the screenshot is ai generated by openart, it's not a capture of the game or the original game's models"), so it is new art and may ship. The lead removed its HUD (health bar, crosshair, weapon panel) with one OpenArt Nano Banana 2.1 image-to-image edit and saved it as `client/assets/menu/background.jpg` (2752x1536, JPEG q2; was 3840x2160). `MenuKit.MenuBackground` still covers the window without stretching. Source and cleaned copies: `<media folder>\previews\menu-background\`.
**Musou contraptions destructible (owner, 2026-11-09; branch `musou/contraptions-destructible` from main 45572fae; `TfwRules.Version` 60, no protocol bump).** The owner: "not all of the scrap mek's contraptions can currently be destroyed. ensure they have hitboxes and have a low health value to be destroyed at zero." Found: the shield generator stood inside its own dome, which stopped every shot, blast and grenade from outside; projectiles (plasma, missiles, grenades) flew through every contraption; splash counted from a contraption's middle; health 800 / 400 / 500 / 150. Now every kind (shield generator, beacon, Rokkit turret, scrap trap) has 75 health (`MusouMekRules.ContraptionHealth`), any melee blow that reaches one destroys it, the dome lets attacks through to its own generator, a player's projectile strikes a contraption's body and detonates there with its direct damage (`ExtrasProjectileStop` now takes the projectile), and blasts count from the body's edge (`MusouMeks.Reach`). At zero the existing removal stops its effect, and the client's destroyed cue plays the break effect, the frag's sound and the wreck. Tests: `MusouContraptionDestructibleTests` (per kind: rounds to zero, one blow, a frag's splash; a projectile striking a turret; the low health). Implemented, not playtested.

**Musou contraptions: review follow-ups (2026-11-09; branch `musou/contraptions-review` from integration/playtest-2026-11-09b cdeb064a; `TfwRules.Version` 60, unchanged).** A projectile fired from outside the dome at its generator now passes the shell (`MusouMeks.GeneratorOnRay`: the generator lies on its ray; it strikes on a later step), a ray starting inside a contraption's cylinder no longer strikes it (a player standing in a beacon does not set his own shot off at the muzzle), a tie between a contraption and a player stops the projectile at the contraption (it was struck but flew on), and the projectile, blast and melee hooks begin the Musou tick first so a destroyed cue raised in the projectile step reaches the client (a projectile kill showed no destruction effect). Tests: `MusouContraptionDestructibleTests` (a dart from 16 m outside the dome destroys its generator; a dart fired from inside a beacon flies on). Implemented, not playtested.
**Stalker hit confirm (branch `claude/stalker-hit-sound-8555cc`, 2026-11-09; client and content only, Classic and Musou; no protocol, wire, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner: the Stalker Bolter "isn't playing the right sound when shooting an enemy target ... Find that sound in the original game files and use it for both the stalker bolter and daemon eye bolter." The data binds `play_stalker_smack` to both rifles' `player_hit_something_action` (docs/discovery.md "Stalker hit confirm"; the penetration and impact events ruled out). Classic already posted it, but at -34 / -29 dB at the voice under the hit-confirm distance falloff (-18 dB from 40 m) and the mix pass's high-pass; Musou played the bolter family's pitched-down `play_bolter_smack` at the Ork and no confirm. Now (`StalkerHitConfirm`): the two rifles' confirm plays on the shooter at the data's level (no falloff, no mix-pass gain or high-pass; live -20 / -15 dB) with the victim's material, and in Musou an own hit on an Ork posts it on the shooter instead of the wet bolter smack (the explosion stays). Every other weapon is unchanged. Switch `--old-stalker-hit-confirm`. Tests `StalkerHitConfirmTests` (mapping, other weapons, offset, an install pin of both rifles' binding). Aid: `smtool stalker-confirm-preview` (before/after WAVs, `<media folder>\previews\stalker-hit-sound\`). Checked: a headless Classic bot run (Stalker on a Chaos bot) logged the new confirm. Not verified: no human has listened; Musou was not run live (built only); the full `dotnet test`.
**Plasma projectiles in the original look (plasma-original-fx, 2026-11-09; client presentation only, no simulation, wire, protocol or config-hash change; Classic PvP and Musou alike).** The owner: "In Musou mode and classic PvP make the plasma projectiles for plasma gun and plasma pistol to be the visuals from the original game files." Evidence (docs/discovery.md "Plasma projectile visuals"): the light shot of the gun (primary) and pistol (secondary) binds the data tracer `plasma_gun_tracer` (Chaos `chaos_plasma_gun_tracer`) at `fx_muzzle` in `hit_fx`; the charged shot launches `plasma_altfire_mp` / `plasma_pistol_altfire_mp` (Chaos `*_chaos_mp`), whose model is `invisible_projectile` (no mesh; its `fx_trail` marker at the origin, scale 1) and whose whole look is its `lifetime_action` `plasma_gun_charged_trail` (Chaos `chaos_plasma_gun_trail`) at scale 1. Now the default for every shooter (own predicted ball, own and others' snapshot balls, own and others' tracers): the light shot plays the data tracer with its own colours and sizes (a teal `plasma_tracer` streak crossing at 800 m/s, soft smoke and linger beams), and the charged shot draws only its data trail (a cyan billboard ball, two streamers, sparks, a light). Off by default (all ours, kept behind `--old-plasma-look`): the light ball of fix/plasma-light-tracer, the recoloured thin bolt of fx/tracers-impact, the solid roiling ball mesh (gun and pistol; the plasma cannon keeps it) and the softened ribbon head of fix/plasma-trail-slab. One reading changed (interpretation, `FxEffect.WidthAlongTrail`, gun and pistol trails only): a streamer's width keys run along the ribbon like its colour keys (the `blue trail` 1 m at the ball to 6 m where it has faded), not over loop time (which swelled the whole ribbon to 6 m once a second), drawn in 30 quads. Kept: the Compatibility renderer's thin safety streak under the light tracer, now in the data's smoke colour. Review minor fixed (old-look code): the light ball's follow closure is made once per ball, and a ball that cannot be drawn is not launched, so its impact no longer waits for it. `smtool fx-dump --fields` now prints streamer keys. Tests `PlasmaOriginalLookTests`. Captures in `<media folder>\previews\plasma-original-fx\`: `before_after_forward.png`, `before_after_compat.png` (the `--bolt-fx-demo` side view, slow motion), `clips\*.mp4`, `match\` (bot matches on Manufactorum, player view and `--spectate shot`, Forward+ and Compatibility, against a Chaos Raptor with the plasma pistol). Cost: in the match runs the effect quads peaked at 338 to 371 a frame against 509 to 525 with the old look; the effect update averaged 0.7 to 0.9 ms either way (the runs differ in what is on screen, so not a clean comparison). Open for the owner's look check: the data's `short trail` is 3.9 m wide at the ball (`beam_gradient`, soft across its width), so the charged trail starts with a wide glow band cut straight at the ball, plainest from the side and in the Compatibility renderer; the Chaos light shot's core streak is the same teal texture as the loyalists' (only its smoke is purple). Not verified: the original by eye (no footage compared), an old GPU, a human's own shots, Musou in-game (same code path), the full `dotnet test`.
**Musou: the Weirdboy throws his bolt (branch `claude/musou-weirdboy-bolt-8fde3a`, 2026-11-09; `MusouSim.Version` 34, renumber at integration; no protocol or wire format change; Musou Mode only).** The owner, with a clip (1152): "the weird boy currently does nothing. ensure he shoots his magic bolt ranged attack". Cause: his bolt went through the crowd's shooter tokens (8 a player, 10 a Guard squad), which go each tick to the nearest Ork asking; in a war the Shoota Boyz at 12 to 20 m always beat him at 20 to 50 m, so he stood in his band and never threw (the sim tests had no crowd, so they passed). Measured: a Weirdboy 30 m from a player behind 12 Shoota Boyz threw 0 bolts in 15 s before, 6 after. Fix (`MusouSim.WeirdboyRanged`, one hook line in `MusouSim.Ai.cs` Behave): his bolt is his own, with no token; his own line of sight (as a shooter's, kept for the usual ticks); thrown from beyond his staff's reach (5 m) up to 50 m, his 20 to 50 m band kept for where he stands; each bolt cast first, 0.5 s in `Casting` (ours), so the client plays his cast clip `WIB_WIB_MEL_Cast_Magic_01` (the crowd's attack clip for Casting); the bolt leaves at the cast's end at the target's feet as they stand then; a stagger cuts the cast and the bolt is lost. Damage 35, 3 m burst, 40 m/s, every 2.5 s unchanged; the client's muzzle, trail, hit and staff sound for the bolt cue were already in place. Restore switch: server `SM_MUSOU_OLD_WEIRDBOY=1`. Client: his bolt (muzzle, trail, hit) and his shield now draw at effect priority 1: in a war the 160 live effects are full of gunfire (a fight's log: about 1000 priority-0 effects evicted in 40 s) and at priority 0 his shield bubble, the oldest, was evicted first. Capture aids: server `SM_TFW_WEIRDBOY_TEST=1` (one extra Weirdboy 30 m ahead of the first human, 1,000,000 health, `TFWWEIRDBOY` lines for his states and bolts), client `--tfw-fight-weirdboy` (the scripted fighter looks at him; a `Weirdboy bolts drawn` note). On a local server (127.0.0.1) with it: he casts and throws every 2.5 s, mostly at the nearest Guard squad, and the client drew 22 of his bolts in 22 s; stills in `<media folder>\previews\musou-weirdboy\` (the Guardsmen's and the AI Marines' fire staggers him often, which cuts a cast). Tests `MusouWeirdboyBoltTests` (4: through a crowd holding every token he casts within 2 s and the bolt lands for 35 on a player and on a Guard squad; a stagger cuts the cast; on the real map in a war he casts and the bolt reaches the player and hurts). Seen in the World test: with the AI Marines in the field he often aims at them, and a walking Marine steps out of the 3 m burst (the milestone's telegraphed bolt, a player who moves on is spared). Not verified: no human has seen it; the full `dotnet test`.
**Musou: the big Orks' deaths and gait (branch `claude/musou-big-ork-deaths`, 2026-11-09; Musou Mode only, client presentation; no protocol, wire, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner: "the elite and boss orks and the warboss need to have death animations. they also look like they move in slow motion because of the way they're scaled up." A new stage (`--musou-crowd-test`, `MusouCrowdTestView`) runs the real crowd: the Nob's and Boss Orks' death clips did play whenever a body was handed over; what took them away was the gore tearing apart every explosion death (most bolter kills are bolt blasts) and the Warboss's death clip being a blast reaction that stands him up. Now an elite or boss is never torn apart (`MusouBigOrkRules.KeepsBody`), the Warboss dies by `WB_Get_Up` played backwards (`Look.ReversedClip`), and a scaled body's run stride grows by the square root of its scale (Boss Orks 0.27x to 0.46x, feet sliding 1.7x; the Warboss's walk measured on his own feet, `FootBones.Warboss`). Simulation speeds unchanged (faster big Orks would be the gameplay option). Tests: `MusouBigOrkTests`. Test aids: `--musou-old-big-orks`, `--musou-stride-exponent f`, `--musou-crowd-test`, `--warboss-test --clip-name`. Spec "Musou Mode: the big Orks' deaths and gait". Not seen by a human in a match.

**Musou: the big Orks against the map (same branch, 2026-11-09; `MusouSim.Version` 34, to be renumbered at integration).** The owner, with a recording on Ashfall: "boss enemies are getting stuck along objects and moving in slow motion". On the Ashfall draft 10 walk graph the big Orks never stood stuck where a Boy did not, but the Boss Orks lost 13 % of their ground speed scraping along walls (3.8 of 4.4 m/s); and the recording's stuck Boss Orks stood at a stair's foot because every body's level reach was 1.5 m. Now the level reach and the shooters' eye grow with the body (1.5 m x height / 1.9 m, 1x to 3x), a Boss Ork's wall lean keeps his speed, and a big body's blocked step slides along the wall (`MusouSim.BigBodies.cs`). Boss Orks 4.38 to 4.40 m/s, longest stand 0.5 s on four Ashfall crossings; a Boss Nob at the foot of a 2.4 m ledge strikes the player on it. Tests: `BigOrkSnagTests`. Server `SM_MUSOU_OLD_BIG_BODIES=1` restores. Not seen by a human.

**Musou: the Orks' pace and charge (same branch, 2026-11-09; `MusouSim.Version` 35, to be renumbered at integration; no wire change).** The owner: "make orks run 20% faster, and sprint to 'charge' the enemy when they reach within 30m of an enemy". Every Ork on foot 1.2x (elites, bosses, Warboss included; not the Squig or the Chaos Marine); a melee-first Ork within 30 m of a player, retainer or Guard squad sprints (`MusouSim.Charge.cs`): paced run x 9.91/5.98 (the boy rig's sprint and run clips), at most 9.9 m/s; the gun kinds hold range; the Warboss keeps his own charge. The client plays `BOY_1HM_NAV_Sprint_F_01` when the drawn speed tells a sprint (`MusouGaitRules.Sprinting`; no byte), the far tier bakes it once. Tests: `MusouChargeTests`; TF3's Guard box and the AI pair's fight pinned to the old pace (the box now goes to the Orks: `Six_squads_against_sixty_charging_boyz`). Server `SM_MUSOU_OLD_ORK_PACE=1` restores. Not seen by a human.

**Musou: the Guardsmen meet a charge (branch `claude/musou-big-ork-deaths`, 2026-11-10; `TfwRules.Version` 58, to be renumbered).** The owner chose "Rebalance Guards" after the Orks' 1.2x pace and charge made six Guard squads lose TF3's box to sixty Boyz. A strength rise would have tipped the mixed counterattack trial (matched to the far clash) the Guards' way, so the one change is aimed at the charge: a hit on a charging Ork does 1.5x damage (`GuardRules.ChargeDamageScale`). Box: 34.3 s, 31 lost, 5 squads left (before the pace 44.1 s, 34, 4); hold trial 12 of 20 (8 at the pace without it, 10 before); near army trial 200 v 200 3 of 8 (as before). Tests: `GuardSimTests` (the box back at the new pace, its old-pace pin dropped; `A_charging_ork_takes_the_volleys_extra_damage_and_a_shooter_does_not`). Restore: server `SM_MUSOU_GUARD_BRACE=1`. Not played by a human.
**Network responsiveness (net/responsive, 2026-11-09; client and server, no protocol, wire, config-hash or gameplay-rule change).** The owner: Classic PvP and the networking in general feel "delayed, not responsive, slow. its smooth, but we're missing something" (decision 2026-11-09-net-responsiveness: measure, then the quick fixes; no 60 Hz tick). **Measured first:** an opt-in readout (`SM_NET_LATENCY=<s>` / client `--net-latency [s]`: `NETLAT` lines; `NetLatencyReadout`, `GameClient.Latency.cs`) and an engine-free probe (`tests/SmNet.Tests/NetLatencyProbe.cs`, `SM_NET_PROBE=1`: a server and a shooter firing full auto at a strafing target on the loopback transport, clients at 60 fps frames, 30 s a link). Baseline (commit b19aa900, means; links 127.0.0.1 / 60 ms / 80 ms round trip / a 400 ms warm-up handshake then 60 ms): server-reported input lead 3 / 2 / 2 / 4 ticks (the old steering acted only below 1 and above 5; the warm-up case sat at 4 for good); own shot to the server's hit report and marker 128 / 162 / 186 / 226 ms; remote players drawn behind the server 109 / 142 / 156 / 146 ms (100 ms interpolation, 20 Hz snapshots); an input edge to the drawn own position 5 cm off its old path 29 / 29 / 26 / 26 ms. **Changes, each with a switch back** (client `--old-input-lead`, `--old-own-draw`, `--interp-delay 100`, `--no-predicted-hits`, all four `--old-net-feel`; server `--snapshot-rate 20`; the probe's "old switches" run reproduces the baseline to the digit): (a) the input lead is filtered and kept at 2 ticks by a 4 % clock slew (`GameClient.Responsive.cs`), whole-tick jumps only for late inputs (a report below 0: catch up to 1) and a filtered lead 3 over the target (pause, at most 2 ticks a time), their waits from a round trip measured from snapshot echoes instead of the handshake's; a jitter guard adds up to 2 ticks after a report of 0 or a tick the server ran without this client's input (`Snapshot.LastInputTick`), a tick back every 10 s clean; (b) the own marine is drawn from the newest predicted tick toward a speculative next tick (`GameClient.Ahead`: the newest input stepped once more), a tick sooner, own clips a tick ahead with it (`ClipLead`), and the step any tick or lead jump makes in that drawing is blended out over 3 ticks (`DrawBlendOffset`; the drawn fraction runs over the length each tick was scheduled with, so the slew moves nothing drawn); (c) snapshots every tick (30 Hz) and an adaptive interpolation delay (`InterpolationDelayEstimator`: two snapshot intervals, more with jitter and loss, 67 to 100 ms, the server's lag-compensation bound unchanged); Musou Mode keeps a 100 ms floor for its crowd (`GameClient.InterpolationFloor`, set in `client/Extras/Musou`); (d) an own hit-scan hit on an enemy as drawn shows the hit marker and plays the hit confirmation on the shot's frame (`client/NetworkView.Responsive.cs`), the server's report never again unless it adds hits, a kill or a headshot (`PredictedHitLedger`). **After (same probe):** lead 2 / 2 / 2 / 2 ticks (the warm-up case is at 3 within 0.5 s and at 2 by 3 s); shot to the server's report 101 / 150 / 174 / 153 ms, and the marker itself on the shot's frame in the client; remote players behind the server 86 / 111 / 125 / 116 ms (interpolation 69 to 71 ms); edge to 5 cm 13 / 13 / 12 / 13 ms (to 1 cm: 8, was 9 to 13). Bandwidth: Classic 8v8 (16 players running and firing) 20.0 → 29.5 KB/s per client; Musou's stream stays within its 110 to 120 KB/s by construction (its budget already counts the core snapshot bytes, which grow about 7 → 11 KB/s by the musou-net-budget measurement, leaving the crowd about 3 % less). On the 2-minute lossy-link run of `ControlFeelTests` (70 ms, 25 ms jitter, 5 % loss, latency spikes) the largest drawn own step fell from 452 to 17 mm a millisecond and 6.9 in calm periods. Tests: `NetResponsiveTests` (the delay on clean, jittery and lossy links; the ledger; the clip lead; the own marine never behind the newest tick and without steps; the lead after an inflated handshake against the old steps; the slew; 30 and 20 Hz), the control-feel tests drawing as the client does now, and four determinism tests pinned to the old lead steering (`EvadeTests`, `JumpPackTests`: their 5 % loss needs a lead covering several losses in a row; the kill-mid-roll test also to 20 Hz, its kill cadence). Capped run of the netcode-adjacent classes and every Musou extras test: 2,170 passed. Risks: on a link with heavy loss a lead of 2 to 4 mispredicts on two or three lost packets in a row where the old lead of about 5 did not (each a correction faded over 0.1 s; the jitter guard raises the lead after the first); the predicted marker can show for a shot the server judges a miss (lag compensation draws the same target, so rarely; counted as `PredictedHitLedger.Unconfirmed`); the speculative tick can show a frame of motion a correction then takes back. Real processes (127.0.0.1, UDP, Manufactorum, two headless `--bot` Godot clients with `--net-latency 10`): new defaults after the first 10 s lead 2.0 ticks (67 ms), interpolation 66.7 ms, remote players 83 ms behind the server, shot to the server's hit report 100 ms; a client with `--old-net-feel` on the same server lead 4.0 to 4.9 ticks (133 to 163 ms, the owner's log's 4 to 5) and remote 120 ms. A client's own stall (an update gap over 100 ms) made its inputs late and raised the jitter guard to lead 3 to 4 in the first run: reports within a feedback wait of such a gap no longer raise it. Not verified: no human has played it (bots draw no predicted hit marker); the Godot `--latency-probe` and a windowed run were not repeated; the full `dotnet test`.

**Network responsiveness, round 2: the floors (net/responsive, 2026-11-10; protocol 65; no gameplay-rule change).** The owner's follow-up: "buffering as low as it can go while still playing well", each floor adaptive and behind its switch. (a) The snapshot's 4-byte input lead became a 2-byte lead and a 2-byte **input slack** (ms from an input's first arrival to the run of its tick, the least a snapshot covers; negative when the tick ran without it; snapshot size unchanged): the client aims it at one tick (one lost batch survived) plus the measured jitter (median less 2nd percentile over 2 s) plus 5 ms, more ticks on measured snapshot loss (3 in 10,000 a tick: 1 % keeps 2, 5 % keeps 3), by a proportional slew (1 % per 10 ms off, at most 4 %; `--lead-ticks` keeps round 1's whole-tick lead of 2). (b) Interpolation 1.5 snapshot intervals plus jitter (floor 50 ms; at a 20 Hz server about 89 ms, its gaps alternate 1 and 2 ticks), and remote players carried on for at most one tick when a snapshot is late (`--no-extrapolation`). (c) Click-frame cosmetics measured, not changed: the Godot `--latency-probe` (10 trials each, 60 fps) shows the muzzle flash, the shot's sound, the melee clip and the roll 0.3 to 0.4 ms into the click's frame, in both modes (feel/controls' early tick); the tick still decides the shot. **Two bugs found and fixed on the way:** a client stall (a hitch, a load) left the tick schedule behind when a snapshot moved the client's tick up, so the loop ran the skipped ticks on top and every stall added its length to the lead (10 ticks after a 400 ms stall in the test; very likely part of the owner's 4 to 5 ticks): the schedule now moves with them (`StallSkips`, new mode only), and no late catch-up runs within a feedback wait of the client's own stall; and the speculative next tick of the ahead drawing kept a predicted charge contact, which took the victim's body out of the next real step (RushTests caught it): it now restores that state. **Floors (engine-free probe, means; links 127.0.0.1 / 60 ms / 80 ms with 10 ms jitter and 1 % loss / a 400 ms warm-up then 60 ms; round 1 and the original in brackets):** input slack 49 / 51 / 94 / 65 ms (round 1 97 / 84 / 85 / 87; original lead 3 / 2 / 2 / 4 ticks = 100 to 133 ms); own shot to the server's hit report 53 / 117 / 185 / 131 (101 / 150 / 174 / 153; original 128 / 162 / 186 / 226); interpolation 53 / 53 / 54 / 56 (69 to 71; 100); remote players behind the server 64 / 96 / 108 / 101 (86 / 111 / 125 / 116; 109 / 142 / 156 / 146); input edge to 5 cm of drawn movement 12 to 14 (13; 26 to 29). The 80 ms link with 1 % loss deliberately keeps 2 ticks for losses (at one tick every double loss is a mispredict) and so sits a little above round 1 there. Tests: `NetResponsiveTests` (16: the slack on the wire and negative when a tick ran without the input, the floors, a client stall that no longer piles up lead, the capped extrapolation and its switch, the rest as round 1); determinism tests that demand zero mispredictions through 5 to 8 % loss pinned to the old lead steering (`EvadeTests`, `JumpPackTests`, `SpreadTests`, `InputBufferTests`, `RushTests`, `SolidBodiesTests`); `AimTests` waits for its handshake through 30 % loss (the snapshot rate changes how the seeded loss falls); `MusouIsolationTests` hashes slack 0 so the old golden bytes stand. **Open:** `RushTests.Prediction_reconciles_after_contacts` mismatches 2 and 15 of about 714 ticks at 30 Hz snapshots even with the old lead and interpolation (two marines pressed together after a charge contact; at 20 Hz none): pinned to 20 Hz, root cause not found; a 30 Hz Classic match may mispredict there. Capped run of 118 netcode-adjacent classes and every Musou extras test: 2,808 passed, 1 skipped, the one remaining failure (SolidBodies' connect count) pinned as above and passing.

**Musou slash distance 30 m (owner, 2026-11-10; branch `claude/musou-slash-30m-421306`; Musou Mode only, client drawing only, no protocol, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner: "make it so that blue and red slashes don't appear beyond 30m" / "musou mode only". `MusouSlashRules.Metres` 60 -> 30; both paths that draw a red or blue stroke already gate on it (`NetworkView.MusouMeleeSlash` for every melee hit event (marker 3) of a player or retainer, and `MusouOwnStrikeContact` for the predicted own strike); `MusouSlashView.Add` has no other caller. The dark gore's ink slash (`GoreRules.SlashMetres`, 60 m) is not red or blue and is unchanged; Classic never draws these strokes. Test: `MusouMeleeFeelTests.No_red_or_blue_slash_is_drawn_beyond_30_metres`. Implemented, not playtested.

**Musou: combat stims regenerate like grenades (owner, 2026-11-09; branch `claude/musou-stim-regen`; Musou Mode only; `TfwRules.Version` 58, renumbered 61 at the 2026-11-10 integration; no protocol change).** The owner: "stimulants need to regenerate the same way grenades do". The combat stims' charges now refill on the grenade rule, one back every 15 s up to the most a player carries (`World.TfwSupply.cs`, the supply tick no longer skips stims). Spec and changes-from-original rows added on the branch; `TfwSupplyTests` cover the refill. No restore switch yet (review follow-up).
**Musou HUD at the screen edges (musou/ui-edges, owner 2026-11-10; client only, Musou Mode and the old 5-wave run; no rules, wire or protocol change).** The owner: "move all musou mode specific UI elements to the edges of the screen, prioritizing the corners nd minimizing impact on free screen space to view the game world." Every Musou-only HUD element moved (`client/Extras/Musou/MusouHudLayout.cs`): the battle commander's (Warboss's) bar and the Boss Orks' bars to the bottom left (the team score panel's corner, empty in Musou; 380 and 300 wide, stacked upwards), the capture tiles top left made smaller (46 instead of 56) with the on-point line and bar under them (it was a 440-wide bar at y 760), the KO chain to the bottom right over the weapon box's winged skull (40 px instead of 56, it stood right of the crosshair), the call-outs (WAAAGH!, ENRAGED, BOSS ORK INCOMING / SLAIN) to a strip along the top edge over the armour bar (38 px instead of 70 in the middle), the war's prompts, the redeploy line and the pickup hold to a strip along the bottom edge, the weapon-drop prompt (a Label) over that strip, growing upwards, and the incoming-rocket arc onto an ellipse along the screen's edges; the old 5-wave run's break lines under its run panel. Follow-up (owner 2026-11-10, "Bottom left, approve"): in Musou only, the own armour and health bar (the match HUD's `Hud.Vitals.cs`, the original's top centre) moves bottom left over the Boss Ork bars at 0.65 of its size, its box's bottom 228 above the screen's bottom (clear of the commander's bar and up to three Boss Ork bars), through a new generic `Hud.Frame.VitalsCorner` that Musou sets each frame (null, the original's place, in Classic PvP). Left in place: KILLED (where the match HUD's own death line stands), the end-of-run panel, the M war map and the menu pages, the Librarian's gauge (already the weapon box's corner), world markers. Classic PvP's HUD (`Hud.cs`, `Hud/*`) is not touched. `--musou-old-hud` restores the layout before; `--musou-hud-demo campaign` (new) shows every element in a real Musou Mode battle (a made-up commander, two Boss Orks, the chain, a call-out every 4 s, the on-point bar, a pickup hold and the drop prompt) for screenshots. Shots (player view, `--tfw-test-fight --tfw-fight-hold`, windowed on the private desktop) at 16:9, 21:9, 16:10 and 1280x720, before and after: `<media folder>\previews\musou-ui-edges\`. Gate: the owner's screenshot approval. Plan and before/after table: the lead's notes folder, `musou-ui-edges-plan.md`.
**Loading screen picture and screen blink (ui/loading-blink, branch `claude/ui-loading-blink-2c12e6`, 2026-11-10; client only, no protocol or config change).** The owner: "in the coming playtest release we're shipping i want the old main menu screen to be the new loading screen background" and "transition between main menu and load screen and game to make it feel smoother. like blinking." The loading screen shows `client/assets/menu/loading-background.jpg` (the main menu's picture before 38438193, byte for byte; the main menu keeps today's) behind LOADING, cover-fit, with a dim of 0.2 in the middle to 0.65 at the corners and a shadow on the text (`NetworkView.Loading.cs`, `UiKit.LoadingBackgroundImage`; halved while at least twice the window's height, freed once the match shows; release.ps1 copies it beside the exe). The loading layer moved from 60 to 100 so the loadout picker and Musou's modals never show over it. `ScreenBlink` (a black layer at 127, made by `ModelViewer`, never for bots) closes over 0.18 s, keeps 2 frames black, runs the change (the Join, the hide of the loading screen at connect, LEAVE MATCH, Esc back from a failed join), holds at least 0.08 s and 3 settled frames (into the match: no character build deferred; back to the menu: the menu's rows built; cap 1.5 s real) and opens over 0.26 s, smoothstep both ways; it never takes input. The first recording found the map load (a long frame) landing inside the black on a local server, so the loading screen flickered in for 4 frames before the blink turned back; the client now starts its handshake only once the blink has opened on the loading screen (`LoadingWaitsForBlink`, at most 2.5 s). Switch: `--no-screen-blink` (all at once, as before); capture aid `--loading-linger <s>`. Tests: UI self-test `ScreenBlinkChecks` (14 checks: close before the change, black frames first, a long frame keeps it black, the hold waits for readiness, the open's time, turning back while opening, a failing change still opens). Evidence: `<media folder>\previews\loading-blink\` (Movie Maker clips at 30 fps, stills, a Compatibility-renderer still); the full flow also ran in the Compatibility renderer and headless (no hang). Not verified: a human's look approval; a real remote server's join (simulated with `--loading-linger 3`).
**Musou T key lines, no automatic barks (musou/hotkey-lines, owner 2026-11-10; client only, Musou Mode only; no protocol, wire, cooldown or hash change).** The owner: "remove the voice barks feature we added previously. we'll stick to the hotkey and simply add more lines for it to say based on what i mark to keep in the interactive sheet you gave me earlier", then, with six lines from the listening sheet: "use these voice lines in rotation with 'for the emperor' when pressing T on the keyboard." Done: musou/battle-ambience's random Marine barks are off (`MusouKeyLines.AutoBarks`; `--musou-auto-barks` restores them); in Musou Mode each accepted T press says the next of seven lines in order (`MusouKeyLines.Pool`): FOR THE EMPEROR (the voice pack's take, as before), then Titus's "Purge the xenos!", "Send the Horde, brother.", "Excellently done.", "One less traitor.", "OFF, YOU ALIEN PEST!" and Sidonus's "AHHH!" (the install's speech-bank leaves, posted by node id on the speaker's voice emitter; nothing copied into the repository). The slot is (shout sequence - 1) mod 7 from the server's per-player shout count, so every client hears the same line; the u8 sequence's wrap restarts the pool after four lines once per 256 presses (documented, tested). T is shared with Classic PvP's loyalist barks: the one hook (`MusouKeyLine`, called from the key's `BarkSay`) returns at once outside Musou Mode, so Annihilation and Seize Ground say FOR THE EMPEROR alone as before. A campaign line that cannot play falls back to the take. Level: the first capture had the six lines 11 to 18 dB under the take (their files are -15 to -25 dB, the speech mix takes about 9 dB more), and one +12 dB offset still left three of them 7 to 9 dB under it, so each line has its own offset (+12 to +20 dB, from its decoded file's level, capped at the take's loudest; `MusouKeyLines.Pool`, ours; `--musou-key-gain <dB>` adds, `--musou-key-data-level` removes them). Aids `--no-musou-key-lines`, `--log-sound musou-key`. Superseded and not merged: branch `musou/generic-barks` @ 5e4cb4f5 (the reviewed bark pool). Tests `MusouKeyLinesTests` (the 7-line pool, the order and no repeat before all seven, the wrap, FOR THE EMPEROR's takes still stepping, Musou only, the barks off unless restored). Capture: a real server on 127.0.0.1 and a hidden windowed bot pressing T every 2.5 s (`--bot-shout 2.5`, Movie Maker 24 fps): three runs, every accepted press said the next line in order (1 to 7, then 1 again), every campaign line started, no automatic bark posted; third run levels FOR THE EMPEROR -15.5 dB, the six -13.7 to -22.7 dB, a battle bed about -18 dB; audio in `<media folder>\previews\musou-hotkey-lines\`. Not verified: no human has heard it in play; others' lines in 3D (one client only in the capture); the full `dotnet test`.

The slot is (shout sequence - 1) mod 7 from the server's per-player shout count, so every client hears the same line; the u8 sequence's wrap restarts the pool after four lines once per 256 presses (documented, tested). T is shared with Classic PvP's loyalist barks: the one hook (`MusouKeyLine`, called from the key's `BarkSay`) returns at once outside Musou Mode, so Annihilation and Seize Ground say FOR THE EMPEROR alone as before. A campaign line that cannot play falls back to the take. Level: the first capture had the six lines 11 to 18 dB under the take (their files are -15 to -25 dB, the speech mix takes about 9 dB more), and one +12 dB offset still left three of them 7 to 9 dB under it, so each line has its own offset (+12 to +20 dB, from its decoded file's level, capped at the take's loudest; `MusouKeyLines.Pool`, ours; `--musou-key-gain <dB>` adds, `--musou-key-data-level` removes them). Aids `--no-musou-key-lines`, `--log-sound musou-key`. Superseded and not merged: branch `musou/generic-barks` @ 5e4cb4f5 (the reviewed bark pool). Tests `MusouKeyLinesTests` (the 7-line pool, the order and no repeat before all seven, the wrap, FOR THE EMPEROR's takes still stepping, Musou only, the barks off unless restored). Capture: a real server on 127.0.0.1 and a hidden windowed bot pressing T every 2.5 s (`--bot-shout 2.5`, Movie Maker 24 fps): three runs, every accepted press said the next line in order (1 to 7, then 1 again), every campaign line started, no automatic bark posted; third run levels FOR THE EMPEROR -15.5 dB, the six -13.7 to -22.7 dB, a battle bed about -18 dB; audio in `<media folder>\previews\musou-hotkey-lines\`. Not verified: no human has heard it in play; others' lines in 3D (one client only in the capture); the full `dotnet test`.

**Public scrub (owner, 2026-11-10; branch `claude/public-scrub`; text and a guard test only, no behaviour change).** The owner: "Scrub local pc folder paths ands any other sensitive or identifying information from public view". The owner's local media folder (a drive-letter path) appeared 25 times in docs/milestones.md, docs/musou-ashfall-graybox.md, spec/behavior.md and a comment in `MusouKeyLines.cs`; each is now `<media folder>\previews\...` ("the owner's media folder"). Nine path separators an earlier shell had turned into control bytes are restored. A `PackageScanner.cs` comment no longer spells a sample address. Guard: `PublicTextGuardTests` reads every tracked file (git ls-files; config/local.json is never opened) and fails on a drive-letter path under a user's folder or into the project's media folder, a home or Git Bash user path, an e-mail that is not a public noreply or example address, a Discord webhook or bot token, a SteamID64, and the user name and machine name of whoever runs it (read from the environment); findings print file, line and rule only, and the allowlist is empty. The release scan's rules are shared with it (made internal). Left as they are: generic examples (`D:\path\to\game`, the launcher tests' `C:\Users\test\...`), the public GitHub owner name, and the public server's address in `GameOptions.PublicServer` (the client needs it; moving it is a behaviour change for the owner to decide).
**Musou: the Orks' pace and charge (same branch, 2026-11-09; `MusouSim.Version` 35, to be renumbered at integration; no wire change).** The owner: "make orks run 20% faster, and sprint to 'charge' the enemy when they reach within 30m of an enemy". Every Ork on foot 1.2x (elites, bosses, Warboss included; not the Squig or the Chaos Marine); a melee-first Ork within 30 m of a player, retainer or Guard squad sprints (`MusouSim.Charge.cs`): paced run x 9.91/5.98 (the boy rig's sprint and run clips), at most 9.9 m/s; the gun kinds hold range; the Warboss keeps his own charge. The client plays `BOY_1HM_NAV_Sprint_F_01` when the drawn speed tells a sprint (`MusouGaitRules.Sprinting`; no byte), the far tier bakes it once. Tests: `MusouChargeTests`; TF3's Guard box and the AI pair's fight pinned to the old pace (the box now goes to the Orks: `Six_squads_against_sixty_charging_boyz`). Server `SM_MUSOU_OLD_ORK_PACE=1` restores. Not seen by a human.

**Musou: the Guardsmen meet a charge (branch `claude/musou-big-ork-deaths`, 2026-11-10; `TfwRules.Version` 58, to be renumbered).** The owner chose "Rebalance Guards" after the Orks' 1.2x pace and charge made six Guard squads lose TF3's box to sixty Boyz. A strength rise would have tipped the mixed counterattack trial (matched to the far clash) the Guards' way, so the one change is aimed at the charge: a hit on a charging Ork does 1.5x damage (`GuardRules.ChargeDamageScale`). Box: 34.3 s, 31 lost, 5 squads left (before the pace 44.1 s, 34, 4); hold trial 12 of 20 (8 at the pace without it, 10 before); near army trial 200 v 200 3 of 8 (as before). Tests: `GuardSimTests` (the box back at the new pace, its old-pace pin dropped; `A_charging_ork_takes_the_volleys_extra_damage_and_a_shooter_does_not`). Restore: server `SM_MUSOU_GUARD_BRACE=1`. Not played by a human.

The elite share, 'Ard Boyz, Warboss and the specials unchanged. Guard hold trial 1 of 20 with the twins (pinned at one of each, 12; Guardsmen at 1.1x strength would hold 10). Restore: server `SM_TFW_OLD_BIG_SPAWNS=1`. Not played by a human.

**Musou contraptions destructible (owner, 2026-11-09; branch `musou/contraptions-destructible` from main 45572fae; `TfwRules.Version` 59, no protocol bump).** The owner: "not all of the scrap mek's contraptions can currently be destroyed. ensure they have hitboxes and have a low health value to be destroyed at zero." Found: the shield generator stood inside its own dome, which stopped every shot, blast and grenade from outside; projectiles (plasma, missiles, grenades) flew through every contraption; splash counted from a contraption's middle; health 800 / 400 / 500 / 150. Now every kind (shield generator, beacon, Rokkit turret, scrap trap) has 75 health (`MusouMekRules.ContraptionHealth`), any melee blow that reaches one destroys it, the dome lets attacks through to its own generator, a player's projectile strikes a contraption's body and detonates there with its direct damage (`ExtrasProjectileStop` now takes the projectile), and blasts count from the body's edge (`MusouMeks.Reach`). At zero the existing removal stops its effect, and the client's destroyed cue plays the break effect, the frag's sound and the wreck. Tests: `MusouContraptionDestructibleTests` (per kind: rounds to zero, one blow, a frag's splash; a projectile striking a turret; the low health). Implemented, not playtested.
**Musou Librarian, third pass: cast pose, chain lightning, instant cast, 60 m Shockwave, no Warp Pull (branch `claude/librarian-lightning-ab6ddc`, 2026-11-10; `MusouSim.Version` 37 (34 renumbered at integration); no protocol or extras wire bump; Musou Mode only).** The owner: "add a firing animation where the librarian holds his hands up in an aggressive pose - hands pointed palms forward towards his target - and shudders with power as he casts", "improve the chain lightning visual and audio effects ... make it feel powerful and look good and powerful", ".1 second max between clicking left mouse button and the chain lighting hitting its target", the Shockwave at "a range of 60m and massively increased effect and damage", and the Warp Pull removed so he can "use all equipment items that other classes can use". No cast clip exists on the MP marine rig (docs/discovery.md), so the pose is procedural through a new client hook `CharacterViewer.ExtrasPoseOverlay` (`CharacterViewer.LibrarianCast.cs`): the chest turns to the target from planted legs, a lean and a shrug, a two-bone reach of both arms, palms square to the target with open, spread fingers, a shudder, a release thrust; checked numerically with `--librarian-cast-log` (both elbows 52 degrees, palms 1.00 toward the target). `LibrarianBolts` was rewritten (fractal forked bolts from both palms, camera-facing strips with a hot core and a blue glow, re-strikes with a violet afterglow, hand arcs, impact flares and bursts, budgeted lights; on a frame clock so recordings keep their pace); the old bolts stay as `LibrarianBoltsOld`. Speed: the own chain is foreseen on the client from the press (`LibrarianPrediction`, the server's rules; drawn 0 to 1 ms after the press), the client sends a cast command at the press (kind 17, tag 16) and the server casts from its next tick (`World.LibrarianCastEarly`): its links came back 15 to 36 ms after the press on a local server instead of 226 to 245 ms (the input lead), and 78 to 96 ms at a 60 ms round trip (a test relay); tag 16 goes out at once on a cast's start or stop and at 20 Hz while casting. The Shockwave: 60 m, 300 damage, ordinary Orks thrown 40 to 50 m, elites 15 to 20 m, bosses staggered, a 60 m ring (192 KOs in one cast at the Firing Range). The Librarian now carries every Space Marine equipment item; the HUD's WAVE cell moved left of the grenade box. Tests: `MusouLibrarianTests` updated, `MusouLibrarianPass3Tests` (the foreseen chain equals the server's on the same pool, the cast command, the send edges). Evidence: `<media folder>\previews\librarian-lightning\`. Restore switches `--old-librarian-lightning`, `--old-librarian-cast`, `--no-librarian-predict`, `--no-librarian-early`. Sound (the owner chose no downloads): the install's events as before, the psyker's cast and hit decoded at run time and played again pitched down, and layers synthesized in code (`LibrarianSynth`: crack, arc sizzle with hum, snaps, thunder roll, Shockwave boom) on the client's own players. Restore switches for the server-side changes: `SM_LIBRARIAN_OLD=shockwave,pull,send,early` on the server and the clients (`LibrarianVariant`, read in `GameplayTuning.ExtrasLoad`; `pull` changes his class, so the config hash refuses a mismatch). `PickLibrarian` now sends the player's perks and equipment as positions in the Librarian's own lists (the player's perk numbers were sent as positions). Tests `MusouLibrarianSwitchTests`. Open: the look, the feel and the sound wait for the owner; damage online still waits one-way latency plus up to a tick.

**Musou GPU spray particles (owner's choice of 2026-11-09; branch `musou/gpu-particles` from main dc8771e3; client only, Musou Mode only; no protocol, wire, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner picked GPU particles as the first step to many more effects in a Musou fight. In Musou Mode the effect player now hands one-shot sprays to the GPU: every ring sprite and streamer a spray's particles carry (directly, or under one combo there; sprays nested inside other sprays' particles included, which is how the blood effects `body_explode` and `body_dismemberment` are built) is written once, when the spray first shows, as a spawn record (time, seed, offset, direction, speed, a streamer's segment) into a texture-array pool; a shader computes the particle's place (the CPU path's closed `ParticlePos` formula), the combo's offset, scale and turn, and the leaf's size, colour, sprite cell and turn from the time, then hands the quad to the CPU batch's own vertex tail and fragment (`FxBatch` split into shared parts; the CPU shader's maths unchanged). Each frame the CPU writes one frame per spray (place, axes, scale, opacity, tint, smoke rein) and the time, and leaves the GPU's leaves out of its walk. Beams, lights, decals, meshes, deeper combos, looping sprays and soft-headed (plasma) trails stay on the CPU path. The live-effect cap is **1,200** with the GPU path (160 on the CPU path; `--fx-cap N` overrides). Code: `client/Extras/Musou/FxPlayer.MusouGpu.cs`, `FxGpuSprays.cs`, the engine-free allocator and curve packing `src/SmContent/Extras/Musou/FxGpuLayout.cs` (tests `FxGpuLayoutTests`), six `Extras*` hooks in `client/FxPlayer.cs` and one in `client/FxTest.cs` (pinned in `ExtrasBoundaryTests`). Classic PvP never turns it on. Restore switch: client `--fx-cpu` (Musou on the CPU path, cap 160). Test aids: `--fx-gpu` in the effects test view; `--fx-amount`, `--fx-keep-smoke`, `--fx-gamma` there play Musou's blood. Look: CPU and GPU stills of the same effects at the same moment in the test view (blasts, Musou blood, a tinted plasma and Weirdboy burst; player-distance and third-person cameras, `<media folder>\previews\musou-gpu-particles\`) differ only where alpha sprites overlap (max 68 to 98 of 255 there; the additive-only tinted set within 7): the GPU's alpha sprites are not depth-sorted (drawn first, in spawn order; spec "Musou Mode: GPU spray particles", provisional). Measured on the final build with `tools\musou-perf.ps1` (127.0.0.1 server, windowed client 1600 x 900, vsync off; other sessions' Godot and server processes were running on the PC, so the numbers carry some noise; each fight run gave about 100 s of battle). Fight (`clash500`): CPU path (cap 160) effects update **2.24 ms** a frame average (worst 10 s window 3.34 ms), about 141 effects live, 522 CPU quads a frame (244 alpha), frame mean 9.99 ms, GPU 2.93 ms; GPU path **2.24 ms** (worst window 4.22 ms) with about **380 effects live (up to 749)**, 495 CPU quads (100 alpha), up to about 7,500 GPU records drawn, frame mean 9.41 ms, GPU 2.34 ms. Burst stress (`burst`: 200 Orks die by one blast every 4 s, 15 bursts): CPU path about 27 effects live, effects update 3.35 ms, 1,133 CPU quads a frame, frame mean 16.65 ms (p99 41.7), worst burst frame median 53.4 ms; GPU path about **134 effects live**, 3.41 ms, 58 CPU quads, frame mean 12.11 ms (p99 54.7), worst burst frame median **63.6 ms** (starting about 10,000 sprays on a burst's frames costs up to about 14 ms), and 34,192 sprays dropped because the 131,072-record alpha pool was full (a full pool drops a spray's GPU particles, as the CPU batch drops quads past its 3,072). Earlier builds of this branch (labelled, not shipped): rings-only GPU at cap 1,200 drew about 450 effects for 4.63 ms with the CPU still drawing about 1,200 quads a frame (the blood streamers); the CPU path with cap 2,000 drew about 457 effects for 5.96 ms (frame mean 15.95 ms). Playtest check (spec "Musou Mode: GPU spray particles"): in the burst stress the GPU path's worst frames are worse than the CPU path's (worst burst frame median 63.6 against 53.4 ms, p99 54.7 against 41.7 ms) and 34,192 sprays were dropped by the full alpha pool; whether a big blast's hitch and the missing particles show in a real fight is for the owner's playtest. Review fixes (independent review of b9a24a38, APPROVE WITH MINORS): safe mode (the Compatibility renderer or `--safe-mode`) keeps the CPU path and its 160 cap, and a texture array the renderer cannot make falls back to the CPU path instead of drawing nothing (`FxGpuLayout.UseGpu`, test `Safe_mode_and_fx_cpu_keep_the_cpu_path_and_its_cap`); a one-at-random combo with no children picks nothing (was an index of -1); the `--fx-cap` argument is read once; the table uploads reuse their buffers. Residual risks: a finished GPU spray's entry stays in its effect's list until the effect is released (a long looping effect with inner sprays could grow it); the GPU shader ignores a node's own transform (right only at identity, which every spray it takes has today); a freed pool block is reused only by a request of the same size class. Follow-ups: spread a burst's spray starts over frames (the worst burst frame), depth-sort or order the GPU's alpha sprites, GPU beams and the light and decal budget. The owner's playtest is the gate.
**Musou Mode's customizer: Standard Marines, Librarian, Heretic (branch `claude/musou-customizer-bd44e2`, 2026-11-10; client and front end only, Musou Mode only; no protocol, config-hash, rules-version or profile-format change).** The owner: "adjust the existing loadout customizer that exists for both classic pvp and musou mode currently - leave classic pvp as it is now and only use this new adjustment for musou mode. ... the top level options to replace faction options are these: standard marines, librarian class, heretic class". **How it knows:** no new state: the customizer serves Musou when `CustomizerServices.Content` is the Musou profile (a Musou match's picker takes the match's flags; the front end is on Musou while on MUSOU MODE's pages). MUSOU MODE's page has a new CUSTOMIZER row (BACK returns there); the main menu's CUSTOMIZER and every Classic match keep the old creator. **Top level** (`client/Extras/Musou/Customizer/CreatorView.Musou.cs`, model `src/SmContent/Extras/Musou/MusouCustomizer.cs`): the header's faction row becomes "Musou Mode: Standard Marines | Librarian | Heretic (not yet)". *Standard Marines* is Classic's creator on the Space Marine side alone (Musou players are always Space Marines): Space Marine class names, no Chaos preview, the appearance editor on the Space Marine look (`CustomizerServices.ExtrasFactions`); the same CUSTOM 1-10 as Classic; Musou Mode arms the full chosen loadout plus the run's kit, so nothing else is locked. *Librarian* (no slots of his own): steps CLASS / WEAPONS / POWERS / PERKS / LOOK and the summary line read from the data (lead, 2026-11-10: the Librarian branch is changing his powers and equipment): his melee, guns and equipment from his class as `MusouLoadout.Prepare` appends it (`LibrarianLoadout.Of`; the first equipment fixed, other choices NOT YET), and each power with its numbers only while `LibrarianRules` holds them (`LibrarianPowers`, looked up by constant name, so a removed power drops out and changed numbers show without an edit here; a new power needs a line in its table); today: power sword, no grenades, no gun; chain lightning, Warp Pull, Psychic Shockwave and the stress scale; perks kept from the current class, what carries over (the active loadout's look: the preview shows him dressed with `LibrarianLook.Dress` and the force sword in hand, `PreviewStage.Musou.cs`; EDIT LOOK opens that look) and NOT YET rows for his own perks, other melee weapons, a choice of powers and a look of his own. In a match PLAY AS LIBRARIAN on his page takes the Esc menu row's path with the active loadout's look (saved first), and a Librarian's picker opens on his page. *Heretic*: a placeholder page, "not yet available", no class or preview. Core hooks (pinned in `ExtrasBoundaryTests`): `CreatorView` ExtrasTopLevel / ExtrasRefresh / ExtrasRoleLabel / ExtrasStepCount / ExtrasOpenAppearance / ExtrasDeploy, `PreviewStage` ExtrasDress / ExtrasWeapons, `CustomizerServices` ExtrasFactions. Other core edits: the Musou page row and BACK target, `AppearanceView.Open` falls back to an offered side, the screenshot gate ignores a hidden preview, RENAME / COPY do nothing while their buttons are hidden. Restore: client `--musou-old-customizer`. Test aid `--musou-entry marines|librarian|heretic`. Tests `MusouCustomizerTests` (17) and four UI self-test checks (the Musou page's CUSTOMIZER shows the three entries and no faction, BACK returns to the page, the main menu's keeps Classic's row). Screenshots `<media folder>\previews\musou-customizer\` (Classic before/after identical but for the idle model). For the owner: separate Musou loadout slots, and a Librarian loadout of his own (perks, melee, look), need a profile-format addition; PLAY AS LIBRARIAN sends the current class's perk indices into the Tactical perk list (found, not changed). Not verified: PLAY AS LIBRARIAN from the customizer in a live match (built, not run); no human has used it. Same branch, the lead's follow-up: the creator's EQUIPMENT note "Combat stimulants are listed but not simulated yet: the server gives you the default grenade" is gone (stale since perks/inert-2: `SmSim/Stims.cs` runs them in Classic, and Musou's combat applies their melee and damage modifiers and stim strike boosts); an item the simulation does not run keeps its own NOT SIMULATED YET tag. Crops `stim-note-before/after-*-crop.png` in the same folder.

**UI self-test back to 0 failures (branch `claude/sweet-easley-d0fc62`, 2026-11-10; client only, no protocol, config-hash or gameplay change).** `--ui-selftest` failed 8 checks on main since 2026-11-09. Two were out of date: since the sound mix pass (ac78dcbb) the master bus carries its 10 % boost (`SoundMixPass.MasterBusDb`: 50 % is -5.19 dB, 100 % +0.83 dB), so "Master moves the Master bus" and "restored to the defaults" now expect that value (no boost under `--sound-mix-classic`). Six were a real layout fault: the combat feel pilot's Camera shake and Screen flashes rows (7064c7cc) gave OPTIONS, GRAPHICS 17 rows, and the main menu's two-line note under them (where the game was found, the builds' address) pushed the column past its list at every tested window size but 1280x1024: the page scrolled, a scroll bar stood over the picture (at 1280x720 it cut the RENDERER line) and the note was hidden. The note is now the page's `MenuPage.Foot`: one row under the last row shown (where it stood before), outside the scroll list, at least `FootMargin` (12) inside the window, the list ending above it if the rows are ever too many. SOUND, CONTROLS and the Esc menu's OPTIONS (no note) look as before. New check per window size and tab: the foot is under the rows and in the window. The flaky checks now wait for readiness by the clock instead of frame counts: the armour bar (`Hud.VitalsDrawnFor`, `VitalsArmourCurrent`, `VitalsHealthCurrent`: drawn for the state with the state's own pictures, not the kept picture that stands in while a background thread renders the new one; the sweeps wait for both layers of the new kind) and the CONTROLS screen (`SendKey` / `SendPad` / `SendTrigger` wait until Input has taken each event, `Arm` until `ControlsView.CaptureReady`, prompts until shown and gone; helper `UiSelfTest.Until`). Result: 1034 pass, 0 fail in 3 runs (two of them side by side). GRAPHICS is full: one more row needs another layout at 1280x720 (a fourth tab or two columns, the owner's call). Unchanged and older: at 1280x720 the RENDERER line and a long game path in the note are cut at the list's right edge (the text grows to its 10.5 px minimum). **Musou sound A/B (musou/sound-ab, owner 2026-11-10: "remove the 'drowned out sound overload'"; test aids only, no default changed; the owner picks from the clips).** `--musou-sound-off` turns off, in Musou Mode only, any of: the data's bus Set/Reset actions (duck), the rendered low-pass (lowpass), the on-hit high-pass (hitfilter), the SmSfx and Master limiters (limiter), the 48+16 voice cap (steal: 160+48), the data's instance limits (instlimit), the far battle and war bed (ambience), the near Orks' voices (crowdvoices), the first-hit blast (blast), the deep layers under other Marines' bolter shots (allylayers), the bolt blasts' detonation sound (boltblast), the own bolter's deep layers (ownlayers); `--log-sound mixab` measures what engages, `--musou-record-mix` records the output, `--tfw-sound-capture` is the scripted fight. Measured in it (as now): the positioned pool is full the whole battle (thousands of steals, loud voices cut in their first 0.3 s; even a lifted cap of 160 + 48 fills); the bolt blasts' frag detonation sounds hold up to 46 voices and, off, the walk-in is 5.4 LU quieter; the own bolter's protected layers hold up to 48 voices (unstealable); the far battle's `play_big_damage_med_explosion` puts LPF 60 on three buses and -6 dB for 1.5 s and is live in about 40 % of the first half-minute of a battle (the fixed-seed far battle, the same in every run); the SmSfx limiter takes up to about 5 dB off peaks, rarely; Master's limiter sits before its +0.83 dB boost (Godot applies a bus's volume after its effects), so the output peaks at +0.53 dBFS (0.01 to 0.07 % of samples over full scale); instance-limit kills are footsteps only. Clips, sheet and numbers: the media folder's `previews/musou-sound-ab/` (outside the repository). Recording note: Movie Maker with sound hung Godot 4.7.2 in this fight, and a log line per steal (about 1000 a second) stalled the main thread for seconds; the recorder and the half-second tallies avoid both. **Then (owner, 2026-11-10, approved through the lead: "disable that sound effect for bolter explosions and leave it for regular grenades"), musou/bolt-blast-sound:** a bolt blast posted the frag's own detonation event `play_sm_grenade_explode_mp` (3 voices; no Set/Reset, low-pass or ringing in it), measured 276 times in a 50 s battle (about 330 a minute, 570 while fighting) against 2 thrown grenades; it no longer posts it (`NetworkView.TfwBoltBlastFrame`; restore `--musou-old-bolt-blast-sound`); thrown grenades, Bomb Squigs and the bolter's own sounds are unchanged.

**Musou: review fixes for the big Orks (branch `claude/musou-big-ork-deaths`, 2026-11-10).** The independent review found a soft-lock: with the big Orks off the armies' real cap, the armies' bodies (Nobs and twins) could pass their 512 slots, the crowds refilled to 1968, the pool had no slot left and the commander's spawn failed for good (BossId 0, never retried: the battle unwinnable). Now the armies keep to their own slots (`TfwBattle.ArmySlots`), the Boss Ork's and the crowd squad's pool checks count the Nobs' twins (`EliteBodies`), and a boss that finds no slot is tried again each tick with room made (`RetryBoss`, `MakeRoom`: the farthest ordinary Orks outside the armies go). Test: `A_full_pool_still_brings_the_commander_when_the_last_position_falls` (fails without the fix).

**Musou Mode's own loadout slots and the Librarian's loadout (branch `claude/musou-loadout-slots`, 2026-11-10; client, front end and profile only, Musou Mode only; no protocol, wire, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner approved the customizer's follow-up through the lead ("Musou own loadout spans approved"): Musou's pages stop sharing Classic PvP's custom-class slots. **Profile format** (schema 1 stays; both blocks optional and written only when present, so a profile without them reads and writes byte for byte as before; `docs/customizer-architecture.md` section 3): `sets` (`CustomizationProfile.Sets`, `LoadoutSet`: named slot sets with their own selection, read and repaired by the profile's own class rules, repair paths `sets.<name>...`) and `extras` (`CustomizationProfile.Extras`: added content's own JSON objects, kept as read, so a build without that content writes them back). **The view**: the client's `ProfileSession` holds an `IProfileView` (core, generic) that the services choose for the content profile (`CustomizerServices.ExtrasProfileView`, a new hook pinned in `ExtrasBoundaryTests`; applied when the content profile changes and at load): `Working` and `Saved` are the view's profile (cached per stored profile), edits are folded back (`Keep`), Save writes the whole stored profile, so the creator, the appearance editor, the picker and the Join work on Musou's slots unchanged. **Musou** (`SmContent/Extras/Musou/MusouSlots.cs`, `MusouProfileView`): the Standard Marines edit set `musou`; the first time Musou's pages open it is made as a copy of Classic's slots and selection (`MusouSlots.Opened`: the Ork Boy's loadouts left out, an Ork selection becomes the Tactical defaults; made in the saved and the working copy alike, so nothing reads as unsaved), and from then on the two are apart; a look deleted through the view is cleared from Classic's slots and the Librarian too (the looks are one list). **The Librarian's loadout** (`extras.musou.librarian`, `MusouLibrarianLoadout`): his melee weapon and equipment from his class's lists (`LibrarianLoadout.MeleeOptions` / `EquipmentOptions`, from `MusouLoadout.Prepare`: on main the power sword or the knife and no equipment; the Librarian pass's equipment shows by itself), two perks from his class's (the Tactical's; a weapon perk only for a weapon he can carry, so none of the Tactical's gun perks), and a look: the active loadout's (the default, as before), a saved look, or a new one copied from the one he wears (named Librarian). His page's rows on WEAPONS, POWERS, PERKS and LOOK are choices (`MusouRowKind.Choice`, SELECTED), saved with SAVE; while his page is open the view shows him as a class in slot 11 (`MusouSlots.LibrarianSlot`, past the ten, which the slot strip and the Join never reach), so EDIT LOOK opens his own look in the appearance editor as any loadout's. The preview holds the melee weapon he chose. `MusouSlots.LibrarianChoice` turns his loadout into his class's wire indices (an unknown name is his default) and `LibrarianLook` his look's code. PLAY AS LIBRARIAN sends this loadout and look (review fix 1 below). Restore: `--musou-shared-slots` (and `--musou-old-customizer`, which implies it): the shared slots and the read-only Librarian page of before. An older build that saves the profile drops `sets` and `extras` (Classic's part is kept). Tests: `CustomizationProfileTests` (sets and extras: an old profile byte for byte, round trip, repairs, dropped names, extras kept; the session's view with a test view), `MusouSlotsTests` (migration from an old profile, the two sets apart both ways, deleted looks, the Librarian's slot and entry, lenient reading, his wire indices), two UI self-test checks (his page shows his loadout; a loadout made on the Musou page is Musou's, not Classic's). UI self-test 1056 pass, 0 fail. Screenshots (`--customizer --content musou|extended --profile <scratch profile> --slot 1 --musou-entry marines|librarian --step ...`, windowed on the private desktop): `<media folder>\previews\musou-loadout-slots\` (README.txt: Classic's and Musou's slots side by side from one profile, the Librarian's weapons, perks and look). For the weapons to come (claw, spear, autocannon, demolition charge): Musou's slots store names and are checked against the catalogue like Classic's, so the weapons' own catalogue entries make them choosable here; the Librarian's names are checked against his class only when a loadout is made, so a weapon added to his class can be stored as it is. No human has used it. **Review fixes (independent review: CHANGES NEEDED, 2026-11-10):** (2) the creator no longer stays on the Librarian's slot 11 when it leaves his page (`CreatorView.LeaveLibrarianSlot`: the active loadout opens; before, after his look's EDIT LOOK the Standard Marines showed "CUSTOM 11 - empty", a class chosen there was dropped and DEPLOY said the slot was empty; a UI self-test check); (3) removing a look clears it from every loadout set and from the Librarian's entry (`ProfileViews.RemoveLook`, a new hook `ProfileViews.ExtrasLookRemoved` pinned in `ExtrasBoundaryTests`, `MusouSlots.LookRemoved`; before, a look removed in Classic stayed named in Musou's set, a reload showed a reset notice and the next new look, taking the lowest free id, was put on the Librarian and the Musou slot unasked); (4) a line for testers in the release notes (Musou loadouts are kept apart now; an older build can reset them); (5) an extras entry with a key used twice is dropped alone on reading, and the Librarian's reading and writing catch it (before, it could make every Musou edit fail). Tests for each. (1) After main took the Librarian's pass 3 (61c152b7, merged here), PLAY AS LIBRARIAN (`PickLibrarian`, `NetworkView.LibrarianLook.cs`) sends his saved loadout through `MusouSlots.LibrarianChoice` and his own look through `MusouSlots.LibrarianLook` (else the active loadout's, as before); with `--musou-shared-slots`, `--musou-old-customizer` or no profile loaded it keeps pass 3's carry-over of the player's current equipment and perks. Before, the page said "SAVE keeps it" and the match ignored it. Spec rows "Musou: own loadout slots" and "Musou: the Librarian's own loadout".
**Musou Librarian: the press after a death (branch `claude/librarian-press-reset`, 2026-11-10; client only, no protocol, wire, `MusouSim.Version` or `TfwRules.Version` change).** From the pass 3 re-review: the own press was ended only while the own Librarian was in the server's section, and the server leaves dead Librarians out, so a Librarian who died holding Fire and let go while dead kept his press; his first press after respawning sent no cast command and waited the input lead (about 230 ms).
