**Lightning claw and power spear: strike animation previews (branch `claude/claw-spear-anims`, 2026-11-10; client and SmContent data only, Musou Mode only; no gameplay, protocol, wire, config-hash or rules-version change).** Previews for the owner's approval of the two new Musou weapons' animations (`docs/new-weapons-design.md` sections 5 and 6; nothing is simulated yet). The strikes are our own keyframes (`SmContent/Extras/Musou/ClawSpearClips.cs`: the spine, head, clavicles and hands as turns in the stance's frame, the arms as aimed directions read against the install's stances with the stage's `--pose-log`) laid over the install's clips through the pose hook the Librarian's cast already uses (`CharacterViewer.ExtrasPoseOverlay`, now calling `WeaponPoseOverlay` in `client/Extras/Musou/Weapons/`); no new hook, no original byte copied, the legs never keyed so the feet stay planted. The timing is the design's exactly: the claw's five strikes are the power sword's X1..X4 and Y backhand at 1.25x (hits 0.256 / 0.230 / 0.346 / 0.426 / 0.264 s), the spear's three sweeps the thunder hammer's X1..X3 at 0.85x (0.711 / 0.667 / 0.824 s), the impale at the hammer landing's 0 s; `ClawSpearClipsTests` pins them. Each strike has a gathering wind-up, a snap onto the hit (the spin sweep passes the front at a constant rate and runs on, about 250 degrees of blade travel), an overshooting follow-through and a settle; a chained strike fades from the previous one over 0.14 s. Stand-in models from primitives (`ClawSpearStandIns.cs`: a piston-backed gauntlet with four talons on the right forearm, a 2.8 m spear with a bronze collar and a glowing 0.9 m blade on the line through both hands) and a preview stage (`--claw-spear-test`, three cameras, stills and Movie Maker clips) render them; previews in `<media folder>\previews\claw-spear-anims\`. Approach, timing table and the owner's open points: `docs/claw-spear-animations.md`. Restore: `--no-weapon-pose` (the stances alone); nothing was drawn in a match then (the spear's clips are since "W3b" below; the claw's stay on the stage). **Owner's review the same day:** spear approved with the rest pose "upright at his side" (`spear_rest`, a held pose every sweep starts from and returns to) and the impale's release kept at 0.5 s; claws "redo: too stiff / small motions, reads like a sword; keep the diagonal rake": every claw strike re-authored with the lower spine as the hips, spine yaw to about 70 degrees, arcs from far behind the body to far past the target, a two-frame hold on the cocked apex, the off hand bracing or shoving, and claw moves (diagonal rake, gutting rake, punching stab, tearing rip, overhead rake); the previews re-rendered over the first set. **Second review:** "no part of the character's body should remain still through this.. he should be putting his entire body into the strokes", "add pelvis now", "keep the stab-and-rip pair": the overlay gained `Move` channels (the pelvis turns, drops to 0.26 m and shifts its weight) and `Foot` channels with a two-bone leg solve (a lead foot lifts, steps and replants: X1 the left 0.40 m ahead, X2 the right, X3 a 0.75 m left lunge, X4 the right stamping back, the heavy a left stamp; a planted foot is solved back onto its spot, so it never slides; thighs, calves and the root are never keyed), the stage keeps its facing from the hips as read before the pelvis moves; the claw previews re-rendered (third set), the spear's unchanged. **Claws approved ("approve, refine later"); the spear's fourth pass:** "carried 1 handed in the right hand when running or idling", sweeps "wider and longer" (300 degrees, 15 m), "the pelvis and legs should be greatly active in facilitating a powerful swing animation": a `Grip` track on the clip (the left hand on the shaft 0 to 1; the stand-in stands the shaft upright from the right hand at 0), the rest one-handed with the left arm free, each sweep's wind-up bringing the left hand to the shaft and the settle letting go; the three sweeps re-authored with the claw's full-body treatment (pelvis coil, drop and drive; a lead-foot step of 0.50 / 0.55 / 0.65 m; the spin a 70 degree hip pivot with the left foot replanting forward-left) and about 300 degrees of blade travel through each hit; hit times unchanged; the spear previews re-rendered (fourth set). **Fifth pass, from the owner's reference clip** (a halberd's "Wrath hew from Field Guard", kept out of the repository; "each light attack combo swing should be a different hewing cut, and the F + F stun strike combo should end in a massive stab", "grip higher up on the spear shaft towards the blade [running], then slide the spear inside his hand to hold it lower towards the butt end for melee"): the light string is three hewing cuts (the wrath hew from the steer overhead down diagonally into the field guard, a rising hew, a reverse hew looped overhead and cut flat at the waist), the F, F chain is a head-height snap cut (the hammer's Y interrupt, 1.961 s, hit 0.509) then a massive lunging stab (the hammer's Y,Y slam, 3.529 s, hit 1.294, chained at 0.627), all full-body with steps; a `GripPoint` track (the right hand's place on the shaft in metres from the butt: the carry then 1.3 m, 0.95 m since the sixth pass, to `LowGrip` 0.5 m; then also as a 0..1 slide for W3's `WeaponRig.GripSlide`, dropped in W3b for the metres themselves) slides the shaft through the hand over 0.25 s into the first strike and 0.4 s back after the last, the carry tilted forward-up at the side; spear previews re-rendered (fifth set). **Sixth pass ("redo again": "the legs becoming disconnected from the body", "straight back the entire time", "the blade needs to face forward at rest", closer to the reference):** the leg bug found and fixed in the overlay: the marine rig hangs `RIG_SpineA` beside `RIG_Pelvis` under the root, so a pelvis moved or turned alone left the torso behind; `CharacterViewer.WeaponPose.RigidWith` now carries the spine with the pelvis as one rigid piece (every clip, the approved claws too, their keys unchanged); the spear's spine keys capped (`SpineLimitPitch` 8, roll 5, yaw 16; a test pins it) with every lean and turn the pelvis's; the hews re-authored to the reference's shapes (the steer with the hands straight up, the haft's overhead circle, a 0.3 m drop and 0.6 to 0.85 m steps, the hard diagonal cut into the field guard); the blade's edge forward at rest, the carry 80 degrees; clips also written as H.264 MP4s (sixth set).
**Polish pass P1: quick wins (branch `claude/polish-p1`, 2026-11-10; client, options, server runtime; both modes; no simulation, wire, protocol or config-hash change).** The first milestone of `docs/polish-pass-plan.md` (the owner's request of 2026-11-10 and his answers of the same day). **(1) Sound instance limits for every post, opt-in:** `--sound-limits all` applies the banks' per-node "limit sound instances" and the below-threshold culling to every post, not only to footsteps; measured in the baseline harness (13 players, 90 s, the measuring client with sound): 2,475 instance kills, **322 of them on 20 nodes the footsteps default never limited** (blasts, shots and hits stacking on themselves; 2,514 kills, all footsteps, before). The review (2026-11-10) kept **the default at `footsteps`** until the owner has heard an A/B: the flag bytes' order is an interpretation (`SoundBank.cs` reads kill newest, virtual behaviour, ignore parent; `docs/discovery.md` now says the same and that it is unverified), the all-parents rule is low confidence and the -60 dB cut is ours, so with `all` a misread byte would reach hit confirms, speech and the match-end stingers. For the A/B: `--log-sound footstep` ends a run with `sound at exit:` and one `LIMITNODE` line per node that fired (id, limit, kill-newest / kill-oldest, global / per-emitter, ignore-parent, the below-threshold byte, kills, drops), and the clips `<media folder>\previews\polish-pass\sound-limits\footsteps.avi` and `all.avi` (the same 13-player match, 45 s each, Movie Maker at 30 fps with sound). Their numbers: footsteps **288 kills** (10 nodes, every one a footstep layer: per-emitter limits of 1 or 2), all **1,196 kills** (25 nodes; the new ones are four global limit-4 nodes with 238, 89, 34 and 9 kills and per-emitter nodes of 1 to 3 with 66, 59, 16, 15, 14, 11, 11 ...), no drops in either (no kill-newest node fired); voices made virtual / revived 991 / 958 against 1,144 / 1,116 and culled under the 2D threshold 0 against 2: the demotion of quiet non-positioned loops is not what `all` changes. Every revive was a loop and resumed its position (`loops resumed` 958 and 1,116). Also from the review: a looping non-positioned voice revived from its virtual wait resumes its running position instead of restarting (`LoopsResumed` in the sound summary); F3 is a reserved key in the keybinds screen; the safe-mode grime flag is `SafeMode.GrimeFoldedInSafeMode` in the core (the Options view names nothing from `Extras/`; `ExtrasBoundaryTests` checks namespaces, so it could not have caught the class reference). **(2) Performance readout:** F3 cycles OFF, FPS, FPS + NETWORK (fps, mean and worst frame ms of the last second; ping, snapshot loss, interpolation delay, input slack from `GameClient`'s own numbers) in the match's top right corner (`HudReadout`), remembered as `performanceReadout` in `frontend.json`; no Options row (the owner: the original's options only; and the GRAPHICS page's 17 rows fill its list: an 18th made the UI self-test's fit check fail); `--readout fps|network|off` pins it for a run (a bot too, for captures). Capture: `<media folder>\previews\polish-pass\p1-readout_003.png` (175 fps, 5.7 ms, ping 20 ms, loss 0 %, interp 53 ms, slack 49 ms on loopback). **(3) `LOADTIME` line** per map load (content, collision world, ragdoll world, navigation, visuals, looks and warm-ups, total): Manufactorum here 2.6 to 3.0 s (content 0.75 to 0.9 s, collision world 0.37 to 0.47, ragdoll world 0.22 to 0.32, visuals 0.84 to 0.86, looks and warm-ups 0.39 to 0.48); the loading captions wait for P2's map load off the main thread (the main thread is blocked during the load, a caption set before it would not draw). **(4) Server runtime:** `GCLatencyMode.SustainedLowLatency` (`TICKPACE` now says so; paused 0.5 to 1.2 ms per 5 s window with 13 players) and `PublishReadyToRun` for a server published with a runtime identifier (the release zips; `dotnet build` and `server.cmd` unaffected; `-p:SmReadyToRun=false` publishes JIT-only; checked by the review's publishes: see the R2R note at the end of this paragraph); `SM_OLD_SERVER_RUNTIME=1` keeps the GC default. **(5) Ashfall grime in safe mode:** always FAST (folded) on the Compatibility renderer or with `--safe-mode`, the Graphics row shows it and rests; `--ashfall-grime-exact-safe` restores the option's choice. **(6) `--physics-ticks <n>`** (measurement aid, a human client): Godot's physics steps a second for one run; measured 30 against 60 in the harness: **inconclusive** (physics step 3.2 ms at 30 against 3.1 to 4.8 ms at 60 in runs with sound, 1.65 ms in the quieter baseline run: the engine's physics time here follows the PC's load more than the step rate), so the default stays 60 and the item goes back to P7 with a ragdoll capture. **Also found:** the `sound` phase stalls the main thread after the warm-up (416 ms at 50 s, 47 to 67 ms at 11, 35 and 71 s, 174 to 181 ms at the join) in both sound runs: plan item 29 for P3. Checks: both builds 0 errors; `dotnet test tests/SmFormats.Tests --filter GameOptionsTests|CustomizerModelTests|SoundLimit|InstanceLimit` 100 passed; the UI self-test 1,057 passed, 0 failed; `smtool refine-register --check` ok. Not run: the full `dotnet test` (the lead's capped run), a server publish, a human's listen. Harness: `tools/polish-pvp-baseline.ps1` (new `-ClientArgs`, `-Sound`, `-SafeSeconds 0`; the bots' PIDs are now captured from the information stream, so they are stopped by PID at the end); logs under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\perf\polish-pass\p1-*`. **ReadyToRun checked (review):** `dotnet publish -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained` and `-r linux-x64` both succeeded from this checkout (the crossgen2 and runtime packs restored from NuGet as any publish does); the published assemblies are the ahead-of-time images (SmServer.dll 716 KB against 267 KB plain, SmSim.dll 6.9 MB against 2.3 MB), and the published win-x64 server reports **2,990 methods jitted** at start against **6,822** for the plain Release build (the rest precompiled); R2R stays on by default. The VM's `vm-build-server.sh` publishes on the live box, so it downloads crossgen2 there once and compiles there (`-p:SmReadyToRun=false` skips it). Not measured yet: the first-join tick with the R2R server (the baseline's 65 ms), so `release/NEXT.md` makes no promise about it.
**Musou weight pass MW1: ground contacts (claude/musou-weight, 2026-11-10; client only, Musou Mode only; no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules-version change).** The first step of the owner's weight and impact pass (plan and baseline: docs/musou-weight-impact-plan.md, approved with his five answers the same day). Each frame the own marine and the 7 nearest other marines within 45 m report their ground contacts (`MusouWeightRules`, `MusouContactTracker`, `Weight/NetworkView.MusouWeight.cs`): footfalls and plants from the clips' foot tags through a new core hook in the sound's tag pass (`ExtrasFootfall`, after a tag is admitted, so one footfall is one contact), and for poses without foot tags the toes, knees, hands, pelvis and shoulders against the ground under the character (touches, skids along the ground every 0.08 s, landings after 0.15 s in the air by fall speed). No visuals yet; MW2 draws them. Measured with `--tfw-weight-capture --log-musou-weight` (headless, sound loaded, 127.0.0.1): walk, sprint and approach give a step per footfall (sprint 9 to 10 own steps in 3.3 s), the sprint stop 1 to 2 plants, each roll 6 touches in order (right shoulder, right hand, pelvis, right knee, then the feet) and about 21 skids (the roll's skating, MW3), every jump-pack landing 2 landings plus the slide's skids, each melee swing 1 to 3 plants from the combos' foot tags; never an Ork. Restore: `--no-musou-contacts`, `--musou-old-weight` (the whole pass). Tests `MusouWeightContactTests`; `ExtrasBoundaryTests` pins the hook.

**Musou weight pass MW2 to MW4: puffs, the body's settle, attack punch (claude/musou-weight, 2026-11-10; client only, Musou Mode only; no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules-version change).** On the MW1 contacts. **MW2, puffs** (`MusouPuffRules`, `Weight/NetworkView.MusouPuffs.cs`): each contact plays the install's own foot dust (`knockback_kick_footslide`) and, for plants, body falls and landings, the grit and stones of `jumppack_land_light`, scaled by the contact's strength and the surface (metal 0.4, stone 0.8, no dust off bodies), on the GPU spray path; the dust draws although the no-smoke rule is on (`KeepSmoke`, the owner's "small dust allowed"); allies at half size and every other step; the CPU path (old GPUs) every other step and skid; lowest cull priority; no decals. **MW3, the settle** (`MusouWeightRules.SettleOf`, `CharacterViewer.MusouSettle`, through the pose overlay that now runs the Librarian's cast and then the settle): landings drop the pelvis 6 to 14 cm by fall speed (0.06 s down, 0.25 s back), a sprint stop 5 cm with a 7-degree lean back, a melee step's plant 3 cm leaning 3 degrees into the blow, a roll's end 5 cm; the ankles are held where the pose put them, so the knees bend. **The roll fit was dropped after measuring:** the plan assumed the roll clip covered 8 m; the frame log (`--tfw-weight-capture --tfw-weight-log`, new `et`/`ed` fields) shows the body follows the clip's own extracted path to within 0.1 m and the three directions travel 8.9, 9.2 and 9.6 m, so the clip's rate is already right and the roll's sliding contacts (about 21 skids a roll, MW1) come from the clip's in-place pose against its extracted motion, not from the rate; left as it is (a follow-up would compare the extracted path with the pelvis's own track). **MW4, punch** (`MusouPunchRules`, `Weight/NetworkView.MusouPunch.cs`; core hooks `ExtrasAttackTime` in the attack pose and `ExtrasCameraOffset` in `FxApplyShake`): every marine's strike is drawn with the wind-up at 0.85x (heavy 0.8x) and the last 0.15 s (heavy 0.18 s) before the hit faster, the hit at its own time and the clip's end at its end (the effects, sounds and the simulation unchanged); the own heavy strikes and combo finishers that meet Orks hold the pose 50 ms at the hit (no freeze, no shake; the owner's 40 to 60 ms) and push the camera 4.5 cm (heavy 7 cm) forward and 2.5 cm to the swing's side for 0.22 s, times the Camera shake option; kills are not known at the strike, so they get no hold. Hit Orks of the rank and file are pushed back by the weapon (hammer 0.35 m, axe 0.28, knife 0.12, the rest 0.2). Measured (headless, 127.0.0.1, `--log-musou-weight`): in the scripted run 3 of 6 strike presses were accented (the finisher and the heavies, 2 to 7 Orks met each), every own strike retimed; puffs 1 to 3 effects a contact. Captures: `<media folder>\previews\musou-weight\mw2` and `mw4` (player view and third person, Forward+). Restore: `--no-musou-puffs`, `--no-musou-weight-body`, `--no-musou-punch`, `--musou-old-weight`. Tests `MusouWeightContactTests` (13 at MW4); `ExtrasBoundaryTests` pins the two hooks.

**Musou weight pass MW5 and MW6: stance cross-fades, thinner blast jolts, contact sounds (claude/musou-weight, 2026-11-10; client only, Musou Mode only; no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules-version change).** **MW5** (`MusouTransitionRules`, `Weight/NetworkView.MusouTransitions.cs`; core hook `CharacterViewer.ExtrasBlendSeconds` in `SelectLayer`): a marine's stance changes cross-fade over at least 0.25 s (the core's 0.15). Measured with `--transition-probe` (headless, pooled runs, 4 without and 2 with): the body's turn at moving to ready 107 to 47 degrees a frame (median), its jerk 43 to 27 cm/frame², ready to idle jerk p90 78 to 52, ready to melee 60 to 44, melee to move 19 to 14, idle to ready unchanged (64 to 66). Tried and dropped on the same probe: an eased body heading (moving to ready unchanged, ready to idle's turn 23 to 78 degrees a frame) and a 0.15 s floor on clip entries (idle to ready's jerk p90 64 to 109). The install's unused transition clips (the 180-degree turn into a sprint, the half-speed sprint stop, the other hit directions, the sprint stagger, the stun recovery, the mid-air hit, the light classes' drop) are not wired: each needs root-motion and branch data the client does not read yet, and the hit reactions already turn the body toward the attacker (anim/melee-interaction); left for a later pass. **MW6** (`MusouImpactRules`, `Weight/NetworkView.MusouImpact.cs`; core hook `ExtrasBlastFeel` in `FxDetonation`, also used by the Stormboy's crash): a detonation shakes and jolts the own camera only within 12 m and once in 0.25 s (the owner's "Thin the jolts"): in the tactical capture 123 blast jolts and up to 17 in a second before, 24 and at most 3 after; the own roll's end dips the camera 0.4 degrees. A knee, hand, pelvis or shoulder meeting the ground plays the class's heavy footstep command on the surface (the data's `EVT_*_Foot_Rush`, the owner's footstep level), a jump-pack dash's landing the pack's lightest landing entry; one a marine in 0.15 s, within 25 m, through the sound system's limits: about one per roll and per dash landing. Checked against main's bolter-blast sound change (bolt blasts no longer play the frag detonation): the pass posts no blast sound; it only thins the blasts' camera feel. Captures `<media folder>\previews\musou-weight\mw6`. Restore: `--no-musou-transitions`, `--no-musou-impact-camera`, `--no-musou-contact-sound`, `--musou-old-weight`. Tests `MusouWeightContactTests` (14); `ExtrasBoundaryTests` pins the two hooks.

**Musou weight pass MW7: cost and the Compatibility renderer (claude/musou-weight, 2026-11-10).** Cost at 1,000 Orks (`SM_TFW_STRESS=1000,4`, windowed Forward+, `--frame-profile`, the pass on and `--musou-old-weight` run side by side): the weight pass's own phase (`musou: weight`: contacts, settles, sounds) stays under the profile's 0.1 ms listing; the effects phase rose from 1.12 to 1.35 ms a frame on average (the puffs); frame time p50 12.6 vs 14.3 ms and p99 51.5 vs 50.2 ms, within the noise of two clients sharing the GPU. Compatibility renderer (`--rendering-method gl_compatibility`, safe mode, the CPU effect path; stills from `--tfw-weight-capture` with `--tfw-test <dir>`, since Movie Maker crashes with that renderer): the settle, the punch and the grit and stones of the landings show; **the dust clouds do not draw there** (also with the soft ground fade off; cause not found): open for the next pass. The capture aid now takes stills at the stop, the roll, the pack landings and the first heavy strike. Captures `<media folder>\previews\musou-weight\mw7-compatibility`. Not done: a human playtest; the roll's skating (the clip's in-place pose against its extracted motion); the install's unused transition clips; kills getting the pose hold.

**Musou weight pass: review fixes (claude/musou-weight, 2026-11-10).** From the independent review (approve with minors): the puffs play at cull priority -1 (below shot impacts, hit feedback and sparks at 0) and landings at 0 (below tracers), so a full CPU effect player drops them first; the remapped strike time is the drawn clip time only, the hand-over, root-driven and foot-lock gates keep the simulation's attack time (the legs no longer hand over late under the 0.85x wind-up); the blast jolt limiter keeps the strongest blast of each 0.25 s window (a later one at least 1 m closer jolts too) and the own grenades always shake (a thrown item first seen within 3 m of the own marine within 0.6 s of his throw; hook `ExtrasBlastFeel` now takes the detonation); a marine no longer tracked loses its roll state (no roll-end settle and dip at a respawn after dying mid-roll); the contact counts and their strings are built only with `--log-musou-weight`. The combo finisher's hold is its own spec row, tagged ours. Noted: the step contacts come only through the sound's tag pass (none with `--no-sound` or no audio device). Restore switches as before.

**Musou loadout slots: re-review minors (branch `claude/musou-slots-saved` from main 4f4b63f5, 2026-11-10; client and profile only, Musou Mode only; no protocol, wire, config-hash or rules-version change).** The focused re-review of 931a0402 (approve with minors) found two things. (1) PLAY AS LIBRARIAN from the Esc menu sent unsaved choices: `PickLibrarian` read the session's working copy, and closing the picker keeps unsaved edits. It now reads `session.Saved`, as Classic's close path sends the saved active loadout (the customizer's own button saves first, so there nothing changes); a UI self-test check pins that an unsaved Librarian choice is in the working copy but not in the saved profile. (2) Removing the look he wears rebuilt his whole entry and dropped keys this build does not know; `MusouSlots.LookRemoved` now removes only the `look` key (his entry, and Musou's, go when nothing else is left), with a test.
**Musou's arsenal W0: the base (branch `claude/arsenal-w0` from main 61c152b7, 2026-11-10; Musou Mode only; no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner approved docs/new-weapons-design.md as written ("i approve the design as written - don't use a fable agent yet until i actually approvate creating the custom animations"); W0 lays the base the four items are built on, with no item yet. The registry (`ArsenalRules` in SmSim, `Arsenal` in SmContent, both in `Extras/Musou/Arsenal/`) names the four items and gives each a set of partial methods its own milestone implements in its own file, so W1 to W4 share no file. `Arsenal.Append` runs in the load dispatcher before `MusouLoadout.Prepare` and returns the config itself while every entry is a stub. Six core hooks (seven pinned partials), each pinned in `ExtrasBoundaryTests` and a no-op without Musou's content (the client's model and clip hooks check the Musou flag: `WeaponRig.Content`, set by the match view and the customizer's preview, and the match's config; review 2026-11-10, since the Remote Detonators' name is an install name): `MpClasses.ExtrasMeleeMap`, `Loadouts.ExtrasWieldsHammer`, `PerkCatalog.ExtrasItems` (with `PerkCatalog.For` / `CustomizationCatalog.For`, which `CustomizerServices.Catalog` now applies to the content profile in effect: the data's catalogue itself for every profile without Musou; and `ProfileViews.ExtrasSetCatalog`, so Musou's loadout set, merged from claude/musou-loadout-slots, is read with Musou's catalogue and a Musou slot keeps an arsenal item), `WeaponRig.ExtrasWeaponModel` (with an always-held flag for the claw), `NetworkView.ExtrasThrownVisual` (the charge's model) and `AnimationAlias.ExtrasAnimationAlias` (read by the hip-fire, sprint, reload and flinch name rules and the client's hammer stance). The clip-speed factor is a `MeleeTuning.WeaponMap` field (1 for every data map, applied over the graph's and Fast Stomp's speeds). Checking how the client applies Fast Stomp found that a strike with distance variants is posed scaled to the step's duration, but a single-clip strike at the simulation's time; so `NetworkView.MeleeClipSpeed` now scales the single-clip time by the weapon's factor (1 for the data: posed as before). The animation seam (lead 2026-11-10: the owner wants custom animations for the claw and the spear, made to the design's hit times, used once he approves them): the two play the power sword's and the thunder hammer's clips as stand-ins (their light and heavy clip lists through `AnimationAlias`), and one pinned client hook, `NetworkView.ExtrasMeleeClip`, gives a strike a clip of its own and its rate, posed alone, without touching the simulation; a source for clips that are not in the install comes with the approved clips. Six Musou call sites call no-op partials of `World.Arsenal.cs`: the cleave, a weapon's own blast on the bolt blasts' path, the jump events, a projectile meeting an enemy or a contraption, a per-tick step and the per-item refill period. Not hooked, noted for W2 and W3: the jump pack's own moves (the factor does not reach them) and the presentation name rules beyond the five. Rebased onto main 4f4b63f5 (with the Musou loadout slots). Tests: `ArsenalBaseTests` (names, every entry a stub, Musou's set catalogue), a clip-speed test in `MeleeTuningTests`, the content-scoped catalogue in `CustomizationCatalogTests`, `ExtrasBoundaryTests` (the hooks' pins and every call site, the seam's included), `ConfigHashPinTests` (the install's faithful and extended match configs hash as on main 61c152b7: 0x5277E16C8E7F6260 and 0x2AAB9E068C454594, the VM's Classic hash). The briefs for W1 to W4 are in the design doc, section 11.

**Musou's arsenal W0b: presentation by source and the pack moves' clip speed (branch `claude/arsenal-w0b` from main 1f95a3f1, 2026-11-10; client presentation only, Musou Mode only; no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules-version change).** W1 to W3 met the two gaps W0 left: the claw was silent ("sound note: wargear sm_mp_melee_lightning_claw not found"), and the autocannon's muzzle flash, tracer, casings, fire sound and HUD reticle and ammunition never loaded, because the effect and sound catalogues read only class-named wargear and the twin `csm_mp_exotic_auto_cannon` is in no class. Now each item names the install files it shows and sounds as (`Arsenal.PresentationSources`: the claw the power sword, the spear the thunder hammer, the autocannon its twin, then the heavy bolter only if the twin has none), asked through one pinned client hook, `NetworkView.ExtrasPresentationSources`, in a Musou match only. The client reads the effect catalogue with those files too (`EffectCatalogue.Load(gameDir, extraWargear)`), and both catalogues copy the first candidate's entries under the item's name (`EffectCatalogue.WithSources`, `SoundTriggers.WithSources`); the name rules (power flash, sword glow and flare, deployed effects, idle hum, the procedural hit sound) read the source's name (`PresentedAs`). Without sources both loads are the old calls and the catalogues the same objects. The HUD has two pinned hooks under `Hud.Content` (the match's content): the autocannon's own movie reticle (`autocannon_mc`, `autocannon_active_mc`; the twin's `weapon_type` is the launcher's) and the heavy bolter family's `ammo_autocannon_mc` display. A third pinned hook, `NetworkView.ExtrasMoveClipSpeed`, gives the claw's 1.25 and the spear's 0.85 to the charge and the dash attack (the clip at the phase's time times the factor) and to the pound's and the air slash's impact and get-up (clip seconds since the impact times it); the air slash's dive stays fitted to the dive. The Y,Y finishers were already reached (heavy steps, built and posed with the factor). The hammer's own air slash, sprint attack, two-handed grip (which holsters the pistol: W3 saw the pistol stay in the left hand during a spear swing) and stride rule, and the transition probe's two-handed flag, now read `AnimationAlias`, so the spear plays them as the hammer. Not hooked, noted: Musou's predicted strike contact (`MusouContactRules.PredictsMelee`, a sword name rule in Musou's code) and the weapon picture (`UiArt.WeaponIcon`). Tests: `PresentationSourcesTests` (both `WithSources`: the same object without sources, the first candidate with any, the name's stale entries replaced, every other property carried over), `ArsenalPresentationTests` (the table, the autocannon's reticle and box, and an install check that the twin has its own effects and sounds), `ExtrasBoundaryTests` (four new hooks and fourteen call sites pinned, each changed alias line by its exact text (review 2026-11-10); `ArsenalRules.IsArsenal` is a set lookup now, allocation-free for the per-frame checks), `ConfigHashPinTests` unchanged.

**Musou's arsenal W1: the autocannon.** Not started (brief: docs/new-weapons-design.md section 11).
**Musou's arsenal W1: the autocannon (branch `claude/arsenal-w1` from main 1f95a3f1, 2026-11-10; Musou Mode only; no protocol change; `MusouSim`/`TfwRules` versions not bumped: the weapon enters only through the Musou profile's config hash).** The owner's design (docs/new-weapons-design.md section 4): "the autocannon should fire slower but do more damage than the heavy bolter and have 2x the HE explosion size of the bolter and bolt pistol". `Arsenal.Append` reads `csm_mp_exotic_auto_cannon` from the install (`WeaponTuning.Read`) and appends its twin `sm_mp_exotic_auto_cannon` (full auto, 0.4 s, 50, heat 15, clip 400, the heavy bolter's handling, no brace) to the weapons and to the Space Marine Devastator's primaries (last of four on the install: the heavy bolter, lascannon and plasma cannon keep their indices); the catalogue row, the animation alias (the heavy bolter's) and the model (`turret_aa` in the heavy bolter's mounts) are the entry's other parts. The explosive round is `World.ArsenalShotBlast` (`AutocannonBlast.cs`): the bolt blasts' path with a 2.5 m splash, so a round through 5 Orks blasts at each of the 6 struck. One core change, asked for in the W1 brief and in its own commit: `CustomizerServices.ExtrasConfig` (pinned), so a Join from the Musou page names the autocannon in Musou's config instead of sending the default. Tests: `AutocannonTests` (10: the twin's numbers, the list, 0.4 s, 15 rounds, the blast through 6 Orks, a kill torn apart), `AutocannonContentTests` (2), `ArsenalBaseTests` updated for the one row. Checked on the install: the twin reads with heat 1/15/9/1/4.5/0.41 and joins `sm - devastator` after the plasma cannon; the Classic profile has none. Follow-up (lead's answers): the blast's effect is drawn at radius / 1.25 of the bolt blast's (`NetworkView.TfwBoltBlast.cs`, `BoltBlastSizeOf`; the bolt blast itself unchanged); the screenshot gate is the scripted `--tfw-autocannon-capture` (PNGs in `previews\arsenal-w1\`: the model in hand reads as a long barrel across the chest with no clipping in the side and rear views; no muzzle flash, tracer, fire sound, reticle or ammo box yet). Left for W0b (the presentation source hook, the W0 author): the Chaos file's effects, sounds and HUD for the twin; the recoil clip is then checked.

**Musou's arsenal W2: the lightning claw (claude/arsenal-w2, 2026-11-10; Musou Mode only; the Musou config hash changes (a melee choice is appended to the Assault Marine); no wire or protocol change; no Classic change).** One claw on the right hand plus the pistol (owner's answers D2, D13, D16): an Assault Marine melee choice `sm_mp_melee_lightning_claw` (no wargear file in the install), built from the power sword's own combo as the loader reads it (`Arsenal.ClawCombo`: every step time divided by 1.25, every damage x0.8, the charge likewise, no perk variants), on the sword's map with `ClipSpeed` 1.25 and the sword's animations through the alias; the customizer row "Lightning Claw" beside the sword's. The model is built in code on the sword's grip (`ClawModel`: a steel gauntlet with brass bands and pistons laid along the armour's forearm, four long curved steel talons 1.9 x the forearm; ours, from the lead's description of the owner's images; reworked after his first look: "longer, bigger talons", "fit it to the forearm", "materials and glow"), always worn, with a blue power glow along the talons that brightens with a crackle while a claw strike is posed (`ClawCrackle`; `--claw-crackle-demo` is a still aid). Stills: `<media folder>\previews\arsenal-w2\`. The simulation's hit tick is the sword's divided by 1.25 and the client poses the same clip 1.25 times faster, so contact and hit coincide by construction (`ClawTests`). Tests: `ClawTests` (scaling, the Assault-only append at the end of the choices, the map and alias, the catalogue), with the boundary, Musou isolation, config hash pin and public text guard tests. Not done, raised with the lead: the Musou customizer's claw row and JOIN (the customizer's config has no Musou arsenal until W1's ExtrasConfig hooks land: check after merging main), the pack's dash attack, ground pound and air slash, the charge's client clip speed, and the name-keyed sounds (the claw is silent: no swing, hit or power-flash sound); the custom claw clips: the owner chose (2026-11-10: "for now just make the power claw use the sword animations") to keep the sword's install animations at 1.25x, so the claw does not drive `CharacterViewer.WeaponPose` and `LightningClawClip` stays a stand-in. Review fixes (2026-11-10): the claw's glow is driven per player from that player's own strike state (a copy of the glow material per claw, because the Compatibility renderer draws no instance uniform) and its driver drops a freed view's callback (a rejoin makes a new view); the claw is worn, so a stim does not stow it on the hip; `--claw-crackle-demo` and `--claw-glow-test` are classified test aids (`--claw-glow-test` pulses the own claw's per-claw glow without a strike, for stills under any renderer; a real swing in a battle was not recorded).

**Musou's arsenal W3: the power spear (branch `claude/arsenal-w3` from main 1f95a3f1, 2026-11-10; Musou Mode only; `MusouSim.Version` 38, no protocol or wire change; the config hash of the Musou profile changes (a combo added), the faithful and extended profiles' do not).** The owner approved the design (docs/new-weapons-design.md section 6). The spear is the Assault's thunder hammer combo slowed to 0.85 (`SpearRules.FromHammer`: every timing divided by it, the swings' damage x0.75, the slam and the charge the hammer's), appended at the end of the Space Marine Assault's melee choices and the customizer's melee row (`PowerSpear.cs`), on the hammer's graph map with clip speed 0.85 and the hammer's animation names as stand-ins. Its sweeps are a 15 m, 150-degrees-each-side flat cone of at most 12 Orks (12 m and 120 degrees until the owner's "Wider and longer", 2026-11-10; he also dropped the Boss pin: damage only; and set the grip: the right hand alone idling and running, both hands on a swing, `WeaponAsset.SwingWield`) (`World.ArsenalCleave`); its pound landing impales the nearest Ork within 2 m for 600 (`World.ArsenalJump`, Impact); it takes the hammer's jump-pack rules (`ArsenalRules.SpearWieldsHammer`). The model is built in code (`WeaponRig.BuildSpear`) in the hammer's root space: the hammer's chest-prop mount for a swing, the power sword's hand mount for the one-handed carry. Grip slide (owner, 2026-11-10): the one-handed fist rides high (1.34 m from the butt, where the butt clears the ground by 4 cm at the run clip's lowest, measured with `ModelViewer --spear-probe`) for run and rest and slides to the low grip (0.45 m from the butt) while a strike is shown (`WeaponRig.GripSlide` 0..1, `GripSlideDriven` for the animator's poses; `WeaponAsset.OneHandGrip`); `ModelViewer --grip` shows either. Review fixes (2026-11-10): the impale has the cleave's in-play guard and begins the tick's Musou events (tested through a real pound); the melee marker follows the holder's mount; the drop pool and reward equipment skip arsenal items. Cost: `Query` insertion-sorts the Orks in reach, but one swing among 1,000 Orks in reach (the 15 m cone) measured about 1 ms a tick in `SpearTests.A_sweep_among_a_thousand_orks_costs_little` (140 ticks in 146 ms, the whole step), so the candidate buffer is not narrowed. Arsenal items are kept out of Orks' weapon drops and reward cards (`MusouDropRules.Pool`, `TfwRewards.Roll`) while their drop model is a placeholder. `ModelViewer` gained `--content` for the still. Not done: the WeaponPose hookup (the approved clips), the dive's point-down pose, a clip of the sweep against a crowd, a hit-tick-versus-contact comparison. Tests: `SpearTests` (11), `PowerSpearContentTests` (3).

**Musou's arsenal W3b: the power spear's approved clips in a match, and the clip review's minors (branch `claude/spear-anims-2` from `claude/claw-spear-anims`, 2026-11-10; client and SmContent data only, Musou Mode only; no simulation, protocol, wire, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner approved the spear's sixth pass; the claw keeps the power sword's clips. **In a match** (`Arsenal/Spear/NetworkView.SpearPose.cs`; docs/claw-spear-animations.md section 4b): W3 keeps posing the thunder hammer's clips for the spear's strikes (their sound and footstep tags, the hand-over to the legs and every timing stay the hammer's), and each spear player's `CharacterViewer.WeaponPose` shows the spear's clip over them: a strike's clip from its step (`ClawSpearClips.SpearStrike`: X1..X3 the hews, the Y interrupt and both sweeping attacks the snap cut, the Y,Y slam the stab) at the attack pose's drawn time (`ExtrasAttackTime`, now a dispatcher: the weight pass's retime, `MusouPunchTime`, then `SpearStrikeShown`; predicted for the own player, from the snapshots for the others), through `WeaponPoseClip.TimeAt` (as authored where the hits match, else the wind-up fitted onto the strike's hit); the pound's dive and impale while its clips are posed; the one-handed carry over the hammer stance (standing, walking, running, sprinting); nothing (a 0.15 s fade, W3's mounts) for the pistol up, reactions, rolls, jumps, the charge and the air slash. A strike's and the pound's keys lie over the clip they were authored on (`WeaponPoseState.Base`: the hammer's idle, its dive loop and landing, laid by `CharacterViewer.LayWeaponBase` while a clip is posed), so they show as on the stage; the clip foot lock is off for a spear strike. The spear's model is put on the hands as the stage puts its stand-in (`WeaponRig.PlaceSpearOnHands` through `SpearHold.Place`, shared with the stand-in), blended from W3's mount by the overlay's weight; W3's own grip slide waits at the clip's point meanwhile. Measured with the new `--tfw-spear-capture` (stills cropped round the marine; `SPEARPOSE` lines): the game's camera faces the skeleton's +Y and the hammer idle stands side-on with its hips 71 degrees right of it, so the one-handed carry leans and turns its edge to the player's facing (ours; the stage's cameras followed the hips), the two-handed strikes keep the hips' frame as authored (at their hits the snap cut's shaft points 6 degrees and the stab's 27 degrees right of the facing); the carried hand hangs about 1.28 m up standing and 1.08 m running, so the butt rides 0.34 m and 0.14 m off the ground (the earlier 0.04 m was an estimate; the approved stills show the same; for the owner); the impale's held keys (0.12 to 0.5 s) lay the shaft flat at knee height pointing to his left, as on the stage (the steep, point-down look of the approved still is the dive's pose fading out in its first 0.14 s): the keys, not the wiring, for a refinement. Restore: `--musou-spear-stand-in` (the hammer's clips and W3's mounts alone). **The review's minors (approve with minors):** (1) the grip contract is the clip's grip point in metres from the butt (`GripPointAt`: carry 0.95, hews 0.5, stab 0.3, `StabGrip` new), `GripSlideAt` removed; `SpearHold` (SmContent) holds W3's shaft geometry (`AxisFromButt` 1.05, `AxisAt`, its mount's 1.34 / 0.45 m grips, `SlideAt`), W3's `SpearButt` / `SpearGripHigh` / `SpearGripLow` derive from it; (2) the weight pass's MW3 settle drops the torso with the pelvis (`RigidCarriedWith`; before, only the hips and legs dropped); (3) a carried bone is ordered right after its carrier whatever the indices, the float clamps are Godot's, the legs are the core's (`ResolveLegs`, so the Ork rig's `RIG_LLeg_*` too); (4) no per-frame allocation (the grip tracks sampled without a channel, `PoseChannel.Sample(keys, kind, t)`), the overlay's per-viewer objects made lazily, `WeaponPoseState.Advance` documented (`FromShare` new); (5) docs and the dead foot clamp in `PoseChannel.Sample` removed. Tests: `ClawSpearClipsTests` 33 (3 new: the grip contract and W3's axis, the placement on the hands, the strike map and `TimeAt`). Stills: `<media folder>\previews\spear-anims-wired\` (`spear-player-*` the game's camera, `spear-front-*` the stage's front view; idle, run, a light hew, the stun, the stab, the dive, the impale). In Musou a light press picks a random swing of the light chain, so hew 2 or 3 often starts from the carry (the 0.14 s hand-over). No human has played it.

**Musou's arsenal W4: the Remote Detonators.** Not started (brief: docs/new-weapons-design.md section 11).

With W0b's sources the capture (`--tfw-autocannon-capture`, now with its own `AutocannonDeploy`, a 90 s landing wait for a Movie Maker run, and a 150 s walk) shows: the HUD reticle (`autocannon_mc`) and the ammo box with the rounds and the heat bar, a muzzle flash, tracer and the blast at twice the bolt blast's size, and the fire sound is on the clip. Found off: the effects and the sound are the Chaos file's, so the muzzle flash and tracer are purple on a Space Marine (`chaos_autocannon_muzzle`, `chaos_autocannon_tracer`, sound `play_ch_autocannon_fire`); the loyalist names (`autocannon_muzzle`, `heavy_bolter_tracer`, `play_autocannon_turret_fire`) are in the install but need a remap in the two `WithSources` (reported to the lead, not changed here). **Musou's arsenal W1b, the autocannon's sounds (2026-11-10).** The owner: "make the autocannon use stalker bolter sounds". **Musou's arsenal W1c: the autocannon's loyalist flash and tracer and its 1.6 m barrel (branch `claude/arsenal-w1c` from W1b 035a1e02 with main merged, 2026-11-10; client presentation only, Musou Mode only; no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner, after W1b's clip: muzzle flash and tracer "Loyalist effects", and the barrel "shorten it to 1.6m, then show me a screenshot". **Effects**: a new pinned hook, `NetworkView.ExtrasEffectNames` (beside W1b's `ExtrasSoundSources` in `NetworkView.Presentation.cs`), gives the effect catalogue's load per added weapon a map of effect names to play instead (`EffectNameMap`); the core `EffectCatalogue.WithEffectNames` renames those effect commands in the named entry only (and its projectiles'), keeping every other part of each command, the hit containers and the source file's own entry, and is the same object without names. Musou's map (`Arsenal.EffectNames`): `chaos_autocannon_muzzle` to `autocannon_muzzle` (the loyalist autocannon's flash: the campaign's `auto_cannon` and the install's `test_assault_cannon` fire it with the twin's scale 1.5 and length 1.5) and `chaos_autocannon_tracer` to `heavy_bolter_tracer` (the multiplayer heavy bolter's tracer, bound by its file with the twin's very scale, length and marker; thinned as every bolt tracer). Both names are in `master_fx`. Sounds (the Stalker Bolter's), reticle and ammo box unchanged. Not changed: the twin's impacts (`weapon_hits\chaos\ranged_weapons\autocannon`), whose world hit `chaos_autocannon_dmg` is a white-lavender burst in the stills (its data has purple flashes and sparks): a candidate for the same treatment if the owner wants it (the containers are shared tables, so it needs a per-weapon copy). `--old-autocannon-fx` restores the purple pair. **Barrel** (`AutocannonBarrel`, `WeaponRig.AutocannonModel`): `turret_aa`'s parts are `gun`, `ammobarrel` and `Recoiling_Barrel` (the barrel with a clamp riding the rod under it); W1b's "2.6 m" is the muzzle locator's distance from the model's root along +Y (2.621 m), so the muzzle now sits at 1.6 m. Only what lies ahead of the receiver's front face (1.072 m) moves, by a piecewise-linear map along +Y: the barrel is a plain tube there (no vertex between 1.072 and 2.277 m but the clamp's, checked on the install), so the plain tube on both sides of the clamp gives up 1.021 m in proportion and the clamp with the rod's end cap (1.364 to 1.527 m) and the ribbed front (2.277 m to the muzzle) only move back; normals and texture coordinates are kept. The rig gets a shortened copy of the loaded asset (baked meshes and locators moved; the object tree, so the mounts and stow, untouched), so the flash and the tracer leave the new muzzle. The barrel past the receiver is 0.53 m (was 1.55 m), the gun 1.77 m from stock to muzzle. Aids: `--old-autocannon-barrel`, `--autocannon-muzzle m`. **Capture** (`--tfw-autocannon-capture`): the three views idle as well, each firing still on the frame after a round leaves, the camera held per view, aiming at the nearest Ork in sight within 45 m (W1b's run fired into a wall 8 m away); an `ACCAPTURE effects:` line names the effects as loaded (checked: `autocannon_muzzle` at `fx_muzzle`, `heavy_bolter_tracer`, the twin's impacts; muzzle locator found). Stills (cropped to the gun, PNG) and a 9 s H.264 clip of the fire (Movie Maker at 24 fps on the private desktop): the media folder's `previews\arsenal-w1c\` (`ac-before-after-side.png`, `ac-side-*`, `ac-player-*`, `ac-rear-*`; full frames in `raw\`). Looked at: the barrel reads as receiver, clamp on the rod, ribbed front; the flash is warm cream at the new muzzle; no purple flash or tracer; the rear views keep W1's framing (the body hides most of the gun). Tests: `EffectCatalogueTests` (+2, `WithEffectNames`), `AutocannonContentTests` (+3: the names, the barrel map, an install check that the cut runs through plain tube only), `ArsenalPresentationTests` (+1 install check: the client's load gives the loyalist pair with the twin's commands, both effects in `master_fx`), `ExtrasBoundaryTests` (the hook and the call site). Spec "Autocannon: muzzle flash and tracer (W1c)", "Autocannon: barrel length (W1c)". No human has seen it in a match yet; the owner approved the screenshots and the clip ("Looks good", 2026-11-10).
**Musou's arsenal W1c, the loyalist impact (2026-11-10; client presentation only, Musou Mode only; no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner: "Loyalist impact" (the rounds still burst on walls and the ground with the twin's white-lavender `chaos_autocannon_dmg`). The install has two `autocannon` hit containers: the Chaos one the twin names and a Space Marine one whose world hit `autocannon_dmg` (scale 0.3, as the twin's) is the same effect element for element in warm colours, so Musou's map (`Arsenal.EffectNames`) gains `chaos_autocannon_dmg` to `autocannon_dmg` (ours: the autocannon's own loyalist impact, not the heavy bolter's `bolter_dmg_*` the lead's brief named; reported to the lead). The containers are shared tables, so the core `EffectCatalogue.WithEffectNames` now gives a named entry its own copy of each hit container its commands (and its projectiles') name that plays a mapped effect, under `EffectCatalogue.CopyKey` (`<entry>#<path>`, so the file name stays last), and points those commands at it; the copy keeps every other surface, class, command part and the hit sound, the shared table and every other weapon's impacts are untouched, and without names the catalogue is the same object (W1c's own rewrite: the renaming is one `EffectRenamer` per entry). Body hits that fall back to the default entry (an Ork shot hit asks the player's surface) turn loyalist with it; the twin's flesh and armour entries were loyalist names already. Checked: the explosive round's blast plays the configuration's first frag, `sm_mp_eq_frag_grenade`, whose `frag_grenade_explosion` is warm (no change). `--old-autocannon-fx` restores the burst with the flash and tracer. New test aid `--tfw-autocannon-impact-capture` (`NetworkView.AutocannonImpactCapture.cs`, a presentation aid in `LeanBot`): walks to about 6 m from a wall, fires at it and at the ground on a heading no character stands across (the retainer at the shoulder took the rounds on the first tries), stills 0.05 to 0.3 s after rounds; the `ACCAPTURE effects:` line, now shared with `--tfw-autocannon-capture`, names the impact container, its world hit and the blast's frag. Looked at: before, a blue-white and lavender burst with a lavender wash over the frame; after, a warm white flash, then an orange-red fire and hot crater with grey debris, on the wall and the ground alike. Tests: `EffectCatalogueTests` (+1: the entry's own copy, a projectile's container, each container once), `AutocannonContentTests` (the third pair), `ArsenalPresentationTests` (the install check: the copy's key, every surface's world hit as the twin's but loyalist, the body fallbacks, the Space Marine container's own world hit at 0.3, `autocannon_dmg` in `master_fx`). **Musou powerups (musou/powerups, owner 2026-11-10; branch from main 1f95a3f1, main e2b28443 merged in; `MusouSim.Version` 40 (38 on the branch until the merge); wire tag 6 extended, no protocol bump).** The owner: "change the drop cards UI elements to be much more minimalistic and match the black and white theme. they don't drop weapons anymore but powerups, and more rarely" (Double Damage 30 s, Fear 15 s, Supercharged Melee 20 s, Rapid Fire 20 s; answers: "Double damage + wider cleave", "20 s each", "Elites and bosses only, ~10%", "Hold the use key"). Sim (`MusouPowerupRules`, `World.MusouPowerups.cs`, `MusouSim.Powerups.cs`): a boss's KO always, an elite's about one in ten (a deterministic hash), drops a powerup for every living player on the existing per-player drops (item `0x4000 | kind`); the use key takes it and starts the buff (again: the full time again; a death or the round ends it). Double Damage and Supercharged Melee are per-player scales in `MusouSim.Damage` (melee told apart by its death kind; together held to x2 on melee, the owner's cap: see the review fixes below), Supercharged also widens and lengthens the cleave x1.5; Fear makes Orks within 30 m drop their target and run up the flow field like the Scrap Mek (the Warboss, the Boss Orks, Squigs and Meks never fear); Rapid Fire sets the new core field `PlayerState.FireBoostLeft` (not on the wire, counted down like `StimLeft`; `SimConfig.FireBoost` 2 under Musou, 1 elsewhere) so the client predicts the 2x fire rate and the free rounds, re-carried at a reconcile through the new `GameClient.ExtrasCarry`. Wire: tag 6 may end with the player's buffs (`[u8 m] m x [u8 kind][u16 ticks left]`), sent on a change and refreshed while any lasts; an empty list keeps the old layout. Client: the drop is a small black tile with a white line icon and name, a thin floor ring and a faint line (no gold, light or turn; `MusouDropView.Powerup.cs`, `MusouPowerupIcons`), the prompt small white capitals, the own buffs as chips right of the own bar (icon, draining bar, seconds; `MusouHud.Buffs.cs`), Supercharged a white-blue glow over the melee weapon in hand. The post-map reward cards already use the front end's menu look and share no UI with the drops: left as they are. Capture aid `SM_MUSOU_POWERUP_TEST=<s>`. Tests: `MusouPowerupsTests` (rules, drops, pickup, durations and restart, death, damage scales, Fear, Rapid Fire and Classic's 1x, the wire). Stills: `<media folder>\previews\musou-powerups\`. **Review fixes and the owner's answers (claude/musou-powerups-2, main 22cd46be merged in; `MusouSim.Version` stays 40, main is at 39):** no multiplier stacks past x2 (`MusouPowerupRules.Cap`): Supercharged and Double Damage are x2 together on melee in the pool's scale, and a stim's melee share is held under the same cap at the charge, the cleave and the spear's impale (`World.MusouMeleeDealt`; Musou's stim is x2 alone, so the powerups add nothing to melee while it runs); Rapid Fire with a stim's x1.2 fires at x2 (`SimConfig.FireBoostCap` through the widened `ExtrasFireBoost(ref rate, ref cap)`; Classic's fire rate keeps its old expression). A powerup is taken by holding the use key 0.5 s (`MusouPowerupRules.HoldSeconds`, an estimate; `World.MusouHoldsStep` checks the input's use flag on the server, a release, death or leaving reach ends it, only a press starts one; the client fills a bar under "HOLD E name" and hides the drop at its own hold's end); weapon drops and crates keep the press. The client clears its buffs when it sees its player dead or back alive and ignores buff lists from before; the server resends the list every 5 ticks for a second after a buff change. The misplaced arsenal comment on the cleave fixed. Tests: `MusouPowerupsTests` (the hold, a death or the drop's expiry mid-hold, the caps with all three at the swing, the charge and the impale, the wider cleave, a set fire boost in Musou and Classic, a new round's clear), `MusouPowerupsWireTests` (tag 6's sends, refresh and resend; Rapid Fire predicted through `ExtrasCarry`, and without it the replay spends rounds), `ExtrasBoundaryTests` pins `ExtrasCarry`.
**Musou's arsenal W3b, pass 2: the spear held out, no clipping, the impale point-down (branch `claude/spear-anims-2`, 2026-11-10; client and SmContent data only, Musou Mode only; no simulation, protocol, wire, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner's review of the wired stills: "the blade is facing away from the character model at idle and when running, and the spear should be held out away from the body ... Make a pass at all the animations to ensure the spear isn't going through the player models body at any time", and the impale "Point-down". **The check** (`SpearClearance` in SmContent; `SpearClearanceTests`, install only): the body as capsules fitted to the install's basic armour and the Assault's jump pack in the bind pose (88 % of each cluster covered; the forearms and hands left out, they hold the spear) plus a spine core, the spear as W3's model; every spear clip sampled every 1/60 s on the install's rig through `WeaponPoseMirror` (the overlay in System.Numerics; checked against the client's own overlay on the stage, `--claw-spear-test --clearance`, to 0.01 to 0.02 m) and every hand-over; no pose may pass 0.02 m into the body. Before: up to 0.34 m (hew 3's overhead loop through the jump pack), every strike 0.18 to 0.34 m, the carry 0.23 m into the shins; after: all within 0.02 m, but one allowance (the dive fading into the impale while the landing slams the body down: one frame, 0.085 m, budget 0.10 m, open). **The carry** (over the hammer stance, in the stance's frame as on the stage, no longer the player's facing, which put the shaft across the side-on idle): the right hand held out wide of the hip, the shaft leaning forward to 55 degrees and 15 in at the top, the edge facing out and forward (`SpearHold.CarryElevation`, `CarryAzimuth`, `EdgeAzimuth`); clear of the body by 0.107 m over all twenty hammer stance clips, the butt at least 0.56 m up (it was 0.14 m running; for the owner). **The strikes** keep their timing, hips, steps and grip tracks; only arm keys moved, placed in the chest's frame with a two-bone IK where the hips' turn had left the right hand behind the torso (hew 2, hew 3, the snap cut, the stab), hew 1's swing-around routed through the front, the shared recovery brought forward. **The dive and the impale**: the dive's hands before the face; the impale driven home point-down by 0.14 s (the hand-over's end), the hands sliding to 1.5 m up the shaft so the tip reaches the Ork at his feet from the landing's crouch, the hips lifting the landing's fold to a 35 to 45 degree lean, held until 0.85 s ("until the pound ends"), free by 0.95 s, ending on the carry's arms. **Review minors**: `tfw-spear-capture` and `claw-spear-test` classified in `LeanBot.PresentationAids`; `--no-weapon-pose` turns the in-match spear posing fully off (`SpearPosesOn`); the `ExtrasAttackTime` comments name the spear too. The stage fades the grip tracks from the clip before, as a match does. Stills: `<media folder>\previews\spear-anims-pass2\` (`spear-*` in a match: the game's camera and the stage's front and side views; `stage-*` on the preview stage). Tests: `SpearClearanceTests` 2 (install only), `ClawSpearClipsTests` 33 (the carry, the edge and the impale's end updated). Not playtested.

**Musou swing arc (owner, 2026-11-10; branch `claude/musou-slash-arc`; client presentation only, Musou Mode only; no rules, wire, prediction, protocol, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner: "can we make slash strokes appear as a flat curved line that matches the cleave of the weapon swings hitbox? so it visually overlaps cleave targets in one cohesive tear line as opposed to many random small lines that don't line up". A melee swing that strikes now draws one thin glowing arc (`MusouSlashArcView`, a camera-facing ribbon built each frame along a level circle segment; no depth test, hidden only by the striker's own model through the strokes' stencil twins). Its width is the cleave's own (`MusouCleaveShape` in SmSim, the server's formula for `World.MusouCleave`: 240 degrees in the war for every melee weapon; the power spear's 15 m and 150 degrees each side through `SpearRules.Sweep`, the one function W3's `World.ArsenalCleave` reads too). It runs through the enemies struck: their mean flat distance from the swinger, at least 1.5 m, at most the cleave's reach, and their mean chest height. The first stills put the line at the full reach (8.8 m, 10.7 m for the hammer's track-to-hit steps); there it ran far past the Orks struck, so the default goes through the targets and `--musou-slash-arc-radius 1` keeps the hitbox-edge version. The arc sweeps in the swing's direction in 0.12 s (the light chain alternates), holds 0.05 s and fades in 0.22 s. Thickness is 0.16 m light (+8 % a later step) and 0.26 m heavy. Red and blue and the 30 m limit (from the swinger) are the strokes'. The own swing's arc comes at the predicted strike for every melee weapon; another player's (AI Marines too) once a frame's reported hits are in, one per player and server tick. A melee hit with no swing behind it (a charge, the spear's impale, the air slash's landing) keeps the old stroke. `--musou-old-slashes` restores the strokes; `--log-musou-arcs`; capture aid `--tfw-arc-capture` (`Tfw/NetworkView.TfwArcCapture.cs`). Shared files touched: `NetworkView.MusouContact.cs` (the arc's call, the stroke's gate, and the predicted pick `MusouStrikeTargets`, now from `MusouCleaveShape` with the weapon and once a frame and strike), `Weight/NetworkView.MusouPunch.cs` (the pick's weapon), one line each in `NetworkView.MusouSlash.cs` and `Tfw/NetworkView.TfwTest.cs`; in W3's files `SpearRules.Sweep`, `IsSpear` and `MeleeWargearOf` (`Arsenal/SpearImpale.cs`) and `World.ArsenalCleave` reading them (`Arsenal/World.Spear.cs`, same numbers), and the arsenal's body of `MusouCleaveShape.ArsenalShape` (`Arsenal/MusouCleaveShape.Arsenal.cs`). Tests: `MusouSlashArcTests` (a real World's cleave, war and 5-wave run, plain and track-to-hit steps, no weapon, the hammer and the power spear, strikes exactly the Boys inside the arc's shape, 0.6 m and 6 degrees either side of its reach and edges, and the shape's count of a crowd; only the spear's name, and only with Musou's content, sets its own shape; radius, angle, timing and thickness rules). Review fixes (same day): the spear's arc had no shape of its own after W3 (a 240-degree arc at the war's reach for a 300-degree, 15 m sweep); an arc still waiting from an earlier tick was dropped when a later tick's hit of the same player came; a charge's contact or the spear's impale within 0.6 s of an own strike lost its stroke; the Compatibility renderer made stencil twins for nothing (now none; the own arcs depth tested, pulled 1 m toward the eye); the own pick ran twice a strike and every group cleared its mesh every frame. Stills before and after (hammer, power sword; the player's camera and a high third-person camera): `<media folder>\previews\musou-slash-arc\`; after the review fixes the power spear's 300-degree, 15 m sweep: `after-spear\`. Implemented, not playtested: the radius rule, the sweep direction and the thickness are estimates for the owner's playtest. Re-review (lead 22, approve with minors): the own swing's report is matched even after its melee step has ended (a short step's tail or an evade is often over before the round trip), unless the own player started a charge or a landing since the strike (`MusouArcOwnFrame`); before, a late report drew the old strokes over the arc for every weapon but the power sword. Left: during a backlog, two waiting arcs of one remote player share its newest pose.
**Polish pass P1: quick wins (branch `claude/polish-p1`, 2026-11-10; client, options, server runtime; both modes; no simulation, wire, protocol or config-hash change).** The first milestone of `docs/polish-pass-plan.md` (the owner's request of 2026-11-10 and his answers of the same day). **(1) Sound instance limits for every post, opt-in:** `--sound-limits all` applies the banks' per-node "limit sound instances" and the below-threshold culling to every post, not only to footsteps; measured in the baseline harness (13 players, 90 s, the measuring client with sound): 2,475 instance kills, **322 of them on 20 nodes the footsteps default never limited** (blasts, shots and hits stacking on themselves; 2,514 kills, all footsteps, before). The review (2026-11-10) first kept the default at `footsteps` until the owner had heard an A/B; **the owner then decided for `all` the same day** ("yes lets apply the cap to all for sound A/B"), so `all` is the default and `--sound-limits footsteps` the restore switch. The review's grounds, still true: the flag bytes' order is an interpretation (`SoundBank.cs` reads kill newest, virtual behaviour, ignore parent; `docs/discovery.md` now says the same and that it is unverified), the all-parents rule is low confidence and the -60 dB cut is ours, so with `all` a misread byte would reach hit confirms, speech and the match-end stingers. For the A/B: `--log-sound footstep` ends a run with `sound at exit:` and one `LIMITNODE` line per node that fired (id, limit, kill-newest / kill-oldest, global / per-emitter, ignore-parent, the below-threshold byte, kills, drops), and the clips `<media folder>\previews\polish-pass\sound-limits\footsteps.avi` and `all.avi` (the same 13-player match, 45 s each, Movie Maker at 30 fps with sound). Their numbers: footsteps **288 kills** (10 nodes, every one a footstep layer: per-emitter limits of 1 or 2), all **1,196 kills** (25 nodes; the new ones are four global limit-4 nodes with 238, 89, 34 and 9 kills and per-emitter nodes of 1 to 3 with 66, 59, 16, 15, 14, 11, 11 ...), no drops in either (no kill-newest node fired); voices made virtual / revived 991 / 958 against 1,144 / 1,116 and culled under the 2D threshold 0 against 2: the demotion of quiet non-positioned loops is not what `all` changes. Every revive was a loop and resumed its position (`loops resumed` 958 and 1,116). The Musou A/B (a helper's recording on this build: a 1,000-Ork clash with the scripted melee-and-fire player, `musou-footsteps.avi` 52 s and `musou-all.avi` 43 s, phone-sized `-30s.mp4` copies beside them): footsteps **737 kills** on 7 nodes (footfalls 1 per emitter 321 + 117 + 70, the bull-rush footfalls 70, bolter fire 8 global 75), all **1,803 kills** on 19 nodes (bolter fire 1 per emitter 319 + 310 + 162 and 2 per emitter 113, footfalls 199 + 78, the reactive blast 1 per emitter 153, bolter hits 4 global 137 + 61 + 58); no drops in either; none of the Ork events' nodes among them; virtual / revived 4 / 4 against 13 / 13. Named by `smtool audio-event` (`audio-node` takes an event, not a node id). Also from the review: a looping non-positioned voice revived from its virtual wait resumes its running position instead of restarting (`LoopsResumed` in the sound summary); F3 is a reserved key in the keybinds screen; the safe-mode grime flag is `SafeMode.GrimeFoldedInSafeMode` in the core (the Options view names nothing from `Extras/`; `ExtrasBoundaryTests` checks namespaces, so it could not have caught the class reference). **(2) Performance readout:** F3 cycles OFF, FPS, FPS + NETWORK (fps, mean and worst frame ms of the last second; ping, snapshot loss, interpolation delay, input slack from `GameClient`'s own numbers) in the match's top right corner (`HudReadout`), remembered as `performanceReadout` in `frontend.json`; no Options row (the owner: the original's options only; and the GRAPHICS page's 17 rows fill its list: an 18th made the UI self-test's fit check fail); `--readout fps|network|off` pins it for a run (a bot too, for captures). **Polish pass P2: the Ashfall layout cache and the map load off the main thread (branch `claude/polish-p2`, 2026-11-10; client, content and server; load time only: no simulation, wire, protocol or config-hash change).** The plan's items 1 and 2 (`docs/polish-pass-plan.md`). **(1) Ashfall layout cache** (`SmContent.Extras.Musou.AshfallLayoutCache`): the generated level and dressing are written once to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\cache\ashfall\<layout>-v17-g5-d13-<8 bytes of the simulation assembly's module version id>-<8 bytes of the reader assembly's>-<process>.bin` (format 2; the first cut's `<layout>-v17-g5-d13-<8 bytes>.bin` had no reader id and no process name; 8.1 MB; a derived file, nothing from the install, never in the repository) and read back by the client at every join and by the server at every start; a new build has a new key (so a changed generator never serves a stale layout, and the client's and the server's builds each write their own file: two generations per build, not one); the level's hash is in the file and in the map hash the handshake compares; the review (2026-11-10) added a checksum over the whole payload (format 2), the reader assembly's build in the key, the process name in the file name with the newest two files kept per kind, a per-process temporary name and the unreadable reason kept in the note, and switched the cache off in the test processes (the Musou world tests had written 24 MB into the owner's real cache); the re-review's minors (branch `claude/polish-p2b`): the end mark and the checksum are checked before anything is parsed and any parse failure (a damaged length prefix's `FormatException` before) counts as unreadable, so the layout is generated and the file written over instead of failing the server start or the client load; `IsCached` reads the memory under its own lock; each write also deletes the layout's first-format files (no process name) and write temporaries older than 10 minutes (a crash's leftovers), never the other process kind's files nor a foreign file; the disk side has tests in a temporary folder of their own (`AshfallLayoutCacheDiskTests`: round trip, damaged file written over, damaged length prefix, pruning, a file in use), and the wide-route test's walking graph goes to a temporary folder instead of the real `cache\nav`. Measured (human client, this PC): the client read the layout in **59 to 93 ms** and the server in **79 to 174 ms**, against **21 to 23 s** of generation (the client's Debug build; the Release server generates it in 5.9 s). `SM_NO_ASHFALL_CACHE=1` (both) and `--no-ashfall-cache` (client) generate as before. **(2) The map load off the main thread** (`NetworkView.MapLoad.cs`; `ClientOptions.BeginLoadMap` and `IMapLoad` in `GameClient`): the Challenge starts `Stage1` on a worker (the install's map content or the generated level, the collision world with added content's solids and hash, the ragdoll world's triangles, the map scene's meshes and textures), the client polls it each update and sends its Hello with the map hash once it is done (the connect timeout waits meanwhile; `MapLoadAsyncTests`); then one frame shows the caption, one frame builds Godot's nodes (`Stage2Visuals`: the ragdoll body, the navigation's start, added content's hub through the new main-thread hook `ExtrasMapCollisionVisuals`, the map view and its lights, blockers and props), then one warm-up a frame (`WarmupStep`: the looks, the Ork, the default loadouts' weapon models, the grenades, the pickups, the crosshair's first ray), then `Finish` (the `LOADTIME` line, now worker / main thread / warm-ups). The loading screen shows the stage under LOADING (READING THE MAP, BUILDING COLLISION, READING THE MAP'S MESHES AND TEXTURES, GENERATING or READING ASHFALL CITADEL, DRAWING THE MAP, PREPARING LOOKS AND WEAPONS, JOINING; capture `<media folder>\previews\polish-pass\p2-loading-musou_001.png`). Bots, demo replays and **`--sync-map-load`** (the restore switch) load whole on the main thread as before. **Measured (human client, Forward+, vsync off):** Classic Manufactorum **before** 3.5 s in one frozen frame (P1's baseline; this build synchronous: 3.47 s); **after** worker 2.17 s behind the moving loading screen, **one frame of 0.80 s** (ragdoll body 0.31, visuals 0.49), the warm-ups 0.47 s over six frames (82 and 221 ms the largest), total 3.45 s; the join's worst frame fell from 3,527 to 804 ms. Musou Ashfall **before** 28 s in one frame (23 s the generation); **after, warm** worker 3.1 s (the collision world with the Stormbird 2.96 s) behind the moving screen, **one frame of 2.75 s** (the ragdoll body's concave shape 1.18 s, the Ashfall view 1.57 s), the warm-ups 0.92 s over frames, total 6.8 s; **cold** (first join of a build) the same plus 23 s of generation on the worker with GENERATING ASHFALL CITADEL (ONCE PER BUILD) on screen. **Still one frame, next:** the ragdoll body's `ConcavePolygonShape3D` (1.2 s on Ashfall, 0.3 on Manufactorum) and the Ashfall view's build (1.6 s) stay on the main thread (Godot resources; a worker build is possible in Godot 4 but was not tried blind), and a 668 ms "between frames" hitch sits at 2.0 s of the Classic join before the main-thread stage (the engine's side; cause not found): plan item 2's remainder for P3. A first cut built the Stormbird's nodes on the worker (Godot's "only allowed from the main thread" errors in a helper's run): fixed by the hook split before this commit. Checks: both builds 0 errors; `SmNet.Tests` MapLoadAsync / ConnectTimeout / ExtrasBoundary 26 passed (the new hook pinned); `SmFormats.Tests` AshfallLayoutCache / TfwWorldContent 5 passed; `refine-register --check` ok. Re-review fixes: both builds 0 errors; `SmFormats.Tests` AshfallLayoutCache (with the disk tests) 9, TfwWorldContent 2, PublicTextGuard 32, RefineRegister 107 passed; `SmNet.Tests` MapLoadAsync 3, ExtrasBoundary 23, TfwWideRoute 5 passed (6 min: its walking graphs are now built in a temporary folder, not read from the real cache).
