**Main menu video (owner, 2026-11-10; branch `claude/menu-video` from main c9536f86; client only, both modes; no protocol, wire or config change).** The owner: "use this video loop as the main menu background in the next shipped release" (his own cinematic of our Ashfall Citadel map, a Space Marine with a glowing power sword: owner-made, not an original file, so it ships). Before, every menu screen but the customizer drew `UiKit.MenuBackground()`, a cover-fit `TextureRect` of `client/assets/menu/background.jpg`; the loading screen has its own picture (`UiKit.LoadingBackgroundImage`, not touched). Now `MenuBackground()` returns a `MenuVideoBackground` (`client/Customizer/MenuVideo.cs`): a looping `VideoStreamPlayer` on a `VideoStreamTheora` of `client/assets/menu/menu-loop.ogv` (read as a file like the pictures: beside the project, or `assets\menu\` beside the exe, where release.ps1 copies it), sized to cover the window at any aspect ratio (centred, clipped, no letterbox) over the plain dark background, paused while the customizer covers it, not played headless; one that shows no frame within 2 s gives way to the still. No dim: the brightness behind the rows (81 to 92 of 255 over the loop) matches the still's 89. `--menu-still` restores the still picture. The file: `tools/menu-video.ps1` from the owner's 2560 x 1440 H.264 source (31.8 s, a variable ~88 fps): a constant 30 fps, 1920 x 1080 Lanczos, 4:2:0, Theora q 7 (q 6 / 7 / 8 gave 14.8 / 20.3 / 28.1 MB and SSIM 0.983 / 0.987 / 0.989), no audio: 20.3 MB, 939 frames, 31.3 s. The source's seam jumped (last against first frame SSIM 0.94; a step of its slow start is about 0.997), so its last 0.5 s fades into its first 15 frames and its 16th plays unblended last: the seam is one of the source's own frame steps (a capture at 30 fps: one held frame at the restart, no jump). Cost (60 fps cap, menu idle, 12-thread PC): Forward+ 27 % of one core against 9 % with the still, Compatibility 25 % against 7 %, no frame over 16.7 ms on either, the loop included; safe mode keeps the video. `--perf-probe` now also measures the menu. Release: release.ps1 copies the .ogv beside the exe; the content guard allows `.ogv` in the binary packages and the source offer (our own media), and reads an .ogv's e-mail and /home/ rules in its Ogg header packets only (`PackageScanner.OggHeaderBytes`; the 20 MB loop's compressed frames gave three false e-mail findings; a file that is not plain, well-formed Ogg is scanned whole; every other rule reads the whole file). Tests: UI self-test `MenuVideoChecks` (13 checks: the file, the front end's background, a looping Theora stream, played with a display and not headless, covering the screen, paused under the customizer, cover-fit at 16:9, 21:9, 4:3, 5:4, 16:10 and portrait, the still on request); `PackageScannerTests` (an .ogv's header-only rules, the whole-file fallbacks, .ogv allowed), `PartsTests` (the .ogv in the media part). Two Musou join checks of the self-test passed a null detail when they failed, which threw and ended the run inside the menu checks (570 checks ran); their details are null-safe now and the whole run goes on (1070 headless, 1069 windowed). Open, not this change (the join code is untouched): the Musou page's JOIN LOCAL LOBBY connect check fails with and without the video (`--menu-still`, headless), and the ready Musou server's join check fails in the windowed run. Evidence: `<media folder>\previews\menu-video\` (a 1080p screenshot of the main menu, a Compatibility one, a 10 s H.264 clip across the loop seam). Not verified: a human's look approval; an old GPU or CPU (measured on the owner's PC only).
**Effect eviction order and the HUD show-set leak (polish items 27 and 30; branch `claude/fx-hud-leaks` from main ce8aa368, commit `9b42e901`, 2026-11-11; client and content; both modes; bug fixes: no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or look change).** **(27)** A full effect player's victim pick (`FxPlayer.Play`) took "lower priority, or older", so an older effect at priority 0 could go before a younger one at -1 (the weight pass's puffs). Now `SmContent.FxEviction.Victim`: of the effects that are not ambient and at or below the new one's priority, the lowest priority first, the oldest only among equal priorities (ties: the first, as before). The drop and refusal counters (`FxPlayer.Evicted`, `Refused`) now have five slots, priority -1 to 3 (`FxEviction.Slot`; -1 was counted with 0), and Musou's `musou gore budget:` line labels them `dropped by priority -1..3`. The other eviction paths were read: decals and glows drop the oldest by insertion (no priority), casings are refused when full, the GPU sprays evict nothing; none has the mistake. **(30)** The HUD's weapon box keyed its show-set cache by the identity of `spec.Show`, but `WeaponBoxRules.For` built a new spec and list on every call, so the cache gained a `HashSet` every HUD frame for the whole match (Classic too). Now `For` returns one spec per display, built once with the same paths, bars and counts, and the cache is `SmContent.WeaponBoxShowSets`, keyed by the paths' values (allocation-free lookups). No restore switch (bug fixes). Tests: `FxEvictionTests` 16 (mixed priorities and ages, the old pick's wrong case, every order of six effects, ambient and higher never dropped, the counter slots, a source pin on `FxPlayer.cs`), `WeaponBoxShowSetTests` 28 (every display's paths pinned as before the change, checked against the old code first; one spec per display; the cache bounded over 5,000 frames of fresh lists; a source pin on the HUD). Not run: a match with `--frame-profile` (the allocation itself was not measured), the full `dotnet test` (the lead's capped run).

**Musou balance: cleave x0.6, ranged x1.2, the chain lightning struck as drawn and +25 % (branch `claude/musou-balance-1111` from main ce8aa368, 2026-11-11; Musou Mode only; `TfwRules.Version` 65 and `MusouSim.Version` 41, the lead renumbers at integration; no protocol, extras wire or tag 16 format change; the faithful and extended config hashes unchanged).** The owner (2026-11-11; scope through the lead: "Musou, players only"): "reduce melee attack cleave range by 40%", "increase all ranged attack damage by 20%", "librarian chain lightning spell doesn't seem to be reliably delivering damage, increase its range, damage, and reliability of delivering damage" ("+25% range and damage"). **Cleave.** `TfwCombatRules.PlayerCleaveReachScale` 0.6 multiplies the whole reach of every human player's cleave in the war (`TfwCombatRules.ScalesPlayer`: not an AI Marine's, whose arc the client also draws at the old reach), last, after each weapon's own shape (the power spear's 15 m sweep through `SpearRules.Sweep` becomes 9 m; `SpearImpale.cs` untouched), before the Supercharged powerup; the server's `World.MusouCleave`, the contraptions' `TfwMekMelee` and the client's `MusouCleaveShape` (the drawn swing arc and the predicted pick) and `MusouFx.MusouMeleeTarget` read the one value, so the line and the hitbox stay together (`MusouSlashArcTests` places Boys 0.6 m either side of the new reach in a real World). The 4 m class's 8.8 m (10.7 m track-to-hit) is 5.27 m (6.44 m). Angles, caps and the height band unchanged; the Orks' melee and the 5-wave aid unchanged. **Ranged.** `TfwCombatRules.PlayerRangedDamageScale` 1.2 through one helper, `World.MusouRangedDealt` (1 outside the war, for an AI Marine and for anyone not a player), at every human player's ranged hit on the enemies: hit-scan and piercing shots, cones, a projectile's direct hit and burst, every non-melee splash (frags, melta bombs, bolt and autocannon blasts), the Remote Detonators' blasts, and the contraptions' shot, projectile and blast damage (the stomp's blast on a contraption stays melee: `TfwMekBlast` gained a melee flag); a plasma burn follows its scaled hit. Not the Librarian's spells, the orbital strikes, an Ork's own explosion or any damage to players. Grenades and charges are our reading of "all ranged". **Chain lightning.** Measured first (`MusouLibrarianReliabilityTests`, a crowd of 140 Orks crossing his view, 450 casting ticks; the client's foreseen chain on the crowd as it showed it a few ticks behind the server, the aim tracking the drawn Ork, the server casting with the same aim): the server picked its chain on its crowd now, while the own client draws the chain on the crowd at the render tick (100 ms of interpolation, plus the input lead and the round trip); 3, 7 and 10 ticks behind, only 75.9, 68.1 and 60.7 % of the drawn targets took damage, and the server struck another primary on 170, 279 and 285 of about 400 ticks (12 Orks: 96.2, 84.4, 82.5 %). No tick was lost and no damage was under a threshold: the damage fell on Orks other than the drawn ones. The fix: one chain rule for the server and the client (`LibrarianChain` in SmSim, moved from the client's `LibrarianPrediction`, which now calls it; `LibrarianCandidate` moved with it); the World keeps the pool's places for the last ticks while a Librarian is in the match (`LibrarianHistory`, recorded at each tick's end from `ExtrasRecordBodies`, as sent) and picks each caster's chain on the crowd at his input's view tick and fraction (`LibrarianSight`, capped at `MaxRewindTicks`, never past the newest tick; a view tick of 0 casts on the crowd now), then strikes every member alive now; one dead since stays a link and takes nothing, one farther than 3 m a tick from where it was seen (a reused slot) takes nothing; the links are where he saw them. After: 100 % of the drawn targets damaged and nothing else, the same primary on every tick, 0 to 15 ticks behind. Then `LightningRange` 30 to 37.5 m and `PrimaryDps` 90 to 112.5 (the jump radius 8 m and the falloff x0.85 unchanged: our reading of "range"). Restore switch `SM_LIBRARIAN_OLD=rewind` (the crowd now). Allocation-free per tick (tested). Tests: `MusouBalanceTests` (25: an AI Marine's cleave (four weapons) and shot unchanged; the shape of every weapon in the war and the 5-wave run, the server's cleave against the old and the new reach, a gun shot with its bolt blasts, a launcher round and burst, a frag, the Remote Detonators at x1.2 against twin worlds at x1, melee, an Ork's blow and the 5-wave run unchanged), `MusouLibrarianReliabilityTests` (15: the measure, every drawn target damaged at 0 to 15 ticks, the World's view tick, fraction, clamps, the dead link, the far slot, the switch, 37.5 m and 112.5 dps, no allocation); updated for the new numbers: `MusouSlashArcTests`, `TfwMeleeTests`, `SpearTests`, `MusouMeleeFeelTests`, `AutocannonTests`, `MusouLibrarianTests`, `MusouLibrarianSwitchTests`. Ran: the Musou test folders without Ashfall (1424 passed, 1 skipped), `MusouIsolationTests`, `PvpCombatIsolationTests`, `ConfigHashPinTests`, `ContentProfileTests`, `ExtrasBoundaryTests`; the full `dotnet test` not run. Not done: no bot or human run of the lightning on a real server (the measure is a headless model of the client's delay); the spear's own docs (`SpearRules`) still say 15 m (the war's x0.6 makes 9). No human has played it.

**Hit reactions: the death clip by the graph, blast deaths, the clip's motion into the ragdoll, flinches by the attacker (branch `claude/hit-reactions`, 2026-11-11; client only, every mode; no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules-version change).** The lead's task: the playtest list's two missing items (death animations before the ragdoll, flinches). Found first: both were drawn since animation pass 2 (a headless bot duel showed `P1 dies: SM_REC_MP_BolterDeath_F_01 (DefaultFront) for 0.60 s` and flinches), the list was stale, and pass 2's rules were guesses. Read this time (`smtool graph-dump --upper` prints it all; docs/discovery.md "Hit reactions"): the reader now takes Havok's to-nested-state id and flags (@20, @28) and the marine's one `hkbWeightedRandomSelector`; `SM_Base_MP`'s ROOT enters DEATH by priority straight into a nested state (jump pack 10, `BRANCH_Headshot` 9, `BRANCH_Las_Death` 8, `BRANCH_Melta_Death` 7, sprint 6, `BRANCH_Plasma_Death` 5, `BRANCH_Death_Ranged_Left` / `_Right` / `_Back` 4 / 3 / 2, else the conduit: bull rush, sprint, default pair), and the branches are raised by the flinch slot the killing hit plays; the flinch set is picked by the hit's reaction type through thirteen `PORT_` events in the order of the set states (the attacker's weapon, not the victim's), the slot by the sets' `hkbReactionStateChooser` names (front / back, high / low, side, head); the grenade reactions carry "Set Reaction Death Bool" and "Death Powered Ragdoll Controls" from 0.3 (a blast death plays them); "Random Flinches" are six equal-weight additive clips on `Hit_Flinch`. Now (`DeathRules`, `FlinchRules`, `WeaponReactions`, `DeathHandover` in `SmContent/UpperBodyAnimations.cs`; `NetworkView.UpperBody.cs`, `Ragdoll.Start`): the death clip by those routes (new: the side deaths, `SM_REC_ChaosDeath_01` from the right; the transitions' own blends, the default pair's 0.5 s), blast kills on the ground in the grenade reaction to its 0.3 s tag, every ragdoll body starting with its bone's motion over the clip's last frame (capped; the whole body's throw counts only beyond the push, lifts at most 3 m/s: summed, the stage's grenade death flew 10 m), shot flinches from the attacker's set with low slots, and light melee hits (the knife's included) showing a random flinch for every viewer: the attacker on its hit frame, the victim from its own record's flinch counter, others from the inferred hits (now also with the sounds off, not on lean bots). The jump pack's mid-air death is read and chosen but not played (its effects belong to the ragdoll). Owner's recollection kept: light hits stagger and interrupt nothing. Test aids: `--old-hit-reactions` (pass 2's rules), `--hit-reaction-test --hrt-case <case>` (a stage playing one death or flinch case with the same rules, for Movie Maker clips). Tests: `HitReactionsTests` (24 cases: nested transitions, routes and blends, the new clips and hand-over times, the hold cap, the choice by branch, sprint, bull rush, blast and jump, conditions, flinch branches, ports, random flinches, high / low slots, the weapons' reaction types, the hand-over velocity and its combination with the push), `HitReactionNoBlockTests` (8: gunfire and light melee hits on a reload, a melee combo, an evade and a weapon switch leave the action's timeline tick for tick as unhit), `UpperBodyAnimationsTests` (pass 2's choice kept as `ChoosePass2`). Checked headless on 127.0.0.1 with bots: shot kills `RangedRight; killing hit's flinch Bolter Flinch slot 5: BRANCH_Death_Ranged_Right`, `RangedLeft`, a bull-rushing victim shot `RangedRight` (ROOT's branch before the conduit), sprinting victims the stagger, melee kills the default pair, random flinches from the hit frame and the own record, low slots. **Polish pass P3: first frames and loads (branch `claude/polish-p3`, 2026-11-11; client only; no simulation, wire, protocol or config-hash change; no version constant raised).** The plan's items 16 (in part) and 29, item 2's remainder and item 31 looked at (`docs/polish-pass-plan.md`), then the Musou performance re-check against 2026-11-08 (`docs/musou-perf-pass.md`, its last section). Measured on a quiet PC (Debug client 1600 x 900 on the private desktop, vsync off, Release server on 127.0.0.1; `tools/polish-p3-measure.ps1 [-Before]`, `tools/musou-perf.ps1`), one run a number unless a count is given. **Kept, each on its numbers:** **(a) a crash in P2's asynchronous load, so in main since P2:** on the Compatibility renderer a Musou join crashed during the load's warm-up frames (signal 11, the main thread between frames) in **28 of 55** joins (warm layout cache, `--no-shader-sweep`; 3 of 5, 12 of 25, 13 of 25); the synchronous load (`--sync-map-load`) 0 of 15, Forward+ 0 of 12 (Classic on the Compatibility renderer was not counted with P2's behaviour; with the fix 0 of 10). The viewport now draws no 3D from the frame that builds the map until the last warm-up (`LoadDraws3D`; the loading screen covers those frames; `--load-draws-3d` restores): **1 of 57** joins still crashed, at the same place; running the warm-ups in the build's frame on that renderer did no better (1 of 40) and was not kept. The cause inside the engine is not known (no symbols in the backtrace): a rare crash remains, open. **(b) the shader sweep:** for six frames after the warm-ups the camera looks round the map from over its centre behind the loading screen (`--no-shader-sweep`). Classic on the Compatibility renderer, the frames after the join: 70.5 / 59.7 / **148.8** (132 of it between frames: the first-sight compile) / 40.6 ms before, 72.5 / 64.0 / 47.5 and 72.5 / 63.6 / 48.6 after (the warm-up's p99.9 40.6 -> 28.7 ms); cost: one sweep frame of 85 ms and 0.1 to 0.2 s more loading (2,256 -> 2,443 to 2,572 ms). Forward+ Classic the same before and after (85.5 / 76.1 against 85.9 / 64.8 ms); the Compatibility compile frames of 348 / 353 ms in P1's baseline no longer occur with or without it. **(c) item 29's real cause:** the first frame of play with sound held 153 to 167 ms in its `sound` phase in five runs; 145 ms of it was the map's sound emitters and regions (`MapAudio.Load`, an install read) on the main thread. The map load reads them now (on its worker for a human client; `--map-audio-in-play` restores): that frame's sound part **162 to 167 -> 20 ms** (the frame 260 -> 117 and 232 ms; the rest is the first effects frame and the own model). **(d) Musou's hub sky** made by the map load's main-thread stage, not in the first frame aboard (`--hub-sky-in-play`): the second frame after a Musou join **385 to 417 -> 214 to 241 ms** (`tfw: hub` 139 to 166 ms gone), the load's frame +50 to +80 ms behind the loading screen. **Tried and taken out again:** the sound stream made on the decode worker (item 29's guess): the `sound` phase's stalls did not move with it (the first frame 165 / 167 / 153 ms; in-match worst 19.5 ms with the stream made in the frame, 5.7 and 34.8 ms on the worker: the battles' spread; a decode with its stream averages 0.5 to 0.8 ms); the ragdoll world's concave shape on the load's worker (item 2's remainder): with it the load crash came in 10 of 18 joins even with the sweep's camera, against 1 of 16 with the shape made on the main thread; per-instance material copies for the Compatibility renderer (item 31): stills there of an Assault bot's power sword swings and of the drawn melta cone are the same with the shared materials' per-instance values (the blade flares in the swing and fades, the cone ages), so nothing was broken; Musou's powerup drops made ahead (a fight's first drop costs a 29 to 30 ms frame; making the four kinds aboard the Stormbird cost 149 ms in one frame, or 117 ms and three times 28 ms spread, more than it saved). **Not reproduced any more, nothing to fix:** the 668 ms engine frame 2 s into a Classic join (no frame over 150 ms after the load in five Forward+ joins, with or without the sweep); the landing's 420 to 460 ms frame (the clash runs' worst client frame after the warm-up is 35 to 37 ms, the first powerup drop). **Musou re-check against 2026-11-08 (same scenes, camera, workload, settings):** the clashes are faster at every size (frame mean 7.7 / 8.1 / 8.3 ms at 200 / 500 / 1,000 a side against 9.1 / 10.4 / 10.4; p99 11.8 / 12.6 / 13.4 against 13.8 / 16.5 / 19.0; the server's worst tick 20 / 23 / 59 ms against 73 / 110 / 119; 65 to 129 KB/s a client against 32 to 79, the 120 KB/s stream); the one regression is the mass-death burst: worst burst frame 23.5 -> **38.8 ms**, p99 21.6 -> 32.1 ms, which is the GPU sprays' live-effect cap of 1,200 (the same build with `--fx-cpu` gives 25.3 ms / 22.2; `--fx-cap 400` gives 32.4 / 26.5): the effect player walks 13,000 to 15,400 sprays of about 148 live effects in that frame (27 on the CPU path); the GPU path's own parts are small (finding 1.0 ms, frames 1.0 to 1.2 ms, uploads 0.8 to 7.5 ms, starts up to 8 to 12 ms). Not changed: the cap is the owner's choice of 2026-11-09, with its playtest check. **Measurement aids kept:** the Musou frame's phases `tfw: stations`, `tfw: hud`, `tfw: markers`, `tfw: hub`; the sound phase's parts; the `effects gpu:` line's worst-frame numbers; the `sound: map ... read in` line; `--scene-on-main`; `tools/polish-p3-compat-stills.ps1`. **Open after P3 (each with its number):** the residual Compatibility load crash (1 of 57); the Musou join's one frame of 1.6 to 1.7 s behind the loading screen (the ragdoll world's shape 0.69 s, the Ashfall visuals 0.92 to 0.99 s of which the storm 0.48 s) and its first frame aboard of 320 to 360 ms (`musou: crowd, deaths, ragdolls` 153 to 156 ms, effects 53 to 61 ms) and second of 214 to 241 ms (own model's weapons 72 to 97 ms); Classic's first frame of play 72 to 117 ms (first effects 30 to 40 ms, own model 20 to 27 ms, sound 20 ms); the burst frame at the 1,200 cap; a fight's first powerup drop (29 to 30 ms).

**Musou power spear follow-ups (claude/spear-followups, 2026-11-11; Musou Mode only, client and content, no rules, wire or version change).** The point-down impale now shows only when the landing impaled an Ork: the client reads the server's existing Musou events (the spear player's melee-marker hit or melee kill within 6 ticks of the landing; the pack's own blast marks body hits and blast kills), guesses its own landing from the Orks it draws within 2 m until the snapshots are 4 ticks past it, and fixes the choice 0.25 s into the landing (`SpearRules.ImpaleEvidence` / `ShowsImpale`, `NetworkView.SpearLandingOf`); without a hit the plain landing plays (`ClawSpearClips.SpearLand`, built from the impale's keys: the same touch-down, the spear back up by 0.3 s). The owner's added brief: the shaft runs through the rig's grip sockets in the palms (`RIG_Prop_RHand` / `RIG_Prop_LHand`, `SpearHold.RightGripBone`; before, the wrists), every arm key of the strikes, the dive and the impale re-solved numerically so the palms hold the approved shaft line and stay clear of the body between the keys at every idle phase; the carry is read in the facing frame (`WeaponPoseClip.FacingFrame`), the fist close at the chest (0.43 m from the spine at idle, 0.77 m before), the blade 5.9 degrees left of the crosshair's column at idle; the spear is placed against the facing in every clip; the recovery keeps the hips low until the stepped foot is back and hew 3 starts low, so planted feet no longer float (before up to 0.11 m). Tests: the landing's evidence on real pounds (hit, kill, miss, blast-killed, hammer) and the client's guess (`SpearTests`), the plain landing's clip (`ClawSpearClipsTests`), clearance with the plain landing and the change-of-mind hand-overs, the shaft within 0.03 m of a holding palm on every frame, planted feet that neither float nor slide, the crosshair column at idle (`SpearClearanceTests`, install only), the jump pack's flight pinned as on main. Not done: the light attacks were not widened (the blade's arc 125 to 163 degrees, as approved; every widening tried passed through the body under the clearance check: a real wide pass needs the hips turned toward the target, the strikes' steps go toward the side-on stance's front, 71 degrees right of it); in a match the simulation's lunge still slides the planted feet; the run's blade still crosses the crosshair's column; the in-match impale on a hit was not filmed (the scripted player reached no Ork; the stage shows both landings). Evidence: `<media folder>\previews\spear-followups\`. Not verified: a human's look approval.

**Musou tuning: 600 spray cap, a 16 m chain with no fall-off, orbital strikes x1.2 (branch `claude/musou-tuning-1111b` from main 1b057697, 2026-11-11; Musou Mode only; `MusouSim.Version` 42 and `TfwRules.Version` 66, the lead renumbers at integration; tag 16's jump bytes change with MusouSim 42; no protocol change; the faithful and extended config hashes unchanged).** The owner's answers of 2026-11-11 through the lead: "Drop to 600 blood spray cap"; "Widen the 8m jump and make the damage not falloff anymore - it always stays constant", "16 m (double)"; "Add it to orbital strikes and stack it with double damage yes". **Spray cap.** `FxGpuLayout.GpuMaxEffects` 1,200 -> **600** (client; the CPU path's 160 unchanged; `--fx-cap 1200` gives the old cap); P3 measured the 200-death burst frame at 38.8 ms with 1,200 and 32.4 ms with 400; 600 itself was not measured. **Chain lightning.** `LibrarianRules.JumpRadius` 8 -> **16** m and the fall-off gone (`JumpFalloff` 0.85 removed): every enemy of the chain takes 112.5 a second, the 20th and the 40th as the first (a full chain of 40: 4,500 a second, about 1,190 before). The rule is still the one `LibrarianChain` for the server's pick and the client's foresight, so the drawn chain is the struck chain (`MusouLibrarianReliabilityTests` unchanged in substance, all passing). Tag 16 carried each jump as signed decimetre bytes (12.7 m), too short for a 16 m jump (another player's drawing would have stopped at such a jump): its jump bytes now count in 0.2 m (`LibrarianWire.JumpStep`, 25.4 m; same 3 bytes a jump and 557 bytes for four full chains), each taken from the point the reader rebuilt, so the drawn ends are within 0.1 m an axis and the rounding does not add up. The customizer's card reads "jumps up to 16 m from Ork to Ork" and "112.5 damage a second to every Ork in the chain". **Orbital strike.** A shell carries its caller (`TfwShell.Caller`, set by `World.TfwOrbital`); `World.TfwShellLands` multiplies its damage on the enemies by `World.MusouRangedDealt(caller)`: x1.2 for a human player, x1 for an AI Marine, for no caller (the test aid's barrage) and for a caller who left. An ordinary Ork dies either way; a boss takes 36 a shell (30). The kills still carry no player (Barrage deaths), the players and Guardsmen take what they took. The Double Damage powerup does not reach the shells (they deal their damage as nobody's, as before; left so, the lead: "already so: leave it" for the x1.2 stacking on Double Damage). Tests: `MusouTuning1111bTests` (7: the shared rule's 16 m and no further, the client's foresight the same; 40 Orks 12 m apart all at the full damage over a second; drawn = struck on a 12 m chain and tag 16 carrying it whole; the customizer text; a shell's boss damage x1.2 / x1 / x1 for a human / an AI Marine / nobody; a human's called strike x1.2 against a twin world at x1, the player's own damage the same; the kills nobody's), `FxGpuLayoutTests` (the cap 600); updated for the new numbers: `MusouLibrarianTests` (constant damage down the chain, the gap test at 15 / 17 m, the tag 16 tolerance), `MusouLibrarianReliabilityTests` (B 17 m to the side, out of the 16 m jump, with the swap's slack widened by more ticks; the second link's share the first's; 16 m), `MusouLibrarianPass2Tests` (jumps to 15 m an axis, the 0.1 m bound, the too-far jump 26 m). Ran (capped): the Librarian, fire, balance, wire, config-hash, isolation, autocannon, charge, Tfw melee, skirmish pin, score and send tests, `FxGpuLayoutTests`, `MusouCustomizerTests`, `MusouSlotsTests` and the docs guards (561 passed, 0 failed); the full `dotnet test` not run. Not done: no human or bot run on a real server; the 600 cap's burst frame not measured.

**No on-hit effects on shot players in Classic PvP (branch `claude/classic-no-player-hit-fx` from main 980871d2, 2026-11-11; client presentation only, no protocol, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner: "simply remove instances of weapon on hit visual effects like the stalker bolter explosion cloud on the player target you shot and hit - classic pvp only". What drew the cloud (captured before any change with `--bolt-fx-demo sm_mp_ranged_sniper_rifle --bolt-fx-armour 0` on an idle bot, 127.0.0.1): pvp-hit-fx's health-hit burst (`HealthHitBurst`, ours, built from the install's sprites), a red-orange fire burst that turns into a grey smoke cloud for about a second, played by every gun on a hit with no armour left; the bolter draws the same burst, the Stalker's hits just nearly always find the armour gone. On armour the hit drew the spark fans of `hit_ranged_armour_generic` (with their orange light) and the blueprint's `sm_armor_dmg`. Now (`PlayerHitFxRules`, `NetworkView.ClassicHitFx.cs`): in Classic PvP (any match that is not Musou Mode) a body or head hit draws none of `FxImpact`'s on-hit effects (armour-hit effects at the hit point and on the body markers, spark fans, health-hit burst or blood splash, melta burn, hit container whatever the victim's id), `DetonationBodyHit` no armour-hit effects (the explosion stays), and a break a shot caused no `sm_armor_break_shoulders` (a melee break keeps it: `NoteMeleeBreak` from the hit report's melee bit). Kept: the model's own flash and glow (`CharacterFlashHit`: the yellow hit spot, the red break glow; a shader, not an effect), sounds, the HUD, tracers and projectiles, explosions, the map's impacts. Consequence to know: since pvp-hit-fx a hit on a body with no armour shows only the burst (the model's re-flash was dropped for it), so such a hit now shows nothing on the body (`--old-health-hit` brings the model's re-flash back without the streaks). Musou Mode unchanged. Restore: `--player-hit-fx` (in `LeanBot.PresentationAids`); `--log-hit-fx` logs `HITFX classic` lines. Before / after stills (Stalker and bolter, armour and no armour, 8 shots each, plus a restore run) in the owner's media folder under `previews\classic-no-player-hit-fx\`. Tests: `PlayerHitFxRulesTests` (14), `LeanBotTests` (19), with the other impact-rule, extras-boundary, public-text and refine-register tests (capped, all passing). Spec "No on-hit effects on shot players in Classic PvP" (the reading of what stays is tagged ours). Not verified: a live fight with real shots, the own body's view, the melee-break exception by eye.
**The jump-pack death in mid-air (branch `claude/jumppack-death`, 2026-11-11; client only, both modes' marine view; no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner, asked whether to play the graph's mid-air death: "Yes". Before, a marine killed in a jump-pack jump went to the ragdoll at once (the hit reactions pass read and chose "Jumppack Death" but did not play it: the dead were not placed and its effects belonged to the ragdoll). Checked again on the install (`smtool graph-dump --upper`, which now prints each death clip's `StartAction`; docs/discovery.md "The jump-pack death in mid-air"): `SM_REC_MP_MidAirDeath_Hit_01` to its branch at 0.565 s, `SM_REC_MP_MidAirDeath_Fall_01` looping at speed 0.65 (2.256 s) under a blender until `BOOL_IsSupported` or `BOOL_Floor_Hit` (no blend), `SM_REC_MP_MidAirImpact_01` to its powered-ragdoll tag at 0.367 s; `StartAction` at 0.02 s in the start and 0.033 s in the floor clip. Now (`JumpDeathRules`, `JumpDeathRun` in `SmContent/JumpDeath.cs`; `NetworkView.JumpDeath.cs`; `DeathClip.ActionAt`): such a death begins at the death frame (its route needs no kill cause), the client places the body (the last velocity, the world gravity 20 m/s², walls and ceilings against the side's character collision, a slide on the floor), plays the three clips and hands over to the ragdoll at the floor clip's tag with the clip's motion and no push; the floor is met by the posed body's lowest bone (measured: the fall loop hangs the hands 0.5 m below the feet, the floor clip lifts every bone above them within 0.11 s), the feet follow in the floor clip; no floor within 4 s (a pit, a kill volume) and the ragdoll takes it where it is, no impact (ours). The jump death's effects move with it (`DeathBody`): the pack's `actn_jumpdeath_start` and Final Vengeance's steps are queued at the death on the falling body and follow its bones, then the ragdoll's; `actn_jumpdeath_impact` (crater, smoke, impact sound) at the floor clip's `StartAction`. The own death camera follows the falling body. `--no-jump-death` restores the ragdoll at once; the stage `--hit-reaction-test --hrt-case death-jump` plays it with the effects (now driven by an effect player). Tests: `JumpDeathTests` (10: the clips and action tags read, the route in the air whatever the blow, nothing changed on the ground, the fall loop until the floor and its wrap, the impact action and the ragdoll at 0.367 s, the floor met by the lowest point, the cap without an impact, a floor before the branch, walls and ceilings, entries, cancel and hitch); `HitReactionsTests`, `UpperBodyAnimationsTests`, `LeanBotTests` pass. Checked headless with bots on 127.0.0.1 (no map): an Assault bot shot in the rise of a jump played it in its own view and the shooter's (1.7 s of the fall loop, the hands on the floor with the feet 0.4 to 0.5 m up, the impact's effects at the floor clip's `StartAction`, the ragdoll 0.372 s into it with no push, 6 death effects each); a second, killed falling 4.9 m up, reached the floor during the hit clip and went to the floor clip at its branch (no fall loop); no error in 240 s. Clip (stage, H.264): `<media folder>\previews\jumppack-death\death-jump.mp4`. Spec "The jump-pack death in mid-air"; docs/changes-from-original.md rows; the refine register regenerated.

**Charge cancel: S, not the grenade; no recoil on an ally (branch `claude/charge-cancel-ally-bump` from main ef496d67, 2026-11-11; protocol 66, the lead renumbers at integration; no layout change; the faithful and extended config hashes unchanged, the restore switches hash only when on).** The owner: "throwing a grenade no longer cancels a bull rush/charge animation. what should cancel a charge animation is tapping or holding the S key (backpedal)"; "no animation should play when hitting an ally. that animation should only play when charging or clashing with an enemy" (Classic PvP). **Cause of the grenade cancel** (reproduced on main with a synthetic charge: a Grenade press past the stick branch ended the rush at once with 0 and with 1 grenade, and threw with 1): the rush's data branch `BRANCH_Attack2Idle` lets the stick, Fire, Aim or a Grenade press end it; protocols 48 and 53 took Fire, Aim and the stick off it, which left the Grenade press as the one early end, tested before the throw's own check for a grenade in hand (and input-buffered 0.3 s). **Now** (`ChargeCancel`, `Combat.StepPlayerCore`): a Grenade press ends no charge phase (the bull rush, its collision stop, the dash attack's states) in any mode and waits in the input buffer, so with a grenade left the throw starts on the tick the charge ends if that is within 0.3 s; S held back (S, S + A, S + D; a pad's stick in the back three of eight sectors) ends the bull rush from the same branch (0.467 s on the install), tapped or held, into normal movement with no stop clip; a tap released before the branch does nothing (ours). Musou Mode's players share the charge and get the same. **Ally bump** (Classic PvP only; `World.ResolveRush`, `StopRushes`): a charge (the bull rush, the dash attack's lunge) that meets an ally it cannot harm (no friendly fire) ends where it met him, with no collision stop, no turn and the velocity zeroed; nothing on the ally (no hit-stop, effects or camera kick either: the own client's predicted bump is no connect). The contact rule and the bodies' collision are unchanged, so the charge stops where the recoil began before (ours; running on and sliding past is the alternative, an open question for the playtest). Enemies (hit, stun, recoil, clash), friendly fire and Musou Mode as before. Predicted exactly (`ChargeLock.Predict`, friendly fire from the scoreboard). Restore switches `--old-charge-cancel` and `--old-ally-bump` (server and every client; config hash). Tests: `ChargeCancelTests` (30: the grenade at every rush tick with 0 and 1 grenades, the buffered throw after the end, S held in four directions and tapped, other sticks, the collision stop and the dash attack's states, the switches and the hash, the ally bump, friendly fire, the enemy, the own prediction against the world, and three allied clients under 150 ms RTT and 5 % loss: 25 bumps, 4 S cancels, 0 mismatches in 1110 ticks each, nothing excluded); `ChargeDirectionsTests`, `NoFireInChargeTests`, `ChargeLockTests` and `MeleeCooldownTests` moved to S or the switch; every protocol pin 65 -> 66. `MusouIsolationTests`' golden replay is unchanged (its script presses no grenade in a charge and bumps no ally). A ship needs the VM servers updated (protocol). Spec "Charge cancel: S, not the grenade; the ally bump"; docs/changes-from-original.md section 1 rows; the refine register regenerated.
**The autocannon pass: Musou's one-shot blast and endless clip, the heavy bolter's backpack, and Classic PvP's autocannon in the extended profile (branch `claude/autocannon-pass` from main ef496d67, 2026-11-11; Musou `TfwRules.Version` 67 and `MusouSim.Version` 43, the lead renumbers at integration; Classic: a new added-content flag `ContentExtras.Autocannon` (16) in `ContentExtras.All`, so the extended profile's config hash changed (the install's 0x7556F708CE2FD9A2, was 0x2AAB9E068C454594) and a ship needs the VM's Classic server updated; the faithful hash is unchanged (0x5277E16C8E7F6260); no protocol or extras wire change).** The owner's five requests of 2026-11-11. **Musou Mode:** the blast is 100 everywhere in its 2.5 m (`AutocannonRules.BlastFallOff`: full to the edge; was 15, full to 1.0 m, 30 % at the edge), so with a human's x1.2 it deals 120, the most health of any fodder Ork (`AutocannonRules.Fodder`: the Boy, Shoota Boy and Rokkit Boy 85, the Gretchin and Bomb Squig 30, the Stormboy 120; no wave, army, Guard or difficulty scale touches an Ork's health, only the Warboss's; which Orks count as fodder is ours: every one neither an elite nor a boss); the round is the blast's + 30 (`AutocannonRules.DirectDamage` 130, 156 after the x1.2; `Arsenal.MusouTwin`); the clip is never spent in the war (`World.TfwEndlessAmmo` puts the whole clip back every tick, `AutocannonRules.EndlessClip`; heat and overheat unchanged) and the HUD box shows the movie's endless sign (`Arsenal.EndlessAutocannonBox`). **Every mode:** a carried autocannon counts as the heavy bolter for the class overrides (`AppearanceResolver.WornAs`, a new pinned hook `ExtrasWornAs`, implemented by `Arsenal.WornAs`), so the Devastator wears `sm_backpack_heavy_bolter` with it, in the match and the customizer's preview; the Havoc's pack is the data's one override for every weapon. **Classic PvP (extended only):** `SmContent.Extras.Autocannon.ClassicAutocannon` appends the same twin (`Arsenal.ClassicTwin`: the Stalker Bolter's damage 50 and its four multipliers as Classic reads them, head x2 / x2.5 on armour; the autocannon's rate, heat, range, fall-off, clip of 400 and the heavy bolter's handling) to every heavy class that lists a heavy bolter, last and at one position on both sides (one weapon, `sm_mp_exotic_auto_cannon`, for the Devastator and the Havoc); Classic's hit-scan path has no blast, so no splash; its clip spends; the arsenal's client hooks act for it under the flag (`ArsenalRules.Shown`), so it has Musou's model, loyalist effects, reticle and the counting box, but its sounds stay its install twin's (`Arsenal.SoundSources(ContentExtras, ...)` is Musou's alone: no Stalker swap). The customizer offers it on both heavy classes (`ClassicAutocannon.Catalog` through `PerkCatalog.ExtrasItems`), reads the profile with that row so a saved slot survives a faithful start (`CustomizerServices.Load`), and plans an extended Join with the data's configuration plus the autocannon (`client/Extras/Autocannon/`, behind the new dispatcher `client/Extras/CustomizerServices.Extras.cs`). `ContentProfiles.Describe` names a flag list once ("orks,gore (extras wire 2)"), so every profile's refusal still fits its 200 characters. Tests: `AutocannonTests` (26 cases: 14 facts and two theories over the six fodder types; one blast kills each fodder type at the centre and at the edge with the x1.2, a round kills each it strikes, 276 a struck Ork, the endless clip with the heat still running), `ClassicAutocannonSimTests` (5: a round hurts as a Stalker round and nobody beside him, no detonation, the clip spends, the Havoc's position, no autocannon without the flag), `ClassicAutocannonContentTests` (11: the profiles, the append, the round, the presentation per mode, the catalogue, the read catalogue and the backpack), the hash pins (`ConfigHashPinTests`, `MusouIsolationTests`: extended moved, faithful unchanged), `ContentProfileTests`, `ExtrasBoundaryTests`. Stills (a Classic match on 127.0.0.1, the own view and an observer; looked at: the heavy bolter's pack with its brass ammunition rows on the Devastator's back, the autocannon's reticle and 400 in the box; the shortened gun in hand): `<media folder>\previews\autocannon-pass\`. No human has played it. The faithful build (`-p:SmExtras=false`) still fails on main in files this branch does not touch (core files naming Extras-only members); this branch's core changes compile there.
**Bot grenade safety (branch `claude/bot-grenade-safety`, 2026-11-11; Classic PvP bots, client only; no simulation, wire, protocol or config-hash change).** The owner: "change bot behavior in classic pvp mode - i want to set a rule that includes a minimum distance at which they will throw grenades. they should also not (as a raptor/assault marine) jump in near where the grenade landed until it has exploded", "the end result is no more or very few bot suicides to their own grenades." Measured first (headless Manufactorum Annihilation on 127.0.0.1, 8 bots: per side two jump-pack bots, a Tactical and a heavy, all on frag presets; 3 x 5 min): **15 of 184 deaths were a bot's own frag** (103 throws, 19 enemies killed by frags, 7 of them together with the thrower), 11 of them Assault or Raptor bots; every throw was at a target 6 to 17 m away and the old script aimed **8 m short of the target** (at least 2 m in front), written before the owner's 2026-10-29 bounce change, so the frag came to rest 2 to 6 m from the thrower, who then charged (7), jumped or pounded (4), swung (3) or walked on (3) inside its blast. Now (`SmNet.BotGrenadeSafety`, engine-free; `client/NetworkView.BotGrenades.cs`): a damaging throw only when the target's chest and the predicted landing point (the target's feet moved by its horizontal velocity over the release and the flight, or the first level contact on the aimed line) are both at least the item's own blast radius from the data + 1.5 m from the bot's chest (3D; the frag 11.5 m), never at a target in the air or from the air, aimed at that landing point; the bot follows its own grenade (the first new thrown projectile of the snapshots that its throw could have carried that far by then: snapshots carry no owner) and, while it is out (in flight its planned landing, once down its place), does not walk, jump, dash, hop, charge, melee or pound into the blast and backs straight out when inside; launcher rounds are not set off with the bot inside their reach. The splash weapons had no suicide in the first 8 matches, then two in one after-run (a plasma cannon fired into the level in front of a Devastator, a plasma pistol charge), so a shot whose projectile has a blast (plasma cannon, plasma charges, launcher) is no longer fired where it would burst within that blast of the bot, and its own resting or stuck sticky rounds join the hazards. Stims and the blind grenade keep the old 6 m rule; Musou Mode's co-op bots are untouched (`BotGrenadeSafety.Applies`, the hold skips added content's bot tick); `--old-bot-throws` restores the old script (`LeanBot.LeanSafeAids`; one of the before-runs used it on the new build). Measured again with the same matches and the final build: **0 of 175 deaths** by an own frag or splash (57 throws, all at 11.5 m or more, every own grenade followed until it went off with the thrower alive, the nearest 8.5 m from a chest; 11 frag kills, none with the thrower: 19 % of throws against 18 % before; 45 % fewer throws); over all 15 after-runs of the five passes (626 deaths) no death by an own frag. Tests: `BotGrenadeSafetyTests` (the safety distance per item, the 3D, landing, level and in-air throw rules, the claim, the hold of moves, jumps and charges and the back-out, the splash-shot and detonation rules, Musou and the restore flag, and in the simulation with Classic's bounce the old aim at 8 m putting 200 damage on the thrower against the new aim at 14 m going off 13.2 m out with none), `LeanBotTests`, `GrenadeTests`. Not measured: Seize Ground (the same fight code), the grenade launcher and Master-Crafted Wargear (no bot preset carries them); throws at targets well above still fly far past them (unchanged). Spec "Classic PvP bots: grenade safety"; docs/changes-from-original.md row; docs/commands.md; the refine register regenerated.

**Bot grenade safety, review follow-ups (same branch, 2026-11-11).** The independent review approved with minors; fixed: (1) no deadlock: an own grenade and a waiting round of the bot's own weapons (launcher, sticky) are hazards for at most 6 s from their release or first sighting (`BotGrenadeSafety.TrackOwn`, `RoundIsHazard`), and a back-out (straight away from the blast, blind to walls) that gets no 0.25 m farther for 1.5 s gives up: the bot's own input goes through and the blasts holding it are left out of every hold until it is out of them (`StepBackOut`, `StillGivenUp`); remote rounds still go off only with the chest outside their reach. (2) A plasma-cannon heavy no longer stands idle from point blank to 8.5 m: 1 s of held splash shots (no gap over 0.25 s) takes a loaded pistol, back to the cannon once its burst point is 2 m beyond the safety distance (`TakePistol`, `BackToSplash`, `NetworkView.BotSplashSwitch`). (3) A throw under way aims at the farther of the press's landing point and the current one (`FartherLanding`). (4) A claimed grenade in flight also counts at its own place once it has been outside the bot's reach (a bounce back off a wall). (5) No snapshot scan when nothing is out, and no per-tick lists, lambdas or arrays (index loops in the rules). (6) A navigation take-off the hold drops used to count as a jump miss, and two misses drop a link for the match: `NavAgent.CancelTakeOff` hands it back without a miss (the link is pressed again once clear, as one start). Also, from a focused review run: a Raptor flying at a Devastator met its ball 6.5 m from the heavy's chest and killed it, so the splash check also tests where the shot meets a target coming on (velocity over the interpolation delay plus the flight; `MeetingPoint`). Re-measured, 2 x 5 min with the same lineups: 0 of 115 deaths by an own frag or splash (38 throws, every own grenade gone with its thrower alive); the heavies killed 21 and 14 (14 to 21 before); no give-up, capped hazard or held take-off came up; 7 nav jumps landed, none missed. Two focused 3 min runs (a plasma heavy and a jump-pack bot per side): the pistol taken after 1.0 s of held shots (and put away 15 s later), the Raptor-meets-ball death in the first, 0 of 13 in the second with the meeting point; the Havoc's close fights broke its held runs with melee and jumps, so it never took the pistol. Tests: `BotGrenadeSafetyTests` (39: tracking, expiry, unseen, down, the round cap, the give-up of a cornered bot, the farther landing, the pistol run, the meeting point, the waiting-round weapons), `NavJumpTests` (a held take-off is no miss). Spec rows updated; the refine register regenerated.

**The autocannon pass 2: no range fall-off in Musou, the Stormboy out of the fodder, no clip in Musou, a clip of 120 in Classic, the Havoc's Chaos effects (branch `claude/autocannon-pass-2` from `claude/autocannon-pass` 20118245, 2026-11-11; Musou `TfwRules.Version` 68 and `MusouSim.Version` 44, the lead renumbers at integration; Classic: the extended profile's config hash moved again (the install's 0x479768E19E322CCA, was 0x7556F708CE2FD9A2) with the clip and the drops' amount, so a ship needs the VM's Classic server updated; the faithful hash unchanged (0x5277E16C8E7F6260); no protocol or extras wire change).** The owner's answers of 2026-11-11: "There should be no damage falloff for any ranged weapon in Musou mode"; "Stormboy is not fodder"; "In classic PvP only. 120 clip size. No clip in Musou mode - just infinite shooting."; "Give the chaos autocannon the chaos visual effects all the way through". **No range fall-off (Musou Mode's war):** one place, `World.MusouRangeFallOff` (1 in the war under `TfwCombatRules.RangeFallOff` false; the weapon's `Combat.FallOff` in the 5-wave run), read by `MusouShotDamage` (the 5-wave rays, the war's piercing rays `TfwPierceShot`, the contraptions' `TfwMekShot`) and `MusouConeMultiplier` (`MusouCone`: the coverage multiplier alone, so the melta deals its 200 to its 20 m); every shooter and weapon, the arsenal's included; projectiles and charged stages had none already; a blast's fall-off from its centre, the pierce share per enemy and the 5-wave run unchanged; Classic unchanged. **Fodder:** the Stormboy left `AutocannonRules.Fodder` (Boy, Shoota Boy, Gretchin, Rokkit Boy, Bomb Squig; the most health 85), so the blast is **71** everywhere in its 2.5 m (85.2 after a human's x1.2, 85.2000046 in single precision: an 85 Ork dies; 70 would leave 1) and the round **101** (121.2); a Stormboy takes a blast and stands at 34.8. **No clip in Musou:** a new pinned hook `SimConfig.ExtrasEndlessClip` (declared in `src/SmSim/Stims.cs`, read by `SimConfig.EndlessClip` at the three spends of the shot step in `Combat.cs`, false in Classic and faithful) makes Musou's autocannon spend no round, so the server and the client's prediction agree and nothing reloads it; the first pass's per-tick refill in `World.TfwEndlessAmmo` is gone; heat and overheat as before; the HUD keeps the endless sign. **Classic:** `Arsenal.ClassicTwin` takes the multiplayer file's clip, **120** (no reserve; 400 before), and `ClassicAutocannon.WithBoxAmounts` gives the drops' types the Space Marine heavy bolter's amount at the autocannon's index (100 on the install, into the clip, capped at 120): the drops are read before the append, so until now a box gave the autocannon nothing (the first pass's "refilled by an ammunition box" was not true). **Chaos effects:** a new pinned client hook `NetworkView.ExtrasShooterEffects` (declared in `client/NetworkView.Presentation.cs`, read by `EffectsWargear` for the own shot, the others' shots, a launch and the stop smoke) picks `Arsenal.EffectsFor`: a shooter of the Chaos race (`Races.Of` of his class and team; the Havoc) plays the install twin's own catalogue entry `csm_mp_exotic_auto_cannon` whole (purple flash, tracer, impact container, stop smoke, casing), a Space Marine the loyalist renames; one weapon, no catalogue index or saved class changes. Tests: `MusouRangeFallOffTests` (7: the bolter, stalker bolter, lascannon and plasma gun at 8 and 100 m at full damage in the war and at x0.5 with the switch on; the melta at 5 and 15 m; the default; the 5-wave run's fall-off), `AutocannonTests` (updated: 71/101, the fodder list without the Stormboy and its single-precision check, a Stormboy living through a blast, no clip in the war and in `Combat.StepPlayer` alone with R reloading nothing), `ClassicAutocannonSimTests` (clip 120 that spends, the drops' amount and the 120 cap, Classic's fall-off kept), `ClassicAutocannonContentTests` (the clip from the file, `EffectsFor` per side and profile, the drops), `EffectCatalogueTests.A_Havocs_autocannon_shot_plays_the_Chaos_twins_effects_and_a_Devastators_the_loyalist_ones` (a synthetic twin through the client's catalogue pipeline), `ConfigHashPinTests` (extended recaptured, faithful unchanged), `ExtrasBoundaryTests` (the two hooks and their call sites pinned). Stills (an extended Classic match on 127.0.0.1, windowed bots firing at the walls; looked at: the Havoc's purple-white flash and lavender glow, the Devastator's warm orange impact, both with the autocannon's counting box): `<media folder>\previews\autocannon-pass-2\` (the raw series in `frames\`). No human has played it.

**The damage answers: the AI Marines' range fall-off back, no pierce loss for the players, the melta and Double Damage pinned (branch `claude/musou-damage-answers` from main 83720ee3, 2026-11-11; Musou `TfwRules.Version` 69 and `MusouSim.Version` 45, the lead renumbers at integration; no Classic, faithful or protocol change, no config hash change).** The owner's answers: "melta should keep its full 200 damage out to 20m"; "alliedmarine should not lose range falloff"; "a shot should not lose 15% of its damage for each ork it passes through - but only for the players"; "double damage should not affect orbital strikes". **Fall-off:** `World.MusouNoRangeFallOff(shooter)` is now true only for a human player's shots in the war (`TfwCombatRules.ScalesPlayer`, an AI Marine holds a puppet id), so `MusouShotDamage` and `MusouConeMultiplier` (new shooter argument; the rays, the war's piercing rays, the contraptions' shots, the cone) give an AI Marine's gun its own `Combat.FallOff` and the melta's cone its distance fall-off again; a player's shots keep none. **Pierce:** `TfwPierceShot` applies `PierceKeep` (0.85 per Ork) only to an AI Marine's shot; a human's loses nothing (a projectile, a charged stage and a plasma shot never lost any). **Melta and Double Damage:** already right (the melta's cone has no distance factor for a player; a shell's damage carries no attacker, so `AttackerScale` leaves it at 1 and only the human caller's x1.2 applies), now pinned by tests. Tests: `MusouRangeFallOffTests` (AI Marine's bolter, stalker bolter, lascannon, plasma gun at 8 m full and x1, at 100 m x0.5; the AI melta at 15 m about x0.325; a player's melta full at 18 and 20 m; a player's lascannon shot through three Orks at equal damage, an AI Marine's x1, x0.85, x0.85^2), `MusouTuning1111bTests.Double_Damage_does_not_multiply_an_orbital_strike`. No human has played it.

**Graphify, the code graph (branch `tools/graphify`, 2026-11-11).** Owner decision: Graphify 0.9.106 joins the workflow for change-impact questions. `graphify.cmd` (`tools/graphify.ps1`): `setup` (pinned venv, idempotent), `index` (incremental, code only, no clustering, about 30 s for the whole repository; stamps the HEAD it indexed), `serve` (stdio MCP server on this checkout's index, else the main checkout's; a stale-index warning on stderr; fails fast without the venv) and `explain|affected|path|query`; every call runs in a clean environment with `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none`. `.graphifyignore`, a committed `.mcp.json` (the graphify server only; not pre-approved in the repo, so each checkout approves it once in its local settings: a fork or foreign branch cannot auto-run it) makes it available in the main checkout and in agent worktrees; the source zip leaves the Graphify files out; `graphify-out/` is ignored. Rules and blind spots (the `Extras*` partial hooks) in docs/commands.md and CLAUDE.md. No gameplay change.

**Charge ally slide (branch `claude/charge-ally-slide` from main 83720ee3, 2026-11-11; protocol 67, the lead renumbers at integration; no layout change; config hashes unchanged, `--old-ally-bump` hashes only when on).** The owner answered protocol 66's open question: "when a charge hits an ally it should slide past", and "early s tap should not be remembered". A charge now passes the players of its own side that it cannot harm (match rules without friendly fire): `ChargeLock.Find` leaves them out (`passAllies`, from `ChargeCancel.AllyPasses`), so there is no contact, stop, turn or impact, on the server (`World.ResolveRush`) and in the own prediction (`ChargeLock.Predict`) alike; the shared player collision still keeps the bodies apart and slides the charger along the ally's capsule, and nothing happens to the ally. Every mode, Musou Mode included (protocol 66 had kept the recoil on an ally there; no Musou rule of its own was found, so the owner's answer is applied to it, and `MusouCombatTests`' last-move check now uses `--old-ally-bump`'s stop). Enemies and friendly fire as before. The protocol 66 bump (`ChargeCancel.Bumped`, `RushEvent.Bump`, `ChargeContact.Bump`, `ChargeBumpsPredicted`) is removed. **S tap**: an S press before the rush's stick branch was already not remembered (the stick is tested on the branch tick only, the input buffer keeps button presses); now pinned for every tap tick 1 to 17 with the buffer window 0 and 0.3 s. Tests: `ChargeCancelTests` (32: the pass keeps every tick of the charge equal to one with nobody ahead, friendly fire, the switch, Musou, the prediction against the world, the 150 ms RTT / 5 % loss run with allies passed: 0 mismatches), `ChargeLockTests`, `RushTests`, `MusouCombatTests` (a Musou pass test), every protocol pin 66 -> 67. A ship needs the VM servers updated (protocol). Spec "Charge ally slide"; docs/changes-from-original.md; the refine register regenerated.
**The autocannon's kick (branch `claude/autocannon-arm-recoil` from main 83720ee3, 2026-11-11; client only, no sim, wire or protocol change).** The owner: "the arm currently moves completely away from the gun when firing. it should only slightly move straight back from the direction the gun fires in." Cause: the autocannon borrows the heavy bolter's animations (`ExtrasAnimationAlias`), so every shot laid the heavy bolter's additive recoil clip `SM_RNG_TB_FireIdle_S_01`, which turns the arm bones (right hand 7 to 22 degrees, upper arm 10 to 17) and the chest prop by different amounts while the gun rides the chest prop bone: measured on the own character, the right hand slid up to 13 cm along the gun relative to its mount each shot. Fix: a new pinned hook `NetworkView.ExtrasHipRecoil` (core `NetworkView.HipFire.cs`) lets the autocannon show no clip; instead `RIG_SpineD`, the bone the arms and the chest prop hang from, moves 0.04 m back along the muzzle's axis (0.04 s out, 0.26 s back, smoothstep; `AutocannonKick`, `CharacterViewer.AutocannonKickOverlay` through `ExtrasPoseOverlay`), so gun and both arms move as one. The heavy bolter and every other weapon keep their clips; test aid `--old-autocannon-recoil` restores the clip. Spec "The autocannon's kick" (ours, provisional approximation, low). Stills (`--tfw-autocannon-capture`, before and after; looked at: the right hand on the drum's grip in the after frames, floating above the receiver in the before): `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\tmp-build\ac-recoil\` (`before\`, `after\`). Test: `AutocannonContentTests` (+1), `ExtrasBoundaryTests` pin. No human has played it.
**Hit effects: the owner's answers (branch `claude/hit-fx-answers` from main 83720ee3, 2026-11-11; client presentation only, no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner: "the model flash should come back on for bare-armor hits, and break prticles should appear when a shot breaks armor, and the melta should burn the body in classic and in musou mode of targets it kills"; "ensure the pack's flash from jump-pack death isn't left hanging in the air. it should disappear once the jump-pack user dies." **What had been removed:** pvp-hit-fx (33a2091e, 2026-11-06) turned the 0.2 s red re-flash of a hit on a bare body off for its burst (`ArmourFlashTracker.Reflash`), and classic-no-player-hit-fx (5d9f7a07, 2026-11-11) dropped the break effect for a shot's break and the melta burn on hits. **Now:** in Classic PvP the re-flash is on again (`PlayerHitFxRules.BareHitFlash`; Musou keeps the burst), a shot's break plays `sm_armor_break_shoulders` again (the install's own effect, *original asset loaded*), and the melta's whole-body burn comes from the kill (`NetworkView.MeltaKillBurn`, called from `ScheduleDeathFx`, for players; Musou Mode's crowd deaths carry no weapon, so `MusouMeltaBurn` (added content, `Extras/Musou/NetworkView.MusouMeltaBurn.cs`) burns a crowd body when the killer's weapon in hand is the melta and the cause a shot: four effects over the fall point, 3 sets a frame, none beyond 45 m; at the corpse's focus only for a rig with none of the named bones; once per death, also the own, and again at a jump death's ragdoll), not from the hit. **The pack:** the launch / dive / dash flashes are tracked (`JumpFxTrack.Flashes`) and cut when the pilot dies; the death's burst `jumppack_death_mp` (data: fixed in the world at `rig_spinea`) now rides the falling body and ends when it lands or settles (`DeathFxJob.PackDeath`, `PackBurstLanded`). Switches `--old-classic-hit-fx`, `--melta-burn-on-hit`, `--old-pack-death-flash`. Tests: `PlayerHitFxRulesTests` (bare flash, shot break, switches; 60 passed with `MeltaBurnRules`, `LeanBot`, `CharacterVisuals` and `HitDecalRules`). Checked on a local server (127.0.0.1) with an idle bot and a windowed observer: the cycle demo showed the red body flash on the bare-armour hit and the break glow with `sm_armor_break_shoulders` logged; the melta hit demo drew no burn and the melta kill demo burned 14 of 16 bones. Review round: the Musou crowd burn, the jump death's second look, the own body and the bone-less fallback were fixed (the first version burned players only); `--melta-burn-on-hit` now works alone. Stills under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\tmp-build\hit-fx\shots`. Spec "Hit effects: the bare-armour flash and the break particles back"; docs/changes-from-original.md row; the refine register regenerated.

**Install transitions the client did not play (polish item 10, claude/install-transitions, 2026-11-12; client only, Classic and Musou, no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner: "i want to integrate the transition animations that you found before in the original game, that are not currently used in sm-reimpl. they are animations that play between actions or modes or directions" (answer 2: "Yes, where the original wires them."). Inventory first (`smtool graph-dump`, new `--root-motion` turn column): of the clips the plan listed, the install's graphs wire three the client could show now. **The half-speed stop** (`SM_NAV_Bullrush2Idle_F_HalfSpeed_01`) is the sprint graphs' "Transition To Idle on Interrupt" state, entered from the start state on `!BOOL_SprintIsActive` once `BRANCH_Sprint_Interrupt` is open (0.4286 of the start): a sprint stop that begins inside that window (about 0.4 to 1.1 s after the marine stood; the simulation's stop flag, as the full stop) plays it instead of the family's full stop (`SprintInterruptRules`, `SprintStartTracker.InStartWindow`, `NetworkView.InterruptClipOf`); every family. **The 180-degree turn into a sprint** (`SM_TRN_BO/CS/HB/TH_180Turn_to_Sprint`, "180 Idle to Sprint": the rifle's two-handed and one-handed states, the heavy bolter's and the hammer's; the cannons' graph has none) replaces the start when the body stood more than 100 degrees off the aim (`SprintTurnTracker`; the dump prints the entry edges the other way round from what the clip can mean, interpretation; the clip's root turns 180 degrees at 0.27 to 0.4 s and then travels away): it plays in real time from the time the marine has been moving, the drawn body turning from where it is with the clip's root turn (`SprintEdgeClip.TurnProgress`, `NetworkView.SprintTurnYaw` in `BodyYawFor`); the own marine's clip choice comes from the predicted state (the planted body's offset, the speed), so a correction pops nothing. **The thunder hammer's sprint stop** (`SM_NAV_Sprint_to_Idle_F`, `SM_TH_NuSprint`): the hammer had no sprint edges at all; `SprintTransitions.DefaultMaps` gains its graph. Checked and not new: `SM_REC_Sprint_Stagger` is the death machine's "Sprinting Death" (already `MarineDeathKind.Sprint`). Not wired, with the reason (spec "Install transitions the client did not play", `docs/changes-from-original.md` section 3): the other hit directions (only the Bloodletter's, the Nob's and the counter's states hold them; the marine's own "CSM Reactions" has FHL and BHR, which play), `SM_REC_Stun2Idle_D_01` (the downed player's revive: Exterminatus), the chainsword's and the hammer's drop and landing in `SM_Pistol_NAV`, and the sprint loop's wall edge into the half-speed stop (needs the simulation to brake a sprinter). Aids: `--no-extra-transitions` restores the before; `--log-sprint-edges` prints the edges; `--transition-sweep` starts with three new legs (a sprint tap, a 180 and a -135 degree view whip before a sprint); `--feel-shots-dense` with `--feel-shots-on turn | interrupt | start | stop` writes a frame every 33 ms for the event, and `--transition-sweep` with `--feel-shots` has the human follow camera. Measured with `--transition-probe` on the sweep's first three legs, three pairs of 38 s runs of a Tactical (a rifle marine), `--no-extra-transitions` / this build (headless, 60 fps cap, live server): into the sprint's first clip (12 switches each) jerk median 9.0 / 48.1, max 11.3 / 128.1 cm/f² (half of the twelve are 180 turns: the clip's own pivot; a first version that turned the whole standing offset of about 130 degrees from the first sprint frame measured median 119, max 241 and was dropped for starting from the drawn body's offset); stops: 9 full stops before (jerk median 16.5, max 16.7), after 6 full stops (4.5, max 7.5) and 3 half-speed stops (10.5, max 15.1). Live logs (`--log-sprint-edges`): the half-speed stop and the 180 turn on the rifle and pistol graphs (Tactical, Assault), the hammer's stop `SM_NAV_Sprint_to_Idle_F` and `SM_TRN_TH_180Turn_to_Sprint` (Assault with the thunder hammer), and the same edges in a Musou Mode client; a Devastator played none in its 34 s run (its always-ready weapon keeps the stop's old rule: no stop while the weapon is up). Frames looked at (windowed, a frame every 130 ms, `--feel-shots-dense` on the human follow camera; MP4s in the media folder `transitions`): the 180 turn shows the body turning round into the sprint without a pop, the half-speed stop slows from the run-down pose; the first full demo replay at 1600x900 never left its loading screen in Movie Maker mode, so no time-faithful movie. Tests `InstallTransitionsTests` (11: the graph reading with and without the edges, the hammer's map, the interrupt window, the start tracker's window, the turn's trigger, progress, real-time play, staleness, drop). Restore: `--no-extra-transitions`.

**Install transitions, pass 2 batch 1 (claude/install-transitions-2, 2026-11-12; client only, Classic and Musou, no simulation, wire, protocol or config-hash change).** The owner: "start the work to add the transition animations that the original game had but we haven't deployed to sm-reimpl yet" (standing: "where the original wires them"). **Inventory first**: `docs/transitions-inventory.md` lists every transition-type clip of the marine rig (576 clips, 46 graphs) with the graph state, the edge condition, whether the client plays it, and its status; its preface notes that a name search of the client under-counts (most families read their clips from the graphs' state names). Ranked remaining gaps: the braced heavy bolter's turn (`SM_RNG_TB_Brace_TurnLeft/Right`), the hammer's air dash and landing (`SM_JMP_TH_Dash_*`), the hammer's second strike after the 180 sweep; blocked for the owner: the plasma cannon's, lascannon's and plasma pistol's fire-mode change clips (no fire-mode input in the simulation) and the sprinter's wall stop. **Wired now**: the thunder hammer's and the chainsword's drop and landing (`SM_2HM_NAV_TH_Dropdown/_Landing`, `SM_NAV_CS_Dropdown/_Landing`, the heavy bolter's whole-body shape: from 1 m above the ground, the landing from 0.5 m whatever the speed; `FallFamily.Hammer` / `Chainsword`, the chainsword's states found two machines down in `SM_Pistol_NAV`; `NetworkView.MeleeFallFamily` picks them from the melee wargear, ours for the graphs' `BOOL_Thunderhammer` / `BOOL_Chainsword`) and the hammer's jump-pack landings (`SM_JMP_TH_Landing_LowRun` 1.133 s, `_Low` 1.2 s, in place of the plain 0.9 s run landing). Behind `--no-extra-transitions` (the rifle's fall and the plain landings come back). Every class has `mp_fall_protection`, so the landing after the whole-body drop is the short protected exit (about 0.27 s of the clip plus a 0.1 s blend), not the full 1.1 s; chainsword and hammer marines lose the rifle's leg layer and soft settle for falls under 1 m (faithful to the graph); a chainsword Assault running off a 1 m ledge is drawn upright in the drop pose (playtest check). The family choice is `SmContent.MeleeFallChoice` (tested, spear and mace aliases and the switch included). Measured live (`--bot --bot-gait --bot-ledge --class assault --log-fall --transition-probe`, 110 s each, `--no-extra-transitions` / this build): before 2 falls over 1 m, both soft legs-only; after 4 falls, 3 hard whole-body landings and 1 soft; the switch jerk into the fall 0.9 / 3.5 cm/f2, the exit into the run unchanged (140.2 / 141.5). Tests `InstallTransitionsMeleeFallTests` (4) and `MeleeFallChoiceTests` (13 cases), with `InstallTransitions*` and `FallAnimations*`. Not wired and why: spec "Install transitions, pass 2 batch 1", `docs/changes-from-original.md` section 3.

**Musou Mode: the second support ability, the drop pod assault (2026-11-12, branch `claude/support-ability-drop-pod`; `TfwRules.Version` 70 (the lead renumbers), `MusouSim.Version` and `Protocol.Version` unchanged, Musou Mode only).** The owner: a SUPPORT section in the Customizer, every loadout gets it; the first option the artillery strike, the second a drop pod assault: B marks a point with the laser, a few seconds later an original drop pod falls in fire and smoke, the screen shakes hard, the doors drop open and 4 Tactical Marines fight 30 s, retreat to the Imperial HQ and vanish. Design: `docs/drop-pod-assault.md`. **Choice:** a sixth creator step SUPPORT (the marines' page shows it fifth after PERKS, the Librarian's sixth; `CreatorView` got two hooks, `ExtrasStepShown` and `ExtrasSupportRows`), stored per loadout (`d:<role>`, `c:<slot>`, `l`) in the profile's Musou extras (`MusouSlots.SupportOf`/`WithSupport`; Classic's file is byte for byte as before); B sends `TfwCommand.Orbital` or the new `DropPod` 16 with the crosshair point, so nothing is sent at deploy and the server validates either. **Sim:** `World.TfwDropPod` (the strike's conditions, one pod per player, 4 free puppet ids, 10 m from the caller, the strike's 60 s cooldown shared) lays a `TfwPod`; tag 11's new record kind `Pod` 8 carries the touchdown (and, with `To` X, the wreck's end); the touchdown kills every ordinary enemy within 6 m (ours, the owner did not say); `MarineRole.Pod` Marines (the Tactical's default loadout, the caller's look) step out 1.6 s later, hold the spot 30 s (the retainer's Hold), then sprint to `Layout.Hq` and are gone within 6 m or after 40 s; the fallen are cleared after 3 s. **Client:** `NetworkView.TfwDropPod.cs` loads the install's `DropPod` mesh (campaign chunk `part_01__s_004_r350_airlock`: a singleplayer-content dependency, a capsule when missing) and `DropPodRig` reads its five doors' shut pose from the object file's rig; the fall (90 m, accelerating over 1.5 s) with `drop_pod_trail`, `play_droppod_incoming`, the touchdown (`droppod_land_close`, `drop_pod_landing_destruction`, dust, crater, the install's landing and door sounds, a 0.12 rad shake), the doors turning outward flat (our approximation; the original's is Havok data); `--no-drop-pod` restores the artillery strike as the only call and hides the step. **Checks:** `TfwDropPodTests` (10: wire, call, refusals, crush, 4 Marines, 30 s, retreat, wreck, id limit, battle end, the switch), `DropPodRigTests`, support tests in `MusouSlotsTests`/`MusouCustomizerTests`; the Classic and Musou-isolation pins unchanged. On a real server (`--tfw-pod-test`, headless): 9 of 9 passed (record, touchdown 0.1 m from the crosshair, cooldown, a second call refused, 4 Marines, gone with the pod). Windowed captures looked at: the pod falling in fire, the impact, the landed pod with its doors flat on the ground; the MP4 and the Customizer before/after in the media folder `drop-pod`. Not played by a human; in a live battle the Orks at the landing zone killed all four Marines within about 15 s in two of three runs (the retreat was seen in the third and in the sim tests). Spec "Musou Mode: drop pod assault"; owner questions at the end of the design note.
**Musou: only actual NPCs make noise, voices carry farther (musou/npc-voices-only, branch `claude/musou-npc-voices-only`, 2026-11-12; client only, Musou Mode only; no protocol, wire or hash change).** The owner: "Remove the ambient voices and yells from Musou mode. Only actual in game npcs should make noise. Just make it so you can hear everyone from further away." Audit of every Musou voice source: removed the two that belong to no body, the far battle's Ork mob yells (`MusouAmbienceKind.OrkMob` of musou/battle-ambience: `play_or_bo_*` growls, barks, roars, snorts and the `ork_boy`, `ork_boy_2`, `ork_nob` exertions, 60 to 130 m round the listener) and the armies' Waaagh! war cries (`TfwWaaaghFrame`, `WaaaghBarkPlanner`: an aggregate's shout, not a body's); the automatic Marine barks were already off since musou/hotkey-lines. Kept: the far battle's bolter, lasgun, artillery and explosion sounds, the war bed, every crowd Ork's own grunts, barks, roars, hurt, stun and death yells, the T key lines and other players' speech (all from a living or dying body). `--musou-ambient-voices` restores the two. Reach: the voice of a crowd Ork (its mouth emitter) and every player's character speech read their distance curve at 1/1.75 of the real distance (`SoundEmitter.DistanceScale` for the Orks, a new `VoiceDistanceScale` that applies to speech only for players, default 1 so Classic PvP is unchanged), the crowd's speech ranges and the emitter range (45 m) are x1.75 (`MusouVoiceRules.Reach`, `MusouSoundBudget.VoiceReach`); the voice caps and rates are unchanged, so the voice count stays bounded. `--no-musou-voice-reach` restores x1. Tests `MusouVoiceRulesTests`. Not verified: by ear in play (the factor is a provisional estimate, refine register).
**Musou: the stims' reliable use and the cleave x1.2 (branch `claude/stims-key-cleave` from main 99a2903c, 2026-11-12; Musou Mode only; `MusouSim.Version` 46 and `TfwRules.Version` 70, the lead renumbers at integration; no protocol, wire or Classic config-hash change).** The owner (2026-11-12): "Pressing the equipment use hotkeyb with stims equipped doesn't always use the stims. Ensure it's more reliably working the first time you press the button." and "Increase all melee attacks cleave distance by 20%." Stims: a scripted sweep (one-tick presses at every tick of a swing, a heavy, a charge, a reload, a switch, a jump, a roll, the jump-pack phases, with every sim gate) found no lost press edge: the client's tap latch and the sim's press edge are sound. The misses were two rules. (1) The use key is a bufferable press kept 0.3 s (9 ticks), so a press made more than 0.3 s before a swing (1 s), a charge or a recovery ends lapsed unused. (2) A hit reaction that starts before the stim's release (0.3 s into the 0.9 s use) cancels the use ("before its release nothing is spent", `Reaction.Start`) and the press is gone. In Musou Mode (`StimBoost.Reliable`) the press is now kept 15 ticks (0.5 s, the wire's most) and `Stims.WindUp` lets no reaction start before the release; Classic PvP keeps both rules (they are Classic's, not a lost edge). Not fixed: a use-key press in the very tick of another bufferable press (melee, Jump) is outranked by it (`InputBuffer.Pressed` takes one). Cleave: `TfwCombatRules.PlayerCleaveReachScale` 0.6 to 0.72 (x1.2 of the pass before), the one scale every human's cleave reads (server, contraptions, the drawn arc, the hit-sound pick): every weapon, light, heavy and charge strikes, the spear's sweep 9 to 10.8 m, the 8.8 m (10.7 m) hammer-class cleave 5.27 to 6.32 m (6.44 to 7.72 m); angles, caps and damage unchanged; AI Marines and the 5-wave run keep their reach. Tests: `MusouStimReliableTests` and the pins in `MusouBalanceTests`, `MusouSlashArcTests`, `TfwMeleeTests`, `SpearTests`.
**Librarian's zoom and the autocannon's barrel join (branch `claude/librarian-zoom-ac-barrel` from main 99a2903c, 2026-11-12; Musou Mode only; `MusouSim.Version` 46 (renumber at integration); no protocol, wire or `TfwRules.Version` change).** The owner: "Add a zoom to the librarian - he should have the same zoom as the other classes." and "The autocannon has a small gap where there should be barrel material - right where the barrel begins to protrude outwards from the main body of the gun." **Zoom, cause:** aim mode (`PlayerState.Aiming`, which the camera zooms on, protocol 12) needs a weapon in hand (`Combat.StepPlayer`: `aimDown && weapon is not null`), and the Librarian carries none (his cast keys are Fire, Grenade and Reload; Aim was free, there was no input conflict). **Fix:** a new core hook `SimConfig.AimsWithoutWeapon(classIndex)` (`ExtrasAimWithoutWeapon`, an empty partial outside Musou; true for the Librarian only) lets the Aim key put him in aim mode in the same conditions as a gunner (not in a melee swing, throw, pound or evade); the sprint rule (`SprintApplies`, the sprint-no-fire gate) follows it. The client needed nothing: its camera already falls back to the rifle's two sets for a class with no weapon, so the field of view (40 to 20), the blend time, the camera offset, the mouse speed and the aim walk are exactly the other classes' (verified: `ZOOMCAPTURE` lines, the Librarian and the Tactical both 40.0 to 20.0, the same way back). Prediction: `Aiming` is already networked (the flags bit), and the client predicts through the same `Combat` code, so server and client agree; he can cast while zoomed (Fire is unaffected). No aim pose or reticle (both need a weapon class; his cast pose is unchanged). Restore: none needed (the hook is his class only). **Barrel, cause:** W1c's map took the length out of the plain tube on both sides of the clamp, which left 2 cm of the bare neck (radius 0.067 m) between the receiver's front collar (0.085 m) and the clamp (0.093 m): it read as a dark groove, a gap, right where the barrel leaves the body (a close-up still showed it; the barrel is a rigid part of the model, the kick moves the whole gun on a bone, so the kick cannot open it). **Fix:** `AutocannonBarrel.Knots` now takes the rear tube out whole at the owner's 1.6 m muzzle (the clamp flush on the receiver; between 1.6 m and the install's 2.621 m the rear tube grows in proportion, so `--autocannon-muzzle` and `--old-autocannon-barrel` still work); the front tube between the clamp and the ribbed front keeps the 2 cm. Test aids: `--tfw-zoom-capture` (`Librarian/NetworkView.ZoomCapture.cs`) and three close-up stills in `--tfw-autocannon-capture` (`ac-close-*`). Tests: `MusouLibrarianTests` (the Aim key zooms him, Classic unchanged), `AutocannonContentTests` (the clamp flush, the in-between case). Evidence: `<media folder>\zoom-barrel\` (`before`, `after`, `librarian`, `tactical`, `compare-top.png`, `compare-zoom.png`). Open: no reticle for the zoomed Librarian (the reticle is drawn from the weapon in hand).
**Classic stims: the reliable use in every mode (branch `claude/stims-classic` from main 5b82c614, 2026-11-12; protocol 68, the lead renumbers at integration; Classic config hash changes only with the restore switch).** The owner, asked whether the Musou stim fix should apply in Classic PvP too: "Classic too". The Musou-only `StimBoost.Reliable` is now the core `SimConfig.StimReliable` (default on, in every mode and profile): the use key's press with a stim equipped is kept 15 ticks (0.5 s) instead of 9 (`InputBuffer.WindowOf`) and a hit before the stim's release starts no reaction (`Stims.WindUp` in `Reaction.CanReact`; the damage is still taken).
