Musou's behaviour is unchanged. Restore switch `--old-stim-use` (server and every client; config hash `old-stim-use`, written only when off, so no other hash moves). Tests: `StimReliableClassicTests` (new), `MusouStimReliableTests` (both modes, switch), the lossy-link stim test runs with the switch since it needs hit-cut uses; every protocol pin 67 to 68. No layout change. Spec "Stims: a reliable use", changes-from-original, `release/NEXT.md`.

**Musou: the drop pod answers (2026-11-12, branch `claude/drop-pod-answers` from main 75dc638b; Musou Mode only; `TfwRules.Version` 72 (the lead renumbers), no `MusouSim`/`Protocol` change).** The owner answered the design's questions: the touchdown deals 3x one shell's damage in 30 m (`TfwDropPodRules.CrushRadius` 30, `CrushDamageFactor` 3; a shell is flat health-or-30 per enemy, so ordinary enemies die and a boss takes 90), the 60 s cooldown (shared, none at the range), 30 s defence, one pod per player and reduced damage (a tenth, by puppet id; not invulnerable) are confirmed and recorded in spec and `docs/drop-pod-assault.md`. The customizer step and its heading are now SUPPORT ABILITIES. Each pod Marine shouts a FOR THE EMPEROR take from his own body 0.15 to 0.35 s after the one before (`TfwDropPodRules.ShoutDelay`, client `TfwPodShouts` through the loyalist bark path; the voice pack's takes: the install has no plain emperor line of this kind in the speech banks we use). Tests: `TfwDropPodTests` (30 m and 90 on a boss, 2000 Orks in one pass, the Marines' damage scale, the stagger).

**Musou: more dangerous bosses, stun windows, more bosses (branch `claude/musou-bosses-drops` from main 5b82c614, 2026-11-12; Musou Mode only; `MusouSim.Version` 48 and `TfwRules.Version` 71, to be renumbered at integration; no protocol or wire change).** The owner: "make ork warboss and bosses more dangerous. More damage but not 1 shotting the player. ... stunned for a 5s window ... every time a boss or warboss reaches 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% hp", "Make more bosses spawn", "Only elites and bosses drop power ups". **Danger:** `MusouBossRules.DangerScale` 1.5 on the Warboss (swing 90, slam 90, charge 112.5) and the Boss Orks (3x the base kind's, was 2x); `World.MusouHit` caps one boss hit at 0.75 of the target's full health plus armour (after the received-damage multipliers), so a full player never dies of one. **Stun:** `MusouSim.BossStun.cs`: `Damage` marks the shares 80, 60, 40, 20 % a boss has fallen to and, if one is new, puts it in the existing Stunned state for 5 s (150 ticks): it stands, attacks nothing, `MusouBoss` drops an ability under way, no extra damage; one stun per hit however many shares it crosses; war only. Clients already draw Stunned as the stagger clip (provisional look; Telegraph cue 60 sent, no effect yet). **More bosses:** up to 12 alive (was 8), waits halved again (first 15 to 30 s, next 22.5 to 45 s). **Drops:** already elites and bosses only; unchanged. Tests: `MusouBossDangerTests` (9) and the pinned values in `TfwBossOrkTests`, `OrkArmyAggregateTests`.

**Musou: the boss stun rolled back to melee stuns only (branch `claude/musou-boss-stun-rollback`, 2026-11-12; Musou Mode only; `MusouSim.Version` 51 and `TfwRules.Version` 76 (renumbered from 75 at integration), to be renumbered at integration; no protocol or wire change).** The owner: "roll back the boss stun change - bosses should remain unstunnable in any form", "they should be susceptible to melee attack stuns though". The 80/60/40/20 % stun windows (and Telegraph cue 60, `BossHurt`, the marks) are gone; `DangerScale`, the one-hit cap, the 12 Boss Orks and the drop rule stay. Bosses stay immune to every non-melee stagger (`Stagger`/`KnockDown` false for them: grenades, blasts, demolition charges, plasma, artillery, the drop pod, the Librarian's powers). New `MusouSim.StaggerMelee` (`MusouSim.BossStun.cs`) is called by the three melee paths in `World.MusouCombat.cs`: the heavy cleave (heavy swing, stun/stagger steps, so the spear's and the claw's heavy sweeps and the hammer's heavy strike), each enemy a charge touches, and a stomp's ground pound blast. It stuns a Warboss or Boss Ork for the stagger's 0.6 s (no knockback, Stunned state, `MusouBoss` drops its ability); ordinary Orks stagger as before. Reading of the owner's words: "melee attack stuns" = the melee strikes that carry a stun, not every hit (a light step does nothing). **Stun-lock figure:** no immunity window was added (the owner decides); a strike every 12 or 18 ticks (0.4 to 0.6 s) held a Warboss the whole 30 s measured, one every 19 ticks leaves it one free tick in each 19. Tests: `MusouBossDangerTests` (10), `MusouCombatTests` (+6).

**Lightning claw gauntlet (branch `claude/claw-gauntlet`, 2026-11-12; client only, Musou Mode only; no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner: the claw is part of the hand, blades out of the gauntlet, never held, and the old model "is not good enough" (references: three private pictures). The claw's item is now drawn on `RIG_R_Hand` with no offset (`ClawGauntlet.OnHand`; before, the power sword's grip mount on `RIG_Prop_RHand`), its model built in code in the hand bone's own space from the rig's rest pose (`ClawHandFrame`): an arched dark armour shell, side guards, knuckle bar, four brass sockets with coiled pistons, a vented dome in a brass ring, four long curved tapering steel blades (0.62 m from the knuckle line, flat and spread like fingers, ours), the blue power field re-anchored along them. One claw (right hand), so nothing to mirror. Restore: `--old-claw-model`. New test aid `--tfw-claw-capture` (stills and a clip in the open on Ashfall, game camera, orbit and hand-riding views). Checked in captures against the references; not playtested. Open: the stage's stand-in is unchanged, the fingers keep the sword's grip pose.

**Lightning claw power field and worn metals (branch `claude/claw-power-field`, 2026-11-12; client only, Musou Mode only; no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules-version change).** The owner approved the gauntlet model and asked for a strong blue glow with live electrical arcs like his power sword reference, and for wear and texture so the housing reads as the marine's own gauntlet. The blades now glow always (HDR emission, brushed steel with nicks) with a view-facing additive halo; 15 vertex-shader arcs per claw crawl along the blades, jump between them and spit off their edges, re-drawn every few frames (no CPU, no allocation; level of detail by distance; `--no-claw-arcs`); a faint conduit crackle loop plays under near claws. Brass and steel are procedural worn metal; the housing plates copy the wearer's right-gauntlet armour material (UV window, same paint colours). Details: docs/claw-spear-animations.md 6b. Checked in real Musou captures; not playtested; the sound is to check by ear.
**Musou: no aerial tackle, a light attack at any point in a hop (branch `claude/musou-no-aerial-tackle` from main 1211a64c, 2026-11-12; Musou Mode only, temporary; `MusouSim.Version` 49 and `TfwRules.Version` 74, to be renumbered at integration; no `Protocol` change).** The owner: "Temporarily disable the Arial/flying tackle move for all assault and raptor marines in musou mode only. You should be able to start a melee light attack at any point in a hop without delay or cooldown. The arial tackle/flying tackle should never trigger in Musou mode - only light melee attacks." The tackle is the jump-pack dash attack (`Rush.CanDashAttack`: a melee press 0.333 s into a hop starts the lunge); an earlier press cancelled the hop into a swing and `MeleeCancel` held the next swing until the cancelled clip would have ended. New `SimConfig.AerialTackleOff` (core file `AerialTackle.cs`, hook `ExtrasAerialTackleOff`, true only under Musou unless restored) makes `CanDashAttack` false and gives the hop cancel no wait, so a melee press at any tick of a hop (landing part included) starts a light attack in that tick; in the air it keeps the hop cancel's behaviour (rise stopped, 0.4 of the horizontal speed carried; ours). Prediction is the same step on both sides; the pad's Y-as-tackle remap needs the window, so it never applies. Restore switch `--musou-aerial-tackle` (server and every client; `SimConfig.AerialTackleRestored`, hashed only when on). Classic PvP unchanged. Tests: `MusouNoAerialTackleTests` (every hop tick, Classic tackle intact, restore). Spec "Musou Mode: no aerial tackle, a light attack at any point in a hop (temporary)".
Charge responsive: a charge after a swing, an instant S cancel (branch `claude/charge-responsive` from main 1211a64c, 2026-11-12; every mode; protocol 69, to be renumbered at integration). The owner: "You should immediately be able to charge after a melee attack, or vice versa" (Assault and Raptor) and "The charge should be cancelled instantaneously as soon as the S key or back on left joystick is triggered" (Tactical and Assault/Raptor). **Cause 1:** `Rush.CanStart` refused any body with a melee attack under way, so a Shift + W + F press during a light attack, a combo or a heavy strike was left unused and the input buffer (0.3 s) replayed it only after the whole clip; the melee wait, the 1 s spacing and the jump-pack ground rule were not the blocker. **Fix:** `ChargeCancel.CanChargeFromMelee` (the attack's hit has landed) lets `Combat.StepPlayerCore` end the attack, its queued next attack and its melee wait and start the charge in that tick; the melee wait is also cleared whenever a charge starts, so a swing follows a charge or an S cancel at once (a melee press cancelling a charge keeps its own cancel wait). Heavy strikes count too. **Cause 2:** `Rush.Begin` ended the rush on the stick only from its `BRANCH_Attack2Idle` time (0.467 s). **Fix:** with `ChargeInstantCancel` S (S, S + A, S + D; a pad's stick back in the back three of eight sectors and at least 0.5 of full length, `ChargeCancel.InstantBackStick`) ends the bull rush on any tick after the start (S cannot be held at the start: the start needs W); the speed it carries is capped at the sprint's (`Rush.Landed`). The dash attack's lunge, which no input ends, is unchanged; bots never charge. Restore switches (config hash, server and clients): `--old-charge-after-melee`, `--old-charge-cancel-delay`. Tests: `ChargeResponsiveTests` (24: first legal tick, heavy, queued combo, refused cases, buffer, swing after charge, S at ticks 1 to 29, sticks, held S, switches, hash, world, prediction 2 seeds); older tests whose rules moved now use the switches (`ChargeCancelTests`, `ChargeDirectionsTests`, `MeleeCharge2Tests`, `ChargeClashTests`).


Charge melee chain: melee cancels a charge at once, charge > melee > charge chains, Musou melee spam (branch `claude/charge-melee-chain` from `claude/charge-responsive`, 2026-11-12; protocol 70 and `MusouSim.Version` 49, to be renumbered at integration). The owner: a light melee press mid charge (or on its last tick) happens immediately, no charge during a charge, charge > melee > charge > melee endlessly with no delay, the 1 s spacing only for discrete combat moves, and in Musou Mode melee spammed with no cooldown. A light press now ends the bull rush on that tick for every class (`ChargeCancel.MeleeEndsCharge`; the Devastator and Havoc too) and the swing starts at once without protocol 54's wait; any melee attack start lifts `RushLock` (charge, S cancel, charge within 1 s with nothing between stays spaced); Musou (hook `ExtrasMeleeSpam`) restarts a swing the tick its hit lands and queues an earlier press for that tick, with no wait after cancels. Also fixed the base's failing tests: the stomp is left out of `CanChargeFromMelee` (it stays uninterruptible but for the hop), and the SolidBodies charge script no longer sends a back-off while charging (its S input was now the instant cancel). Goldens: the faithful and extended replay hash moved together; protocol pins 70; MeleeCancelTests pin the protocol 54 wait under `--old-charge-melee-chain`. Restore switches `--old-charge-melee-chain`, `--musou-melee-cooldown`. Tests: `ChargeMeleeChainTests`.
**Musou HUD corners (branch `claude/musou-hud-corners` from main 051f7301, 2026-11-12; client only, Musou Mode only; no protocol, wire, rules or config-hash change).** The owner: "For Musou mode only move this marked with red marker weapon and grenade/equipment hud to the bottom right corner of the screen. Match the same margins to the edge as the recent change to the health and armor bar to the bottom left. They should match in distance from the edges of the screen in their respective corners. Also rework the ability cooldown icons to fit perfectly uniformly to the left side of the grenade/equipment HUD. They should match in visual aesthetic and style as well." and "Scale up the health and armor HUD in musou mode only by 10%." **Margin:** one constant, `MusouHudLayout.CornerMargin` 44 (1080-high virtual units: the distance from the screen's edge to the outermost visible pixel). Measured before the change (1920 x 1080 windowed shots, 1 unit = 1 px): the own bar 44 from the left and 43 from the bottom (its box 34 and 40), the weapon panel's gold frame 115 from the right and 66 from the bottom. After: bar 44 / 44, panel 44 / 44 at 1920 x 1080 and 2560 x 1080 (the bar's box is anchored at its corner, so the larger scale keeps the margin: `VitalsScale` 0.715 = 0.65 x 1.1, the box's left 33 and bottom 40.7), 42 / 42 at 1280 x 1024 (44 x 1024 / 1080, both corners alike). **Panel:** a new core field `Hud.Frame.WeaponBoxCorner` (Musou sets it each frame; null in Classic PvP, where the code path is untouched: a Classic shot has the panel at 115 right as before) shifts the whole weapon box (the movie's, or the M44 box when a class has no gun) by its original margins minus the target (71 right, 22 down; `Hud.MovieBoxMargin` measured, `Hud.ClassicBoxMargin` computed from the box's size and 2.5 degree turn); the jump pack meter and the "no grenades" line, which hung under the panel, stand over its winged skull instead (they would leave the screen); the KO chain's right edge is flush with the panel's and clears the meter; the Librarian's box (`LibrarianHud`) moves the same way. **Cells:** `MusouHud.Cells.cs`: the support call (B: the artillery strike or the drop pod, the loadout's choice, the shared 60 s cooldown from the war's own view) and the Librarian's Shockwave (and the restore switch's Pull) as cells of the equipment column's size (85 x 147 in the movie box's frame, the Librarian's 80 x 122), 10 (his 6) apart like the column and the weapon box, in the box's tilted frame so their bottoms stand on its line (`MusouHudLayout.CellFrame`): the dark chamfered panel with the thin gold line (dim while cooling, as the column's at no grenades), the key top left, a drawn glyph (target ring, falling pod, spreading rings, drawn-in arrows), the seconds in the weapon box's large thin white digits or READY, the name, and a white bar along the bottom that fills as the cooldown runs out; LOCKED in red for the Librarian's overload. On a narrow screen (4:3) the bottom strip's prompts and the weapon-drop prompt shift left to stay 16 units clear of the cells (`MusouHudLayout.PromptShift`). The boss column and the buff chips follow the bar's new scale. `--musou-old-hud-layout` restores everything above (bar 0.65 at its old margins, panel in the match HUD's place, the Librarian's own cell, no cells). **Evidence:** windowed shots of a Musou battle on Ashfall's landing ground (open, no wall) at 1920 x 1080, 2560 x 1080, 1280 x 1024, 1920 x 1200, 1024 x 768 and 1280 x 720 after, before (the switch) at three of them, the Librarian, and a Classic shot: `<media folder>\musou-hud\`. Not verified: by the owner's eye; the glyphs and the cell text are first drafts; five buff chips with a Librarian at 4:3 can touch the cells (rare).

**Musou HUD cells, second pass (branch `claude/musou-hud-cells` from `claude/musou-hud-corners`, 2026-11-12; client only, Musou Mode only; no protocol, wire, rules or config-hash change).** The owner: remove the unnecessary text from the cooldown cells, draw the artillery icon to match his black explosion-burst reference exactly, make a drop pod icon from his top-down pod reference in the same style, space everything evenly and centred, and put the cooldown bars beneath and outside the cells. **Text:** the key letter (B, RELOAD, GRENADE) and the names (STRIKE, DROP POD, SHOCKWAVE, PULL) are gone; a cell shows its icon and the seconds left, READY or LOCKED. The key letter went too (the owner called labels unnecessary; B is the support key the war's prompts name). **Icons** (`MusouHud.CellIcons.cs`): original polygons traced by hand, nothing of the pictures embedded; the burst is a zig-zag ribbon (the tall central spike, side spikes, open bottom) plus four shards, fitted against the reference by an overlay until the silhouettes agreed; the pod is the tapering hull with three fins and slits, a centre seam, shoulder seams and a chevron cut in the panel's black; the Shockwave (core, ring, four outer arcs) and the Pull (two arrows drawn in to a bar) in the same solid style. Each is one triangulated mesh built once on first draw (`Geometry2D.TriangulatePolygon`, `DrawMesh`) with a thin antialiased outline; no per-frame allocation. **Layout:** icon (50 high) and number band (24) are spaced with three equal gaps in the cell, centred on its axis; measured on 1920 x 1080 shots: icon centre 0 to -1 px and text centre 0 to +1 px off the frame's mid line, gaps about 18 / 19 / 20 px (the cell is tilted 2.5 degrees with the weapon box). The bar (7 high, 6 under the cell, the cell's width) sits outside the cell; the cells are the column's size minus that 13-unit block (85 x 134, the Librarian's 80 x 109), so cell plus bar fill the column's footprint, the bars' bottoms stand at the column's bottom and the 44-unit corner margin is not crossed (the box's own frame is lower). Shots (open ground on Ashfall, 1920 x 1080 and 2560 x 1080, artillery, drop pod, Librarian, the Pull via `SM_LIBRARIAN_OLD=pull`) and a references-vs-cells sheet: `<media folder>\musou-hud\cells-v2\`. Checks: both builds 0 errors; PublicTextGuardTests and ExtrasBoundaryTests passed. Not verified: the owner's eye on the icons; the pod's panel lines are a first draft.
**Spear authored-animation pilot (claude/spear-authored-pilot, 2026-11-12; Musou Mode only, presentation only; label: ours, a pilot not approved by the owner).** The owner's direction (2026-11-12): original keyframe authoring in Blender with Python-assisted authoring and IK, proved through one representative hew before the set; no motion capture, no video-to-motion; reference footage for study only. **Hew 1** (the swing every string starts with) is authored by `tools/blender/spear_hew_author.py` (Blender 4.5.15, `-b`): the marine's rig and the hammer idle's rest pose come from the install through `smtool spear-rig-dump` into a private folder (never committed), the controls are Blender F-curves (hips, spine, head, clavicles, feet, the right palm and the shaft in the chest frame), solved with the overlay's own arithmetic plus a two-bone arm solve (elbow swivel kept off the shaft) and the overlay's leg solve, sampled at 60 Hz (exact keys at the apex and the hit) and exported as `src/SmContent/Extras/Musou/Authored/spear_hew1.json` (format `sm-spear-authored-clip/1`: units, axes, rest pose, bone map, sample rate, timing; the same JSON regenerates byte for byte). `AuthoredPoseClip` (SmContent) turns it into the existing `WeaponPoseClip` (the channels already carried every authored motion, so no extension) and refuses data that moves the hit, the length or the base stance; `ClawSpearClips.SpearHew1` is the authored clip, `SpearHew1Original` pass 3's, and **`--old-spear-hew`** (or `SM_OLD_SPEAR_HEW=1`) is the rollback. The hew: a compact coil to the apex 0.19 s before the hit, the hips' yaw accelerating into the hit (rate 0 at the apex, about twice the average at the hit), the weight shifted a beat ahead of the turn and the left foot planted by 0.64 s, the finish held 0.95 to 1.18 s (the hips move under 4 degrees), then the approved recovery; hit 0.711 s and the combo opening 1.098 s unchanged. Carried over from pass 3 and named (docs/spear-authored-pilot.md section 3): the swing's palm and shaft geometry between 0.50 and 0.80 s (the palm held 0.12 m further right around 0.65 s) and the recovery's arm aims from 0.95 s; the key poses at the hit, the follow-through and the settle therefore look almost as before, and the difference is the wind-up, the acceleration and the hold. Tests (filtered runs): `SpearAuthoredHewTests` (adapter identity, timing, refusal, determinism, the compact apex, acceleration and brief hold, the export's stated units; with the install the in-game overlay's joints against Blender's at the same times, worst 0.2 cm), `SpearClearanceTests`, `ClawSpearClipsTests` (its snap test learned the sampled clip), `FootPinTests`, `SpearTests`. `--tfw-spear-film` films the light chain in a real match (the recording is cut by the frames' own wall-clock and clip times because the real-time sim and a fixed-rate recording differ); evidence under `<media folder>\spear-pilot\`. The remaining hews, the stun, the stab, the dive and the landings are not re-authored. Docs: docs/spear-authored-pilot.md, docs/claw-spear-animations.md section 3g, docs/commands.md.

**Spear pass 2 (claude/spear-pass-2 from claude/spear-authored-pilot, 2026-11-12; Musou Mode only, presentation only; label: ours, not approved).** The owner's reference image of a hip carry, "blade forward", "concise and powerful" attacks from halberd manuals. Standing carry: hips squared (`WeaponPoseClip.SquareYaw`, faded by the fist weight; overlay and test mirror), arm hanging beside the hip, blade forward and up (`SpearHold.Pass2Carry*`, `Place(..., moving)` eases to the old lean while moving), `CarryDrop`; running keeps the chest carry because no hip-level fist passes the clearance and column gates (about 150 combinations measured, docs/claw-spear-animations.md section 3h). Hews 1 to 3, the F snap cut and the F,F stab are re-authored by `tools/blender/spear_pass2_author.py` (carry-based starts, short coil, hip-progress acceleration law to the hit, brief finish, ordered recovery; palm geometry carried over and named); timings unchanged. Rollback `--old-spear-pass2`. Tests: new `SpearPass2Tests`; pilot and `ClawSpearClipsTests` pins moved to the old carry objects; in-game versus Blender joints worst 0.2 cm. Open: two hand-over frames of `SpearClearanceTests` (carry to hew 3 -0.027 m, hew 1 to hew 3 -0.12 m). Evidence (stage only) under `<media folder>\spear-pass2\`.

**Spear pass 3 (claude/spear-pass-3 from claude/spear-pass-2, 2026-11-12; Musou Mode only, presentation only; label: ours, not approved).** The owner after pass 2: clipping may be momentary, hold the spear parallel to the spine while idle and running, one-handed in the right hand at the side like the marines' one-handed weapon, the hand connected to the arm; the hews stay. One carry for idle, walk, run and sprint (`ClawSpearClips.SpearRestPass3`): the shaft's fore-and-aft lean is the spine's (`SpearHold.Place(..., spine)`, read from the pose: waist to the middle of the shoulders), blade up, butt low (grip 0.95 m, butt at least 0.097 m up); a fixed 13 degree side lean in toward his centre line (`SpearHold.Pass3CarryRoll`) is the one deliberate departure from strictly parallel, because a parallel shaft puts the blade across the crosshair column the owner ruled out (the lead kept that gate); the right grip socket is solved onto a point beside the right hip every frame (`FistTarget` from the pelvis, `FistAlways`, `FistFromPelvis`), the left arm hangs and swings freely, both swing against the stride (`FistSwing`, `LeftFistSwing`); the hand-overs to pass 2's strokes are the existing 0.14 s fade (strokes untouched). `SpearClearanceTests` now reports clipping (gross error only: more than 0.15 m deep for over half of a clip); new `SpearPass3Tests` (switch, placement, shaft parallel to the spine over all twenty hammer stance clips, hand at the hip, arm bone lengths unchanged by the carry, swing); mirror and client overlays in step. Rollback `--old-spear-pass3`. Aids: stage `--clip carry[:stance] --dist`, match `--tfw-spear-carry-film`. **Spear pass 4 (claude/spear-pass-4 from claude/spear-pass-3, 2026-11-12; Musou Mode only, presentation only; label: ours, not approved).** The owner after pass 3's match clips: the hands misbehave when running, the idle's left hand should be the bolt pistol idle's, the right hand should grip naturally, the swings need reworking, keep the 13 degree tilt. The carry's left arm is the install's bolt pistol relaxed idle (`SM_NAV_IdleL_CS_01`: spine, left clavicle, arm and fingers laid at run time under the keys while he stands, `WeaponPoseClip.PistolArmFrom`, `CharacterViewer.LayPistolArm`), going over to a runner's bent-elbow pump with the speed (left fist solve with the speed only, 0.30 m swing per metre of foot split, the hand rising as it comes forward; the right fist's swing 0.06 with a 3 cm rise); every spear clip closes the right hand's fingers round the shaft (`LayGripFingers`, authored curl about the finger bones' local Z); the three hews, the snap cut and the stab are re-authored over pass 2's pipeline (`tools/blender/spear_pass4_author.py`, `Authored/spear_*_p4.json`: the coil's apex 0.03 s nearer the hit, a higher-power acceleration, the hips carried 6 to 10 degrees past the finish and settled), every timing the strike's. **Spear pass 4b (claude/spear-pass-4b from claude/spear-pass-4, 2026-11-12; Musou Mode only, presentation only; label: ours, not approved).** The owner's bar after pass 4: a full pass, no jank, the right hand gripping the spear naturally, the left hand matching the pistol idle, reworked swings, the 13 degree tilt kept. The grip is fitted to the shaft (`CharacterViewer.GripFit.cs`: the rig's grip sockets moved to the fist's grip point, the carry's wrist laid so the shaft crosses the palm diagonally with the arm solved for that hand, each finger group curled until its joints sit a finger's thickness off the 2.1 cm shaft, the thumb searched onto the shaft's far side; the rig's thumb is too short to wrap, stated); the left hand is brought onto the shaft while it takes it (hew 1's 6 cm gap closed to 1 cm); the left arm's elbow hint, which lay along the hanging arm's own line and flipped the forearm in single frames (100 to 500 rad/s found by a new numeric pop probe, `SM_POP_PROBE`), has its own hint; the carry leans the torso 8 degrees forward (the shaft stays parallel to the spine); the five strokes get a second iteration in `tools/blender/spear_pass4b_author.py` (`Authored/spear_*_p4b.json`: a still more compact coil, a higher-power acceleration, a deeper carry-through; every timing the strike's). **Customizer weapons: the added weapons in the 3D viewer, checked (branch `claude/customizer-new-weapons` from `integration/merge-2026-11-12g`, 2026-11-12; client test aids only, presentation only; no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules change; no rendering change).** The owner (2026-11-12): "Ensure the new weapons appear in the 3d player model viewer when using the loadout Customizer". Finding: they already do, through the match's own code. The preview's `ConfigureWeapons` hands the chosen wargear to a `WeaponRig` whose `Content` is the page's profile (`PreviewStage`, set on every call), so `ExtrasWeaponModel` (the `Arsenal` dispatcher) builds each item exactly as a match does: the claw gauntlet on the right hand bone (`ClawGauntlet`, housing, four blades, the always-on power-field glow and arcs), the spear in its carry on the power sword's hand bone, the autocannon (`turret_aa`, shortened barrel, the heavy bolter's stow, its backpack through `ExtrasWornAs`). Looked at in windowed shots (Musou Assault with each melee, Musou Devastator with the autocannon, front and from behind; Classic extended Devastator and Havoc with the autocannon; Classic faithful unchanged): `<media folder>\customizer-weapons\after\`. The viewer's relaxed bolt-pistol pose (owner 2026-10-29) holds the pistol and stows a primary, so the autocannon is slung across the back with its muzzle past the right hip (the heavy bolter's stow looks the same from behind); the claw and spear are in the hand. Switching: each choice rebuilds the rig's nodes (queued free, shared meshes and materials), so 18 choices of claw, spear and chainsword left the node count at 359 and the orphans at 2, and 12 autocannon, heavy bolter and lascannon choices in Classic extended likewise (resources constant). **Test aids** (docs/commands.md): `--demo-primary`, `--preview-weapon-cycle` and `--preview-weapon-rounds` (chooses the items on the open slot as the rows do, then logs whether the rig carries each and draws nodes for it, with Godot object, node and orphan counts), `--preview-yaw`, `--preview-zoom` (`PreviewStage.ViewFrom`); two new pinned hooks (`ExtrasPreviewScript`, `ExtrasScreenshotHold` in `FrontEndView`; `ExtrasBoundaryTests`), implemented in `client/Extras/Musou/Customizer/FrontEndView.WeaponCycle.cs`. Not done: the in-match Esc picker (same code, not looked at); the Havoc shot from behind (`--preview-yaw` is reset by the side switch).

**Customizer weapons, second step: added weapons drawn in the viewer's ready stance (same branch, 2026-11-12; client presentation only).** The owner could not see the new weapons (the relaxed pistol idle stows a primary). While the primary or melee on show is an added one the page carries (`ArsenalRules.Shown`), `PreviewStage` plays the match's standing idle (`RigProfile.Clips.IdleCandidates`, no new clip) instead of the pistol idle, so `HoldsPistol` turns false and the autocannon is held across the body (the heavy bolter's ready mount); the claw and spear are shown in that stance, from the same three-quarter side. New pinned hook `ExtrasReadyPose` (`client/Extras/Musou/Arsenal/PreviewStage.Arsenal.cs`). Original weapons and the faithful pages are unchanged (the key carries the ready flag; a switch back replays the relaxed idle). Stills: `<media folder>\customizer-weapons\after2\`.

**Drop pod assault: five Marines, retreat to the Imperial base (branch claude/droppod-five-imperial-retreat, 2026-11-12; `TfwRules.Version` 75; Classic PvP and the protocol unchanged).** Owner: "5 instead of 4, and retreat to the imperial base not the ork stronghold." `TfwDropPodRules.Marines` 4 -> 5 (a fifth name; the 5 m door ring spaces five 6.3 m apart; the 12 puppet ids still fit one squad with 4 humans). Cause of the wrong retreat: `TfwLayout.Hq` is the Ork commander's stronghold (the battle's `CommanderObjective`), not the Marines' base; `TfwPodHome` now returns `Layout.LandingZone` (the Marines' own base; the Range's start at the range). Tests, spec rows and `docs/drop-pod-assault.md` updated.

**Musou Mode: melee heal capped at 3 per swing (branch claude/musou-melee-heal-cap, 2026-11-12; `MusouSim.Version` 52, `TfwRules.Version` 77; Classic PvP and the protocol unchanged).** Owner: "limit the healing of melee attacks in musou mode - cap it at 3 instances of healing per 1 melee swing." One swing is one strike step by one attacker, which resolves in one tick: its stomp blast and its cleave together (the existing once-per-enemy-per-tick set already treated them as one attack), or a spear impale. `World.MusouMeleeHeal` counts the heals given to an attacker this tick (`_musouHealCount`, reset with `_musouHealed`) and gives none past `MusouCombatRules.MeleeHealsPerSwing` (3), to the first three struck (no ordering claim: the stomp heals in the blast's query order, the cleave nearest first). Capped: the light and heavy cleave, the heavy's ground-pound stomp, the spear's sweeps (a cleave), the spear impale (one enemy, so at most one). Not changed: the air slash's landing (one heal per landing, no enemy count), the charge contact (never healed), grenades and other non-melee sources; no perk or Librarian rule heals per melee hit. AI Marines share the path, so they are capped too. Restore switch `--musou-uncapped-melee-heal` (server and every client; config hash, only when on). The skirmish pin golden was recaptured (its swings strike more than three). Tests in `MusouCombatTests` (ten Orks: three heals; two swings: three each; stomp plus cleave: three in all; switch and hash).
**Ork swings commit to a direction (branch `claude/musou-ork-swing-commit`, 2026-11-12; `MusouSim.Version` 53, `TfwRules.Version` 78, to be renumbered at integration; Musou Mode only, Classic PvP, the 5-wave run and the protocol unchanged).** Owner: "Make Ork attacks commit to a direction ... bounded early tracking followed by a committed swing, so positioning and dodging feel more trustworthy." Finding confirmed: `MusouSim.Ai.cs` `Behave`, the `WindUp` case, called `Face(i, toward)` every tick up to the contact check, which then read that same facing, so the 60 degree cone could never fail; a player circling an Ork at 2 to 8 m/s at 1.2 m was hit every time, 0 to 5 degrees off. Now `MusouSim.Swing.cs`: the first 30 % of the wind-up (4 of a Boy's 15 ticks) turns toward the target at 540 degrees a second, then the facing is locked; the blow needs reach and the cone of the locked facing. Measured (`MusouSwingCommitTests`): a Boy circled at 1.2 m from the wind-up's start is still hit at 3 m/s (walk, 41 degrees off) and dodged from 4.5 m/s (run 5, 69 degrees off); a still target is hit; Gretchin, Nobs and Boss Boyz dodged at 9 m/s; the Warboss's swing (5.4 m reach) is only dodged by stepping out of reach (27 degrees off at 6 m/s round 4.8 m), his slam and charge are untouched. The wire's yaw byte already carries the facing, so the client draws the locked direction. Restore switch `--musou-ork-swing-tracking` (`SimConfig.MusouOrkSwingTracking`, hashed only when on; server and client args). Values are estimates in the refine register: check the share and the cone in play.
**Musou own bolter: the original shot only (branch claude/musou-own-layer-samples, 2026-11-13; client only, no protocol, rules or hash change).** The owner listened to four recordings of the same crowded fight (A lighter layers, B as before, C no thump, D the original shot only) and chose D: "i want d original bolter sound for now". The own rifle no longer posts the deep copy, sub copy or thump (`MusouFireLayers`); others' lighter layers are unchanged. `--musou-own-layers` restores the old gains; `--musou-own-layer-db thump,deep,sub` (the sample aid) sets them. Spec row "Deeper fire" and docs/commands.md updated.

**Musou soundscape tuning (musou/soundscape-tuning, owner interview 2026-11-12; client only, Musou Mode only; no sim, wire, protocol or hash change; branch `claude/musou-soundscape-tuning-bc6747`).** Six changes, each with a restore switch (`--musou-sound-off clipguard,threat,softduck,bgduck,bed,waaagh`, or `soundscape` for all six). (1) Clip guard: Master's hard limiter sat before Master's +0.83 dB boost, so its -0.3 dB ceiling left peaks at +0.53 dBFS at full volume; in Musou Mode the ceiling is -1.13 dB with a soft limiter ahead of it. Measured in a 60 s crowded scripted fight (meters at the limiter input): before, peaks to +1.6 dBFS, limiter acting in 15 of 203 half-second windows, output +0.53 dBFS; after, peaks -1.2 dBFS, 0 of 215 windows, output -0.37 dBFS (same with the Orks' voices +14 dB: +2.0 and 38 of 214, then -1.2 and 0 of 206). The recorded WAV itself never reached full scale (the test master volume is low, peak -10 dBFS), so no clipped-sample count is available. (2) Threat cues: boss attacks (roar, wind-up, slam, charge, hits), a Nob's swing, a melee Ork winding up at the player from outside the view, a rokkit aimed at the player (launcher fire and the incoming whine), a Big Shoota's burst at the player, a lit Bomb Squig near the player play +3 dB on their own emitter outside the crowd's group: never stolen, cut, ducked or instance-limited (`SoundEmitter.Threat`), at most 6 a second. Existing sounds only; missing: the Big Shoota has no spin-up sound, so his burst plays his gun's ready cue; a lit Squig's beeps are the generated placeholder tone, lifted +3 dB. In the run 55 threat posts (Nob swings). Not exercised in the run: bosses, rokkits, Squigs, Big Shoota (no human test; the rules are unit-tested). (3) Explosion duck: only blasts within 12 m cut, at half depth and half time (-6 dB and low-pass 60 for 1.5 s become -3 dB, low-pass 30, 0.75 s); in the run 8 duck actions against 40 before (the far battle's explosions no longer duck at all). (4) The far battle and war bed duck 4 dB while an Ork engages the player (0.4 s in, 1 s hold, 2.5 s out). (5) The armies' Waaagh! is on by default; the far mob's yells stay off. (6) A quiet bed in a battle: the install's `play_world_fire_03` (2 emitters, +0 dB) and `play_wind_open` (flat, -12 dB; the wind sound is in the campaign's region bank `rgn_onthetrail_r100_player_01`, a singleplayer-content dependency, loaded when a battle starts; no wind exists in the multiplayer banks). A first bed at +14 dB was far too loud (+4.6 LU); the bed alone now adds under 1 LU (-21.2 LUFS against -21.5 and -22.9 for two baseline runs). Loudness of the whole minute: before -21.5 and -22.9 LUFS (run spread about 1.5), after -18.7: louder mainly from the milder explosion cut and the +3 dB cues; the owner's "levels stay" is held for the crowd, the bolter layers and the boosts. Not done: positioning the bed toward the map's fires (no cheap fire list). Test aid `--tfw-sound-capture-long`. Clips (AAC in MP4) and numbers: the media folder's `sound/soundscape/`. Not heard by a human.
**Classic soundscape: hearing the other players (branch claude/classic-soundscape-tuning, 2026-11-13; client only: no simulation, wire, protocol or hash change; Musou Mode unchanged).** Owner's interview: "its difficult to hear other player's footsteps and actions (charges, rolls, assault marine/raptor jumps and hops) around the player's vicinity and the map as a whole." `SmContent/ClassicSoundscape.cs` (engine-free, `ClassicSoundscapeTests`): a post of another player's sound carries a `ScapeClass` on its `VoiceOffset` (by the post's kind: `NetworkView.Sound.Soundscape.cs`, `PostBinding`, `Bark`); `SoundSystem.MixOf` raises it to the class's target over its own level at 0 m: movement (steps, rolls, charges, landings, grunts, barks) to 50 m with a 0.3 dB/m fall-off and a low-pass cap, gone by about 65 m; reloads to 20 m; weapons fire, explosions, take-offs, dashes and pounds keep a faint whole-map floor; the -3 dB on others' steps is gone (own steps as now); others' movement posts are protected from stealing, other sources' instance limits and pool drops (at most 20 hold voices, so 15 others cannot starve the pool of 48); others' ground rolls post the install's `play_evade_start`; direction is clearer (panning strength 1.8, a darker sound from behind), `--sound-natural-position` restores Godot's softer positioning, `--old-classic-mix` the whole old mix; `--record-mix <wav>` records the Classic mix; `smtool audio-mix --scape` prints the new levels. Before/after levels in spec "Classic soundscape"; the numbers are ours (refine register). Not done: a per-voice reverb send and HRTF (Godot offers neither cheaply). Evidence: two 70 s headless listener recordings on Manufactorum against 3 Marine and 4 Chaos bots (a different scene each time: the bots are not scripted), `--old-classic-mix` / new, converted to AAC MP4 in the owner's media folder (`sound`): old -16.4 LUFS, peak +0.7 dBFS before the file's limiter; new -15.5 LUFS, peak +0.5 dBFS (Master's limiter holds both at its ceiling).
**The autocannon's dust and chunks (branch `claude/musou-autocannon-dust-debris`, 2026-11-12; client presentation only, Musou Mode only; no sim, wire, protocol or config-hash change).** The owner: "make it or the aoe explosion it causes on hit kick up 50% less dust ... chunks of debris similar to the ground pound effect should fly out". New `FxEffect.DustShare` (default 1): below 1 each particle of a spray that throws alpha sprites is kept by a seeded roll (`FxAmount.Kept`, CPU and GPU spray paths agree) and each alpha sprite outside a spray has its alpha scaled; the autocannon's hit (`autocannon_dmg`, through the pinned hook `ExtrasImpactDustShare`) draw 0.5 and its 2.5 m blast (`FxDetonation`'s new `dustShare`, from `TfwBoltBlastFrame`) 0 (owner 2026-11-13: "remove the dust from the autocannon aoe blast ... retain the on hit explosion flash"; a dropped particle loses only its alpha sprites, its additive flash and fire stay), every other effect 1. The no-smoke rule already removes the smoke and dust cards, so the halved sprites are the debris sprays and beams that read as dust. Each drawn blast also throws 5 to 9 `GroundShards` chunks (scaled by radius, 0.55 of the pound's speeds, 0.7 sizes, 0.6 spread; its own node, 36 live, 2 blasts a frame, 45 m; ours). `--musou-old-autocannon-fx` restores (in `LeanBot.PresentationAids`). Classic PvP's autocannon is unchanged (the hook and blast path act in Musou only). Spec "Autocannon: dust of the hit and the blast", "blast debris chunks". Clips: the media folder's `autocannon`.
**Musou Ork hit reactions, back (branch claude/musou-ork-hit-reactions, 2026-11-13; client drawing only, Musou Mode only; no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules change).** The owner, from his reference preview: add the hit reactions back to Orks, identical to the reference, translated onto our Ork animations (the 2026-11-06 stagger flinch read as a 180-degree turn and was removed). `MusouOrkFlinchRules` (SmNet): the envelope measured from the reference (rise 40 ms, hold 40 ms, fall 270 ms, over at 350 ms), the owner's strength table (shots 1 / 1.3 / 1.5 / 1.8, melee 1.3 / 2 / 2.5 with hammers and axes a step up, blasts 2.5 fading to 1), the size scaling (rank and file 1, 'Ard Boyz 0.7, Nobs 0.5, Boss Orks 0.2, Warboss 0.12) and `MusouOrkFlinchTrack` (a re-kick goes to the same size: no growth). Near (skeletal) Orks: `MusouOrkFlinchPose` lays the flinch over the sampled clip (spine, neck, head tipped back, pelvis back and down, two-bone IK keeps the feet planted), never the facing or the path. Far (baked) Orks lean and jolt as whole instances (`CrowdView.AddFar`); none past 70 m. Hit events give attacker, enemy and marker (the direction is the Ork away from the attacker; the strength the attacker's weapon in hand); blasts come from the detonations the view already plays (`NetworkView.MusouOrkFlinch.cs`). Switch `--no-musou-ork-flinch`; aids `--log-musou-flinch` and `--musou-crowd-test --flinch ...`. Spec "Musou Ork hit reactions", changes-from-original row, refine register. Not on the wire (approximated): the weapon of another player is the one the snapshot shows in hand, the heavy and charge flags of a melee blow are the attacker's current ones, and blasts the view does not play as detonations read as shots.

**Musou Ork hit reactions, twice the magnitude (same branch, 2026-11-13; client drawing only).** The owner watched the preview: "increase the magnitude of all ork reactions by 2x of current - keep the scaling stagger strength." The base pose doubled (torso 19 -> 38 degrees, pelvis shift 0.07 -> 0.14 m, drop 0.07 -> 0.09 m; the far lean 7 -> 14 degrees, its shift 0.06 -> 0.12 m); every multiplier and the timing are as before. The per-hit cap went 3 -> 2 base sizes (the deepest tip 76 degrees; the same body-fold limit as before). Found on the way: the pelvis shift was applied in the pelvis's parent frame, not the skeleton's, so the first versions slid the hips off line (35 to 125 mm of foot drift); fixed, and the shift is cut back for a leg the clip left nearly straight: foot drift now 0 mm at strengths 1, 1.5 and 2.5. The combat-feel push-back (0.2 to 0.35 m) is left out for an Ork while the flinch is on, since it slid the planted feet (`--no-musou-ork-flinch` brings it back). Stage aids: `--flinch charge|blast|drift`, `--flinch-scale`.

**Musou Ork hit reactions, the cap at 2.5 (same branch, 2026-11-13; client drawing only).** The owner on the cap: "Let them go harder." `MaxStrength` 2 -> 2.5 base sizes, so heavy (2) stays below charge and hammer or axe heavy (2.5) and a close blast reaches 2.5; only a hammer's charge (3.1) is clipped. Checked at 2.5: foot drift 0.0 mm at strengths 1, 1.5 and 2.5 (`--flinch drift`; the legs take 100 % of the pelvis shift, 35 cm back and 22 cm down, in the idle phases tested); stills from the side and the front (charge, close blast) showed the head sinking behind the raised shoulders with the face pointing up, so the neck and head tip now stop at 1.5 base sizes (`HeadMaxSize`): the deepest tip is 85 degrees (spine 70, neck and head 15). No visible clipping through the body in the stills.
**On-hit effects at range and 30 % stronger (branch claude/onhit-range-intensity, 2026-11-13; client only: no sim, wire, protocol or config-hash change).** Owner: no yellow (armour) or red (health) on-hit splashes or particles at range with the lascannon and the Stalker Bolter; raise both by 30 %. Cause, measured on a flat test map with the real impact path (`--bolt-fx-demo`, new `--bolt-fx-range <m> --bolt-fx-fov <deg>`): both weapons are hit-scan and take the same path as all others; there is no cull, cap or missing report. The glows and particles are fixed sizes in metres (`CharacterViewer.HitGlowRadius` 0.24 m, the halo card 2.5 m, the data's effect scales), so at 40 to 80 m they shrink to a few pixels (the red glow in a 40 degree hip view: 339 red pixels at 20 m, 9 at 80 m), and in Classic PvP the on-player particles have been off at every range since 2026-11-11 (`PlayerHitFxRules`, `NetworkView.Fx.cs` `FxImpact`), leaving the model's glows alone. Fix (`ImpactRules/HitFxScaleRules.cs`, `NetworkView.HitFxScale.cs`): each effect keeps at least its size at 12 m in a 70 degree view on screen (spot up to 6x, particles 3x, red glow card 1.5x, scoped views grow little) and all are x1.3 (glow brightness via shader uniforms `k_hit`/`k_brk`, particle size). After: 560 against 339 red pixels at 20 m, 23 against 9 at 80 m; the yellow patch on a hit at 40 m is visibly larger and brighter. Switches `--old-hit-fx-range`, `--old-hit-fx-intensity`. Classic particles stay off (decision 2026-11-11): to be confirmed with the owner. Clips: `<media folder>\onhit\` (Stalker 40 m, Lascannon 60 m, before and after).

**Spark and burst particles back on hit players (same branch, 2026-11-13; client only).** Owner: "bring back the spark and burst particles on hit" and "before bringing back the glows, show me preview images and videos". `NetworkView.PlayerHitFxFlag` now reads true unless `--no-player-hit-fx` (new `PlayerHitFxRules.NoParticlesFlag`; also a lean-bot presentation aid), so Classic PvP again draws the armour-hit effects, spark fans, health-hit burst and hit container on a player, at the range growth and x1.3 of the entry above; the 2026-11-11 bare-armour flash and shot-break effect stay. Preview set for the owner (before = this branch with `--no-player-hit-fx --old-hit-fx-range --old-hit-fx-intensity`, which is main's look; after = this branch): `<media folder>\onhit\preview\`.

**Classic hit effects: no large burst, every damage glows (same branch, 2026-11-13; client only).** Owner, after the preview: only the yellow and red sparks and glows in Classic PvP (the large burst in the reference image goes; large explosive effects stay on Musou's ranged hits), and any damage should trigger them. `PlayerHitFxRules.LookFor(kind, extras, particles, burstRestore)` chooses Glows / Sparks / Burst per damage kind and mode; `FxImpact` now skips the health-hit burst and the body's hit container for a ranged hit on a player in Classic (`HitBurstDrawn`) and plays red-tinted sparks instead (`RedSparks`). New `NetworkView.PlayerDamageGlow.cs` wires the glow and sparks into every other damage source: melee strikes at their hit time (`MeleeFxFor`), charge connects (`ChargeImpact`), ground pound and landing blast (`PoundImpactPresentation`, jump landing), the air slash cone (`SlashHitPresentation`) and thrown blasts (`FxDetonation`); a real run on a flat map saw a bot's melee strike and thrown blast draw `HITFX damage` lines on an observer. Switches `--player-hit-burst`, `--no-damage-glow`. Preview set: `<media folder>\onhit\preview2\`; the melee, charge, pound and slash clips use the capture aid `--bolt-fx-melee` (the production helper with a synthetic attacker), not the real moves.

**Hit glows from confirmed damage only (same branch, 2026-11-13, review rework; client only).** The geometry selectors of the previous paragraph (presented melee victim, radius, cone and thrown-blast guesses) are deleted: they lit allies, the thrower and players behind walls. `NetworkView.PlayerDamageGlow.cs` now draws the glow and sparks from the two signals the wire really confirms: the own hit report for a melee or splash damage the own player dealt (`OwnHitReportGlow`; yellow when `ShieldDamage` above 0, red when only health) and the hit reaction that starts or restarts in another player's snapshot record (`ReactionDamageGlow`, always yellow: a snapshot carries no other player's health or shield; none for hyper armour; the own strikes are skipped there). One glow per damage event per victim within 0.25 s (`PlayerHitFxRules.DedupePasses`, stamped by every glow including a shot's). Pure rules and tests: `ArmourUpOfDamage`, `DedupePasses`, `ShowsOnModel`, `ReactionStarted`, `ReportNeedsGlow`, `LookFor`. Capture aid `--bolt-fx-melee` is unchanged. The look did not change, so the preview2 set stands.

**Damage mark: every damage glows, in every view (protocol 71, same branch, 2026-11-13; config hash unchanged).** Re-review: other players' light melee (a flinch, no reaction), hyper-armoured hits and melee kills never showed, and observers always read yellow, because the wire carried no per-player damage. `PlayerState` gains `DamageCount` (modulo 8), `DamageShield`, `DamageHealth`; `Combat.ApplyDamage`, which every weapon, melee kind, rush, blast and Musou enemy hit goes through, raises them; every player's record carries them in one new byte after the evade byte (`Protocol.Version` 71, `SlimRecordBytes` 48, `MaxSnapshotProjectiles` 12 so the fullest snapshot is 1195 bytes and keeps its 4 guaranteed shots). The client (`NetworkView.DamageMarkGlows`, after the remote shots each frame) shows the glow and sparks for a counter change on a living player seen before, yellow when the shield bit is set, red when only health: a respawn and the killing blow show none, a shot that drew its own glow is not drawn twice (one glow per victim per 0.25 s). The reaction-start glow is removed, so the ordering problem of its yellow beating the own red report is gone too; the own hit report still draws the own melee and splash damage at once. Tests: the sim counter, the wire round trip and refusal, the world's light melee marking only its victim, the client rules, and the pins moved by the byte (36 protocol-version pins, the byte offsets in the wire tests, the replay goldens, the 1195-byte budget). Real run: on a flat map the marks reached both an observer and the attacker for every shot and the killing grenade blast (`HITFX mark` lines) and the ally never changed; the bots did not melee in the run, so the light melee is proved by the world test, not by a live fight.

**Damage mark fixes (same branch, 2026-11-13, review).** The counter rises at most once per victim per tick (`PlayerState.DamageFresh`, not on the wire, cleared in `Combat.StepPlayer`) and the shield and health bits of a tick are ORed; the client reads red when health was hit (a shield break that spills into health is red) and skips a mark with neither bit; a damage that takes nothing leaves the mark alone; the client forgets players who left every frame. The replay goldens in `tests/SmNet.Tests/MusouIsolationTests.cs` (`FaithfulReplay`, `ExtendedReplay`) moved with the byte only: the same replay at the commit before the wire change (381a2017) gives 635FDF96... with `ReplayStats` Shots 168, Throws 17, Detonations 16, MeleeHits 49, Rushes 17, Kills 16, End Playing, and at protocol 71 8A5833FD... (the damage byte carries the fresh bit too) with identical stats.

**Dizzy boss (claude/musou-boss-dizzy, 2026-11-14; Musou only, client only).** Owner: "bosses turn around 180 degrees when stunned - fix that. create a new dizzy animation ...". Cause: the sim never turned a stunned boss (`StepBossStun` leaves the yaw alone, tested), but the crowd drew the Warboss's stagger clip `WB_Att_Charge_wall_hit_exit`, which turns the body round (seen in `--musou-crowd-test --dizzy --musou-old-boss-stun`). A boss in `Stunned` is now drawn on its idle clip, leaning 4 degrees in a slow circle, with 3 stars circling above its head until the stun ends (`MusouDizzyRules`, `MusouCrowd.Dizzy.cs`); the snapshot already carried the state, so no protocol or version change. The install has no dizzy clip, so lean and stars are ours (spec "Musou Mode: the dizzy boss", changes-from-original row, refine register). Tests `MusouDizzyTests`.
**Musou swing arc follows the weapon tip's path (owner, 2026-11-14; branch `claude/musou-slash-arc-tip-path`; client presentation only, Musou only; no protocol, rules or hash change).** The owner asked that the red and blue swing arcs match the path of the weapon tip through the air in orientation and shape, still at the cleave distance and not a trail on the tip. `MusouSlashArcPath` (SmNet, pure math) fits the tip positions sampled from the swing's own clip (`CharacterViewer.SampleMeleeTip`: forward kinematics of the clip to the weapon's bone, the tip the far end of the melee mesh from the grip, `WeaponRig.TryMeleeTip`; 28 samples from 0.30 s before to 0.12 s after the hit time, once per clip and weapon) into a polyline of directions seen from the chest: the fast part of the swing only, inside the cleave's cone, held to -60..+75 degrees of elevation. The view puts those directions out at the cleave radius (`MusouSlashArcView` `Offsets`); sweep, fade, colours, stencil, no-depth and the Compatibility path are unchanged, and a swing with no usable path draws the old level arc. `--no-musou-arc-path` restores the level arcs; `--log-musou-arcs` prints each path; `--tfw-arc-film` is the capture aid for a recording. Tests: `MusouSlashArcPathTests`. Preview: `slash-arc-tip-path.mp4` in the owner's media folder (`musou\slash-arc-path`) (part of it in ruins: the capture aid's lane B).
**Musou: Ashfall draft 13, heights (branch `claude/ashfall-high-ground-62bf0e`, 2026-11-14; Musou Mode only, map `tfw_war_heights`, heights version 1, level hash `0x0B35BFB12EF8FD3D`; `tfw_war` stays the city, draft 10 and the field untouched; no protocol or `TfwRules` change).** The owner asked for larger buildings and strong high ground for Devastators and Tacticals, with Assault jumping onto it, and no dead-end stairs, blocked stair entrances or walls in front of doors. New: the layout and map name, overwatch terraces (12, AC-050), larger buildings, `AshfallHighGround` (decks, dead-end flights, sight of the points, Assault jump reach from the spec), `AshfallDoorClearance`, and their enforcement in the pass. 74 decks, all on foot and by jump; no flight, stair foot or door problem outside the authored stronghold (3 dead-end flights and 4 doors there, as authored). `AshfallDraft13Tests` (11) and the 173 Ashfall/map/cache tests pass; both builds clean. Details: docs/musou-ashfall-graybox.md "Draft 13 heights".

**Ashfall draft 13 as the default (2026-11-14, ship).** Owner: "ship it and ensure that the newest ashfall version is included". The default Musou map `tfw_war` now builds the draft-13 high-ground layout (`AshfallLayout.Heights`; `TfwMap.LayoutOf`'s fallback); the draft-12 city moved to its own map `tfw_war_city` (host `--ashfall-layout city`, server `--map tfw_war_city`), the rollback; `tfw_war_heights` stays valid. A stale client on the city is refused with MapMismatch (the level hash differs). Tests pinning `tfw_war` as the city now pin `tfw_war_city`.

**Jump-pack flight blends (2026-11-14, anim/jump-pack-blend; Classic PvP and Musou Mode, client animation only; no protocol, simulation or config change).** Owner: the Assault Marine's and Raptor's flight "feels janky, lots of snapping". Causes found in the drawn flight (`NetworkView.Jump.cs`): the flight clip's direction and aim keys were chosen afresh every frame (steering, a mouse sweep or a velocity near the 3 m/s neutral threshold flipped the clip every few frames, each flip a new cross-fade); the take-off and direction changes faded over only the 0.1 s graph value (the viewer's floor 0.19 s); the landing clip started at the touchdown, so its fade ran after the feet were down; a remote jump flag dropping for a tick while still airborne flashed the landing clip. Now (all "ours", `spec/behavior.md` "Steady flight keys" and the three rows after it; `SmContent.JumpAirBlend`): keys held at least 0.22 s with a band round the neutral speed, a 1.3x margin between directions and 0.1 rad round the aim threshold; flight clips fade in over 0.25 s (`ClipBlends.FlightEntry`); the landing clip (run or idle by horizontal speed) starts 0.19 s before ground contact, predicted from the height, vertical speed and the pack's falling gravity, held at its first frame until the touchdown; a remote flight flag that drops for under 0.07 s while off the ground is kept. The server's hit volumes keep the stateless `FlightPoseRules.Candidates`. `--old-jump-blend` restores all of it for before/after. Test aids: `--jump-test-steer` (the jump-test bot steers left and right in the air), `--observe-distance m` (the follow camera's start distance). `JumpAirBlendTests` (10) and `JumpFlightPoseTests` pass; both builds 0 errors; full `dotnet test` not run. Recordings (third person, replayed from demos so before and after see identical snapshots; Classic on the flat map, Musou on Ashfall; `-before-over-after` has before on top): `D:\sm-reimpl\media\jumppack-anims\`. Not yet checked by a human; root-yaw smoothing in the air was not changed (the body already follows the aim at the follow rate). Pound and air-slash entries keep the existing slash and pound timing curves.
